title: Despicable Me 3
tagline: Oh brother.
overview: Gru and his wife Lucy must stop former '80s child star Balthazar Bratt from achieving world domination.
plot:
Despicable Me 3 is a 2017 American computer-animated comedy film produced by Illumination Entertainment and Universal Pictures. The movie is directed by Kyle Balda, Pierre Coffin, and Cinco Paul.

The story begins with Gru (voiced by Steve Carell), a supervillain who has retired from his life of crime after marrying Lucy (voiced by Kristen Wiig) and having three girls: Margo (voiced by Miranda Cosgrove), Edith (voiced by Dana Gaier), and Agnes (voiced by Nev Scharrel). Gru is now a suburban father, trying to balance his family life with his desire for adventure.

However, Gru's past comes back to haunt him when he discovers that his long-lost twin brother, Dru (also voiced by Steve Carell), has been kidnapped by the Anti-Villain League (AVL). The AVL is a secret organization that deals with supervillains who have retired from their life of crime. Gru sets out on a mission to rescue Dru and uncover the truth about his family's past.

As Gru delves deeper into his family's history, he discovers that his parents were part of a villainous duo known as Vector (voiced by Steve Carell) and Agnes' mother, who was also a supervillain. Vector is now working with the AVL to take down Gru and Dru.

Gru soon learns that Dru has been brainwashed by Vector and is now working for him. Gru must use his skills as a supervillain to rescue Dru and stop Vector's evil plans. Along the way, he also learns more about his family's past and the secrets that have been hidden from him.

The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, including a thrilling chase scene through the streets of Paris and a showdown with Vector at the AVL headquarters. The film also explores themes of family, identity, and redemption as Gru comes to terms with his past and finds a new sense of purpose.

In the end, Gru is able to rescue Dru and stop Vector's plans, but not before learning that he has a long-lost sister named Lucy (voiced by Jenny Slate), who was also a supervillain. The movie ends on a heartwarming note as Gru reconciles with his family and finds a new sense of belonging.

Overall, Despicable Me 3 is a fun and action-packed animated film that explores themes of family, identity, and redemption. With its lovable characters, witty humor, and exciting plot twists, it's a must-see for fans of the Despicable Me franchise.

title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
tagline: More than one wears the mask.
overview: Miles Morales is juggling his life between being a high school student and being a spider-man. When Wilson "Kingpin" Fisk uses a super collider, others from across the Spider-Verse are transported to this dimension.
plot:
Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is a groundbreaking animated superhero film that follows the story of Miles Morales, a teenager who becomes the new Spider-Man. The movie is produced by Sony Pictures Animation and Columbia Pictures.

The film begins with Miles Morales (voiced by Shameik Moore), a shy and awkward high school student who is struggling to find his place in the world. He is bitten by a genetically engineered spider that gives him superpowers, similar to those of Peter Parker, the original Spider-Man.

Miles soon discovers that he has become the new Spider-Man, but he is not alone. There are other Spider-Men from different dimensions, each with their own unique powers and personalities. These Spider-People include Spider-Gwen (Hailee Steinfeld), Spider-Man Noir (Nicolas Cage), Peni Parker (Kimiko Glenn), and Spider-Ham (John Mulaney).

The Spider-Verse is threatened by Kingpin (Liev Schreiber), a villain from another dimension who seeks to destroy the multiverse. Miles teams up with his new Spider-People friends to stop Kingpin and find a way back to his own dimension.

Throughout the film, Miles struggles to balance his life as a superhero with his relationships with his family and friends. He also grapples with the weight of responsibility that comes with being a hero.

One of the standout features of the movie is its unique animation style, which blends traditional comic book visuals with cutting-edge computer-generated imagery. The film's color palette is vibrant and expressive, and the action sequences are fast-paced and thrilling.

The voice cast delivers strong performances across the board, with Shameik Moore bringing a youthful energy to Miles Morales. The chemistry between the Spider-People is undeniable, and their banter and camaraderie add a lot of humor and heart to the film.

Overall, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film that explores themes of identity, community, and responsibility. It's a must-see for fans of the Spider-Man franchise and animation enthusiasts alike.

title: Monster High: Haunted
overview: Lurk what's waiting for the Monster High ghouls when they bring their killer fashion to the howlways of the spooktacular Haunted High! When the ghouls of Monster High follow Spectra Vondergeist one day, they discover a creeperiffic Ghost World with an all-spirit school. But their scary-cute student bodies are hardly welcome with the very strict Principal Revenant, and she punishes Spectra with frightful detention chains that prevent her from re-joining Monster High. Now, it's up to the imperfectly perfect friends to take on ghostly forms in order to save one of their own from disappearing forever!
plot:
Monster High: Haunted is a 2015 American computer-animated fantasy film based on Mattel's Monster High fashion doll franchise. Directed by William Lau and produced by Mattel Playground Productions, with animation by Nerd Corps Entertainment, it was released on DVD and Blu-ray by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment and introduced a new line of ghost characters and dolls. The voice cast includes Erin Fitzgerald as Spectra Vondergeist and Sue Swan as Draculaura, alongside Celeste Henderson, Haviland Stillwell, Karen Strassman, Laura Bailey, America Young and Cam Clarke.

At Monster High, the school for the children of famous monsters in the town of New Salem, the ghostly student blogger Spectra Vondergeist is desperate for a juicy story, while Draculaura becomes convinced she is being haunted. Spectra reveals a secret she has never shared: close by lies a hidden spirit world with its own all-ghost school, Haunted High, which she once attended. Hoping to find help and perhaps a scoop, since there has not been a haunting in ages, not since the legend of the Red Lady, she heads there and fails to return. Led by Clawdeen Wolf, Draculaura, Rochelle Goyle, Twyla and Sirena Von Boo set out after her, entering a realm where non-ghost monsters are feared as "solids." Twyla, daughter of the Boogie Man, devises a way to disguise the friends as ghosts so they can slip into the school. There they find a student body crushed by the strict Principal Revenant, who rules with the help of her Hall Moanitors and punishes pupils with detention chains that would keep Spectra trapped forever. Befriended by Haunted High students such as River Styxx, Vandala Doubloons, the painter Portergeist and Kiyomi Haunterly, the ghouls work to expose Revenant's scheme and her hateful rumors, unravel the mystery of the Red Lady and free their friend.

The film was released on home video in the United States on 24 March 2015. Common Sense Media's Renee Longstreet called it an engaging, mildly suspenseful story that stands on its own beyond selling toys, praising its humor, bright style and message about the harm of gossip and rumors while noting the familiar skimpy costumes. A DVD Talk family review described it as fun and not scary, recommending it for children aged seven to ten.

title: Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising
tagline: New neighbors.
overview: A sorority moves in next door to the home of Mac and Kelly Radner who have a young child. The Radner's enlist their former nemeses from the fraternity to help battle the raucous sisters.
plot:
Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising (titled Bad Neighbours 2 in some markets) is an American comedy of 2016 from director Nicholas Stoller, who wrote it with Andrew J. Cohen, Brendan O'Brien, Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg. Following Neighbors (2014), it stars Seth Rogen and Rose Byrne as Mac and Kelly Radner, Zac Efron as Teddy Sanders and Chloë Grace Moretz as Shelby, with Dave Franco, Ike Barinholtz, Kiersey Clemons and Beanie Feldstein.

Expecting their second child, Mac and Kelly agree to sell their house to the Baier family, but the deal is in escrow for thirty days. Meanwhile, the college freshmen Shelby, Beth and Nora, appalled by sexist fraternity parties and by a rule barring sororities from hosting their own, found an independent sorority, Kappa Nu. Teddy, from the first film, is adrift: his friends have moved on to careers, while his criminal record keeps him out of decent work, and when his best friend Pete gets engaged to his boyfriend Darren, Pete asks him to move out. Teddy wanders back to his old fraternity house next to the Radners, where he finds the girls hoping to rent it, and offers to teach them how to throw parties to pay the rent.

The Radners ask Shelby to hold off, but she refuses, and appeals to the dean and her father fail. A prank war follows: Mac, Kelly and their friends Jimmy and Paula infest the house with bed bugs, while the girls plan to sell marijuana at a tailgate party. Disgusted by their pranks, Teddy is thrown out of the sorority and joins forces with the Radners, distracting the girls while Mac steals their stash. The sorority hits back by tricking Mac into flying to Australia and ransacking the Radners' house, and the Baiers threaten to back out unless the girls are evicted. Facing eviction, Shelby reluctantly stages a raunchy, fraternity-style party, but after Beth and Nora accuse her of betraying their ideals, Kelly urges the girls not to give up on themselves. They throw a party on their own terms and are flooded with new recruits from other sororities, earning enough to keep the house. The Radners rent their own home to Kappa Nu rather than sell it, Teddy reconciles with Pete and becomes a wedding planner, and both couples welcome their babies.

Neighbors 2 premiered in Berlin on April 26, 2016, and was released by Universal Pictures in the United States on May 20. It grossed $108.8 million worldwide on a $35 million budget and received mostly positive reviews, with 65% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Teen Beach 2
tagline: Same surf. New turf.
overview: When characters from the movie musical “Wet Side Story” get stuck in the real world, teens Brady and Mack must find a way to return them home.
plot:
Teen Beach 2 is a 2015 American musical teen comedy released as a Disney Channel Original Movie. The sequel to Teen Beach Movie (2013), it was again directed by Jeffrey Hornaday, with a screenplay by Matt and Bill Eddy from a story by Robert Horn and Dan Berendsen. Ross Lynch, Maia Mitchell, Grace Phipps, Garrett Clayton, John DeLuca, Chrissie Fit and Jordan Fisher are among the cast members who return from the first film.

After their summer adventure inside the 1960s beach musical Wet Side Story, Brady and McKenzie, known as Mack, have become a couple despite their opposite personalities, but going back to school strains their relationship. Mack throws herself into organising a "Save the Beach" dance, while Brady secretly works on surfboard designs and forgets a college fair he had promised to attend with her, and the two break up.

Inside the film world, the lead characters Lela and Tanner have changed since meeting Brady and Mack and begin straying from their scripted story. Finding Mack's lost necklace, they dive into the ocean and emerge in the modern world, where they are thrilled by everything around them. Brady and Mack try to persuade them to go home, while back in the movie their friends struggle to carry on without the stars. At school Lela becomes absorbed in math homework, Tanner worries he is not enough for her, and Brady confides that he and Mack are on a break.

When Brady and Mack show Lela and Tanner clips proving they are only characters in a film, Lela angrily throws the necklace into the sea. Soon the rest of the Wet Side Story gang arrive with news that characters in their world are vanishing, and Brady and Mack realise the film will cease to exist without its leads. The visitors return home, but the gang reappear at the dance, still fading, to help the couple make up. Using a motorised surfboard Brady built and the emblem from Mack's grandfather's board, the couple reconcile, agree to stop keeping secrets and send Lela and Tanner back. In the altered timeline that follows, Brady and Mack meet again at the dance, where the film has become Lela's story.

The film received mixed reviews; Variety's Brian Lowry praised its songs and talented cast but found the storytelling padded between musical numbers.

title: The Infiltrator
tagline: The true story of one man against the biggest drug cartel in history.
overview: A U.S Customs official uncovers a massive money laundering scheme involving Pablo Escobar.
plot:
The Infiltrator is a 2016 biographical crime thriller directed by Brad Furman from a screenplay by his mother, Ellen Brown Furman, adapted from the memoir of the same name by Robert Mazur, the U.S. Customs agent who spent the 1980s undercover as a corrupt businessman to expose the money-laundering network serving Pablo Escobar's Medellín cartel. Bryan Cranston stars as Mazur, with Diane Kruger, John Leguizamo, Benjamin Bratt, Amy Ryan, Juliet Aubrey, Elena Anaya, Yul Vazquez, Saïd Taghmaoui, Art Malik, Joe Gilgun, Jason Isaacs and Olympia Dukakis in supporting roles.

In 1986, Mazur is nearly exposed when the wire hidden under his shirt during a drug bust begins to burn his chest. Although the injury would allow him to retire early to his wife Evelyn and their two children, he stays on with a new idea: rather than seizing shipments of cocaine that are quickly replaced, investigators should follow the money. Posing as Bob Musella, a polished businessman able to launder vast sums through a maze of investments, he works with fellow agent Emir Abreu (Leguizamo) under supervisor Bonni Tischler (Ryan), gains the confidence of low-level cartel figures and climbs the ranks until he befriends Roberto Alcaino (Bratt), a trusted Escobar associate, and his wife Gloria.

Small improvisations carry great risk. To avoid sleeping with a stripper offered by a contact, Mazur claims to have a fiancée, and the agency assigns him one: Kathy Ertz (Kruger), an undercover agent on her first field assignment. The cartel's money manager Javier Ospina distrusts Musella from the start, and Mazur's double life strains his marriage, notably when a chance encounter with a cartel associate while he is out with his real wife forces him to stage a violent outburst at a waiter. As his investigation expands to bankers at the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI), the operation culminates in a staged wedding between Musella and Ertz that gathers the targets in one place, where Tischler's teams arrest the Alcainos and several bankers.

The film premiered at the Tampa Theatre on 6 July 2016 and opened a week later through Broad Green Pictures. Critics praised Cranston's layered dual performance and Kruger's work, but many found the story familiar and short on tension; it holds about 72% on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed roughly $22 million against its budget. In reality, the arrests were made the night before the planned wedding.

title: American Pastoral
tagline: A radically ordinary story.
overview: Set in postwar America, a man watches his seemingly perfect life fall apart as his daughter's new political affiliation threatens to destroy their family.
plot:
In 1996, at the 45th-year reunion of the class of '51 at Weequahic High School in Newark, New Jersey, writer Nathan Zuckerman meets one of his old friends, Jerry Levov. They talk about Jerry's older brother, former all-state star athlete Seymour "Swede" Levov, class of '44, who had recently died after a long illness.
The story moves back to a young Swede persuading his father, glovemaking magnate Lou Levov, to let him marry his high school sweetheart, New Jersey's 1947 Miss America contestant Dawn Dwyer. Lou is skeptical because Swede is Jewish and Dawn is a devout Roman Catholic, but her strength and honesty sway him. They have a daughter, Meredith ("Merry"), and settle in the town of Old Rimrock, where they acquire a farm, with Swede commuting the 30 miles to the Newark glove factory.
Smart and quirky Merry struggles with a stuttering problem, and is deeply affected as a 12-year-old by the self-immolation of Thích Quảng Đức in 1963. By the time Merry reaches high school, she has become increasingly radicalized towards anarchism, as the Vietnam War rages, and frequently goes to New York City to take part in antiwar protests. When Merry lashes out during the 1967 Newark riots, Swede urges her to channel her energy into protesting against the war from closer to home. A few days later, the town's little post office and store is destroyed by a bomb, killing the owner.
Merry disappears, and is the FBI's prime suspect, though Swede and Dawn believe she is innocent or, if involved, being forced to act by older radicals she met in New York. Swede and Dawn visit Penny Hamlin, the wife of the store owner who was killed, to apologize. After Swede unsuccessfully hounds the FBI for information on Merry's whereabouts, 22-year-old Wharton Business School student Rita Cohen visits the factory, ostensibly working on a report for business class. Rita tips off Swede with credible information about Merry, hints that she knows Merry's whereabouts, then asks him to meet her at a hotel with $10,000 cash.
Swede meets Rita in the hotel room, but spurns her mean-spirited attempts to seduce him. Rita runs off with the money and leaves no further information regarding Merry. The strain of Merry's disappearance eventually causes Dawn to have a nervous breakdown. After treatment, Dawn seeks a facelift and starts an affair with a neighbor. She tells Swede that Merry has destroyed their former life, and tries to get Swede to forget about Merry so that they can start a new life.
In 1970, Swede spots Rita on a New York City street. Rita takes him to a skid-row area of Newark where Merry now lives. During two brief visits, Merry confesses to Swede that she made and planted a total of three bombs, killing four people. She tells of how she later slid into the underground, where she was robbed and raped. She has withdrawn from society, and is practicing extreme asceticism within the Indian Jain religion, which Swede attributes to her penance.

title: Frozen Fever
overview: On Anna's birthday, Elsa and Kristoff are determined to give her the best celebration ever, but Elsa's icy powers may put more than just the party at risk.
plot:
Frozen Fever is a 2015 animated short film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. It serves as a sequel to the 2013 film Frozen and was released on February 13, 2015.

The story begins with Anna (voiced by Kristen Bell) waking up on her birthday, only to find that she has come down with a bad cold. She is worried because she had planned a big celebration for Elsa's (Idina Menzel) coronation as the queen of Arendelle. However, Elsa's powers are still unpredictable and Anna fears that Elsa might accidentally plunge the kingdom into eternal winter.

Anna decides to take matters into her own hands and sets out on a mission to find Elsa, who has gone into seclusion after her coronation. Along the way, she meets Olaf (Josh Gad), who is excited about Anna's birthday and wants to help her celebrate. However, his enthusiasm is short-lived as he soon falls ill with a cold of his own.

As Anna searches for Elsa, she encounters various obstacles, including a group of snowmen who are trying to take over the kingdom. She also meets Kristoff (Jonathan Groff) and Sven, his reindeer companion, who offer their assistance in finding Elsa.

Meanwhile, Elsa is struggling with her powers, which are becoming increasingly difficult to control. She becomes convinced that she is the cause of Anna's illness and feels guilty for putting her sister in harm's way.

In the end, Anna finds Elsa and convinces her to come out of seclusion. With Elsa's help, they work together to create a magical snowflake that will cure Anna's cold and bring warmth back to Arendelle. The film ends with Anna and Elsa celebrating Anna's birthday in style, surrounded by their friends and family.

Frozen Fever is a heartwarming and humorous short film that explores the themes of sisterly love, friendship, and the importance of embracing one's unique qualities. The film features stunning animation, catchy music, and lovable characters that will delight audiences of all ages.

title: Extraction
tagline: Vengeance runs in the family.
overview: When a former CIA operative is kidnapped by a group of terrorists, his son learns there is no plan for his father to be saved—so he launches his own rescue operation.
plot:
Extraction is a 2015 American action thriller directed by Steven C. Miller and written by Umair Aleem. Kellan Lutz stars as a young CIA analyst, with Bruce Willis as his father, Gina Carano as a fellow agent, and D. B. Sweeney, Dan Bilzerian and Steve Coulter in supporting roles. Lionsgate Premiere released the film in December 2015 in a limited theatrical run and on video on demand. It briefly attracted renewed attention in 2020, when viewers confused it with the unrelated Netflix film of the same name.

The story opens in 2005, when undercover CIA operative Leonard Turner, played by Willis, is captured and interrogated by Russian arms dealers who know his true identity. They demand a list of people and businesses connected with the agency in exchange for the safety of his family. Leonard breaks free and kills his captors, then calls his colleague Ken Robertson to protect his wife and son, but his wife Kate is shot dead by intruders, while his teenage son Harry freezes when given the chance to shoot the attackers and is rescued by Robertson.

Ten years later, the adult Harry, played by Lutz, works for the CIA's Prague station as an analyst under Robertson. Although he trains hard and repeatedly applies to become a field agent, he is rejected each time, unaware that his father has been quietly blocking his advancement. Leonard is then assigned to recover the Condor, a powerful device capable of hacking the global telecommunications network, but he is abducted by terrorists during the mission. Defying orders, Harry goes rogue to rescue his father, teaming up with Victoria, an agent and his former girlfriend, played by Carano. Their pursuit leads to a series of shootouts and chases, while Harry begins to suspect that the conspiracy involves traitors inside the agency itself.

The film follows the familiar pattern of the low-budget direct-to-video action thrillers in which Willis appeared during the 2010s, often in limited supporting roles, with the younger lead carrying the action scenes.

Critical response was overwhelmingly negative. On Rotten Tomatoes only about 6 percent of critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic assigned it a score of 25 out of 100, indicating generally unfavourable reviews.

overview: The Machine Empire defeats the Power Rangers in battle, destroying the Megazord. It is revealed that Earth's governments then negotiate a truce with the Machine Empire and the Power Rangers are disbanded.  Years later, Rocky, the second Red Ranger has defected to the Machine Empire, is critical of Zordon's use of Power Rangers as child soldiers, and now sports a prosthetic leg. He interrogates a restrained Kimberly, the former Pink Ranger, about the location of Tommy Oliver, the former Green Ranger. He details the fates of the other Rangers in flashback.
plot:
Power/Rangers, also known as Power Rangers: Unauthorized, is a 2015 American superhero fan film that offers a dark, adult-oriented take on the children's franchise Mighty Morphin Power Rangers. Directed by Joseph Kahn, who co-wrote it with James Van Der Beek and Dutch Southern, and produced by Adi Shankar and Jil Hardin, it stars Katee Sackhoff and Van Der Beek, with Russ Bain, Will Yun Lee and Gichi Gamba. The short was released online on YouTube and Vimeo on February 23, 2015, with the Vimeo version including brief nudity.

Years earlier, the Machine Empire defeated the Power Rangers and destroyed their Megazord, and Earth's governments signed a truce with the invaders and disbanded the team. Rocky DeSantos, the second Red Ranger, has since gone over to the Machine Empire. Now walking on a prosthetic leg, he bitterly condemns the Rangers' mentor Zordon for turning teenagers into child soldiers. He is interrogating the captive Kimberly Hart, the former Pink Ranger, about the whereabouts of Tommy Oliver, the former Green Ranger.

As he questions her, Rocky recounts in flashback the grim fates of their comrades. Jason Lee Scott, the original Red Ranger, was gunned down by police hours after marrying Kimberly, apparently betrayed by the school bullies Bulk and Skull. Zack Taylor, the Black Ranger, became a thrill-seeking enforcer for the Machine Empire before being killed by an unknown assassin. Billy Cranston, the Blue Ranger, became an openly gay tech billionaire and was found dead in an apparent suicide. Kimberly insists that Tommy is not hunting the Rangers and that she has not seen him since the funeral of Trini Kwan, the Yellow Ranger, who died during the treaty talks.

Rocky reveals that Kimberly is merely bait. Tommy duly arrives, kills the guards and duels Rocky with a sword. When Rocky gains the upper hand, Kimberly shoots him dead, but Tommy demands to know who she really is, since the real Kimberly died in the final battle. The impostor's disguise falls away to reveal the sorceress Rita Repulsa, who was responsible for killing the others. She tries to recruit Tommy, reminding him that she created him, but he refuses and attacks her as the film ends.

Several details allude to the lives of the original cast, including David Yost's experiences after coming out and the death of Thuy Trang in a car accident in 2001. Saban Brands objected to the film, which was briefly removed from both platforms before being restored, and it drew millions of views.

title: Approaching the Unknown
overview: Captain William Stanaforth is on a one-way solo mission to take the first steps in colonising Mars. Like all pioneers throughout history, Stanaforth will face insurmountable odds and life and death decisions as he rockets bravely through space.
plot:
Captain William Stanaforth is on a one-way solo mission to Mars, taking humanity's first steps towards colonizing it. Although the entire world is watching him, he is completely alone on the space ship. After liftoff and the subsequent rocket separations, Stanaforth takes his suit off to relax and is set on course to Mars for 270 days by the team on the ground.
Through flashbacks we see how Stanaforth had come up with the idea to create water (H2O) by supercompressing sand/dirt and combining the separate hydrogen and oxygen byproducts. It is by this synthesis that the mission is made possible.
Stanaforth's water generation apparatus malfunctions during his mission to Mars. Rather than return to Earth as protocol requires, he takes manual control of his spacecraft and continues to Mars. His spacecraft becomes entangled with a nebula and through voiceover we hear Stanaforth ruminate on the nature of matter and space. Stanaforth says, "This is why I came here. To give everything up. For one moment of pure wonder." Stanaforth is then seen in his spacesuit, exiting the spacecraft.
Without explanation, the scene cuts to Stanaforth, clean-shaven in his spacecraft, preparing to land on Mars. Stanaforth lands on, then walks, on Mars. As he walks, we hear Stanaforth say, "Nothing has ever lived here. Nothing has even died here. Maybe I'll live forever."

title: The Lady in the Van
tagline: A mostly true story
overview: The true story of the relationship between Alan Bennett and the singular Miss Shepherd, a woman of uncertain origins who ‘temporarily’ parked her van in Bennett’s London driveway and proceeded to live there for 15 years.
plot:
In 1970, writer Alan Bennett moves into a wealthy suburb of Camden. Soon afterwards, he meets Miss Mary Shepherd, an irritable, eccentric, unsanitary, and religious homeless woman living in an old Bedford van, who squats outside multiple houses in Bennett's street of Gloucester Crescent. Social workers frequently check in with her, and other neighbours on the street frequently bring Miss Shepherd presents or food.
One day, a couple of youths scare Miss Shepherd, shaking the van and yelling at her, which causes her to wake from a nightmare she was having of a long ago traffic accident. The incident with the boys worries Alan, so he mentions at a meal with neighbours an idea to let her park in his drive. Though initially hesitant, a wealthy neighbour buys her a new van, and Miss Shepherd moves into his driveway, where she proceeds to stay for 15 years, from 1974 to 1989.
Bennett is discreetly gay, and sometimes brings his dates home. Shepherd naively assumes his dates are Communists, meeting secretly with him. During this time, Bennett balances his writing career with watching over Shepherd and providing for his increasingly invalid mother. Though he denies "caring" for anyone, he slowly becomes aware of his growing friendship with Shepherd. Bennett often imagines himself having philosophical discussions with himself.
Bennett discovers her fluency in French, which she learnt while studying the piano in Paris. Despite this, she has an extreme aversion to all music. When asked why, she explained that when she was a novice nun, left alone in a room with a piano she started to play a classical piece. She was forbidden to play it again. Bennett also discovers that she had driven an ambulance during the 1939 blackout in WWII, played Chopin at The Proms, and attempted to become a nun twice. He also finds out her real name: Margaret Fairchild. A mysterious man stops by her van who frightens her every so often, and she gives him money, and she lives in constant fear of the police.
Eventually, Shepherd is sent to a day centre. Bennett takes this opportunity to travel down to Broadstairs and meets with the man she frequently visits, who turns out to be her brother. He explains how he had Mary institutionalised in Banstead (she escaped not long after) and that she studied under the virtuoso pianist Alfred Cortot.
Bennett returns home, to find Shepherd back in her van. She had been scared off by a woman she'd known in Banstead, and had an opportunity to sneak in to play a piano in the centre. She explains that her confessor (in addition to the nuns) had forbidden her from playing, which she was told would help her spirit grow. Before Bennett goes into his house, Shepherd asks to hold his hand. Bennett obliges, and not long after he goes indoors, she dies peacefully in her sleep in her van.

title: The Survivalist
tagline: Every Stranger Is The Enemy
overview: In a time of starvation, a survivalist lives off a small plot of land hidden deep in forest. When two women seeking food and shelter discover his farm, he finds his existence threatened.
plot:
After a catastrophic global population collapse, an unnamed man, known only as the Survivalist, lives alone in woodland. He protects a small cabin and vegetable plot with traps and alarms, surviving by hunting, foraging and farming.
Two strangers arrive: Kathryn, an older woman, and her daughter Milja. At gunpoint, Kathryn attempts to trade jewellery and seeds for food. When he refuses, she offers Milja for sex in exchange for provisions. The Survivalist accepts and allows them to remain on the condition that the arrangement continues. Over time, the three establish an uneasy domestic routine, but mistrust grows as supplies diminish. Privately, Kathryn and Milja consider killing the Survivalist to conserve food, and Milja secretly removes ammunition from his shotgun.
Milja is later abducted by a drifter while bathing. The Survivalist tracks them, but when he attempts to reload his gun he discovers the missing ammunition and is shot in the stomach. He manages to kill the drifter with a knife and escapes with Milja. Milja and Kathryn bring him back to the cabin, remove the bullet and cauterise the wound. As infection develops, Kathryn argues they should let him die, but Milja insists they nurse him until he recovers.
Soon afterwards, a group of raiders arrives at night and attempts to force entry. The trio remains silent until the men leave, but the cabin and plot are ransacked and much of the food is taken. As hunger worsens, Milja realises she is pregnant. Kathryn again urges killing the Survivalist, claiming there is only enough food for two, and Milja prepares to poison him with mushrooms. Instead, Milja poisons Kathryn. As she dies, Kathryn asks the Survivalist to cut her wrists and bury her; he complies.
The Survivalist later tells Milja about his brother, whom he abandoned during a theft from other survivors in order to escape. While foraging, they see the raiders have returned. The Survivalist decides they must flee, but first seeks to recover a cache of stored seeds. The raiders return and begin dismantling the cabin; Milja slips inside to retrieve the seeds and alerts the men as she escapes. The pair is pursued into the woods and separated. The Survivalist distracts the raiders and is killed.
Milja continues alone until she reaches a guarded, fortified compound. She surrenders her belongings at the gate and is told the community will vote on whether to admit her. Noticing her pregnancy, a guard asks what she will name the baby; Milja replies, "If it's a boy…"

overview: A small town news team discovers a box of video tapes where a faceless figure dressed in a dark suit, haunts and torments a family...slowly driving them insane. Soon after, they realize that the "Operator" has begun to stalk them as well.
plot:
Eli (Brendon Huor) is fleeing through the woods with Jamie (Mickey Facchinello), who is recording. Jamie suddenly disappears, and Eli searches for him, but instead finds the Operator (Doug Jones), a tall, faceless creature in a suit. The Operator attacks Jamie before the footage ends.
Milo (Chris Marquette), Sara (Alexandra Breckenridge), and Charlie (Jake McDorman), are the members of a news reporting team. The three are tasked with investigating the disappearance of a man named Dan (Michael Bunin). Milo analyzes a series of Mini-DVR tapes filmed by Dan, discovering the presence of the Operator within them. A power outage occurs, and Milo discovers the Operator Symbol (⦻) engraved into his neck when the power returns. The Operator follows Milo home, and he goes to Sara's house but is forced to leave by her and Charlie. Milo decides to sleep in his car.
The following day, Milo returns home and finds Charlie in an upstairs bedroom. Charlie angrily confronts Milo about filmed footage that he has of Sara. Sara comes in and is disgusted by what she sees, and Milo begins to panic. Charlie refuses to let him touch a camera, and Milo then tells him to grab the camera and look around. Through the camera, Charlie sees the closet door flying open, and the Operator rushing towards him. Charlie drops the camera, and all three flee from the house.
The three go on the run, trying to escape the Operator and find out what happened to Dan and his family. Eventually, they learn that Dan used his money to purchase a new home, which had been burned down. They locate a storm shelter with a working camera feed, which reveals that Dan killed his daughter Tara (Morgan Bastin) before being killed himself by his wife Rose (Alexandra Holden), who then burned the house down.
They contact Rose, now locked up in an asylum, who informs them that she believes the Operator came into their life because Dan became interested in it. When she sees the Operator Symbol on Sara's arm, she attacks her. The crew are forced to leave while medical staff restrain Rose. They decide to make a last stand against the Operator in a cabin. After setting the whole place up with cameras, Milo notices that the camera picked up a detail he missed at the hospital: Rose's mark was gone.
The crew is then attacked by the Operator. Milo hangs himself, believing that if he dies, Charlie and Sara will be safe. The Operator seemingly leaves after Milo dies, but Milo's dead body suddenly rises from the ground like a zombie. It grabs a pipe and beats Charlie to death before catching and killing Sara. Milo then falls to the floor with pale eyes. Moments later, the Operator appears, and his movements seemingly loop. He then vanishes, and Milo's eyes return to normal.
The film ends with Dan and Rose leaving a sale, where Dan has purchased a camera with a "college project tape" inside, presumably a tape from the student film-within-a-film of the original Marble Hornets webseries.

title: Zoolander 2
tagline: Long time no Z
overview: Derek and Hansel are modelling again when an opposing company attempts to take them out from the business.
plot:
Zoolander 2 (promoted as Zoolander No. 2) is an American action comedy of 2016 directed and co-produced by Ben Stiller, who wrote it with Justin Theroux, John Hamburg and Nicholas Stoller. The sequel to Zoolander (2001), it reunites Stiller as Derek Zoolander, Owen Wilson as Hansel and Will Ferrell as Mugatu, with Penélope Cruz as the Interpol agent Valentina Valencia, Kristen Wiig as the designer Alexanya Atoz, Kyle Mooney as Don Atari, Cyrus Arnold as Derek Zoolander Jr. and cameos from Benedict Cumberbatch, Sting and many celebrities.

Valentina, a former swimsuit model in Interpol's fashion division, notices that murdered pop stars died making Derek's trademark "Blue Steel" look. Years earlier, Derek's Center for Kids Who Can't Read Good collapsed, killing his wife Matilda and injuring Hansel, while Mugatu was jailed for life. Having lost custody of his son, Derek became a hermit in the far north of New Jersey. Billy Zane persuades him and Hansel to attend a show by the couture queen Alexanya, where the out-of-date pair are humiliated by a new generation of hipster designers. Valentina recruits them to help find the killer, and through her Derek finds his son at an orphanage but is dismayed that the boy is overweight; urged by Matilda's ghost, he tries to bond with him.

At St. Peter's Basilica, Sting reveals that the stars died protecting a secret: the bloodline of Steve, a forgotten third human after Adam and Eve and ancestor of all models, whose closest descendant, Derek Jr., holds the key to the Fountain of Youth. Derek Jr. is abducted, Mugatu escapes from fashion prison and Alexanya is unmasked as his henchwoman Katinka. At a lavish ball, Mugatu plans to sacrifice the boy, revealing that he gathered the world's designers to kill them and that he sabotaged Derek's centre. Derek holds back a bomb with his "Magnum" look until Sting, revealed as Hansel's father, joins him, Hansel and Derek Jr. in hurling it back at Mugatu. Derek reconciles with his son and finds love with Valentina, and a reformed Mugatu joins the celebrations.

Shot in Rome in 2015 and released by Paramount, the film premiered in London in February 2016, where Stiller set a world record for the longest selfie stick. It grossed $56.7 million worldwide on a $50 million budget and was panned, scoring 21% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Arrival
tagline: Why are they here?
overview: Taking place after alien crafts land around the world, an expert linguist is recruited by the military to determine whether they come in peace or are a threat.
plot:
Arrival is a 2016 American science-fiction drama directed by Denis Villeneuve and written by Eric Heisserer, adapted from Ted Chiang's Nebula-winning 1998 novella "Story of Your Life". Amy Adams stars as the linguist Louise Banks, with Jeremy Renner as the theoretical physicist Ian Donnelly, Forest Whitaker as Colonel Weber, Michael Stuhlbarg as the CIA agent Halpern and Tzi Ma as General Shang of China.

The film opens with what seem to be Louise's memories of her daughter, Hannah, who dies of an illness at twelve. Then twelve alien spacecraft appear above sites around the globe, causing worldwide panic. Weber recruits Louise and Ian to lead the American effort at the craft hovering over Montana. Inside, they meet two seven-limbed, cephalopod-like beings they call heptapods and nickname Abbott and Costello, who write in complex logograms. As Louise makes progress, she is visited by vivid images of her daughter.

When the team finally asks why the visitors have come, the reply seems to say "offer weapon". China, which has been using mahjong to communicate, reads it as a threat and cuts off contact, as do others; Louise argues that "weapon" may simply mean "tool". Rogue soldiers plant a bomb in the Montana craft, but the heptapods eject Louise and Ian before it explodes. With Shang issuing an ultimatum for the ship above China to leave, Ian finds that the message fills exactly one-twelfth of its space, and Louise concludes that it is split among the twelve ships to force nations to cooperate. Returning alone, Louise learns from Costello that Abbott is dying and that the heptapods have come to help humanity because they will need its help in 3,000 years. Their gift is the language itself, which frees its speakers from a linear experience of time. Louise understands that her visions are not memories but glimpses of the future. In one, at a celebration of global unity, Shang tells her that she stopped his attack by calling his private number and repeating his late wife's dying words. Grabbing Halpern's satellite phone, she does so; China stands down, the nations share their data and the ships depart. Louise accepts the future she has foreseen with Ian, including Hannah's birth and death.

After premiering at Venice in September 2016, the film grossed $213 million worldwide on a $47 million budget and was acclaimed, with 94% on Rotten Tomatoes. It earned eight Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, and won Best Sound Editing.

title: Dumbo
tagline: Soar to new heights.
overview: A young elephant, whose oversized ears enable him to fly, helps save a struggling circus, but when the circus plans a new venture, Dumbo and his friends discover dark secrets beneath its shiny veneer.
plot:
Dumbo is a 2019 American fantasy drama film directed by Tim Burton, produced by Walt Disney Pictures, and based on the 1941 animated film of the same name. The story revolves around a young elephant with oversized ears who learns to overcome his physical limitations and find acceptance in a world that fears him.

The film begins with a dramatic sequence showing the tragic fate of Dumbo's mother, who is killed by a hunter while trying to protect her newborn son from poachers. The baby elephant is left alone and adrift, but he is eventually discovered by a kind-hearted circus owner named Max Medici (Colin Farrell). Max takes Dumbo in and decides to feature him as the star attraction of his struggling circus.

As Dumbo grows up, he struggles with the constant ridicule and fear from the other animals at the circus. His oversized ears make it difficult for him to fly or even stand still without falling over. The only one who believes in Dumbo is a kind-hearted mouse named Timothy Q. Mouse (Nick Sahindra), who becomes his confidant and friend.

However, things take a turn when Max's daughter, Holly Medici (Madison Davenport), arrives at the circus. She is a spoiled and entitled young girl who sees Dumbo as a means to get attention and fame for her family. As Dumbo's popularity grows, so does his dependence on Holly, who begins to exploit him for her own gain.

Meanwhile, a villainous character named V.A. Vandevere (Alan Arkin) emerges as a rival circus owner who seeks to buy out Max's circus and turn it into a more commercial venture. Vandevere is determined to capture Dumbo and use his unique abilities to create a new form of entertainment that will make him rich.

As the story unfolds, Dumbo begins to realize that he has the power to fly using his oversized ears. With Timothy's help, he learns to control his newfound ability and becomes a sensation at the circus. However, when Holly's true intentions are revealed, Dumbo must find a way to escape her clutches and save himself from being exploited.

In the end, Dumbo finds acceptance and love from Max and Timothy, who believe in him and help him overcome his fears. The film ends on a heartwarming note as Dumbo soars through the air, finally free to be himself and find happiness.

Throughout the film, Tim Burton's signature style and visual flair bring the world of the circus to life, with vibrant colors and imaginative set designs that transport the audience to a magical realm. The performances by the cast, particularly Colin Farrell and Michael Keaton as Dumbo's voice actor, are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Dumbo is a heartwarming tale of self-discovery and acceptance, reminding us that even the most unlikely creatures can find their place in the world and become stars.

title: Frozen II
tagline: The past is not what it seems.
overview: Elsa, Anna, Kristoff and Olaf head far into the forest to learn the truth about an ancient mystery of their kingdom.
plot:
Frozen II is a 2019 animated musical fantasy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie takes place three years after the events of the first film and follows Queen Elsa, Princess Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven as they embark on a new adventure.

The story begins with Elsa experiencing strange visions that lead her to believe that an ancient magic is awakening in their kingdom of Arendelle. Believing that this magic may be connected to the mythical land of Ahtohallan, Elsa sets out on a journey to find the source of the magic and restore balance to nature.

Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven join Elsa on her quest, facing numerous challenges along the way. They encounter new characters, including the Northuldra people, who possess ancient knowledge about Ahtohallan. The group also discovers that a dark force is threatening the land, causing destruction and chaos.

As they journey deeper into the unknown, the group encounters various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, mythical creatures, and their own personal demons. Elsa struggles to control her powers, while Anna tries to support her sister and keep her safe.

Throughout the movie, the characters face difficult choices and confront their pasts. The film explores themes of identity, community, and the importance of embracing one's true nature. The music, composed by Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez, is a highlight of the film, featuring catchy and emotive songs that add depth to the story.

The movie features stunning animation, with breathtaking landscapes and intricate details that bring the world of Arendelle to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, with Idina Menzel reprising her role as Elsa and Kristen Bell returning as Anna.

Overall, Frozen II is a captivating and emotionally resonant film that expands on the world and characters introduced in the first movie. While it may not be as groundbreaking as its predecessor, it offers a satisfying sequel that explores new themes and deepens our understanding of the Frozen universe.

title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
original_title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
tagline: A Rebellion Built on Hope
overview: A rogue band of resistance fighters unite for a mission to steal the Death Star plans and bring a new hope to the galaxy.
plot:
Rogue One: A Star Wars Story is a 2016 science fiction film directed by Gareth Edwards and written by Chris Weitz, Tony Gilroy, and John Knoll. The film is set just before the events of the original Star Wars film (Episode IV: A New Hope) and follows a group of rebels as they attempt to steal the plans for the Death Star.

The story begins with Jyn Erso (Felicity Jones), the daughter of Galen Erso (Mads Mikkelsen), a brilliant engineer who designed the Death Star. Jyn was raised by her mother, Shaak Ti (Deborah Ann Woll), a former Jedi, and her father's past is shrouded in mystery.

As Jyn grows older, she becomes increasingly disillusioned with her life on the planet Eadu, where she lives with her mother. She discovers that her father has been working for the Galactic Empire, designing the Death Star, and she begins to question his motives.

Jyn soon meets Cassian Andor (Diego Luna), a rebel spy who is tasked with infiltrating the Imperial facility on Scarif, where the Death Star plans are stored. The two form an alliance and embark on a perilous mission to steal the plans.

Along the way, they encounter K-2SO (Alan Tudyk), a reprogrammed Imperial droid who becomes their unlikely ally. They also meet Chirrut Îmwe (Donnie Yen), a blind Jedi monk who possesses a deep connection to the Force.

As the team navigates the treacherous landscape of Scarif, they face numerous challenges and obstacles, including Imperial stormtroopers, deadly traps, and treacherous terrain. Meanwhile, Jyn's personal demons come to the forefront as she grapples with her complicated past and her feelings towards her father.

The film builds towards a climactic showdown between the rebels and the Empire, culminating in a tense battle on Scarif. In the end, Jyn and her team successfully steal the Death Star plans, but not without great cost. The film concludes with Jyn's sacrifice, as she gives her life to ensure the plans are delivered to the Rebel Alliance.

Throughout the film, there are nods to classic Star Wars moments, including a memorable scene in which Jyn and Cassian escape from Imperial forces on a speeder bike. The film also explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the power of sacrifice.

Overall, Rogue One: A Star Wars Story is a gripping and action-packed adventure that expands our understanding of the Star Wars universe. While it may not be as iconic as some of its predecessors, it offers a compelling narrative that sets the stage for the events of A New Hope.

title: The Choice
tagline: Let your heart decide.
overview: Travis and Gabby first meet as neighbors in a small coastal town and wind up in a relationship that is tested by life's most defining events.
plot:
Travis Shaw is a veterinarian, living in the city of Wilmington, NC, who falls in love at first sight with Gabby Holland, who has moved into the house next door.
Their initial meeting, however, is rather rocky as Travis is hosting a noisy barbecue, complete with loud music while Gabby is trying to study next door. She is a medical student who is in a relationship with fellow doctor Ryan McCarthy. Travis has an on-again, off-again relationship with Monica. With Ryan in Atlanta for a few weeks overseeing a new hospital opening, Gabby seeks Travis's help with the delivery of her dog Molly's puppies, whom she at first believed were fathered by his rescue dog Moby.
As Molly has a complication, Travis insists on taking her and the puppies into his clinic. When his dad finds him asleep on the floor with them, he accurately surmises he's smitten with their owner.
The next day, Travis takes Gabby instead of Monica on a boat excursion with his friends. Travis's sister Stephanie, who had previously noted his interest in Gabby, observes it may be mutual. When he proposes to enter her place, she coyly says no. But shortly thereafter Gabby makes Travis dinner. He kisses her passionately, and they spend the night together.
Gabby and Travis spend time together, starting a relationship. They both celebrate his deceased mother's birthday with his family, then he takes her to his privately owned islet where he only visits alone. Travis even buys another wooden Adirondack chair for his lawn, symbolizing his personal investment.
Ryan returns, and is keen to resume his relationship with Gabby. Travis pours out his feelings to her but she, unsure of how she feels, tells Travis that their relationship wasn't necessarily serious, then says yes to Ryan's marriage proposal. Monica breaks up with Travis, telling him that she realizes he and Gabby are in love, suggesting he fight for her.
Travis goes to the hospital, only to find out she left after breaking off her engagement with Ryan. Ryan punches him for the affair. Travis then goes to Gabby's family home in South Carolina to propose. Initially resistant, everyone encourages him, her father suggesting he get down on one knee and her mother giving him her grandmother's ring. After convincing her of his love, she says yes. They marry and over the course of the next few years they have two children and become a happy family.
One evening, after a dinner to which Travis is late again due to a work emergency, Gabby gets tired of waiting. As she drives back home, she is involved in a traffic accident. She survives but is now in a coma, which seems permanent as she's been in it over 90 days. Travis is shown her DNR order, and asked to sign it. Racked with guilt, he has to decide whether to take her off life support.
After a hurricane hits their house, Moby helps Travis find the wind chimes Gabby had on her porch. He goes to his island and builds a gazebo, hanging them there.

title: Evolution
overview: 11-year-old Nicolas lives with his mother in a seaside housing estate. The only place that ever sees any activity is the hospital. It is there that all the boys from the village are forced to undergo strange medical trials that attempt to disrupt the phases of evolution.
plot:
Evolution (French: Évolution) is a 2015 French science fiction horror thriller film directed and co-written by Lucile Hadžihalilović. Set in an isolated seaside village, it stars Max Brebant as Nicolas, a boy who begins to question the strange world around him, with Roxane Duran as Stella, a nurse, Julie-Marie Parmentier as Nicolas's mother, Mathieu Goldfeld as his friend Victor and Nissim Renard as Frank. The film was shown in the Vanguard section of the 2015 Toronto International Film Festival.

Nicolas, a sickly boy living by the sea with his mother, is swimming one day when he glimpses the body of a dead boy on the seabed with a red starfish at his waist. His mother dives down and retrieves the starfish but insists there is no body, yet that night Nicolas sees her bring the corpse back as the other mothers gather around it. After an angry outburst, he is taken to a hospital, where a doctor makes an incision above his stomach and he finds himself in a ward with other boys who have undergone the same procedure, while the nurses watch videos of caesarean sections. Back home, Nicolas grows suspicious, and sneaking out at night with Victor he witnesses the village women writhing together naked on the shore; later he notices what look like suckers on his mother's back. At the hospital an ultrasound reveals the heartbeat of a fetus inside him, to his mother's apparent joy. Victor dies during an operation in which a creature is removed from his body, though the boys are told he is recovering. Nicolas, who refuses to eat what his mother brings him and accuses her of not being his real mother, finds a confidante in Stella, a young nurse who gives him crayons and paper. His drawings of things never seen in the village, such as a car, a bicycle and a giraffe, suggest that he and the other boys may have been brought there from elsewhere. As Stella reveals her own secret to him, Nicolas faces a choice about whether he can ever escape the island.

Evolution received generally positive reviews from critics. It holds an 82% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it creepy, provocative and aesthetically absorbing and a satisfying step forward for its director, and a Metacritic score of 77, indicating generally favorable reviews.

title: Song to Song
tagline: Love. Obsession. Betrayal.
overview: In this modern love story set against the Austin, Texas music scene, two entangled couples — struggling songwriters Faye and BV, and music mogul Cook and the waitress whom he ensnares — chase success through a rock ‘n’ roll landscape of seduction and betrayal.
plot:
In Austin, Texas, Faye feels disconnected from the world. She regularly interacts with others, hoping to feel more deeply. A guitarist, as she is looking for success as a musician, she starts an affair with record producer Cook believing it can help.
Meeting fellow musician BV, he actively pursues Faye, so they begin a relationship. He is slightly more successful than her and is also working with Cook. The producer suggest to Faye to tell BV about their affair, but chooses not to.
Faye's estranged father visits her. As she has not kept close contact with her parents, he pumps her questions, but her answers are not very informative, just that she has a few jobs and dating a musician. Faye shows apartments, walks dogs to pay her bills.
Cook and Faye keep their affair a secret from BV, and the three take a trip together to Mexico. As they move around the country, she and BV are very affectionate. Cook observes their connection, becoming envious.
Cook meets Rhonda, who is a former kindergarten teacher working as a waitress at a diner, where he courts her. As her father left them, she and her mother Miranda become more and more desperate for money. The two eventually marry and he pays someone to build Miranda a house.
Business gets rough between Cook and BV, as the latter is dissatisfied. He confronts him, unhappy to split the profits, not only because he does all of the work, but also he discovers that all of the copywrites are under the producer's name. This results in the end of their professional and personal relationship with each other.
Faye continues to have contact with Cook. After he is no longer working with BV, he offers to produce her. Faye meets up with Cook one last time, saying she can no longer sleep with him, as she realizes she is in love with BV.
Faye feels increasingly guilty about her affair with Cook, which BV picks up on. As she is acting strangely and crying, he point blank asks her if she has slept with him. When Faye says yes, BV asks for details. As she changes the details, from once to several, he breaks up with her.
Faye then has a relationship with Zoey, a French woman living in the US. Rhonda begins to feel uncomfortable with Cook's wild lifestyle, which includes sex with other women and drugs. BV dates New Yorker Amanda for some time, but eventually they break up too.
Rhonda takes her own life, leaving Cook shocked and saddened. Faye and BV reconnect and start dating again. Later, BV moves back west to his hometown to take care of his sick father and the rest of his family, and pursues a simpler life, taking a job as a worker at a drilling rig. Faye follows him and the two of them declare their eternal love for each other.

title: Date A Live: Mayuri Judgment

tagline: Because I've met you....I'm no longer an existance that was born to disappear.
overview: After performing a huge concert, Miku Izayoi invited Shido, Tohka and everyone for a day at a reserved indoor pool. Later at night, Shido keeps spotting a girl named Mayuri, who quickly disappeared after seeing her.
plot:
Date A Live: Mayuri Judgment is a 2015 Japanese animated film based on an original story by Kōshi Tachibana, featuring the characters of his light novel series Date A Live. Directed by Keitaro Motonaga from a screenplay by Hideki Shirane, it was produced by Production IMS and distributed by Kadokawa, and introduces Mayuri, a new character voiced by Sora Amamiya, alongside the returning cast including Nobunaga Shimazaki as Shido Itsuka and Marina Inoue as Tohka Yatogami. It opened in Japanese cinemas on August 22, 2015.

After a concert, the idol Miku Izayoi invites Shido and the Spirit girls whose powers he has sealed, Tohka, his sister Kotori, Yoshino and the twins Kaguya and Yuzuru, to a private indoor pool. On the way home Shido glimpses a mysterious girl whom only he can see, and who quickly vanishes. The next morning an enormous sphere appears floating above Tengu City. It is invisible to everyone else and can be detected only by the radar of the airship Fraxinus.

The analyst Reine Murasame suspects that the sphere has formed from Spirit energy that the six girls are unconsciously releasing because of their intense feelings for Shido. To calm their emotions and make it disappear, she suggests that Shido take each of them on a date, and he goes out in turn with Kaguya, Miku, Yoshino, Yuzuru, Kotori and finally Tohka, all while the mysterious girl watches over him.

During his date with Tohka, interrupted earlier by Origami Tobiichi, Shido meets the girl, who introduces herself as Mayuri. She explains that she was born from the Spirit powers that he has sealed away and is bound to the sphere, an Angel named Kerubiel. Having fulfilled her role of keeping the girls' feelings in balance, she prepares to say goodbye, but Kerubiel suddenly transforms and attacks, kidnapping Mayuri. Reine realises that the Angel has turned violent because of Mayuri's own jealousy of the girls who dated Shido.

When Shido declares that he wants to save Mayuri, the girls' Spirit powers are temporarily released and they battle Kerubiel. After Mayuri is rescued, the Angel transforms again. As Shido tries to protect everyone, the dangerous Spirit Kurumi Tokisaki secretly saves him, and the energy gathered by Mayuri gives Tohka a new Astral Dress. With Mayuri kissing Shido to aid her, Tohka destroys Kerubiel. The kiss seals Mayuri, and she fades away, leaving Shido a necklace and a lollipop as keepsakes. The film grossed about 248,000 dollars.

The movie uses this absurd premise as a metaphor for the fragility of modern society and the ways in which it can be disrupted by external forces.

Throughout the film, the characters' reactions to the sharknado serve as a commentary on contemporary issues such as social media obsession, celebrity culture, and the 24-hour news cycle. The movie pokes fun at these aspects of modern life, using humor and satire to critique their excesses and superficiality.

It asks questions about how we respond to crisis situations and whether our individual actions can make a difference in the face of overwhelming chaos. The film's lighthearted tone and absurd humor serve as a coping mechanism, allowing viewers to laugh at the absurdity of it all while also contemplating the deeper themes at play.

title: Little Women
tagline: Own your story
overview: Four sisters come of age in America in the aftermath of the Civil War.
plot:
Little Women is a 2019 American period drama written and directed by Greta Gerwig. It is the seventh film adaptation of Louisa May Alcott's 1868 novel and chronicles the lives of the four March sisters, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy, in Concord, Massachusetts, in the 19th century. The ensemble cast includes Saoirse Ronan as Jo, Emma Watson as Meg, Florence Pugh as Amy, Eliza Scanlen as Beth, Laura Dern as their mother Marmee, Timothée Chalamet as Laurie, and Tracy Letts, Bob Odenkirk, James Norton, Louis Garrel, Chris Cooper and Meryl Streep. Drawing on Alcott's other writings and her own life, Gerwig restructured the story using a nonlinear timeline.

The film opens in 1868, with Jo working as a teacher in New York and selling her stories to a newspaper editor, Mr. Dashwood. Her youngest sister Amy is in Paris with their wealthy Aunt March, studying painting and being courted by the rich Fred Vaughn, when she meets their childhood friend Laurie, who has fallen into an aimless and dissolute life. Jo is stung when Friedrich Bhaer, a German professor at her boarding house, criticizes her writing, and soon after she returns home to Concord when she learns that Beth's illness has worsened.

The story alternates between these adult years and the sisters' adolescence seven years earlier, during the American Civil War, when their father was away fighting and the family lived in reduced circumstances. In the earlier timeline, the girls befriend Laurie and his grandfather Mr. Laurence, put on plays, quarrel and support one another, and Marmee teaches them generosity toward neighbors poorer than themselves. Meg longs for pretty things but marries the modest tutor John Brooke for love, Jo rejects Laurie's marriage proposal because she wants independence and a writing career, Beth's frailty after a bout of scarlet fever haunts the family, and Amy pursues art and a practical marriage. In the end, Jo turns her family's story into a novel and negotiates with her publisher over both its ending and her rights to it.

Little Women received widespread acclaim for Gerwig's screenplay and direction, the performances, the costumes and Alexandre Desplat's score. It grossed more than $218 million worldwide. It received six Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, Best Actress for Ronan, Best Supporting Actress for Pugh and Best Adapted Screenplay, and won for Best Costume Design.

title: Amy
tagline: The girl behind the name.
overview: A documentary on the life of Amy Winehouse, the immensely talented yet doomed songstress. We see her from her teen years, where she already showed her singing abilities, to her finding success and then her downward spiral into alcoholism and drugs.
plot:
Amy is a 2015 British documentary directed by Asif Kapadia, the filmmaker behind Senna, and produced by James Gay-Rees. It traces the life of the English singer-songwriter Amy Winehouse, from her teenage years through her rise to fame to the addiction that led to her death from alcohol poisoning at her Camden home in July 2011, at the age of 27. Billed as the singer in her own words, it was instigated by Universal Music UK, whose chief executive David Joseph announced the project in early 2015.

The film opens with a 1998 home video of a 14-year-old Winehouse singing with her friend Juliette Ashby at a birthday party in Southgate, London, and then follows her story chronologically: her childhood, her breakthrough with the albums Frank (2003) and Back to Black (2006), her turbulent relationships, including her marriage to Blake Fielder-Civil, and her struggles with self-harm, bulimia, drugs, alcohol and relentless media scrutiny. Kapadia built the narrative from more than 100 interviews with friends, family and collaborators, laid over a wealth of previously unseen archive footage and unreleased recordings. Among the material are her Island Records audition in 2003, a cover of "Moon River" recorded when she was 16 with the National Youth Jazz Orchestra, home movies and holiday tapes, television interviews, her 2008 Grammy Awards performance, beamed live from London, where she won Record of the Year, and her 2011 recording of "Body and Soul" with Tony Bennett, her last session. The film also includes outtakes from her chaotic final concert in Belgrade a month before she died, and closes with Ashby recalling their last phone call, footage from the aftermath of her death and her funeral, and a montage set to Antonio Pinto's "Amy Forever".

Amy premiered in the Midnight Screenings section at Cannes in May 2015 and was released in the UK on 3 July, setting a record for the biggest opening weekend of a British documentary. It earned wide acclaim, with 95% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 85, and won 30 awards, among them the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature, the BAFTA for Best Documentary, the European Film Award for Best Documentary and the Grammy for Best Music Film. Winehouse's father, Mitch, objected to his portrayal and called the film misleading, while still praising its footage of his daughter.

title: Exposed
tagline: Some secrets are better left buried
overview: After witnessing a miracle, a young Latina woman experiences strange things as a police detective searches for the truth behind his partner's death.
plot:
Exposed, originally titled Daughter of God, is a 2016 American crime thriller written and directed by Gee Malik Linton in his directorial debut. Linton is credited under the pseudonym Declan Dale after disputing a final edit that shifted the film's focus. Keanu Reeves stars as the NYPD detective Scotty Galban and Ana de Armas as Isabel de la Cruz, a young Latina woman, with Christopher McDonald, Big Daddy Kane, Mira Sorvino and Laura Gómez. Lionsgate Premiere released the film in limited theaters and on video on demand on 22 January 2016.

Detective Galban investigates the death of his partner, Detective Joey Cullen, whose body has been found in mysterious circumstances. The case draws him into a world of police secrecy, as it soon becomes clear that Cullen was corrupt and abusive. His colleagues fear that a thorough investigation will expose his misdeeds, bringing bad publicity for the department and costing his family his pension. One of the prime suspects is a young former convict whom Cullen allegedly sexually assaulted, and some of Galban's superiors would rather let the killer go free than open a Pandora's box of trouble for everyone involved.

In a parallel storyline, Isabel, a devout young woman from a Latino neighborhood of New York, has a very different experience of the city. She befriends a girl named Elisa and suspects that the child is being abused by her father. Isabel begins to see strange, otherworldly figures in the streets and subways, whom she believes are angels, and when she discovers that she is mysteriously pregnant, she becomes convinced that the pregnancy is a divine gift, a belief no one around her is willing to accept. The two seemingly unrelated stories unfold side by side in separate urban worlds, but as Galban's investigation progresses, it emerges that Isabel is somehow connected to Cullen's death, and the visions she has experienced are revealed to be linked to a traumatic event that she has been unable to confront.

Exposed was poorly received by critics, many of whom felt that the studio's reediting, which marketed the film as a Keanu Reeves police thriller, undermined what had been conceived as Isabel's story, leaving the two narratives disjointed. De Armas's performance was singled out for praise, and the film is often cited as an early English-language role in her career before her rise to international prominence.

title: Storks

overview: Storks deliver babies…or at least they used to. Now they deliver packages for a global internet retail giant. plot:
Storks is a 2016 American computer-animated comedy-adventure film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and directed by Nicholas Stoller.

In a world where storks are responsible for delivering babies to new parents, the main character, Junior (voiced by Andy Samberg), is a young and aspiring stork who dreams of becoming a top delivery stork. However, after being rejected from the prestigious Stork Delivery Service, Junior decides to pursue an unconventional career as a "stork-umentarian," documenting unusual deliveries.

Junior's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets a human girl named Valentina (voiced by Akilah Hughes), who is born via stork delivery. As Junior tries to return the baby to its intended parents, he and Valentina form an unlikely bond, leading him to question his original career goals.

Meanwhile, Junior's boss, Sigourney (voiced by Jennifer Aniston), a no-nonsense and experienced stork, assigns Junior to work with a new partner, a young and inexperienced stork named Matt (voiced by Kimiko Glenn). As they embark on their delivery journey, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, hostile creatures, and unexpected surprises.

As the story unfolds, Junior and Valentina's friendship deepens, and they begin to work together to evade the authorities and find a way for Valentina to stay with her stork family. Along the way, Junior learns valuable lessons about responsibility, loyalty, and the importance of following one's heart.

In the end, Junior and his team successfully deliver Valentina to her intended parents, but not before she has formed strong bonds with the storks who raised her. The film concludes with a heartwarming moment where Junior says goodbye to Valentina, but not before she gives him a special gift – a baby of her own.

Throughout the film, Storks features stunning animation, witty humor, and lovable characters that will leave audiences of all ages smiling. With its unique blend of adventure, comedy, and heart, Storks is a delightful treat for families and fans of animated films alike.

title: Mary Shelley
tagline: Her greatest love inspired her darkest creation
overview: The love affair between poet Percy Shelley and Mary Wollstonecraft Godwin resulted in the creation of an immortal novel, “Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus.”
plot:
Mary Shelley is a 2017 romantic period drama directed by Haifaa al-Mansour and written by Emma Jensen, following the young Mary Godwin's romance with the poet Percy Bysshe Shelley and the experiences that led her to write Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus (1818). Elle Fanning stars in the title role, with Douglas Booth as Percy Shelley, Bel Powley as Claire Clairmont, Tom Sturridge as Lord Byron, Stephen Dillane as William Godwin and Maisie Williams and Ben Hardy among the supporting cast.

Mary is the daughter of the pioneering feminist writer Mary Wollstonecraft, who died shortly after her birth, and the philosopher and publisher William Godwin. At sixteen she lives with her father, a stepmother with whom she clashes, and her stepsister and confidante Claire. Sent to stay with family friends in Scotland, Mary meets and falls for Percy Shelley, a radical young poet who, she later learns, is already married with a child. Shelley follows her back to London, where he becomes her father's pupil, and despite the scandal Mary elopes with him, taking Claire along.

Shelley borrows lavishly against his family fortune, flirts with Claire and argues for free love, leaving Mary hurt and disillusioned. At a public demonstration of galvanism, in which electricity makes a dead frog twitch, they encounter Lord Byron, who becomes Claire's lover. Pursued by creditors, the couple slide into poverty, and Mary's first baby dies shortly after birth. The group then joins Byron at a villa near Geneva, where, kept indoors by bad weather, Byron and his physician John Polidori challenge everyone to write a ghost story. The challenge, together with Mary's grief and her fascination with galvanism, gives rise to the story of a creature brought to life and rejected by its creator. Back in England, publishers refuse to credit a young woman with the novel, and it is first published anonymously with a preface by Shelley, until he publicly acknowledges her as its author.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 9, 2017, and was released in the United States by IFC Films in May 2018 and in the United Kingdom by Curzon Artificial Eye in July. It grossed about $1.9 million worldwide. Critical response was mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reports 41% positive reviews, with a consensus praising its period detail and Fanning's performance but finding that it smooths out its subject's life, and some historians questioned its accuracy.

The story begins with Jackson Maine (Bradley Cooper), a country-rock singer who discovers a young woman named Ally (Lady Gaga) singing at an open mic night in Austin, Texas. He is immediately drawn to her talent and introduces himself, offering to help her pursue a music career. As they spend more time together, Ally becomes his muse, and he begins to mentor her, helping her develop her skills as a singer-songwriter.

As their relationship deepens, Jackson's struggles with addiction become increasingly apparent. He is a heavy drinker and often turns to substances to cope with the pressures of fame and his own personal demons. Meanwhile, Ally finds success in the music industry, releasing her debut album and gaining attention from record labels and fans.

However, as Ally's star rises, she begins to feel overwhelmed by the demands of fame and the pressure to maintain a perfect image. She starts to question whether she can truly be herself in the public eye. Jackson, who has been struggling with addiction, becomes increasingly possessive and controlling, causing tension in their relationship.

As the story unfolds, Ally's success grows, but so does her dependence on Jackson. She begins to realize that his behavior is toxic and that she needs to break free from his grasp. Meanwhile, Jackson's addiction worsens, leading to a series of devastating consequences.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Ally discovers Jackson's infidelity with another woman. Feeling betrayed and hurt, she decides to leave him and focus on her own career. However, in a tragic twist, Jackson dies from an accidental overdose, leaving Ally devastated and heartbroken.

In the aftermath of Jackson's death, Ally finds the strength to move forward, using his music as a way to cope with her grief. She releases a new album, which becomes a huge success, and she finally finds the confidence to be herself in the public eye.

Throughout the movie, Lady Gaga shines as Ally, delivering a powerful performance that showcases her incredible vocal talents. Bradley Cooper also delivers a standout performance as Jackson, bringing depth and nuance to the character's tragic arc.

Overall, A Star Is Born (2018) is a poignant and powerful exploration of love, addiction, and the highs and lows of fame. The movie features stunning music performances, impressive cinematography, and outstanding performances from its leads.

title: The Shallows
