overview: When Nancy is surfing on a secluded beach, she finds herself on the feeding ground of a great white shark. Though she is stranded only 200 yards from shore, survival proves to be the ultimate test of wills, requiring all of Nancy's ingenuity, resourcefulness, and fortitude.
plot:
The Shallows is a 2016 American thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and starring Blake Lively, Brett Cullen, and Jay Ellis. The movie follows the story of Nancy Adams (Blake Lively), a surfer who finds herself trapped on a rock formation in the middle of the ocean.

Nancy, an experienced surfer, is out catching waves off the coast of Santa Cruz, California. She's been surfing since she was a teenager and has developed a deep respect for the ocean. As she paddles out to catch a particularly large wave, she notices a great white shark (Carcharodon carcharias) approaching her from beneath the surface.

The shark attacks Nancy, biting down on her leg and pulling her underwater. She manages to escape by grabbing onto a rock formation in the middle of the ocean, but not before the shark severely injures her leg. As she tries to catch her breath and assess her injuries, Nancy realizes that she's trapped - the shark has taken out its anger on her, and it won't let go.

As the days pass, Nancy becomes increasingly desperate to escape. She uses her knowledge of the ocean and her surfing skills to try and lure the shark away from her rock formation, but the shark proves to be a formidable opponent. Despite her best efforts, Nancy is forced to confront the reality that she may not survive this ordeal.

As the tension builds, Nancy begins to experience flashbacks to her past - memories of her relationship with her ex-boyfriend, Brian (Brett Cullen), and her struggles as a single mother. These flashbacks serve as a reminder of what's at stake for Nancy: her life, her freedom, and her future.

As the shark continues to circle her, Nancy becomes more and more desperate. She starts to use unconventional methods to try and distract the shark, including using a surfboard to create a diversion and even attempting to lure it away with bait. However, the shark proves to be relentless, and Nancy is forced to confront the possibility that she may never escape.

In the end, Nancy comes up with a plan to outsmart the shark once and for all. Using her knowledge of the ocean and her surfing skills, she creates a makeshift "trap" using a piece of driftwood and some seaweed. The shark takes the bait, and Nancy is finally able to escape from its deadly grasp.

As she swims away from the rock formation, Nancy reflects on the experience and realizes that it's changed her in profound ways. She's forced to confront her own mortality and the fragility of life, but she's also discovered a newfound appreciation for the ocean and its power. The movie ends with Nancy swimming off into the distance, free at last from the shark's deadly grasp.

Overall, The Shallows is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of survival, sacrifice, and redemption. With its stunning ocean scenery and pulse-pounding action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

overview: A cinema remake of the classic sitcom Dad's Army (1968). The Walmington-on-Sea Home Guard platoon deal with a visiting female journalist and a German spy as World War II draws to its conclusion.
plot:
Dad's Army is a 2016 British war comedy directed by Oliver Parker, based on the BBC sitcom and set in 1944, after the events of the television series. Toby Jones plays Captain Mainwaring and Bill Nighy Sergeant Wilson, with Tom Courtenay as Lance Corporal Jones, Michael Gambon as Private Godfrey, Bill Paterson as Private Frazer, Blake Harrison as Private Pike and Daniel Mays as Private Walker. Catherine Zeta-Jones plays a German spy posing as a journalist, and the cast also includes Sarah Lancashire, Mark Gatiss and Alison Steadman, with Ian Lavender and Frank Williams from the original series in small roles.

In the spring of 1944, with the Allied invasion looming, Germany is desperate for intelligence after MI5 officers Major Cunningham and Captain Meeks intercept one of its agents in London. In the seaside town of Walmington-on-Sea, Mainwaring's Home Guard platoon feels unappreciated, until an exercise accidentally runs the glamorous writer Rose Winters off the road. Learning that she plans to profile them for a national magazine, the men are thrilled and thoroughly smitten, to the irritation of the townsfolk and their wives. Wilson recognizes her as a former Oxford pupil, and the two grow close.

Rose is in fact the spy, and when one of her radio messages is detected, Cunningham and Meeks arrive to find her. Mainwaring seizes the hunt as a chance to save the platoon, which Colonel Theakes is threatening to disband after a disastrous patrol near Dover. Having discovered Walker's black-market dealings, Rose uses him to join the next patrol and learns where the invasion will land, then convinces Mainwaring that Wilson is the traitor. While Wilson is detained, the others realize the truth and find Rose holding Mainwaring captive with a German landing party from a U-boat. With help from their wives, the platoon rescue him and capture Rose and the Germans. Theakes praises the men, Mainwaring and Wilson make up, and the platoon parades through town.

Released in the United Kingdom on 5 February 2016, the film grossed about $12.8 million. Reviews were generally negative, with a 31% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 38, although The Independent gave it five stars.

title: Bleed for This
tagline: This is what the greatest comeback in sports history looks like
overview: The inspirational story of World Champion Boxer Vinny Pazienza, who after a near fatal car crash, which left him not knowing if he'd ever walk again, made one of sports most incredible comebacks.
plot:
Bleed for This is a 2016 American biographical sports drama written and directed by Ben Younger, based on the life of world champion boxer Vinny Pazienza. Miles Teller stars as Pazienza, with Aaron Eckhart, Katey Sagal, Ciarán Hinds and Ted Levine in supporting roles, and Martin Scorsese served as an executive producer. It premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on September 2, 2016, and was released in the United States by Open Road Films on November 18, 2016.

In November 1988, the brash Providence, Rhode Island, fighter Vinny Pazienza challenges Roger Mayweather for a world light welterweight title. He barely makes weight after hours on a stationary bike, spends the night before the bout gambling at a casino and loses decisively. At the post-fight press conference his manager suggests that he retire, prompting Vinny's father and trainer, Angelo, played by Hinds, to explode. Vinny fires his manager and teams up with Kevin Rooney, played by Eckhart, a gifted but hard-drinking trainer best known for his work with Mike Tyson. Rooney persuades him to move up two weight classes, and the gamble pays off when Vinny wins the world light middleweight title by knocking out Gilbert Dele.

Shortly afterward, while driving with a friend, Vinny is badly injured in a head-on car crash. He suffers a broken neck, and doctors tell him he may never walk again and will certainly never box again. Rather than undergo a spinal fusion that would end his career, Vinny chooses to wear a halo, a metal brace screwed directly into his skull, and spends months in pain at home under the anxious care of his mother, played by Sagal. Defying medical advice and his family's fears, he secretly begins training with Rooney in his basement while still wearing the device. After the halo is removed, Vinny fights his way back into the ring, and his comeback culminates in a bout against the legendary Roberto Durán.

The real Pazienza, later known as Vinny Paz, made one of the most remarkable comebacks in boxing history, returning to win further world titles after his accident. Critics praised Teller's committed performance and Eckhart's transformation as Rooney, with Richard Roeper calling it one of the best boxing films of the decade, while others found the storytelling clichéd. Audiences polled by CinemaScore gave it an A−, but the film was a box office disappointment.

title: Ready Player One
tagline: A better reality awaits.
overview: When the creator of a popular video game system dies, a virtual contest is created to compete for his fortune.
plot:
Ready Player One is a science fiction film directed by Steven Spielberg, released in 2018. The movie is set in a dystopian future where people escape their harsh reality by immersing themselves in a virtual reality called the OASIS.

In the year 2045, the world has become a desolate and war-torn place due to climate change, poverty, and overpopulation. To cope with these problems, people turn to the OASIS, a virtual reality created by James Halliday (Mark Rylance) and Ogden Morrow (Simon Pegg). The OASIS allows users to create their own avatars, build their own environments, and engage in various activities such as gaming, socializing, and even finding love.

When Halliday dies, he leaves behind a challenge: he has hidden his vast fortune, known as the "Easter Egg," within the OASIS. To find it, users must solve a series of puzzles and challenges that test their knowledge of 1980s pop culture, including movies, music, books, and video games.

The main character, Wade Watts (Tye Sheridan), an orphan who lives in a slum called the Stacks, becomes obsessed with finding the Easter Egg. He creates his avatar, Parzival, and joins a group of "gunters" (egg hunters) who are also searching for the treasure. The gunters include Art3mis (Olivia Cooke), Aech (Lena Waithe), Shoto (Win Morisaki), and Daito (Rinko Kikuchi).

As Wade and his friends progress through the challenges, they must navigate the OASIS's dangers, including the corporation that owns it, Innovative Online Industries (IOI). The corporation is led by Nolan Sorrento (Ben Mendelsohn) and his right-hand woman, Soraya (Caroline Blakiston).

Throughout the movie, Wade and his friends encounter various references to 1980s pop culture, including DeLorean cars, Pac-Man, and Michael Jackson's music. The film's visuals are stunning, with intricate details and Easter eggs that reward close attention.

As the final challenge approaches, Wade and his friends must work together to solve a complex puzzle that requires them to understand the true nature of the OASIS and Halliday's intentions. In the end, Wade emerges victorious, claiming the Easter Egg and becoming the new owner of the OASIS.

The movie ends with Wade, now a wealthy and famous figure in the OASIS, reflecting on the impact of his discovery. He realizes that the OASIS has become a symbol of hope for people around the world, providing an escape from their troubles and a sense of community. The film concludes with Wade's avatar, Parzival, standing alone in the OASIS, ready to face whatever challenges come next.

Overall, Ready Player One is a visually stunning and action-packed movie that celebrates 1980s pop culture and explores themes of escapism, community, and the power of imagination.

title: Stephanie
overview: After a mysterious global crisis, a young girl is left alone to hide from a malevolent power that stalks her home. Her parents eventually return and the struggle begins to save their daughter.
plot:
Stephanie is a 2017 American supernatural horror film directed by Akiva Goldsman from a screenplay by Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski. Shree Crooks plays the title character, a young girl left alone in her family's home, with Frank Grillo and Anna Torv as her parents, Eric and Jane, and Jonah Beres as her brother, Paul. Blumhouse Productions was among its producers.

Stephanie has been abandoned by her parents and lives alone in the house with only a toy turtle named Frances for company, watched by a dark supernatural presence. News reports hint at a catastrophe unfolding in the outside world, but she flicks past them in search of cartoons. She keeps the body of her dead brother in his bed, alternately scolding and beating it and, after they make up, holding his cold hand, which squeezes back. Her games and tea parties are repeatedly interrupted by a shadowy figure, and each encounter ends with her waking up in bed.

Eventually Eric and Jane come home, apologise for leaving, bury Paul in the yard and try to resume normal life, though Eric always carries a gun and Jane bears deep scars across her stomach. That night Paul's corpse comes crashing back through the attic window, terrifying the parents while Stephanie remains calm. Questioned about the day they left, she recalls that Paul spoiled her pumpkin and that she broke his neck with telekinesis, a power that manifests as huge invisible tentacles and that also slashed Jane when she came to see what had happened. Her parents explain that the monster she has been seeing is not real: the monster is Stephanie herself. They sedate her and attempt brain surgery to remove her powers, but she wakes and destroys the makeshift lab.

Broadcasts reveal that murderous telekinetic children like her are appearing all over the world, with no cure, and that they must be killed. The parents' attempt to poison her cocoa fails when her power knocks the cup away, and when it lashes out at Eric he shoots her several times. She returns unhurt, tells them they never should have come back, and kills them both. After destroying the house, she leaves their bodies at Paul's grave, crushes her toy turtle and goes on to level the neighbourhood, while the closing images show destruction spreading across the planet.

The film premiered at the Overlook Film Festival on April 27, 2017, and was released by Universal on video on demand in April 2018. It received a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of reviews.

title: 10 Cloverfield Lane
tagline: Monsters come in many forms.
overview: After getting in a car accident, a woman is held in a shelter with two men, who claim the outside world is affected by a widespread chemical attack.
plot:
In a post-apocalyptic world, Michelle (Mary Elizabeth Winstead) wakes up in an underground bunker with no memory of how she got there. She finds herself trapped and unsure if she can trust the man who claims to be her husband, Howard (John Goodman). As she tries to piece together her past, she discovers that Howard has been preparing for a catastrophic event that he believes will destroy the world.

Howard reveals that he has been living in the bunker with his "wife" Emma (Bodhi Elfman), who is actually a man in disguise. He claims that they have been waiting for the apocalypse to arrive, and that Michelle's arrival was part of the plan. Howard tells Michelle that she must stay in the bunker until it is safe outside.

As Michelle tries to escape, she realizes that Howard's story is not entirely believable. She discovers a hidden room with a computer and finds evidence that suggests the bunker is actually a trap set by Howard to keep her captive. Despite this, Michelle remains uncertain about what is real and what is not.

Throughout the film, Michelle's character undergoes significant development as she struggles to maintain her sanity in the face of uncertainty. She begins to question Howard's motives and the true nature of their relationship. As tensions rise, Michelle must make a choice between trusting Howard or taking control of her own destiny.

The plot thickens when Emma is revealed to be a man named Ben, who has been living with Howard for years. The truth about the bunker and its purpose becomes clear: it was designed as a survivalist's lair, where Howard could keep himself safe from the outside world. However, Michelle soon realizes that she is not just a prisoner but also a pawn in Howard's twisted game.

As the story unfolds, Michelle discovers that the apocalypse Howard predicted never occurred. Instead, he created his own reality to cope with the trauma of losing Emma in an accident. The bunker was designed as a way for him to keep himself occupied and maintain a sense of control over his life.

In the climactic final act, Michelle must confront Howard about his deception and make a choice between escaping or staying in the bunker. In a tense showdown, Michelle outsmarts Howard and escapes the bunker, finally finding freedom after being trapped for so long.

The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the true nature of reality and the consequences of Howard's actions. As Michelle emerges from the bunker, she is met with an uncertain future, but one thing is clear: she has gained a newfound sense of independence and self-awareness.

title: Return to Sender
tagline: She will have he revenge.
overview: A nurse living in a small town goes on a blind date with a man who is not the person he says he is.
plot:
Return to Sender is a 2015 American psychological thriller directed by Fouad Mikati, a rape-and-revenge story starring Rosamund Pike as a small-town nurse, Shiloh Fernandez as the man who assaults her and Nick Nolte as her father. Rumer Willis, Camryn Manheim and Illeana Douglas appear in supporting roles.

Miranda Wells is a nurse in a small town who is in the process of buying a new house. A friend arranges a blind date for her with a man named Kevin, and when a stranger turns up at her door on the day of the date, Miranda assumes he is Kevin and lets him in. He is courteous at first, but his manner turns, he refuses to leave, locks the door and brutally attacks and rapes her. The real Kevin finds her and takes her to the hospital. Miranda recognises her attacker as a worker from a restaurant she visited recently, and the police arrest him: William Finn.

Life does not return to normal. Her real estate agent tells her the house has become unsellable because of what happened in it, and she is passed over for a promotion at work. Miranda begins writing to William in prison, but her letters keep being returned until one finally arrives with the words "You win" written on the envelope. She visits him, he apologises again and again, and the visits become regular, friendly and even flirtatious. Her father, Mitchell, is appalled when he learns she is still in contact with the man, and the two fall out.

After his release, William shows up at her house uninvited, and Miranda sets him to work repairing her porch. One afternoon she brings him a glass of lemonade; he soon feels unwell, asks to lie down inside and collapses. He wakes strapped to a bed in her basement, where Miranda reveals that she has been planning her revenge from the start and has poisoned him with antifreeze. Later she amputates one of his hands and then castrates him, telling him that he was right and that she has won. The film closes with Miranda visiting her father and telling him that William will not be coming around again.

The film was released in the United Kingdom in May 2015 and in limited release in the United States in August by Image Entertainment. Critics were largely negative, giving it 14% on Rotten Tomatoes and 23 on Metacritic, although Mark Kermode of The Observer gave it three stars and praised Pike's icy zeal.

title: Mr. Right
tagline: They make a killer couple.
overview: A girl falls for the "perfect" guy, who happens to have a very fatal flaw: he's a hitman on the run from the crime cartels who employ him.
plot:
Mr. Right is an American romantic action comedy of 2015 directed by Paco Cabezas from a screenplay by Max Landis. Anna Kendrick stars as Martha McKay, a relentlessly upbeat young woman who discovers that her new boyfriend is a former hitman, played by Sam Rockwell, with Tim Roth as his old partner and mentor Hopper, James Ransone and Anson Mount as the brothers Von and Richard Cartigan and RZA as the gunman Steve.

Francis Munch, a former CIA agent turned mercenary, has developed the habit of killing the people who try to hire him to kill. After one such job he survives an ambush by a team including a killer named Espinoza; Hopper backs out of the attack and merely watches. Munch then asks out Martha, and they fall for each other at once. After he dodges another attempt by Espinoza, they spend a chaste night together, and the following evening he reluctantly kills Espinoza when attacked over dinner. Over hot chocolate, Munch explains that a current runs beneath all things that can be sensed in advance, and that she shares the gift; when he throws a knife at her, she catches it by the blade without a scratch.

Von Cartigan, the sole survivor of an earlier massacre in which Munch wiped out the Pirrello heroin syndicate, plots with his partner Johnny Moon to have his brother Richard killed by Munch, knowing that Munch kills those who hire him. Munch kills the middleman sent instead in front of Martha, who asks for space. Richard sends Von, Moon and a squad of hitmen, including Steve, to Martha's apartment. Munch fights them off but is hit by Steve and captured, and Moon seizes Martha. At the Cartigan house, Martha defiantly announces that she will kill her captors if Munch doesn't. Munch arrives, shares gummy bears with Steve, shoots the bodyguards and leaves the brothers to fight over a gun; Von kills Richard. When Moon threatens her, Martha's own powers awaken, and she kills him and shoots Von with his own gun. Hopper handcuffs himself to Munch to reprogram him as a killer, but Munch frees himself and Steve shoots Hopper dead, delighted to claim a $5 million bounty. Two months later, Munch and Martha travel the world pursuing her interest in palaeontology, and when a sniper targets them, it is Martha who takes him out.

The film closed the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2015 and was released in the United States by Focus World in April 2016. Critics liked the leads' chemistry but not the tonal jumble, giving it 44% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Magnificent Seven
tagline: Justice has a number.
overview: Looking to mine for gold, greedy industrialist Bartholomew Bogue seizes control of the Old West town of Rose Creek. With their lives in jeopardy, Emma Cullen and other desperate residents turn to bounty hunter Sam Chisolm for help. Chisolm recruits an eclectic group of gunslingers to take on Bogue and his ruthless henchmen. With a deadly showdown on the horizon, the seven mercenaries soon find themselves fighting for more than just money once the bullets start to fly.
plot:
The Magnificent Seven is a 2016 American Western action film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Nic Pizzolatto and Richard Wenk. A remake of the 1960 film, which was itself a remake of Akira Kurosawa's Seven Samurai, it stars Denzel Washington, Chris Pratt, Ethan Hawke, Vincent D'Onofrio, Lee Byung-hun, Manuel Garcia-Rulfo and Martin Sensmeier as the seven gunmen, with Peter Sarsgaard as the villain Bartholomew Bogue and Haley Bennett as Emma Cullen. It was the final film scored by James Horner, who died in 2015 after composing part of the music, which was completed by Simon Franglen. The film opened the 2016 Toronto International Film Festival and closed the Venice Film Festival.

In 1879, the ruthless industrialist Bartholomew Bogue and his army of private agents take control of the frontier town of Rose Creek, forcing its residents to work in his gold mine for a pittance. When the townspeople protest, Bogue has their church burned and several citizens shot dead in public, including the farmer Matthew Cullen. He gives the survivors three weeks to sell him their land at a fraction of its value.

Matthew's widow Emma and her friend Teddy set out to hire men who can defend the town. Their first recruit is the bounty hunter Sam Chisholm, played by Washington, who shows particular interest when he hears Bogue's name. Chisholm assembles a band of six others: the gambler and trick shooter Josh Faraday, played by Pratt; the Mexican outlaw Vasquez; the haunted Confederate sharpshooter Goodnight Robicheaux, played by Hawke; his companion, the knife-wielding assassin Billy Rocks, played by Lee; the eccentric tracker Jack Horne, played by D'Onofrio; and the Comanche warrior Red Harvest. The seven ride into Rose Creek and wipe out the agents guarding the town, sending a message to Bogue. Knowing that he will return with a much larger force, they have only days to train the frightened townspeople and fortify Rose Creek for a final battle, while Chisholm's personal reasons for confronting Bogue gradually come to light.

Fuqua's version emphasises the diversity of its heroes and stages large-scale action sequences and an extended climactic battle.

The Magnificent Seven received mixed to positive reviews, with about 64 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes; critics praised the cast and action while noting the lack of originality. It was a moderate success, grossing about 162 million dollars worldwide against a budget of around 90 million.

title: Woodlawn
tagline: One Hope. One Truth. One Way (John 14:6)
overview: Love and unity in a school torn by racism and hate in the 1970s. A gifted high school football player must learn to embrace his talent and his faith as he battles racial tensions on and off the field.
plot:
Woodlawn is a 2015 American Christian sports drama directed by the Erwin Brothers, Jon and Andrew Erwin, and based on the true story of coach Tandy Gerelds and running back Tony Nathan at Woodlawn High School in Birmingham, Alabama. Caleb Castille plays Nathan and Nic Bishop plays Gerelds, with Sean Astin as the sports chaplain Hank Erwin, the directors' father, Sherri Shepherd as Nathan's mother Louise, Jon Voight as the Alabama coach Paul "Bear" Bryant, and C. Thomas Howell in a supporting role. Produced by Kevin Downes and Daryl Lefever with Crescent City Pictures and Red Sky Studios, it was released by Pure Flix Entertainment on 16 October 2015.

In 1973, Woodlawn High School is desegregated amid fierce controversy, and the gifted Black athlete Tony Nathan and several other Black students join its predominantly white football team. Coach Gerelds urges his players to channel their anger into their game, but the racial divisions of the city spill over into the team, and Black and white players clash both on and off the field. After a riot erupts at the school, Gerelds reluctantly allows Hank Erwin, a travelling sports chaplain, to address the team as a motivational speaker.

Erwin's message of faith and reconciliation has an unexpected effect: many of the players commit themselves to Christianity and begin to see each other as brothers rather than rivals. As the team's unity grows, Nathan emerges as a star, becoming one of the first Black football heroes in Alabama, and his talent attracts the attention of college recruiters. The team's success builds toward what became one of the most celebrated high school football games in the state's history, played before an enormous crowd, while Gerelds, who is initially sceptical of religion, must confront his own beliefs and his responsibility to his players during a time of racial tension.

Nathan later played for Bear Bryant at the University of Alabama and for Don Shula's Miami Dolphins, where he started in two Super Bowls, and the film's closing scenes reflect on the lasting impact of the Woodlawn team. It presents the story as an example of a spiritual revival bringing a divided community together.

Woodlawn grossed about 14.4 million dollars and received generally positive reviews, with a 79 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a rare A+ grade from CinemaScore audiences.

title: War on Everyone
tagline: They have the right to remain violent.
overview: Two corrupt cops in New Mexico set out to blackmail and frame every criminal unfortunate enough to cross their path. Things take a sinister turn, however, when they try to intimidate someone who is more dangerous than they are. Or is he?
plot:
Terry Monroe and Bob Bolaño, two corrupt cops, return to the Albuquerque police force after being suspended for assaulting a racist coworker. Bolaño and Monroe regularly assault, rob and extort criminals, accept bribes, and take drugs. While surveilling small time thieves, the two come to believe Jimmy Harris, a local criminal, is planning a heist. They contact one of Harris' former associates, Reggie, and coerce him into revealing information by threatening to falsely arrest him. Reggie and his friend, Irishman Pádraic Power, identify Clifford Reynard, a getaway driver, and tell them Harris' girlfriend, Jackie Hollis, used to dance at a strip club owned by Russell Birdwell. Birdwell, though suspicious, reveals Hollis' address. After bursting into Harris' house and knocking him out, they extort several expensive possessions.
Meanwhile, Birdwell tells his boss, James Mangan, an ennobled British businessman who is in charge of the heist, that the cops have been asking about Hollis. Mangan tells Birdwell to intimidate both Hollis and the cops. Monroe returns to Hollis and gives her a replacement television. After flirting with each other, they have sex and begin seeing each other. While staking out Reynard's house to extort him, too, they hear a scream. In the house, they find that Reynard's wife has murdered him, though she is too hysterical to explain why. Irritated, the cops attempt to quiet her while they consider their next step. Reynard's teenage son flees, but they are unable to catch him. After a nightmare, Monroe becomes concerned and searches the city for the missing boy. As he does this, Birdwell scares Bolaño's wife by smashing the window of her shop as she talks to Hollis.
With Reynard dead, Reggie takes his place as the getaway driver, though he misleads Bolaño and Monroe into believing it will be taking place elsewhere. When the cops finally catch on to him, they discover Harris and his cohorts dead. Not knowing Mangan's involvement, they assume Reggie is responsible. Before going after Reggie, they learn about Birdwell's harassment and beat him so badly that he loses an eye. Knowing they have numerous enemies and believing themselves untouchable anyway, they do not bother asking who sent him, remaining blind to Mangan's involvement. Reggie's friend Power, when offered a bribe, tells them Reggie fled to Iceland. Though they know nothing more than that, they leave for Iceland, reasoning that an African American man will stick out. To Monroe's amazement, the plan works, and they spontaneously find him in a crowd. Under pressure, Reggie reveals Mangan's involvement and agrees to split his take from the heist with them.
Back in Albuquerque, Lieutenant Stanton says Birdwell has filed charges against them. Monroe and Bolaño assure him that their investigation is nearing completion and will implicate Birdwell. As Monroe and Bolaño search for Mangan, they chance upon Reynard's child, who is living homeless on the streets.

title: Rock Dog
tagline: A new breed of rock star
overview: When a radio falls from the sky into the hands of a wide-eyed Tibetan Mastiff, he leaves home to fulfill his dream of becoming a musician, setting into motion a series of completely unexpected events.
plot:
Teenage Tibetan Mastiff Bodi is expected to be the next guard of the village of Snow Mountain, succeeding his father Khampa, who years ago drove out a pack of gangster grey wolves, led by the villainous Linnux. To maintain the illusion of multiple guards, Khampa has local sheep disguised as Mastiffs, but Bodi struggles to master the Iron Paw, a powerful move that requires him to "find the fire". Khampa has long ago banned music in the village to prevent distractions.
One day, Bodi indirectly causes a nearby flying plane to drop a package, which includes a radio. Entranced with British rock legend Angus Scattergood, Bodi defies his father by modifying a traditional dramyin into a conventional Western guitar and neglecting his duties to pursue music. Despite an incident where Bodi mistakenly alerts the village to a false alarm, elder Fleetwood Yak convinces Khampa to let Bodi follow his dream, giving him a bus ticket to the city with a promise to return and surrender music if unsuccessful. At the bus station, Bodi is discovered by two of Linnux's henchman, Riff and Skozz, and Linnux orders them to kidnap Bodi, reasoning it is his chance to take over Snow Mountain.
In the city, Bodi heads to Rock and Roll Park, hoping to follow in Scattergood's footsteps. He attempts to join a band consisting of bassist fox Darma and goat drummer Germur. Bodi, however, is humiliated after losing a guitar contest to arrogant snow leopard Trey, who after discovering Bodi's idolization for Scattergood, manipulates him into convincing Scattergood to give him some guitar lessons at his mansion. At the mansion, Scattergood is put off by Bodi's attitude and tries to evade him. Bodi and Scattergood later get lost in a back alley and Bodi resorts to busking to get money for Scattergood to return to his mansion. Riff and Skozz mistakenly kidnap Scattergood after they see Bodi at the park; Riff and Skozz drop Scattergood off at his home and continue their search for Bodi. Scattergood believes his career is over since he has less than a day to write a new song, when he hears Bodi playing on his guitar and invites him into his home with the facade of a "guitar lesson", where the duo create a new song called "Glorious".
Back at the park, Bodi feels betrayed when Scattergood takes full credit for the song they wrote together on a radio. Trey mocks Bodi and everyone in the park leaves, with Darma and Germur feeling sorry for him. Soon after, Bodi is captured by Linnux's henchmen via tranquilizer darts, who inadvertently reveals the fake Mastiff guards under interrogation. Linnux plans an attack on Snow Mountain, while Bodi is put into a boxing match at Linnux's Fight Palace, but Bodi has his opponent break the cage surrounding them so he can escape.
Scattergood, guilt-tripped by his robot butler Ozzie for exploiting Bodi for his own selfishness, uses his old tour bus to find him and apologize.

title: Survivor
tagline: His next target is now hunting him
overview: A Foreign Service Officer in London tries to prevent a terrorist attack set to hit New York, but is forced to go on the run when she is framed for crimes she did not commit.
plot:
Survivor is a 2015 action spy thriller directed by James McTeigue and written by Philip Shelby. Milla Jovovich stars as Kate Abbott, a Diplomatic Security Service agent, and Pierce Brosnan as a deadly assassin known as the Watchmaker, with Dylan McDermott, Robert Forster, Angela Bassett, James D'Arcy, Frances de la Tour, Genevieve O'Reilly and, in his final film role, Roger Rees. The film was released in cinemas in the United Kingdom on 5 June 2015 and direct-to-video in the United States later that month.

During a firefight in the Middle East, an American soldier, Johnny Talbot, is captured by terrorists and forced to watch the execution of a comrade. In London, Kate Abbott, who joined government service after losing friends in the September 11 attacks, works at the American Embassy screening visa applications to keep terrorists out of the United States, and introduces stricter checks. When her colleagues gather at a restaurant for the birthday of their superior, Bill Talbot, a bomb explodes, killing most of her team. Kate survives only because she stepped out to buy a last-minute present. Bill, it emerges, is Johnny's father and has been blackmailed into approving visas for terrorists under threat to his son's life.

Fleeing the bomber, Kate is attacked by Bill and kills him in self-defense, and witnesses and camera footage make her the prime suspect in the attack. Investigators find traces of chromium in the bomb, leading her superior at the embassy, Sam Parker, to conclude that the killer is the Watchmaker, one of the world's most wanted assassins, known for his precision. Hunted by the police and by the Watchmaker, who has been hired to eliminate her, Kate goes on the run through London, trying to clear her name and uncover a plot by a terrorist network and its financier to carry out a devastating attack in New York's Times Square on New Year's Eve. With few allies she can trust, she must reach New York and stop the attack before midnight, while the Watchmaker closes in.

Survivor received almost uniformly negative reviews, holding an 8 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it borrowed heavily from better films in the service of a predictable story. IGN gave it 5 out of 10. Critics found Brosnan's villainous turn one of the few highlights of an otherwise generic thriller.

title: The Siege of Jadotville
tagline: The Irish army's forgotten battle
overview: Irish Commandant Pat Quinlan leads a stand off with troops against French and Belgian Mercenaries in the Congo during the early 1960s.
plot:
The film opens with the execution of Congolese Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba and the outbreak of civil war. As the mineral rich State of Katanga secedes under the leadership of Moise Tshombe, United Nations Secretary General Dag Hammarskjöld assigns Conor Cruise O'Brien to head up a UN peacekeeping mission. Privately, Hammarskjöld tells O'Brien that the Katanga crisis could potentially trigger World War III and orders the Irish diplomat to take offensive action.
Meanwhile, Irish Army Commandant Pat Quinlan commands an infantry company of Irish peacekeepers who arrive at the UN compound near Jadotville. After examining the compound, Quinlan decides that it is wide open to attack and orders his men to dig trenches and defensive fighting positions.
While buying food in the nearby town, Quinlan meets French mercenary Rene Faulques, who has been hired by the mining companies allied to Tshombe's government. Afterwards, he visits the estate of a Belgian colonist, Madam LaFongagne, who tells him that Jadotville contains the world's richest uranium deposits.
Meanwhile, O'Brien orders UN forces to launch an attack against government buildings held by the Katangese in Elizabethville. While Indian peacekeepers are attempting to seize the city's radio station, 30 unarmed Katangese radio operators and employees are killed by gunfire and grenades. O'Brien orders the incident to be swept under the rug.
In retaliation, Faulques receives orders to attack Jadotville. Katangese forces and mercenaries under Faulques' command attack and besiege the Irish. During a brief ceasefire, Faulques vainly demands Quinlan's surrender.
Quinlan refuses, and his company is attacked repeatedly in separate waves by the Katangese and mercenary forces. They kill a total of 300 enemy soldiers, and wound 1,000 enemy soldiers, with zero deaths and only 16 wounded for the Irish. Irish, Swedish and Indian UN peacekeepers attempt to reinforce "A" Company but are repelled by separatists. An effort to supply water and evacuate the wounded troops by helicopter fails as separatists shoot down the helicopter.
After numerous extended attack waves, the Irish company is forced to surrender to Faulques's troops after running out of ammunition, food, and drinking water. They are held in a Katangese prison for about a month, then are freed in a prisoner exchange deal and allowed to go home. After arriving home, Quinlan is informed by General McEntee that "A" Company's surrender causes shame to the UN and the higher ups want to bury the truth of the siege for political reasons. Only in 2005 did a full review of the siege clear the soldiers' reputations.

title: Criminal Activities
tagline: Leave the crime to the criminals
overview: Four young men make a risky investment together that gets them into trouble with the mob.
plot:
Criminal Activities is a 2015 American crime thriller directed by Jackie Earle Haley in his directorial debut and written by Robert Lowell. Michael Pitt, Dan Stevens, Christopher Abbott, Rob Brown, Edi Gathegi and Haley star, with John Travolta as a mobster. RLJ Entertainment and Image Entertainment released it in the United States on November 20, 2015.

Four friends, tempted by a tip based on insider information, decide to invest heavily in a company whose stock is supposedly certain to multiply in value. To raise the money they borrow from a mysterious financial backer. The scheme collapses almost immediately: the company folds under federal scrutiny, wiping out their investment, and their benefactor turns out to be Eddie, a polished and seemingly friendly mid-level gangster who expects to be repaid.

Eddie offers the young men a way out of their debt. All they have to do is kidnap a man and hold him for 24 hours before handing him over, after which their obligation will be forgiven and everyone can go their separate ways. The job quickly proves far more complicated than promised. Their captive turns out to be the nephew of a rival mob boss, who is offering a two million dollar reward to whoever returns his relative, and the friends learn that they are expected to take part in killing their hostage before they will be allowed to leave the building. Tensions erupt within the group as loyalties are tested, panic sets in and they argue over what to do with the man tied up in their makeshift hideout.

As the night unfolds, it becomes clear that things are rarely what they seem. The motivations of the various players, including Eddie, the hostage and the friends themselves, differ from what they initially appear to be, and the film builds toward a series of revelations that recasts the events that came before.

Filming took place in Cleveland, Ohio, from May 27 to June 26, 2014; the story was originally set in Detroit. Image Entertainment acquired the film for release in the United States and the United Kingdom in the fall of 2015. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reports a 50% approval rating from 20 reviews, and Metacritic assigned a score of 51 out of 100.

title: 100 Streets
tagline: Anybody can take a wrong turn.
overview: Three people, three extraordinary stories. All lived out within a hundred London streets.
plot:
100 Streets is a 2016 British ensemble drama directed by Jim O'Hanlon from a screenplay by first-time feature writer Leon F. Butler, who also produced and raised its roughly £3 million budget from private investors. Idris Elba, who also served as a producer, stars alongside Gemma Arterton, Franz Drameh, Ken Stott, Charlie Creed-Miles, Kierston Wareing, Tom Cullen and Jo Martin. The production companies included CrossDay Productions and Green Door Pictures and the music is by Paul Saunderson. The title comes from Cicely Fox Smith's poem "The Oldest Thing in London".

The film weaves together three stories unfolding at the same time within about one square mile of London, each centered on a man forced to face the consequences of his past actions as he struggles toward a better life. In wealthy Chelsea, Max (Elba), a celebrated former England rugby captain, is in a bitter trial separation from his wife Emily (Arterton), an actress who gave up her career, after his infidelity came to light. As she tries to return to the stage and drifts into a romance with her old flame Jake (Cullen), Max sinks into heavy drinking and cocaine use. On a council estate south of the river, Kingsley (Drameh), a teenager with a gift for words and performance, has slipped into drug dealing and gang violence, to the dismay of his weary single mother (Martin), until a chance encounter with the aging actor Terence (Stott) offers him a way out through the theatre. Between these two worlds, the gentle cab driver George (Creed-Miles) and his patient wife Kathy (Wareing) hope to adopt a child and start a family, but their plans are thrown into turmoil when George is involved in a fatal road accident. As the stories progress, chance meetings and coincidences increasingly connect the characters, showing how circumstance and choice shape their fates.

The film premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival in June 2016, opened in British cinemas through Vertigo on 11 November 2016, and reached American theaters and video-on-demand via Samuel Goldwyn Films on 13 January 2017. Critical reception was lukewarm, with 41% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44, the consensus finding its talented cast stranded in a well-meaning but contrived drama. Variety likened it to a gentler London version of Crash, praising Drameh's promising performance, Arterton and Blaubach's bright cinematography but calling the script banal, while The Guardian also considered it a misfire.

title: Captain Fantastic
tagline: He Prepared Them for Everything Except the Outside World.
overview: A father living in the forests of the Pacific Northwest with his six young kids tries to assimilate back into society.
plot:
Ben Cash, his wife Leslie, and their six children live an isolated existence on ten acres in the mountainous Washington wilderness. They are left-wing anarchist activists disillusioned by capitalism and American life, who choose to instill survivalist skills, left-wing politics and philosophy into their children.
The children are encouraged to develop critical-thinking skills and physical fitness, and are taught self-reliance with limited reliance on modern technology. They are raised to live in close proximity to nature, given individual names, and celebrate Noam Chomsky's birthday rather than Christmas. They are exposed to a range of college-level literature and demonstrate advanced intellectual abilities for their ages. However, their limited interaction with the outside world contributes to difficulties in socializing with people beyond their immediate family.
Ben has been raising the children on his own while Leslie is hospitalized in New Mexico for bipolar disorder, away from her family and near her wealthy elitist parents. She dies by suicide while undergoing treatment, and Ben learns that her father, Jack Bertrang, plans to hold a Christian burial, despite Leslie being a philosophical Buddhist who abhorred religion. Ben tries to persuade Jack to honor Leslie's wish to be cremated, to no avail, and Jack forbids Ben to attend the funeral, threatening to have him arrested if he comes. Ben initially decides not to go and prevents his children from doing so, but then changes his mind, driving his children across the country in a repurposed school bus.
The family briefly stays at the home of Ben's sister, Harper. She and her husband try to convince Ben that the children should attend school to receive a conventional education; Ben quizzes Harper's children and his children on various topics, such as the Bill of Rights, showing that his children are far better educated than Harper's.
Ben arrives at Leslie's funeral with their children against Jack's wishes and reads her will, which instructs her family to cremate her and flush her ashes down a toilet, in the hopes of convincing Jack to honor her wishes, only for Jack to have him forcibly removed from the church. Angered by Jack's refusal to honor Leslie's wishes, Ben follows the funeral procession to the cemetery, planning to intervene, despite a police presence and Jack's threat to have him arrested. Ben only relents at his children's insistence that they cannot lose both of their parents.
After this, some of Ben's children start to doubt him and his parenting skills, with his second eldest son and middle child Rellian accusing him of failing to treat Leslie's mental health, and eldest son Bodevan accusing him of not equipping them for the real world, showing him acceptance letters from several top Ivy League colleges to which Leslie had helped him apply.
Ben finds a note from Rellian, who has run away to live with his grandparents.

title: The Blackcoat's Daughter
tagline: Abandoned as a child. Raised by the dark.
overview: Two young students at a prestigious prep school for girls are assailed by an evil, invisible power when they are stranded at the school over winter break.
plot:
The plot is split into three timelines. The first two, "Rose" and "Joan", intercut between each other before a third timeline, "Kat", is introduced and comprises the film's climax.
Rose
In February, students at the prestigious Bramford Academy, a Catholic boarding school in upstate New York, are about to be picked up by their parents for a week-long break. Kat, a freshman, and Rose, a senior student, are left behind. Suspecting she may be pregnant, Rose has lied to her parents about the vacation dates to buy time. Kat has a premonitory dream of her parents dying in a car crash. That night, Rose departs with her boyfriend to inform him of the pregnancy. Meanwhile, Kat receives a call. Hours later, Rose returns and finds Kat in the boiler room, repeatedly prostrating before the boiler. Kat speaks cryptically and claims her parents are dead, disturbing Rose. After Rose leaves, Kat's body starts convulsing and contorting in bed.
The next morning, Rose and a sickly-looking Kat join the nuns for breakfast, where Kat behaves erratically, vomits, and curses at the nuns. After receiving an alarming phone call, the nuns order Rose to shovel the driveway "down to the earth" for the abrupt return of Headmaster Gordon. Gordon arrives with a policeman; as they enter the nuns' cabin, a bloodstain is seen on the wall, and the men react with shock to something offscreen.
Joan
A young woman, Joan, arrives at a bus stop after escaping a mental institution. A friendly older man named Bill offers her a ride with him and his wife Linda. They stop at a motel and Joan showers, revealing a scar on her shoulder. A flashback shows her being shot by a policeman. Bill tells Joan that he picked her up because she reminded him of his deceased daughter, revealed to be Rose – the next day will be the ninth anniversary of Rose's death, on which her parents visit Bramford every year. Joan recognizes Rose's name and retreats to the bathroom, where she suppresses laughter. Joan is revealed to be a fake name; the real Joan was a woman she killed to steal her ID.
Kat
During the days leading up to winter break, Kat is in contact with an entity depicted alternately as a horned shadow and a gravelly voice on the phone. This entity informs her of her parents' impending death, and instructs her to kill everyone. After breakfast, the nuns receive a phone call informing them that Kat's parents have died. After Rose is dismissed to shovel the driveway, Kat murders both nuns. She pursues Rose; shortly after Rose has her period, confirming she is not pregnant, Kat stabs her to death and beheads her. Gordon and the policeman find Kat prostrating in front of the boiler again, with the severed heads of her three victims next to her. She exclaims "Hail Satan!" before the policeman shoots her in the shoulder, revealing that "Joan" is Kat. Kat is detained in a mental hospital, where a priest performs an exorcism.

overview: After his older brother passes away, Lee Chandler is forced to return home to care for his 16-year-old nephew. There he is compelled to deal with a tragic past that separated him from his family and the community where he was born and raised.
plot:
Lee Chandler is a depressed and asocial janitor, who lives alone in a basement apartment in Quincy, Massachusetts. He goes to a bar, brushes off a female patron who expresses interest in him, and gets into a fistfight with two men.
One day, he receives a phone call informing him that his brother, Joe, a fisherman who lives in Manchester-by-the-Sea, has suffered cardiac arrest; Joe dies before Lee can reach the hospital. Lee insists on being the one to tell Joe's teenage son, Patrick, about his death. While making funeral arrangements, they are reminded that Joe's body can not be buried until Spring, as the ground is frozen. Lee makes plans to remain in Manchester, living in Joe's house until the delayed burial.
When Lee meets with Joe's attorney, he is shocked to discover Joe has named him Patrick's legal guardian. Flashbacks reveal that Lee once lived in Manchester with his then-wife, Randi, and their three children. One night after hosting a raucous party, an intoxicated Lee forgot to put the screen in front of the fireplace, leading to a house fire that killed his children. No criminal charges were filed against him, as the police ruled it a tragic accident. However, at the station, a guilt-ridden Lee stole an officer's gun and attempted suicide, before being subdued. Lee and Randi subsequently divorced, and he left town. He is reluctant to commit to the guardianship, as it would require him to move back to Manchester. Plans are begun for Patrick to move to Boston with Lee, but Patrick has strong ties to the Manchester community, and stubbornly objects. Lee commits to staying until the end of the school year. Patrick wants to live with his estranged mother, Elise, who still lives in the area. Lee is opposed to this, as her history with alcoholism led her to abandon her family, but Patrick decides to reconnect with her over lunch. Elise has committed to Christianity and sobriety with her fiancé, Jeffrey, but during an awkward meal with them, Patrick finds he is unable to connect with her. He is further unsettled when Jeffrey emails him and insists on being an intermediary in any future communication between them. Lee's positive comments about Elise's sobriety lead Patrick to believe his uncle is trying to get rid of him, assertions Lee denies.
In response to this strain in their relationship, Lee takes steps to possibly extend his stay in Manchester and seeks to spend more time with Patrick. Over time, they re-establish their bond, despite conflicts over Joe's boat, Patrick's girlfriends, and their future living arrangements. However, staying in Manchester is still painful for Lee, as he is surrounded by reminders of his past. Multiple scenes suggest that some residents of Manchester believe that the fire was not accidental. One day, Lee runs into Randi with her newborn child. A sobbing Randi expresses remorse for her treatment of him during their divorce and asks him to have lunch. He deflects her apology, feeling that he does not deserve it.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo: World at His Feet
original_title: Cristiano Ronaldo: World at His Feet
overview: Cristiano Ronaldo: The World at His Feet follows the footballer from his beginnings in Portugal, breakthrough start with Manchester United and current career at Real Madrid.
plot:
Cristiano Ronaldo: The World at His Feet is a 2014 documentary film directed by Tara Pirnia and written by Nick Silverman, profiling the Portuguese footballer Cristiano Ronaldo, who was then playing for Real Madrid and captaining Portugal. Narrated by Benedict Cumberbatch, it runs just under an hour and was first released online through Vimeo in June 2014; it was later distributed on DVD by Vision Films. Ronaldo himself appears in interview, and David Beckham is among the other figures featured.

The film follows Ronaldo from his humble childhood on the island of Madeira to his status as a global sports star and celebrity. It portrays a poor upbringing and a solitary boy whose constant companion was a football. In one of the comparatively rare passages in which he speaks directly to the camera, Ronaldo explains that there was no single reason he took up the game, citing his father and brother as influences rather than claiming a lifelong dream. He joined the local club Andorinha at eight and moved to Sporting Lisbon at twelve, after scouts noticed his talent.

The documentary recounts the turning point of August 2003, when, after Sporting played Manchester United, the English club's players urged manager Sir Alex Ferguson to sign the teenager. Ferguson, presented as a father figure, gave him the famous number 7 shirt, and Ronaldo went on to become a superstar in England, regarded as a hero by some and an arrogant villain by others, before his move to Real Madrid. Combining interviews, archival and recent match footage and dramatised re-enactments, the film charts his awards, his rivalry and constant comparison with Lionel Messi, and his gradual maturing from self-absorbed playboy into a philanthropist and role model. Among the commentators is West Ham United's youth development director Anthony Carr, who explains what scouts look for in young players.

Reviews were mixed. Tom Keogh of Video Librarian gave it three out of five, calling it a brisk and exciting profile and recommending it. Charles Low of Kettle Mag found Cumberbatch's narration tasteful if puzzling and appreciated some insightful interviews, but felt the film zig-zagged between key moments, padded itself with general football commentary and pointless contributors such as an astrologer and skateboarder Tony Hawk, and relied on odd re-enactments that left it somewhere between a celebrity documentary and a sports broadcast, offering less insight into the man himself than he had hoped.

title: My Little Pony: The Movie
tagline: Discover A Different Breed Of Hero
overview: A new dark force threatens Ponyville, and the Mane 6 – Twilight Sparkle, Applejack, Rainbow Dash, Pinkie Pie, Fluttershy and Rarity – embark on an unforgettable journey beyond Equestria where they meet new friends and exciting challenges on a quest to use the magic of friendship and save their home.
plot:
My Little Pony: The Movie is a 2017 animated musical fantasy film directed by Jayson Thiessen and based on the television series My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic, developed by Lauren Faust. The series' regular voice cast, including Tara Strong, Ashleigh Ball, Andrea Libman, Tabitha St. Germain and Cathy Weseluck, return, joined by Emily Blunt as Tempest Shadow, Liev Schreiber as the Storm King, Taye Diggs as Capper, Zoe Saldaña as Captain Celaeno, Michael Peña as Grubber, Kristin Chenoweth as Princess Skystar, Uzo Aduba as Queen Novo and Sia as the pop star Songbird Serenade. Lionsgate released the film in the United States in October 2017.

The ponies of Equestria are preparing for their first Friendship Festival, organised by Princess Twilight Sparkle in Canterlot, when the celebration is interrupted by an invading army. It is led by Tempest Shadow, a unicorn with a broken horn who serves the Storm King, a ruler who has promised to restore her horn in exchange for capturing the princesses of Equestria and using their magic to empower his staff. Tempest turns Princesses Celestia, Luna and Cadance to stone, but Twilight escapes with her friends Pinkie Pie, Rainbow Dash, Rarity, Applejack, Fluttershy and the young dragon Spike.

Following Celestia's incomplete instructions to seek the "queen of the hippos", the friends travel beyond Equestria for the first time. In the desert city of Klugetown they meet Capper, a smooth-talking cat who offers to guide them while secretly planning to sell them to a crime boss to pay off his debts. As Capper develops genuine feelings of friendship, Twilight discovers that the creatures they seek are hippogriffs. Their journey takes them aboard an airship crewed by former pirates, and eventually to a hidden underwater kingdom where the hippogriffs have transformed themselves into seaponies to escape the Storm King. Under increasing pressure, Twilight makes a desperate decision that threatens her friendships, while Tempest closes in on her.

The film celebrates friendship, trust and redemption, especially through Tempest's backstory, and it features original songs, including a number performed by Sia.

The film received mixed to negative reviews, with about 49 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, but it was a box-office success, grossing more than 61 million dollars worldwide against a production budget of 6.5 million.

title: Land of Mine
tagline: They survived the second World War, now they must survive the cleanup
overview: In the days following the surrender of Germany in May 1945, a group of young German prisoners of war is handed over to the Danish authorities and subsequently sent to the West Coast, where they are ordered to remove the more than two million mines that the Germans had placed in the sand along the coast. With their bare hands, crawling around in the sand, the boys are forced to perform the dangerous work under the leadership of a Danish sergeant.
plot:
Following the end of World War II in Europe and the liberation of Denmark from German occupation in May 1945, the Wehrmacht and SS occupiers became prisoners of war. A group of young German prisoners are sent to the west coast where they are trained to use their bare hands to remove the landmines that the Germans had buried in the sand. After their training, the boys are left under the charge of Danish sergeant Carl Leopold Rasmussen, who is determined to treat the young prisoners without sympathy. Marching his squad onto the dunes, he promises that they will return home in three months, if they can each defuse six mines per hour for a total of 45,000 mines.
One of the boys, Sebastian Schumann, attempts to remain optimistic as they discuss their plans for when they return home. The POWs are given little food due to post-war shortages and begin to suffer from malnourishment, with Ernst befriending a young local girl to steal some bread from her. One day, while defusing a mine, Wilhelm's arms are blown off and he later dies in a field hospital. Most of the boys become ill after eating grain contaminated with rat faeces that they found on a nearby farm; they are treated by Rasmussen who makes them purge themselves with seawater. Rasmussen gradually treats his charges more kindly, stealing food from the base for them and tries to maintain morale by reporting that Wilhelm has survived. He also allows the boys to use a device invented by Sebastian to improve productivity.
Hearing rumours of Rasmussen stealing food for the boys, his commanding officer Captain Ebbe Jensen brings a group of British soldiers to abuse and torment the boys. Rasmussen stops them but is confronted about the theft by Ebbe, who accuses him of being sympathetic towards the Germans. During another day of demining, Werner is blown to bits after encountering landmines buried one above another, leaving his twin brother Ernst distraught.
After a casual game of football, Rasmussen's dog is blown up in a supposedly cleared zone of the beach. This causes Rasmussen to snap and begin abusing the boys again. He forces them to march close together across the cleared zones of the beach to confirm that they are safe. When a young local girl walks out into an uncleared area of beach, her mother comes looking for Rasmussen only to find him gone. The boys volunteer to help save the girl. Ernst walks through the uncleared minefield to keep the little girl calm whilst Sebastian clears a path to safety for her. They manage to rescue her but instead of returning to safety with Sebastian, Ernst decides he cannot go on without his brother and commits suicide by walking into the uncleared section and is promptly killed.
After witnessing this act of kindness and bravery from the boys, Rasmussen relents in his treatment of them and reassures a grieving Sebastian that they will soon be able to go home.

title: Risen
tagline: Witness the manhunt that changed the course of human history
overview: Clavius, a powerful Roman military tribune, and his aide, Lucius, are tasked with solving the mystery of what happened to Jesus in the weeks following the crucifixion, in order to disprove the rumors of a risen Messiah and prevent an uprising in Jerusalem.
plot:
Risen is a 2016 biblical drama film directed by Kevin Reynolds and written by Reynolds and Paul Aiello. An American-Spanish co-production starring Joseph Fiennes, Tom Felton, Peter Firth and Cliff Curtis, it tells the story of the resurrection of Jesus through the eyes of a Roman soldier who is ordered to find his missing body. The project began in 2013 as The Resurrection of Jesus Christ, conceived as a mystery thriller and an unofficial sequel to The Passion of the Christ, and was filmed in Malta and Spain between August and November 2015.

Clavius, a Roman tribune of the Legio X Fretensis, crushes a rebellion of zealots led by Barabbas and then oversees the crucifixion of Yeshua, posting guards at the tomb. When the body vanishes, rumors spread that Yeshua's followers stole it to make it appear he had risen from the dead. Pontius Pilate, eager to prevent unrest in Jerusalem before the Emperor's visit, orders Clavius to find the corpse. With his aide Lucius, Clavius interrogates people who claim to have seen Yeshua alive, but their accounts grow ever more miraculous, and followers such as Mary Magdalene and Bartholomew answer only in riddles. As his investigation unsettles Romans and Jews alike, Pilate grows distant. Clavius forces one of the tomb's disgraced guards to abandon his cover story, and the drunken soldier describes a blinding flash, the tomb's seals disintegrating and a figure emerging. Clavius refuses to believe it until, during a raid, he comes face to face with Yeshua, alive among his apostles, the same man he watched die on the cross. Shaken, he calls off the search and soon abandons his old life and gods to follow the group, befriending the apostle Peter and talking with Yeshua as they travel, while Pilate sends Lucius and a contingent of soldiers after him. Clavius helps the disciples evade the pursuing Romans and witnesses Yeshua heal a leper and ascend to heaven, before the apostles part to spread their message and Clavius reflects on how his life has been transformed.

Columbia Pictures released Risen in the United States on February 19, 2016. It grossed $46.8 million worldwide against a $20 million budget and received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes gave it 53%, with a consensus praising its lighter tone and a terrific turn from Fiennes, and audiences gave it an A− CinemaScore.

title: Uncharted
tagline: Fortune favors the bold.
overview: A young street-smart, Nathan Drake and his wisecracking partner Victor “Sully” Sullivan embark on a dangerous pursuit of “the greatest treasure never found” while also tracking clues that may lead to Nathan’s long-lost brother.
plot:
Uncharted is an action-adventure film directed by Ruben Fleischer, released in 2022. The movie is based on the popular video game series of the same name, developed by Naughty Dog.

The story follows Nathan Drake (played by Tom Holland), a young and charismatic treasure hunter who becomes embroiled in a global adventure. Nathan's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Victor Sullivan (played by Mark Wahlberg), an older and more experienced treasure hunter who becomes his mentor.

As they embark on a perilous journey to find the lost city of El Dorado, Nathan and Victor are pursued by a ruthless adversary, Sully's former partner, Chloe Frazer (played by Sophia Ali). Chloe is driven by a desire for revenge against Sully, whom she believes wronged her in the past.

Throughout their quest, Nathan and Victor must navigate treacherous jungles, avoid deadly traps, and fight off rival treasure hunters. Along the way, Nathan discovers more about his own family history and the secrets surrounding his father's disappearance.

As the stakes grow higher, Nathan finds himself torn between his loyalty to Sully and his growing feelings for Chloe. The film's climax features an intense showdown between Nathan and Chloe, with the fate of El Dorado hanging in the balance.

One of the standout aspects of Uncharted is its strong performances from the cast, particularly Tom Holland and Mark Wahlberg. Their chemistry on screen is undeniable, and their characters' banter adds a welcome layer of humor to the film.

While the movie takes some creative liberties with the source material, it remains faithful to the spirit of the video game series. The action sequences are thrilling, and the cinematography captures the lush beauty of the jungle environments.

Overall, Uncharted is an entertaining and action-packed adventure that explores themes of loyalty, family, and redemption. With its talented cast and engaging storyline, it's a great addition to the action-adventure genre.

title: Renegades
tagline: 5 Navy SEALs. $300 million in gold. 1 incredible mission.
overview: In the midst of the Balkan wars, a squad of Navy SEALs attempts to unravel a long-forgotten mystery after discovering an enormous treasure trove hidden at the bottom of a lake in Serbia.
plot:
Renegades, released in the United States as American Renegades, is a 2017 English-language action thriller directed by Steven Quale from a screenplay by Luc Besson and Richard Wenk. Produced by Besson's company EuropaCorp, it stars Sullivan Stapleton as Navy SEAL team leader Matt Barnes, J. K. Simmons as Rear Admiral Levin, Charlie Bewley as Stanton Baker and Sylvia Hoeks as Lara Simić, with Clemens Schick, Diarmaid Murtagh, Joshua Henry, Dimitri Leonidas and Ewen Bremner in supporting roles. After its release was postponed several times, it opened in Germany on 1 September 2017 and in France in August 2018.

The film begins in August 1944, when retreating German forces move looted treasure, including roughly 25 tons of gold ingots, from Paris to the small Bosnian town of Bosansko Grahovo, where it is locked in the bank vault. The Germans massacre the townspeople, and only a small boy escapes to be found by Yugoslav partisans. In revenge for the massacre, partisans later blow up a nearby dam, flooding the town and leaving the gold submerged.

In 1995, during the Bosnian War, a team of American Navy SEALs disguised as journalists captures the Bosnian Serb general Milić, a war criminal responsible for atrocities against civilians. Their escape, which involves a stolen tank and considerable damage to the city, earns them a reprimand from Admiral Levin and a three-day leave. Baker becomes romantically involved with Lara, a local waitress, and when thugs led by her brother come to threaten her, Barnes intervenes. Lara then reveals the secret of the gold lying at the bottom of the lake and explains that it could rebuild her war-torn community. Seeing an opportunity to help her people and enrich themselves, the SEALs devise an unauthorised plan to dive to the drowned town, break into the vault and raise the gold without their commanders finding out, while Milić's second-in-command Petrović and his forces close in.

The film mixes heist caper, underwater action and military adventure, with much of its spectacle derived from the sequences filmed in large water tanks. Its tone alternates between humour among the team members and violent set pieces.

Renegades received negative reviews, with an approval rating of about 11 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, against a reported production budget of around 77.5 million dollars.

plot:
A married couple in their 40s, John and Laura Taylor desperately want to have a baby, but they are unable to have a lasting pregnancy. After attempting all other options, the couple hire a beautiful young woman named Anna, who agrees to become a gestational surrogate mother for the Taylors. After Anna has a doctor's appointment, her boyfriend, Mike, does not pick her up, causing Anna to go to John's job for a ride home. That night, Laura receives an emergency phone call from Anna. John drives to her house seeing the police. It is then revealed that Mike assaulted Anna, leaving her face bloody and bruised. The police suggest Anna find another place to stay, and John invites her to stay at the couple's house for the time being. Anna starts to develop a fixation on John as the pregnancy moves further along. Anna's growing obsession interferes with what was a plan by her and Mike, to scam the couple by demanding money. When Mike pushes Anna to demand a ransom, she kills him.
John and Anna find out that the baby is a boy. Later at work, John gets a call from Anna saying that they should go out for lunch, but he becomes annoyed, and Anna hangs up. John then avoids all calls from her. Anna walks into his office and tries to seduce him, but his boss enters and John prompts Anna to leave. Anna later reveals her feelings to John and becomes outraged when he says he does not feel the same. He is able to calm her down, but she runs out of the guest house into the main house and picks up a knife. The police arrive and Anna lies and says she and John have sex every night. Laura and John then find out that Anna ordered an abortion pill. Laura and John devise a plan to get their unborn baby back by making John act as if he shares Anna's feelings. As Anna thinks she is being played, she walks away. John stops her and kisses her forcefully and asks her to come with him up to the family's lake house. John returns home to Laura the next day. The plan works fine until Anna notices the two embracing each other. Anna leaves John a voicemail claiming that the baby is coming. He leaves to go to the hospital while Laura stays home.
When John and Roland go to the hospital, they are confused to find out that Anna never checked in and she had tricked him into getting away from Laura. Anna returns to the Taylor house, killing the family cat and assaulting Laura before going into labor. While in the hospital, they discover that Anna had given birth to a baby boy and had fled to the lake house. John manages to get the baby, but Anna wakes up and a fight breaks out between them. He throws her on to a cabinet which knocks her unconscious. He goes outside and Laura places the baby in the car. When Laura turns on the lights, she sees Anna standing in front with a shotgun. Anna shoots at the car and misses, but hits the window. Laura runs over Anna with her car, killing her. The next morning, Laura, the baby and John are sitting inside the lake house.

title: Ouija: Origin of Evil
tagline: When you talk to the other side, you never know who will be listening.
overview: In 1965 Los Angeles, a widowed mother and her two daughters add a new stunt to bolster their séance scam business and unwittingly invite authentic evil into their home. plot:
Ouija: Origin of Evil is a supernatural horror film directed by Mike Flanagan, released in 2016 under Universal Pictures. The movie serves as a prequel to the 2014 film Ouija and explores the origins of the demonic entity known as the "Dollmaker."

The story begins on October 12, 1967, in Virginia, where we meet our protagonist, Alice (Lili Taylor), a single mother who has recently moved into a new home with her two children, Sarah (Shanley Caswell) and Toby (Brent Ryan Campbell). The family is struggling to cope with the loss of their father, who died in a car accident.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Alice's husband had been involved in occult practices before his death, which has left the family feeling vulnerable. One day, while exploring the attic, Sarah discovers an antique Ouija board, which she and her brother use to communicate with their father's spirit.

However, things take a dark turn when they begin to receive messages from an unknown entity, claiming to be the "Dollmaker," a malevolent being who was responsible for the death of Alice's husband. The Dollmaker begins to manipulate the children, using the Ouija board to lure them into a world of terror and possession.

As the events escalate, Alice becomes increasingly concerned about her children's safety and the influence of the occult in their lives. She seeks help from a local minister, Father Harris (Douglas Tilden), who is initially skeptical but eventually becomes entangled in the family's struggles.

The plot thickens as the Dollmaker's presence becomes more pronounced, causing chaos and destruction throughout the household. Alice must confront her own demons and make a choice between saving her children or succumbing to the darkness that has consumed them.

In the climactic final act, Alice discovers the true nature of the Dollmaker and the extent of its power. With the help of Father Harris, she manages to banish the entity back to its realm, but not before it exacts a terrible revenge on her family.

The movie ends with Alice, scarred by the experience, vowing to protect her children from the forces of darkness that lurk in the shadows. The final shot is of the Ouija board, now broken and discarded, as if the entity has been vanquished but not forgotten.

Throughout the film, Mike Flanagan weaves a complex narrative that explores themes of grief, trauma, and the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human control. The movie's atmosphere is tense and foreboding, building towards a terrifying climax that will leave viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, Ouija: Origin of Evil is a chilling horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the supernatural. With its slow-burning tension and shocking twists, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

In the end, Buster decides to let all the contestants sing together on stage, and they perform a powerful rendition of "The Greatest Day." The performance is a huge success, and the movie ends with Buster's theater being saved and his friends finding their own unique voices.

Throughout the movie, the characters learn valuable lessons about perseverance, friendship, and believing in oneself. The movie features a talented voice cast, including Matthew McConaughey as Buster Moon, Reese Witherspoon as Rosita, Seth MacFarlane as Jimmy Crystal, and Scarlett Johansson as Meena.

Overall, Sing is a heartwarming and entertaining movie that celebrates the power of music and friendship.
