title: Circle
tagline: In here…everything gets you killed.
overview: In a massive, mysterious chamber, fifty strangers awaken to find themselves trapped with no memory of how they got there.  Organized in an inward-facing circle and unable to move, they quickly learn that every two minutes, one of them must die…executed by a strange device in the center of the room.
plot:
Circle is a 2015 American science fiction psychological thriller film written and directed by Aaron Hann and Mario Miscione. Inspired by the 1957 courtroom drama 12 Angry Men, it features an ensemble cast that includes Carter Jenkins, Lawrence Kao, Allegra Masters, Michael Nardelli, Julie Benz, Mercy Malick, Lisa Pelikan and Cesar Garcia. Shot in 2014, it premiered at the Seattle International Film Festival on May 28, 2015, and was released on video on demand in October of that year.

Fifty strangers wake up in a dark room, standing on platforms arranged in two concentric circles around a black dome. Anyone who steps away from their spot or touches another person is killed by a beam from the dome, and every two minutes the device kills someone else. The captives soon work out that they are voting, through small hand gestures, on who dies next, and that refusing to vote simply leaves the choice to chance. To buy time, they agree to eliminate the oldest among them first while they try to understand where they are; several remember fleeing Los Angeles and being pulled into the sky, and one elderly man insists he saw aliens, but the group refuses to listen. As the rounds continue, the debate turns ugly. People confess to affairs and violence, accusations of racism, homophobia and hypocrisy are traded, and each prejudice becomes a reason to target someone. A few volunteers sacrifice themselves to give the others more time. Eventually the survivors realize that only one person can be left standing, and they split into factions: one wants to protect a pregnant woman and a little girl at all costs, while the other argues that no one deserves special treatment. Alliances shift, lies are exposed, and the ever-shrinking circle is forced to decide who, if anyone, deserves to survive.

The film received a mixed response. On Rotten Tomatoes, four of seven critics' reviews are positive. John DeFore of The Hollywood Reporter described it as a "Twilight Zone-y drama" that works better than expected, and Tony Kay of City Arts praised the way it engineers suspense and the puzzle-box appeal of piecing together what is going on as each execution approaches.

title: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny
original_title: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny
tagline: A legend will face his destiny.
overview: Finding himself in a new era, approaching retirement, Indy wrestles with fitting into a world that seems to have outgrown him. But as the tentacles of an all-too-familiar evil return in the form of an old rival, Indy must don his hat and pick up his whip once more to make sure an ancient and powerful artifact doesn't fall into the wrong hands.
plot:
Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny is a 2023 American action-adventure directed by James Mangold, who wrote it with David Koepp, Jez Butterworth and John-Henry Butterworth. The fifth and final film in the Indiana Jones series and a sequel to Kingdom of the Crystal Skull (2008), it stars Harrison Ford, with Phoebe Waller-Bridge as his goddaughter Helena Shaw, Mads Mikkelsen as the former Nazi scientist Jürgen Voller, and Antonio Banderas, Boyd Holbrook and Toby Jones, while Karen Allen and John Rhys-Davies return.

In the final days of the Second World War, Indiana Jones and the Oxford archaeologist Basil Shaw are captured by Nazis while trying to recover the Lance of Longinus. The astrophysicist Voller discovers that the relic is fake but that he has found half of Archimedes' Dial, a device said to locate fissures in time. Jones seizes the piece aboard a train loaded with plunder and escapes with Basil.

In 1969, Jones is retiring from teaching in New York and is separated from his wife Marion after the death of their son in Vietnam. Basil's daughter Helena turns up wanting the Dial, which her father had asked Jones to destroy. Voller, now working for NASA, attacks them with CIA help; Helena, a smuggler, flees with the artefact, and Jones, framed for murder, escapes the city with the help of his old friend Sallah.

In Tangier, Jones breaks up Helena's black-market auction, but Voller steals the Dial. With Helena's young accomplice Teddy, they follow Voller to Greece, where Jones's diver friend Renaldo helps them recover a tablet from the Antikythera wreck before Voller kills him. In Sicily they find Archimedes' tomb and the second half of the device, but Voller captures Jones, assembles the Dial and flies toward a fissure, hoping to reach 1939 and change the outcome of the war.

Because of continental drift, the plane instead arrives at the Siege of Syracuse in 214 BC and is shot down, killing Voller. Jones meets Archimedes and wants to remain in the past, but Helena knocks him out and brings him home, where he reconciles with Marion.

The film grossed $384 million worldwide against a budget of nearly $300 million, making it one of the most expensive films ever made, and it holds a 71% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

plot:
Blade Runner 2049 is a 2017 science fiction film directed by Denis Villeneuve, set 30 years after the events of the original Blade Runner. The movie takes place in a dystopian future Los Angeles, where synthetic beings called replicants are hunted by special police officers known as blade runners.

The story follows K (Ryan Gosling), a new blade runner who is tasked with "retiring" (killing) a group of advanced replicants that have escaped and are seeking to extend their short lifespan. The replicants, led by Niander Wallace (Jared Leto), are nearly indistinguishable from humans and possess superior strength and agility.

During his mission, K discovers a long-buried secret about the creation of the replicants, which leads him on a quest to uncover the truth about his own existence. He also encounters Joi (Ana de Armas), an artificial intelligence companion who becomes his emotional connection in a world devoid of human intimacy.

As K delves deeper into the mystery, he meets Deckard (Harrison Ford) from the original Blade Runner, who is now an old man living off the grid. However, their encounter raises more questions than answers, and K begins to question whether Deckard is indeed a replicant or a human being.

The plot thickens as K discovers that Niander Wallace has been experimenting with replicants, creating new models with advanced capabilities. He also learns about the existence of a long-lost replicant named Luv (Carla Juri), who was created by the same scientist who created Deckard and Rachael (Rooney Mara) from the original film.

As K navigates this complex web of secrets and lies, he must confront his own identity and the nature of humanity. The movie's climax features a dramatic showdown between K and Niander Wallace, with K ultimately deciding to spare Luv's life and allow her to live out her days in peace.

Throughout the film, Villeneuve explores themes of artificial intelligence, humanity, and what it means to be alive. The visuals are stunning, with breathtaking depictions of Los Angeles and its inhabitants. The performances by Gosling, Leto, and Ford are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Ultimately, Blade Runner 2049 is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that expands on the original's exploration of humanity and what it means to be alive. While it may not have all the answers, it raises more questions than it provides, leaving audiences to ponder the implications long after the credits roll.

He also meets Viviane Wembly (Laura Haddock), a British historian who helps him decipher the mysteries of the Archibald device.

As the story unfolds, Cade and Viviane embark on a perilous journey across Europe, pursued by the Decepticons and facing numerous challenges along the way. They soon discover that the Transformers are not just machines but also vessels for ancient spirits, known as "Primes," who possess immense power.

The movie culminates in an epic battle between the Autobots and the Decepticons, with Cade playing a crucial role in the outcome. In the end, Cade discovers his true identity and becomes the new leader of the Knights Templar, tasked with protecting humanity from the Transformers' existence.

While some critics panned the movie for its convoluted plot and lack of coherence, fans of the franchise generally enjoyed the film's nostalgic value and exciting action sequences.

Overall, Transformers: The Last Knight is an entertaining addition to the live-action Transformers series, with plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers engaged.

title: The Glass Castle
tagline: Find beauty in the struggle.
overview: A young girl is raised in a dysfunctional family constantly on the run from the FBI. plot:
The Glass Castle is a 2017 American biographical drama directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, who wrote the screenplay with Andrew Lanham and Marti Noxon, based on Jeannette Walls's best-selling 2005 memoir about growing up in poverty with her unconventional parents. Lionsgate acquired the rights in 2012 with Jennifer Lawrence in talks to star, but Brie Larson took over the lead in 2015. Filming began on May 20, 2016, in Welch, West Virginia, and Lionsgate released the film on August 11, 2017.

Young Jeannette grows up on the move with her painter mother, Rose Mary, her brilliant but irresponsible, hard-drinking father, Rex, and her siblings Lori, Brian and later Maureen. After she is badly burned cooking alone, Rex sneaks her out of the hospital before social workers can intervene, and enchants her with plans to build the family a dream house of glass. On the run from the law and out of money, the family settles in a ramshackle house without utilities in Welch, near the children's grandmother Erma. Rex briefly beats his drinking by tying himself to his bed, but relapses, refuses to believe that Erma has sexually abused Brian, and fights violently with Rose Mary. The children promise to look after each other and escape. Lori leaves for New York, and after one of Rex's pool hustles leaves her fending off an attempted rape and he steals her savings, Jeannette follows.

By 1989 Jeannette is a gossip columnist for New York magazine engaged to David, a financial analyst, and lies to his clients about her family while her parents are homeless and squatting in the city. After Rex punches David and Jeannette learns that her parents had owned land worth nearly $1 million all along, she disowns her father. Unhappily married, she at first refuses to visit when Rex is dying, but eventually tells the truth about her upbringing and reconciles with him before his death. Divorced and working as a freelance writer, she later spends Thanksgiving with her family, remembering him.

Larson plays Jeannette, Woody Harrelson plays Rex, Naomi Watts plays Rose Mary, Sarah Snook plays Lori and Max Greenfield plays David. Critics praised the cast, especially Larson, but found the adaptation too forgiving of the parents, giving it 52% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed $22 million in North America.

title: Heist
tagline: Never make a bet you can't afford to lose.
overview: A father is without the means to pay for his daughter's medical treatment. As a last resort, he partners with a greedy co-worker to rob a casino. When things go awry they're forced to hijack a city bus.
plot:
Heist, also released as Bus 657, is a 2015 American action thriller directed by Scott Mann and written by Stephen Cyrus Sepher and Max Adams from an original story by Sepher. It stars Jeffrey Dean Morgan as Luke Vaughn, Robert De Niro as the casino owner known as the Pope, Dave Bautista as Cox and Gina Carano as police officer Kris Bajos, with Kate Bosworth, Morris Chestnut and Sepher. The story follows a desperate father whose casino robbery turns into a hostage crisis aboard a city bus.

Luke Vaughn works at a casino in the American South run by Francis Silva, a ruthless boss nicknamed the Pope. Vaughn's young daughter is seriously ill and needs an operation costing 300,000 dollars. When he asks the Pope for a loan, he is refused, fired and beaten by Silva's enforcer, Dog. A security guard named Cox then tells Vaughn that the casino launders money for the mob and proposes a robbery. Because Vaughn knows the vault codes, he agrees to join Cox's crew, and they steal the cash.

The getaway goes wrong when Dog's men intercept the thieves, a gunfight leaves one of the crew wounded and their driver abandons them. The robbers hijack a city bus full of passengers, pursued by Officer Bajos, and soon the police set up roadblocks. Vaughn tries to keep the hostages safe and negotiates with Bajos through a pregnant passenger's phone, while the volatile Cox threatens to kill people if the police do not back off. As the bus races along the highway and runs low on fuel, Detective Marconi and a SWAT team prepare to intervene, while the Pope sends Dog to recover his money at any cost. Vaughn must keep everyone alive, outwit both the police and the mob and find a way to get the money to his daughter.

The film combines a heist story with the confined, high-speed tension of a bus hijacking, setting a father's desperation against the brutality of organized crime.

Heist was released by Lionsgate Premiere on November 13, 2015. It received negative reviews, with 30 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that its all-star cast was dealt a poor hand by a humorless potboiler, and a Metacritic score of 37.

title: White Girl
overview: Summer, New York City. A college girl falls hard for a guy she just met. After a night of partying goes wrong, she goes to wild extremes to get him back.
plot:
Leah, a student about to enter her second year of college, moves in with her friend Katie into an apartment in Ridgewood, Queens. One night, out of marijuana, she asks a group of young Latino men on her corner to sell her drugs. They refuse. After a few days, Leah runs into Blue in a liquor/ convenience store and invites him into her apartment. He explains that, while he is a dealer, he doesn't do hard drugs. They end up having sex on her roof.
Leah tells him he could be making $60 compared to the $20 he has been selling them for. She invites him to a party thrown by her magazine, where she interns, and Blue is able to mark up his prices to the crowd.
Emboldened by his success, Blue asks for a kilo of cocaine from his supplier Lloyd. He agrees and Blue and Leah go to a restaurant for breakfast. While there, he is approached by one of his regulars, who sets him up, and he is immediately arrested by an undercover police officer. Leah picks up the kilo and quietly leaves.
Leah goes to visit Blue in jail and he tells her he may get 20 years in prison due to priors. She decides to help him, telling him that she has the coke, so the police have no evidence. He asks her to return it to Lloyd and explain. As she approaches Lloyd's, she recognizes the same undercover cop right outside, and decides to run. She then finds Blue a lawyer named George, intending to deal the coke to pay his fee. He is optimistic that they have a very good case.
Approaching her boss, Kelly, Leah sells a third of the kilo. Katie and Blue's friends help move the rest, while Blue believes George is representing him pro bono. As her debts pile up, Lloyd finds her, pressuring her for the rest of the money, so she asks Kelly for a $17,000 loan. He instead helps her throw a rave with a cover charge. The party is a success, but Leah takes too many drugs and wakes up alone with no money.
Leah promises George she will get the rest of the money, but he tells her to forget it. He takes her to dinner, explaining that the legal system is unequal and white men who commit violent crimes are more likely to get off for their crimes than non-violent PoC offenders like Blue. The two end up going to Leah's where she passes out, intoxicated. George uses the opportunity to rape her.
Afterwards, Leah becomes silent and withdrawn, staying in bed. She is surprised one day by Blue who arrives in her apartment and crawls into bed with her. He reveals that the lawyer managed to free him and credits Leah with saving his life. Getting on one knee he proposes to her, to which she does not give a clear answer. (However, in the next scene they are happily kissing each other.)
Walking down the street together, Leah and Blue are surprised when Lloyd attacks them both, wanting his money. Blue first hits him over the head with a broken bottle then beats him to death with a wrench. As Leah looks on, Blue silently realizes she caused the attack by not returning the coke.

title: Maze Runner: The Death Cure
tagline: The end will be WCKD
overview: Thomas leads his group of escaped Gladers on their final and most dangerous mission yet. To save their friends, they must break into the legendary Last City, a WCKD-controlled labyrinth that may turn out to be the deadliest maze of all. Anyone who makes it out alive will get answers to the questions the Gladers have been asking since they first arrived in the maze.
plot:
Maze Runner: The Death Cure is a 2018 American science fiction thriller film directed by Wes Ball, based on the novel of the same name by James Dashner. The movie is produced by 20th Century Fox.

The story takes place five years after the events of Maze Runner: The Scorch Trials (2015). Thomas (Dylan O'Brien) and his friends, including Newt (Thomas Brodie-Sangster), Minho (Kieran Culkin), and Brenda (Rosa Salazar), are on a mission to find a cure for the Flare, a deadly disease that is spreading rapidly across the world.

The group discovers that the only way to stop the Flare is to reach the fabled "Cure" in Hong Kong. However, they soon realize that they are not alone in their quest. A new organization, known as WICKED (World In Catastrophe: Killzone Experiment Department), has also been searching for the Cure.

As Thomas and his friends navigate through the treacherous landscape of China, they encounter a group of rogue WICKED agents who will stop at nothing to claim the Cure for themselves. The group must use all their skills and ingenuity to outsmart their enemies and reach the Cure before it's too late.

Along the way, Thomas also grapples with his own identity and purpose. He is haunted by memories of his past life in the Glade and struggles to come to terms with his new reality as a leader. His relationships with his friends are put to the test as they face numerous challenges and setbacks.

As the stakes grow higher, Thomas and his friends discover that the Cure is not what it seems. They must confront the dark secrets of WICKED's true intentions and make a choice between saving humanity or sacrificing themselves for the greater good.

The movie culminates in an epic showdown between Thomas and the leader of WICKED, Ava Paige (Patricia Clarkson). In a heart-pumping climax, Thomas faces off against Ava in a battle to control the fate of humanity. The outcome is far from certain, leaving the audience on the edge of their seats.

Ultimately, Thomas emerges victorious, but not without great cost. The movie ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as Thomas and his friends look towards a brighter future, free from the constraints of WICKED's control.

Overall, Maze Runner: The Death Cure is an action-packed thrill ride that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and sacrifice. With its breakneck pace and pulse-pounding suspense, it's a must-see for fans of the sci-fi genre.

title: Cleveland Abduction
tagline: Based on a true story.
overview: A single mother becomes Ariel Castro's first kidnapping victim, and finds herself trapped in his home with two other women for 11 years.
plot:
In August 2002 in Cleveland, Ohio, 21-year-old single mother Michelle Knight has lost custody of her son, Joey. One morning while walking to court, she accepts a ride from Ariel Castro who abducts her and holds her captive in his home, regularly beating and raping her.
After several months, Castro buys Michelle a puppy for company but kills it when she tries to escape, leaving her devastated. Michelle also discovers she is pregnant but Castro causes her to have a miscarriage by hitting her with a dumbbell. Finding strength through her belief in God and determined to be reunited with her son, she refuses to be broken down and always remains hopeful that she will be found, despite no active investigation as police believe she had ran away.
In April 2003, Castro abducts and brings home Amanda Berry, and later in April 2004, he does the same with Georgina "Gina" DeJesus. The three young women become friends, treating one another as sisters throughout their time in captivity. When Amanda becomes pregnant, Michelle delivers the baby, a girl, performing CPR on her under the threat of Castro killing her if the child does not survive. They name her Jocelyn and she grows up brainwashed into thinking their way of living is normal, believing Michelle and Gina are her aunts.
In 2013 after enduring more than a decade of brutality and captivity, Amanda succeeds in escaping from the house when Castro fails to lock the front door. She and Jocelyn alert their neighbours and they phone the police, releasing all four women. After recovering in hospital, Michelle learns Joey was adopted not long after she was reported missing; his new family decline any interaction and she comes to accept this, knowing Joey is happy and taken care of.
Michelle, Amanda and Gina part ways, forever bonded by their experience, but hopeful for the future ahead. Castro is sentenced to life imprisonment plus 1,000 years, without any possibility of parole. However, just a month after his sentencing, he is found dead in his cell from suicide by hanging.

title: The Wave
tagline: It was only a matter of time.
overview: Although theorised, no one is really ready when a mountain pass above the scenic and narrow Geiranger fjord in Norway collapses and creates a tsunami over 300 feet high. A geologist is one of those caught in the middle of it.
plot:
Geologist Kristian Eikjord is working his final day in Geiranger before moving to Stavanger with his family, when sensors in the mountain indicate groundwater has disappeared at Åkerneset.
Waiting for the ferry with his children, Sondre and Julia, while his wife Idun works a few more days at the town hotel, Kristian has an epiphany and rushes back to the geology center, leaving his children in the car. He and his coworker Jacob investigate the crevice and find that the sensor wires have snapped due to movements inside the mountain. Kristian's former boss Arvid agrees to enter a higher state of alert but does not sound the evacuation alarm to not disrupt the tourist season. Kristian returns to the car hours later, but finds that the children have gone to the hotel. Kristian and Julia separated with Idun and Sondre as Julia wanted to spend one last night at their house. In the evening, Sondre heads down to the basement with his headphones and skateboard.
Arvid and Jacob went down to the crevice to investigate the abnormal readings. Kristian reviews records of previous avalanches that suggest the readings indicate an upcoming avalanche. He calls the station and orders them to sound the alarm for the residents of Geiranger. Jacob's foot becomes trapped as the avalanche occurs. Arvid sacrifices himself to save Jacob, and the alarm is sounded shortly before the rockslide crashes into the fjord, creating a megatsunami expected to hit Geiranger in ten minutes.
Idun and her colleague Vibeke evacuate the hotel guests onto a bus, while Kristian takes Julia and drives uphill to Ørnevegen, before getting stuck in traffic. Realizing his altitude is too low, he abandons the car and takes Julia on foot, shouting for others to run. Their neighbor Anna's leg is trapped by a car, and Kristian attempts to free her, sending Julia to Ørnevegen with Anna's husband, Thomas, and daughter, Teresa. Seeing the tsunami approach and out of time, Kristian seats himself and Anna in a van before the tsunami engulfs the vehicle.
Meanwhile, Idun realizes Sondre is missing and refuses to leave without him. A Danish tourist, Maria, helps her search despite the objections of her husband, Philip. They find Sondre, but as they return to the lobby, they see that the bus is gone and the tsunami has reached Geiranger. They rush back downstairs to the basement's bomb shelter as they are chased by water. Maria was washed away while the rest hid in the bomb shelter.
Kristian survives but finds Anna dead impaled by debris. He walks up to Ørnevegen and finds Julia alive, leaving her with Thomas and Teresa while he heads back to Geiranger to find Idun and Sondre. In the now devastated town, Kristian quickly finds the destroyed evacuation bus full of dead passengers, including Vibeke but not Idun and Sondre, and he starts moving towards the hotel. Down in the bomb shelter, the water level rises, and they are unable to open the door, as it is blocked by debris.

title: Fifty Shades Freed
tagline: Don't Miss the Climax
overview: Believing they have left behind shadowy figures from their past, newlyweds Christian and Ana fully embrace an inextricable connection and shared life of luxury. But just as she steps into her role as Mrs. Grey and he relaxes into an unfamiliar stability, new threats could jeopardize their happy ending before it even begins.
plot:
Fifty Shades Freed is a romantic drama film directed by James Foley, released in 2018. The movie serves as the final installment in the Fifty Shades franchise, based on the novel of the same name by E.L. James.

The story picks up where Fifty Shades Darker left off, with Anastasia Steele (played by Dakota Johnson) and Christian Grey (played by Jamie Dornan) navigating their complex relationship. The couple is now engaged to be married, but Anastasia's desire for freedom and independence creates tension in their partnership.

As the wedding day approaches, Anastasia begins to feel suffocated by Christian's controlling behavior, which she had initially found attractive but now sees as a sign of his emotional immaturity. Meanwhile, Elena Lincoln (played by Laura Haddock), Christian's former lover, returns to Seattle and becomes a thorn in Anastasia's side.

Anastasia also meets Jack Hyde (played by Andrew Airlie), a wealthy businessman who seems to offer her the freedom and excitement she craves. As Anastasia navigates these new relationships, she must confront her own desires and boundaries with Christian.

Throughout the film, the characters' emotional journeys are explored in depth. Christian's backstory is revealed, showcasing his troubled past and the events that shaped him into the person he is today. Anastasia, on the other hand, grapples with her own identity and the sacrifices she has made for their relationship.

The movie culminates in a dramatic confrontation between Anastasia and Christian, as they both fight to maintain control of their relationship. Ultimately, Anastasia must make a choice between her love for Christian and her desire for independence.

Fifty Shades Freed received mixed reviews from critics, with some praising the film's emotional depth and others criticizing its portrayal of BDSM and relationships. Despite this, the movie was a commercial success, grossing over $375 million worldwide.

Overall, Fifty Shades Freed is a thought-provoking exploration of love, power dynamics, and personal growth. While it may not be to everyone's taste, the film provides an engaging and emotional conclusion to the Fifty Shades trilogy.

title: American Made
tagline: Based on a True Lie
overview: The true story of pilot Barry Seal, who transported contraband for the CIA and the Medellin cartel in the 1980s.
plot:
In 1978, Baton Rouge pilot Barry Seal, who flies commercial jets for TWA, is recruited by CIA case officer Monty Schafer. He asks Seal, who has been smuggling Cuban cigars into the country to make a little money, to fly reconnaissance missions over Central America using an Aerostar 600, outfitted with aerial surveillance cameras. Seal accepts the job, but hides it from his wife, Lucy.
In the 1980s, Schafer asks Seal to act as a courier between the CIA and General Noriega in Panama. During a mission, the Medellín Cartel picks Seal up and asks him to fly cocaine on his return flights to the US. Seal accepts and flies the cartel's cocaine to Louisiana, airdropping the drug in the countryside.
The CIA turns a blind eye to the drug smuggling, but the DEA tracks Seal down. To avoid the authorities, Seal and his family relocate to Mena, Arkansas and his wife comes to accept the wealth generated by his side job. The small town becomes wealthy as the hub of US cocaine trafficking.
Later, Schafer asks Seal to run guns to the Nicaraguan Contras in Honduras. Realizing the Contras are not serious about the war and just want to get rich, Seal starts trading the guns to the cartel. The CIA sets up a Contra training base in Mena and Seal flies the Contras in, but many of them escape as soon as they arrive.
Seal makes so much money he buries it in suitcases in the backyard. Seal's freeloading, unemployed brother-in-law JB moves in. JB starts stealing money and is arrested with a briefcase full of cash.
With JB out on bail, Seal gives him money and a plane ticket to Bora Bora for his safety. JB demands weekly cash and insults Lucy. As Seal chases after him, JB is killed by a car bomb placed by the Medellín Cartel, who had previously promised to "take care" of the JB problem.
The FBI catches wind of the sudden exuberance on the streets of Mena, not helped by JB's reckless spending. Eventually, the CIA shuts down the program and abandons Seal, who is arrested by the FBI, DEA, ATF and Arkansas State Police simultaneously.
Seal escapes prosecution by making a deal with the White House, which wants evidence of the Sandinistas being drug traffickers. They ask him to get photos that tie the Medellín Cartel to the Nicaraguan Sandinistas. Seal manages to get them, but the White House releases them as propaganda against the Sandinistas. Seal is prominently shown in the pictures, which leads to his indictment by the crusading state attorney general and the cartel plotting revenge.
Seal is convicted but sentenced to only 1,000 hours of community service. Moving from motel to motel making video recordings detailing his experiences, Seal expects an explosion any time he starts his car. As his community service is performed at the same Salvation Army building every night, Seal cannot hide from the cartel and is shot dead by an assassin.

title: The Fate of the Furious
tagline: Family no more.
overview: When a mysterious woman seduces Dom into the world of crime and a betrayal of those closest to him, the crew face trials that will test them as never before.
plot:
The Fate of the Furious is a 2017 action spy film directed by F. Gary Gray and written by Chris Morgan. It is the eighth installment in the Fast and Furious franchise.

The film begins with Dominic Toretto (Vin Diesel) living a quiet life on a remote island, away from his high-stakes lifestyle as a street racing and heist expert. However, his peaceful existence is disrupted when his estranged brother, Jakob (John Cena), arrives on the island seeking his help to take down their father's former associates.

As Dominic agrees to help Jakob, he begins to receive mysterious messages from an unknown sender, which leads him to participate in a series of high-stakes heists. Unbeknownst to Dominic, these heists are orchestrated by Cipher (Charlize Theron), a skilled hacker and terrorist mastermind who has been manipulating events from behind the scenes.

Cipher's true intentions become clear when she reveals that she has taken control of the world's most advanced artificial intelligence system, which she plans to use to hold the world hostage. She also kidnaps Dominic's girlfriend, Letty Ortiz (Michelle Rodriguez), in an attempt to lure him into a trap.

As Dominic delves deeper into Cipher's operation, he is joined by his old allies, including Roman Pearce (Tyrese Gibson) and Tej Parker (Chris "Ludacris" Bridges). Together, they embark on a perilous mission to stop Cipher and save the world from her sinister plans.

Meanwhile, Deckard Shaw (Jason Statham), Cipher's brother, seeks revenge against Dominic for his role in the death of their father. The two engage in an intense battle, which ultimately leads to Deckard's defeat at the hands of Dominic.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jakob is not what he seems. He is revealed to be working with Cipher, and his true intentions are to take down his brother and claim the family business for himself.

In the climactic final act, Dominic and his team launch a daring assault on Cipher's secret lair, where they engage in an epic battle against her henchmen and artificial intelligence system. In the end, Dominic manages to outsmart Cipher and destroy the AI system, saving the world from her catastrophic plans.

The film concludes with Dominic finally finding closure with his brother, who has come to terms with his past mistakes. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Dominic returning to his island home, ready to start anew and leave his high-stakes lifestyle behind.

Overall, The Fate of the Furious is an action-packed thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane stunts, heart-pumping suspense, and memorable characters.

title: Mulan
tagline: Loyal. Brave. True.
overview: When the Emperor of China issues a decree that one man per family must serve in the Imperial Chinese Army to defend the country from Huns, Hua Mulan, the eldest daughter of an honored warrior, steps in to take the place of her ailing father. She is spirited, determined and quick on her feet. Disguised as a man by the name of Hua Jun, she is tested every step of the way and must harness her innermost strength and embrace her true potential.
plot:
Mulan is an American fantasy action drama of 2020 produced by Walt Disney Pictures, directed by Niki Caro and written by Rick Jaffa, Amanda Silver, Lauren Hynek and Elizabeth Martin. A live-action adaptation of Disney's 1998 animated film, itself drawn from the Chinese Ballad of Mulan, it stars Liu Yifei as Hua Mulan, with Donnie Yen as Commander Tung, Gong Li as the shapeshifting witch Xianniang, Jason Scott Lee as the Rouran leader Böri Khan, Yoson An as Chen Honghui, Tzi Ma as Mulan's father Hua Zhou and Jet Li as the Emperor.

In imperial China, spirited Mulan worries her parents, who hope to see her well married, and a disastrous visit to the matchmaker shames her family. In the north, Rouran warriors led by Böri Khan overrun an imperial outpost, aided by Xianniang, who disguises herself as a surviving soldier to report the attack. The Emperor orders every family to provide one man for the army, and Mulan's father, who has no sons and an injured leg, volunteers. Knowing he would not survive, Mulan takes his armour, horse and sword and enlists in his place, posing as a man.

title: Cruella
tagline: Hello Cruel World
overview: In 1970s London amidst the punk rock revolution, a young grifter named Estella is determined to make a name for herself with her designs. She befriends a pair of young thieves who appreciate her appetite for mischief, and together they are able to build a life for themselves on the London streets. One day, Estella’s flair for fashion catches the eye of the Baroness von Hellman, a fashion legend who is devastatingly chic and terrifyingly haute. But their relationship sets in motion a course of events and revelations that will cause Estella to embrace her wicked side and become the raucous, fashionable and revenge-bent Cruella.
plot:
Cruella is a 2021 American biographical crime comedy film directed by Craig Gillespie, based on the 1972 novel "The Art of Cruelty" by Donald Spoto. The film stars Emma Stone as the titular character.

The story follows Estella de Vil (Emma Stone), a young woman who grows up in an orphanage with her two friends, Lucy and Adrian. Their cruel and abusive caretaker, Miss Havisham, instills in them a deep-seated hatred for luxury and wealth. As they grow older, the three women become embroiled in a world of high society, where Estella catches the eye of the wealthy and influential Baroness von Hellman (Carlyle).

The Baroness takes Estella under her wing, teaching her the art of fashion and introducing her to the world of luxury. However, as Estella becomes more and more entrenched in this world, she begins to lose touch with her friends and her own sense of identity.

As Estella's obsession with fur grows, she becomes fixated on acquiring the finest pelts for her designs. Her fixation leads her down a dark path, where she will stop at nothing to get what she wants. The film takes a darker turn as Estella's transformation into the infamous Cruella de Vil begins.

Throughout the film, Emma Stone delivers a captivating performance, bringing depth and nuance to the character of Estella. The supporting cast, including Emma Thompson as Lady Danbury and Joel Fry as Jasper, add to the film's humor and charm.

The film is a visually stunning exploration of the darker side of human nature, with a keen eye for detail in its costumes, production design, and cinematography. The film's themes of class, privilege, and the commodification of animal fur are timely and thought-provoking.

Overall, Cruella is a stylish and engaging film that offers a fresh take on the classic Disney villain. With Emma Stone's standout performance at its center, the film is sure to delight audiences and leave them eager for more.

title: Elle
overview: When Michèle, the CEO of a gaming software company, is attacked in her home by an unknown assailant, she refuses to let it alter her precisely ordered life. She manages crises involving family, all the while becoming engaged in a game of cat and mouse with her stalker.
plot:
Michèle Leblanc is raped in her home by an assailant in a ski mask. She then cleans up the mess and resumes her life. She is the head of a successful video game company, where her male employees are alternately resentful of or infatuated with her. She carries on an affair with Robert, the husband of her friend and business partner Anna, and flirts with her married neighbor Patrick. Michèle feels detached from her son Vincent, who submits to his abusive, pregnant girlfriend Josie. She has a contentious relationship with her mother, Irène, whom she resents for her narcissism and involvements with younger men. Furthermore, she is the daughter of an infamous mass murderer whose parole hearing is approaching. Haunted by her father's actions, Michèle is wary of law enforcement and does not report her rape to police.
Michèle grows increasingly suspicious of the men in her life. She receives harassing text messages from her assailant at a blocked number, indicating he is stalking her. She at first suspects Kurt, a particularly resentful employee, when a CGI animation of a monster raping her is emailed to everyone at the company. She pepper-sprays a man lurking outside her house, only to find out it is her ex-husband Richard, who was checking on her safety. She later discovers that another employee, who has been infatuated with her, created the animation but did not rape her.
On Christmas Eve, Irène suffers a stroke and begs her daughter to go see her father before she dies in hospital. Michèle is later attacked in her home by the assailant and, after stabbing his hand and unmasking him, learns that he is Patrick. Though she now knows his identity and realizes that he is able to enter her home despite having her locks changed, she still does not call the police and takes no measures to increase her home security.
Michèle decides to visit her father after his parole application is rejected, only to find that he has hanged himself hours before she arrives. On the way home from the prison, she gets into a car crash in a secluded area. Rather than calling an ambulance, she first tries to call her friends, and then decides to call Patrick. After he rescues her from the car and bandages her, Michèle courts a brazenly dangerous sexual relationship with him. She engages in a vivid rape scenario with him. The two of them walk a delicate line in which Patrick has to feel as though he is raping Michèle, even though she consents to the roleplay.
Michèle grows increasingly disillusioned with her life leading up to the launch party for her company's new video game. She confesses to Anna that she was having an affair with Robert. As Patrick drives her home, Michèle professes that she is no longer in denial about their unhealthy relationship and claims she intends to call the police. She takes her time walking in front of his parked car after getting out, and then makes a point of leaving her gate unlocked.

title: The Red Turtle
overview: The dialogue-less film follows the major life stages of a castaway on a deserted tropical island populated by turtles, crabs and birds.
plot:
A man set adrift by a storm wakes up on a beach. He discovers that he is on an uninhabited island with plenty of fresh water, fruit, and a dense bamboo forest. It is dominated by a smooth rock hill. After a few nights he begins to hallucinate, seeing a bridge to lead him offshore and later a string quartet playing on the beach. He builds a raft from bamboo and attempts to sail away, but his raft is destroyed by an unseen creature in the sea, forcing him back to the island. He tries again with a larger raft, but is again foiled by the creature. A third attempt ends similarly, but this time he sees the creature: a giant red sea turtle.
That evening, the man sees the red turtle crawling up the beach. In anger, he hits it on the head with a bamboo stick, then flips it over onto its back, stranding it. While working on another raft, he feels remorse and returns to the turtle but it is too heavy for him to flip over. He fetches water for it, but when he returns, it is dead. He falls asleep next to it. In the morning, the man is surprised to find a red-haired woman lying unconscious inside the shell, which has split. He fetches water for her and builds a shelter to protect her from the sun. When rain hits, the woman wakes up and goes swimming. The woman casts the shell adrift on the sea and the man does the same to his raft. The two reconcile and fall in love.
The couple have a red-haired son. The curious boy finds a glass bottle and his father and mother tell him their story through pictographs. After accidentally falling into the sea, the boy learns he is a natural swimmer, and swims with some green sea turtles. He swims back to his mother, who hugs him and looks out at the sea with apprehension. The boy grows into a young man.
One day, a tsunami hits the island, destroying most of the bamboo forest and separating the family. After the tsunami recedes, the young man searches for his parents and finds his mother wounded with no sign of his father. He swims out to sea and is joined by three turtles. They find his father clinging to a large bamboo tree. Just as he slips under the water, they arrive and rescue him. The young man also finds his glass bottle, and the family clean up the wreckage and burn the dead bamboo.
A few years later, the young man has a dream about swimming away into the sea; the water becomes static, allowing him to swim to the top of a huge wave, from which he can see further over the horizon. Seeing this as his calling, he says goodbye to his parents in the morning and swims away with the three green turtles. The man and woman continue to live on the island and grow old together. One night, after gazing at the Moon, the man closes his eyes and dies. The woman grieves. She lies next to him, and lays her hand on his. As her hand transforms into a flipper and she transforms back into the red turtle, she crawls down the beach and swims away.

title: Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle
original_title: Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle
overview: When Curious George is offered a special space mission, Ted (The Man in the Yellow Hat) can't deny his little friend this exciting journey, especially after Curious George completes the training. But when he crash-lands in Africa, a worried Ted goes searching, expecting the worst, only to have it turn out to be the best.
plot:
Curious George 3: Back to the Jungle is a 2015 American traditionally animated family adventure film directed by Phil Weinstein and written by Chuck Tately, based on the Curious George books by Margret and H. A. Rey. Produced by Imagine Entertainment, Universal 1440 Entertainment and WGBH, with music by Heitor Pereira, it is the third film in the franchise and the second to skip theaters. Frank Welker and Jeff Bennett return as the voices of George and his friend Ted, the Man with the Yellow Hat, joined by John Goodman as Hal Houston, Angela Bassett as Dr. Kulinda and Alexander Polinsky as Andrew.

After a hectic kite chase in the park, George and Ted are approached by Houston, an official of a space agency, who offers George a once-in-a-lifetime mission. As part of a project to stop the floods devastating a region of Central Africa, George is to fly into orbit, retrieve a device called the Regional Dam Synchronizer from a broken satellite, and bring it back so that it can be installed on a dam, where its antenna will coordinate the other dams in the area. Ted is reluctant at first, but agrees after George's pleading, on the condition that he complete the astronaut training, which he does.

The first part of the mission goes smoothly, and George retrieves the device, but during the return his curiosity sends the capsule's systems haywire and it plunges toward Earth. George ejects and lands somewhere in the African jungle, while the capsule disappears with the device still on board. Houston, his assistant Andrew and Ted travel to Africa, where search teams scour an area hundreds of miles wide; eventually Ted sets out on his own, cut off from contact with Houston. Back in the land of his birth, George meets Dr. Kulinda, a veterinarian who runs an animal preserve. The friends must find each other, recover the device and install it before a huge storm bearing down on the region can ravage the jungle, and in the end they complete the mission in time.

The film was released on DVD by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on 23 June 2015 and later aired on PBS Kids. It was the last film in the series to use traditional animation. Reviewers praised its fast, suspenseful yet gentle storytelling, bright visuals and lack of a conventional villain, with the storm serving as the main threat, as well as songs such as "Ordinary Superman".

title: It's Only the End of the World
tagline: It would have been a lovely family dinner. If it weren’t the last.
overview: Louis, a terminally ill writer, returns home after a long absence to tell his family that he is dying.
plot:
In a place identified only as "Somewhere," Louis, a 34-year-old playwright dealing with a terminal illness, takes a short flight to his home to reunite with his family, whom he has not seen in 12 years. His younger sister, Suzanne, has little memory of him. Upon arriving at the house, Louis' mother, Martine, is surprised to realize Louis has never met the wife of his brother Antoine, Catherine, as Louis was not present at their wedding. Catherine begins telling Louis about her and Antoine's children and nervously stammers to explain why they named one of their boys Louis, after Louis and Antoine's father. Antoine creates tension and snaps that Louis is uninterested in hearing about their children. Louis talks on the telephone to someone and says that he plans to tell his family about his impending death and then leave, and he expresses uncertainty as to how they will react.
Louis and Catherine awkwardly meet in the hallway and attempt to apologize to each other for the tense conversations. Louis remarks that he assumes Antoine has attempted to give her a negative opinion of Louis. Catherine replies Antoine actually speaks little of Louis, and Antoine feels that Louis has little to no interest in their lives, and she openly suspects that belief may have some truth in it. She questions Louis if he knows what Antoine does for a living and explains that he makes tools in a nearby location. Martine also lectures Louis about taking responsibility in the family and says that his status, success, and courage give him some authority. She learns that he has moved from the address where she had been sending his mail, and he had not told her where he currently lives.
Louis expresses interest in seeing the family's former house and cites nostalgia, which bewilders the others, who regard it as a ruin. The family argument that follows puts an end to his wish. He rides with Antoine to the shops for cigarettes and makes small talk, which angers Antoine, who is sick of all the secrecy surrounding Louis's life and the reason that he has returned. He later tells Louis that his former lover Pierre died about a week ago from cancer.
During a meal, Louis promises to visit home more and tells Suzanne she is welcome to visit him. However, it soon becomes apparent Louis is about to leave. Seizing upon this, Antoine tries to remove him from the house and insists on driving him to the airport, and the family shouts back at Antoine for his brutality. Antoine lashes back by saying that he is tired of being treated as the family's freak. After a pause, Louis leaves without having told his family of his prognosis.

title: Bloodshot
tagline: Being a superhero is in his blood
overview: After he and his wife are murdered, marine Ray Garrison is resurrected by a team of scientists. Enhanced with nanotechnology, he becomes a superhuman, biotech killing machine—'Bloodshot'. As Ray first trains with fellow super-soldiers, he cannot recall anything from his former life. But when his memories flood back and he remembers the man that killed both him and his wife, he breaks out of the facility to get revenge, only to discover that there's more to the conspiracy than he thought.
plot:
Bloodshot is a 2020 American science fiction action film directed by David S. Goyer and starring Vin Diesel. The movie is based on the Valiant Comics character of the same name.

The story begins with Ray Garrison (Vin Diesel), a former Special Forces operative who was severely injured during his last mission. He is recruited by the government agency known as "The Agency" to participate in an experimental program called "Operation Bloodshot." This program uses advanced technology to enhance human soldiers' abilities, allowing them to fight more effectively.

Ray's body is subjected to the technology, which enhances his strength, speed, and agility. However, the process also has a devastating side effect: it slowly kills Ray's body over time, forcing him to live in a state of limbo between life and death.

The Agency uses Ray as a test subject for their new technology, but he soon discovers that they have ulterior motives. They plan to use his enhanced abilities to carry out covert operations without being detected. Ray is horrified by this revelation and decides to take matters into his own hands.

As Ray delves deeper into the truth about Operation Bloodshot, he uncovers a conspiracy involving corrupt government officials and The Agency's true intentions. He also discovers that his wife, Kate (Vanessa Kirby), has been kidnapped by The Agency, who plan to use her as leverage to control Ray.

Ray sets out on a mission to rescue Kate and take down The Agency from the inside. Along the way, he encounters other enhanced operatives, including Wolf (Samuel L. Jackson) and Dr. Karen Fischer (Deborah Ann Woll). Together, they form an uneasy alliance to take down their common enemy.

As Ray navigates this complex web of intrigue, he must also confront his own mortality. He knows that his time is limited, and he must make the most of it before he dies. The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Ray and the leader of The Agency, who will stop at nothing to achieve their goals.

Throughout the film, Vin Diesel delivers a strong performance as the titular character, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and troubled hero. The action sequences are fast-paced and thrilling, with impressive visual effects that bring the enhanced operatives to life.

Overall, Bloodshot is an action-packed sci-fi thriller that explores themes of identity, mortality, and the ethics of advanced technology. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of Vin Diesel and science fiction will likely find plenty to enjoy in this visually stunning and entertaining film.

title: Hell or High Water
tagline: Blood always follows money.
overview: A divorced dad and his ex-con brother resort to a desperate scheme in order to save their family's farm in West Texas.
plot:
In West Texas, brothers Toby and Tanner Howard rob two branches of the Texas Midlands Bank. Though the robberies are well-planned, Tanner's wild nature leads him to take unnecessary risks, frustrating Toby. Their mother has died after a long illness, leaving their ranch in debt because of a reverse mortgage provided by the Texas Midlands Bank, which would lead to the foreclosure of their lands if not settled. Meanwhile, oil has been discovered on their land, and Toby is determined to ensure a comfortable life for his estranged ex-wife and their two sons.
Two Texas Rangers, Marcus Hamilton and Alberto Parker, are assigned to the case. Hamilton, who is close to retirement, investigates the robberies and quickly determines the robbers' methods and personalities. Meanwhile, Tanner robs another bank, unbeknownst to Toby, who sits at a nearby diner. They bury the getaway cars after each robbery. They then launder the stolen money in Oklahoma at an Indian casino, where Toby has the casino convert their "winnings" into a check made out to the Texas Midlands Bank. With untraceable funds, the brothers head back to Texas.
After staking out another branch of the Texas Midlands Bank without success—and where the two Rangers together are temporarily cowed by the "dragon waitress of the T-Bone"—Hamilton figures a pattern to the bank robberies. Determining the next target, Parker and he head there. Pressed for time, the brothers proceed despite the bank being crowded. A shootout ensues with a security guard and an armed civilian; Tanner kills both of them. During the escape, Toby is shot in the back by an armed posse of locals.
The brothers race out of town with the posse in pursuit, before Tanner drives them back with an automatic rifle. The brothers split up; Toby takes the money using another vehicle, while Tanner acts as bait. He draws law enforcement and the posse to a desert mountain ridge, where he takes potshots at officers with a hunting rifle, killing Parker in the process. Distraught, Hamilton enlists a local's knowledge of the area to circle behind Tanner and fatally shoot him.
Meanwhile, Toby passes through a police checkpoint without incident. He launders the stolen cash at a casino, where he sees the news report of his brother's death. He takes the casino's check to the bank just in time to avoid the ranch's foreclosure and deeds the ranch into a family trust.
Following his retirement, Hamilton visits his former office and learns that Toby has been cleared as a suspect, as he has no criminal record nor motive, as his new oil wells earn more in a month than the total stolen in all of the robberies together. The money from the ranch's oil wells is deposited at the Texas Midlands Bank, which refuses to cooperate with the investigation for fear of losing management of the family's trust fund. Despite the lack of evidence, Hamilton remains certain that Toby was the mastermind.

title: Please Stand By
tagline: Boldly go.
overview: A young autistic woman runs away from her caregiver in order to boldly go and deliver her 500-page Star Trek script to a writing competition in Hollywood. On an adventure full of laughter and tears, Wendy follows the guiding spirit of Mr. Spock on her journey into the unknown.
plot:
Wendy is an autistic young woman with a special interest in Star Trek. She lives a routine life in a San Francisco group home where she is monitored by the house manager, Scottie. She spends her time writing a 427-page Star Trek script to enter in Paramount Pictures' screenwriting contest for the $100,000 prize.
Wendy is visited by her sister Audrey, who shows her pictures of her infant daughter, Ruby, and reveals that she is selling their childhood home. Wendy asks her to take her home, arguing that she will be able to buy back the house and help care for Ruby once she wins the screenwriting contest. Audrey refuses, informing Wendy she is not capable of caring for a baby. Wendy has a meltdown and Audrey leaves the group home weeping.
After Wendy misses the mail-in date to send her script to Paramount Pictures, she decides to deliver the script herself. She leaves the group home early the next morning and is followed by the group home's small dog, Pete. They board a bus to Los Angeles, but are left by the side of the road as Pete urinates on the bus.
Wendy then wanders into a shanty town, where she is robbed of most of her money. She then wanders to a nearby shop and is nearly swindled out of the last of her money by an employee. Luckily, elderly woman Rose intervenes to stop them from exploiting Wendy. She sympathizes with her as her grandson is also autistic, and lets Wendy accompany her on the senior citizens' bus. However, the driver falls asleep at the wheel, crashing the bus.
Following the bus crash, Wendy wakes up in a hospital in Bakersfield. Still determined to deliver her script as planned, she leaves Pete at the hospital and escapes. During her escape, Wendy loses part of her script by chance. She gathers used paper and begins rewriting it.
Simultaneously, Audrey and Scottie have realized Wendy is missing. They begin to search for her and file a missing persons report. After correctly deducing that Wendy left for LA to personally deliver her script, Scottie and her son Sam leave on the road. The Bakersfield hospital notifies Scottie and Audrey of Wendy's whereabouts; police continue the search from there. Scottie and Sam find the missing script pages while scouring the hospital.
Wendy then attempts to buy a bus ticket to LA, but is unable to as she has only coins remaining. She ultimately stows away on the next bus there, inside the baggage compartment. Upon her arrival to LA, Wendy wanders around until two police officers recognize her from the missing persons report. Fortunately, Officer Frank gains Wendy's trust by speaking to her in Klingon. They bring her to the police station, where she is reunited with Audrey and Scottie. They drive Wendy to Paramount Pictures so she can deliver her script as planned.

title: Hellraiser
tagline: Unlock your fears.
overview: A young woman struggling with addiction comes into possession of an ancient puzzle box, unaware that its purpose is to summon the Cenobites, a group of sadistic supernatural beings from another dimension.
plot:
Hellraiser is a 2022 supernatural horror film directed by David Bruckner from a screenplay by Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski, based on a story they wrote with David S. Goyer. The eleventh film in the franchise drawn from Clive Barker's 1986 novella The Hellbound Heart, it stars Odessa A'zion as Riley McKendry, a young woman recovering from addiction, with Jamie Clayton, Adam Faison, Drew Starkey, Brandon Flynn and Goran Višnjić.

At an orgy in his mansion, hedonistic millionaire Roland Voight gives a puzzle box to a young man, Joey, whose attempt to solve it springs a blade that cuts him and opens a portal from which chains tear him apart. Six years later, Riley lives with her brother, Matt, his boyfriend, Colin, and their roommate, Nora. She and her boyfriend, Trevor, find the box in an abandoned warehouse, and after Matt accuses her of relapsing, she storms out and solves it in a park, narrowly avoiding the blade. The Cenobites, mutilated beings from another dimension, appear and demand a sacrifice. Matt, searching for her, cuts himself on the box and vanishes.

Riley and Trevor visit Voight's former lawyer, Serena Menaker, who tries to take the box but is cut and later abducted. In Voight's empty mansion, Riley learns from his journals that each of the box's six configurations requires a victim marked by the blade, after which its holder receives a "gift" from Leviathan, the ruler of Hell. Nora is stabbed by the mutilated Voight, hidden in the walls, and is flayed by the Cenobites' leader, the Priest, who offers Riley a deal: two more sacrifices or herself. Riley marks the Cenobite known as the Chatterer, who is ripped apart. Voight reappears, stabs Colin and reveals that his own reward was a device that endlessly twists his nerves, and that Trevor has been working for him to find victims. When Voight traps the Cenobites to bargain for release, Riley marks Trevor as the final sacrifice. Voight chooses "power" and is healed, only to be impaled by Leviathan's chain and later remade as a Cenobite. Offered Matt's resurrection, Riley refuses, accepting his death, and leaves with Colin.

The film premiered at Fantastic Fest on September 28, 2022, and was released on Hulu on October 7. Reviews were generally positive, with 67% on Rotten Tomatoes and 55 on Metacritic, critics calling it a welcome revival after a string of weak sequels.

title: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald
original_title: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald
tagline: Fate of one. Future of all.
overview: Gellert Grindelwald has escaped imprisonment and has begun gathering followers to his cause—elevating wizards above all non-magical beings. plot:
Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald is a 2018 American fantasy film directed by David Yates and the sequel to Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them (2016). The movie takes place in 1927, one year after the events of the first film.

The story begins with Newt Scamander (Eddie Redmayne), a magizoologist who is on the run from the Ministry of Magic. He is being pursued by the Auror Office, led by Alastor Moody (Jude Law), who believes that Newt has stolen a powerful magical creature known as the Bowtruckle.

Meanwhile, Gellert Grindelwald (Johnny Depp) is on the loose, and his true intentions are revealed. He is a dark wizard who seeks to dominate the wizarding world and establish a new order with himself at the helm. Grindelwald's ultimate goal is to create a magical utopia where wizards and non-magical people coexist.

Newt meets Leta Lestrange (Zoe Kravitz), an old friend from his past, who has been hiding secrets of her own. She reveals that she was in love with Newt, but he rejected her due to their complicated history. This revelation sets off a chain of events as Newt and Leta become entangled in Grindelwald's plans.

As the story unfolds, we see Grindelwald's rise to power, and his manipulation of the wizarding world. He uses his charisma and magical abilities to recruit followers and gain control over various magical creatures. The movie also explores the backstory of Credence Barebone (Ezra Miller), a young man with mysterious powers who is being manipulated by Grindelwald.

The plot thickens as Newt, Leta, and Albus Dumbledore's (Jude Law) past come into play. We learn that Dumbledore was once in love with Gellert Grindelwald, but their relationship ended due to his dark ambitions. The movie also reveals the tragic fate of Grindelwald's sister, Ariana, who was killed by a group of wizards who were angry about her association with Grindelwald.

As the story reaches its climax, Newt and Leta must navigate their complicated past while trying to stop Grindelwald's plans. The movie features an epic battle between good and evil, with the fate of the wizarding world hanging in the balance.

The ending sets up a thrilling conclusion for the Fantastic Beasts series, as Newt and his allies prepare to face off against Grindelwald once again. The movie concludes on a cliffhanger, leaving audiences eager to see what happens next in the story.

Overall, Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of love, power, and redemption. With its richly detailed world-building and complex characters, this movie is sure to delight fans of the wizarding world.

Along the way, she teams up with a group of rebels, including a charming and handsome prince named Edward (Maya Rudolph), to overthrow Queen Narissa and save Andalasia.

Overall, Disenchanted is a heartwarming and entertaining sequel that explores themes of identity, family, and the complexities of growing up. With its lighthearted tone and engaging storyline, it's sure to delight fans of the original Enchanted film and newcomers alike.

As tensions rise, Columbus and Tallahassee must confront their own mortality and the reality of their situation. They also have to navigate their complicated relationships with each other and the rest of the group. Along the way, they meet a new character, Seattle (Rosie Perez), who becomes an ally in their quest for survival.

The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Columbus and Tallahassee riding off into the sunset, ready for their next adventure together.

Overall, Zombieland: Double Tap is a fun, action-packed sequel that expands on the characters and world of the original film. It's a loving tribute to the zombie genre and a testament to the enduring power of friendship and community in the face of adversity.

title: Tomb Raider
tagline: Her legend begins.
overview: Lara Croft, the fiercely independent daughter of a missing adventurer, must push herself beyond her limits when she finds herself on the island where her father disappeared.
plot:
Tomb Raider is a 2018 action-adventure film directed by Roar Uthaug and written by Geneva Robertson-Dworet and Alastair Siddons, based on the video game series and chiefly on the 2013 game. An American and British co-production, it reboots the film series with Alicia Vikander as Lara Croft, who travels to her father's last known destination to solve the mystery of his disappearance. Dominic West plays her father Lord Richard Croft, Walton Goggins the rival archaeologist Mathias Vogel, Daniel Wu the ship captain Lu Ren and Kristin Scott Thomas Ana Miller, an associate at Croft Holdings.

Refusing to accept that her missing father is dead, Lara works as a bicycle courier in London. After Ana bails her out of a police arrest, she warns her that Croft Manor will be sold unless she claims her inheritance. Reluctantly agreeing, Lara finds a secret chamber in her father's tomb containing a video message about his research into Himiko, the mythical Queen of Yamatai said to command power over life and death, and his instruction to destroy his work. Instead, she pawns the jade pendant he gave her and travels to Hong Kong, where she hires Lu Ren to sail his ship into the Devil's Sea in search of the island of Yamatai. The ship is wrecked in a storm, and Lara washes ashore into the hands of Mathias, who leads an expedition funded by a shadowy organization called Trinity that wants to weaponize Himiko's power. Claiming he killed her father, Mathias enslaves Lara and Lu, but Lara escapes and finds Richard alive, hiding on the island to keep Trinity away from the tomb. With help from Lu and the other slaves, she steals Mathias's satellite phone, but Richard is captured and Mathias forces Lara to open the tomb. Inside, they discover that Himiko carried a deadly infectious disease and had entombed herself to protect others. Mathias cuts off one of her fingers to take back to Trinity, and Richard, now infected, sacrifices himself by blowing up the tomb, while Lara forces Mathias to swallow the finger and kicks him into a pit before escaping with Lu by helicopter. Back in London, she accepts her inheritance, finds evidence that Croft Holdings is linked to Trinity and that Ana may be its agent, and reclaims her pendant as she prepares for her next adventure.

Released in the United Kingdom on March 14, 2018, and in the United States two days later, the film received mixed reviews, with a 52% Rotten Tomatoes rating, and grossed $275 million worldwide.

title: The Cokeville Miracle
tagline: Based on actual events.
overview: On May 9, 1986, a small ranching community in Wyoming experiences a divine intervention when a couple detonates a bomb inside a crowded classroom.
plot:
In May 1986, David Young from Tucson, Arizona (and former town marshal of Cokeville), his daughter from his first marriage (Penny), and his second wife (Doris), journey to Cokeville, to take the school hostage and blow it up. Part of the terrorist group (including Penny) bails at the last minute. At the school, Young and Doris gather 136 students and 18 teachers inside Room 4, and Young explains he has a bomb wired to a dead man's switch tied to his wrist. He orders the school principal to call the authorities and deliver his ransom demand: $2,000,000 for each child.
Cop Ron Hartley, begins to question his religious beliefs, wondering whether a just God would really allow the atrocities he witnesses in his work to happen. On that day, Ron learns about the situation at the school and rushes to Cokeville. Inside the school, gas begins to leak from the bomb, making the children sick from the fumes. The teachers convince Young to let them open the doors and windows for ventilation. When Young goes to the bathroom, he transfers the dead man's switch to Doris, who accidentally pulls the switch and triggers the bomb. The room is set on fire and fills with smoke and shrapnel as shells from Young's guns explode in the heat. The teachers quickly evacuate the children through the open doors and windows. Young returns from the bathroom, shoots Doris, shoots teacher John Miller, and finally shoots himself.
A few days after the event, a child (Jason) has post-traumatic symptoms. He consults a psychologist and reveals that he saw angels when the bomb exploded. Other children admitted they saw them too. Ron investigates and is led to believe that angels indeed protected the children that day. Ron's faith is still challenged after the findings of his investigation, but the bishop's sermon finally convinces him that angels divinely interferred. Out of the 154 adults and children, none of them died in a confined room explosion. The only two fatalities were the bomber and his wife.
While Cokeville was predominantly Mormon, the director chose to make the religious faith in the movie nondenominational.

title: Gotti
tagline: He showed the world who's boss.
overview: John Gotti rises to the top of the New York underworld to become the boss of the Gambino crime family. His life takes a tumultuous turn as he faces tragedy, multiple trials and a prison sentence.
plot:
In 1973, Gambino crime family underboss Aniello "Neil" Dellacroce tasks John Gotti, a young associate, with killing gangster James McBratney, who is believed to have kidnapped and murdered boss Carlo Gambino's nephew Emanuel. After executing McBratney at a bar, Gotti is identified as his killer in 1974 and sentenced to 4 years' imprisonment at Green Haven Correctional Facility the following year. Released on parole in 1977 after 2 years, he reunites with his wife Victoria and their children and becomes a "made man", immediately climbing the Mafia hierarchy to become a capo.
By 1979, Gotti operates out of the Bergin Hunt and Fish Club with his childhood friend Angelo Ruggiero. His oldest son John "Junior" Gotti enters the New York Military Academy, but aspires to join the Mafia. Despite Dellacroce's counsel and the assurances of fellow capo Frank DeCicco, Gotti mistrusts the Lucchese crime family's top underboss, Anthony Casso. On March 18, 1980, his 12-year-old middle son Frank is accidentally struck and killed by a car driven by John Favara, his next-door neighbor. Favara later disappears on July 28, and the only witness to his abduction, diner owner Leon Papon, is intimidated into silence.
With the Gambino family having come under increased scrutiny in 1985, Gotti becomes convinced that family boss Paul Castellano is too frail to lead effectively. Junior, meanwhile, instigates a bar brawl that causes a patron's death, infuriating his father. Federal authorities release incriminating tapes, caught on an FBI wiretap of Gambino family meetings, that reveal Gotti's involvement in labor racketeering. He escapes conviction when the case goes to trial, but prosecutor Diane Giacalone, assistant attorney for the Eastern District of New York, discloses that his close associate, Wilfred "Willy Boy" Johnson, has been a confidential informant for the FBI since 1966. Gotti agrees to reprieve Johnson for betraying the family, but does not object when Johnson is eventually murdered on August 29, 1988.
Suffering from brain cancer, Dellacroce informs Gotti of Castellano's plans to reorganize the Gambino family and disband Gotti's crew due to his insubordination and helps him secure the approval of the Five Families to eliminate Castellano, who fails to attend Dellacroce's funeral two days after his death on December 2. Castellano and his bodyguard Thomas Bilotti are gunned down outside Sparks Steak House in midtown Manhattan on December 16. Gotti subsequently takes over the Gambino family, becoming "the real-life Godfather". title: Georgetown
overview: Ulrich Mott  is an eccentric and versatile social climber with grandiose plans to affect United States foreign policy. Encouraged  in his attempts by his strategically chosen (and much older) wife, the well-connected journalist Elsa Brecht, Mott has a knack for making himself indispensable and impossible to ignore. The only one seemingly immune to his charms is Elsa's daughter Amanda, who might simply disapprove of her mother marrying a much younger man - or perhaps she senses something more sinister beneath the smooth-talking surface?
plot:
Georgetown is a 2019 American crime drama directed by Christoph Waltz in his feature directorial debut and written by David Auburn. It is based on Franklin Foer's 2012 New York Times Magazine article "The Worst Marriage in Georgetown", about the 2011 killing of 91-year-old socialite Viola Herms Drath by her much younger husband. Waltz stars as Ulrich Mott, with Vanessa Redgrave as Elsa Breht, Annette Bening as her daughter, Amanda.

Told out of sequence, the story follows Ulrich, a fifty-year-old conman and social climber interning for a congressman, using his boss's ID card to slip into a banquet, where he meets Elsa, a wealthy, elderly journalist and socialite living in Georgetown. Posing as a doctoral student, he arranges a lunch with her. After her husband dies, Elsa retreats from society, worrying Amanda, until Ulrich calls on the eve of 2000 and invites her to a concert. Amanda, delighted by her mother's renewed energy, announces she has been offered a tenured law professorship at Harvard and asks Elsa to move to Boston, but Elsa declines, and Ulrich tells the dismayed gathering that he and Elsa will marry.

Elsa uses her connections to advance Ulrich's one-man consulting agency, which he fills with prominent names through lies. In 2004, after Iraqi diplomats humiliatingly reject his offer to broker peace talks, he comes home drunk and nearly causes Elsa to fall down the stairs. She grows suspicious of his sexuality and, in 2006, finds him in bed with a man in a New York hotel; after he throws her out, she reports him to police for assault. Ulrich then vanishes for two years, claiming to be a freelance peace envoy in Iraq, and returns hailed as a diplomatic miracle worker. After an argument following a dinner party, he goes for a walk and later says he came home to find Elsa dead. Charged with murder, he hides key facts from his lawyers, then fires them, goes on a hunger strike and is hospitalized. An epilogue shows Ulrich being rebuffed by his former lover that night, then confronted by Elsa, who has discovered that he spent his absence as a motel desk clerk in Miami; as she calls him an idiot, he rushes up the stairs toward her.

Filmed in Toronto in 2017, Georgetown premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 27, 2019, and received a limited U.S. release from Vertical Entertainment on May 14, 2021. Reviews were mixed, at 63% on Rotten Tomatoes and 49 on Metacritic, with The New York Times calling Waltz a pleasure to watch.

As the story unfolds, Baby must confront his past and make a choice between his loyalty to Doc and his growing feelings for Debora. In the end, Baby makes a bold move that sets him free from his life as a getaway driver. The film concludes with Baby driving off into the sunset, finally able to pursue his dreams and find happiness.

Overall, Baby Driver is a high-octane action film with a unique blend of music, style, and humor. Wright's direction brings the story to life, and the cast delivers strong performances that add depth and emotion to the narrative.
