plot:
Monkey King: Hero Is Back is a 2015 Chinese fantasy adventure film directed by Raman Hui and produced by Hengdian Chinese Film Production Co., along with other production companies.

The movie begins with the Monkey King, Sun Wukong (played by Donnie Yen), who has been imprisoned in the White Cloud Temple for over 500 years. The story is set in a modern-day China where the Monkey King's legend has become a myth. However, the evil forces of the White Bone Demon and her son, General Zhao, are trying to revive the ancient magic that once made the Monkey King powerful.

The film starts with Sun Wukong being released from his prison by the Jade Emperor (played by Raymond Lam), who is worried about the growing threat of General Zhao. The Monkey King returns to the mortal world to find that he has lost his magical powers and must rely on his human form to survive.

As Sun Wukong navigates this new reality, he meets a young girl named Lin Shaoyu (played by Shu Qi), who is being pursued by General Zhao's men. The Monkey King decides to help her, and together they embark on a journey to stop General Zhao and his plans to revive the ancient magic.

Along the way, Sun Wukong encounters various characters from Chinese mythology, including Zhu Bajie (played by Xuan Liu) and Sha Wujing (played by Danny Chan), who join him on his quest. The group faces numerous challenges as they battle against General Zhao's forces and try to find a way to restore the Monkey King's powers.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that General Zhao is not just a simple villain but a complex character with his own motivations and backstory. His desire for power and revenge drives him to seek out the ancient magic, which he believes will allow him to overthrow the Jade Emperor and rule China.

title: 12 Rounds 3: Lockdown
tagline: Twelve Rounds In the Clip. One Shot at Redemption.
overview: Lockdown Follows a police officer who returns to duty after recovering from a gun shot wound to discover incriminating evidence of illegal activities against those closest to him. He quickly finds himself trapped inside his own precinct, hunted and in search of the truth, as the crooked cops stop at nothing to recover the evidence.
plot:
12 Rounds 3: Lockdown is an American action film of 2015 directed by Stephen Reynolds and written by Bobby Lee Darby and Nathan Brookes. The third and final film in the 12 Rounds series, co-produced by WWE Studios and Lionsgate, it gave the wrestler Dean Ambrose (Jonathan Good) his film debut as Detective John Shaw. Roger Cross plays the corrupt Detective Tyler Burke, with Lochlyn Munro as Darrow, Sarah Smyth as Jenny Taylor and Rebecca Marshall as Captain Ellen Matthews.

Burke and his men Gideon and Saul kill the drug dealer George Freemont after destroying evidence that Burke has been distributing narcotics. Meanwhile Shaw returns to duty at his precinct, having been sidelined with post-traumatic stress disorder after a shooting that killed his partner, Ray Jones. Burke, meanwhile, is being celebrated for the Freemont bust. Burke does not know that Freemont had hidden a backup of the evidence on a flash drive, found during the autopsy and logged by Taylor. Reading the report, Shaw takes the drive. Burke races to the station, sets off the fire alarm to empty the building of everyone but his own crooked officers, and imposes a total lockdown, cutting all communications.

Realising he is being hunted, Shaw ambushes Burke's accomplice Meeks and uses him as a shield, and Burke shoots Meeks. With only twelve bullets in his gun, Shaw must survive the ambushes and take out the corrupt officers by other means. He encounters Taylor who sees Meeks's blood on him and refuses to trust him, and he warns her to hide. Burke tells Matthews that Shaw killed Meeks. Burke then captures Taylor and threatens to kill her unless Shaw surrenders; Shaw gives himself up, but Burke kills her anyway. After a gunfight that nearly kills Burke, Shaw disables the cameras and tries to send the evidence to Internal Affairs, but Darrow cuts the network before it finishes. From the roof Shaw phones Matthews to expose Burke. Captured, he sees Burke destroy the drive, but in a blackout kills Darrow and escapes. Meeting Matthews behind the building, he learns that she too is in league with Burke, who then shoots her as the SWAT team storms in. Facing arrest, he plays a recording of Burke incriminating himself, and when Burke reaches for his gun, Shaw shoots him in the leg with his last bullet and handcuffs him.

The film was released in select cinemas and on demand in September 2015 by Lionsgate. What's on TV called it a nifty Die Hard-in-a-police-station idea wasted on a by-the-numbers film.

title: The Clan
tagline: The true story of Argentina's most notorious crime family
overview: In Argentina, between 1982 and 1985, the Puccios, a well-established family of San Isidro, an upper-class suburb of Buenos Aires, kidnap several people and hold them as hostages for a ransom.
plot:
The story is based on the case of the Puccio family from Buenos Aires, who kidnapped four people—three of whom they murdered—in the 1980s.
The Puccios appear to be a typical middle-class family from the affluent neighborhood of San Isidro, with aspirations of moving up into the upper class.The family comprises Arquímedes Puccio, the family patriarch; Epifanía Puccio, his wife; their three sons, Alejandro, Daniel "Maguila", and Guillermo; and their two daughters, Silvia and Adriana.
At the end of the Falklands War in 1982, Arquímedes, a former state intelligence operative, turns to kidnapping wealthy people for ransom to maintain his financial status. Alejandro assists him by identifying potential victims among his friends and acquaintances.
The first victim is Ricardo Manoukian, Alejandro's friend and teammate. In order to prevent Ricardo from identifying the kidnappers, Arquímedes still kills him, even though the kidnapping succeeds. Although Alejandro was greatly concerned about this murder, he still agreed to remain silent under his father's pressure.
After the first crime, Arquímedes and Alejandro kidnap Eduardo Aulet, another of Alejandro's friends. Eduardo is also murdered, with the Aulet family having paid the ransom.
After the return to democracy in Argentina, imprisoned military officer Aníbal Gordon advises Arquímedes that the military will struggle to protect him under the new government. But Arquímedes does not heed the warning.
Guillermo tells his older brother, Alejandro, at the airport that he already knew about the family’s crimes. This led to his decision to leave this country, and he also advised Alejandro to leave. Afterwards, Alejandro refuses to join the kidnapping plot to kidnap businessman Emilio Naum. This kidnapping fails, and Naum is killed. This caused a serious conflict between Alejandro and his father.
To reconcile with his father, Alejandro convinces Maguila to return to Argentina and join their operations. In 1985, the group kidnaps businesswoman Nélida Bollini de Prado and keeps her prisoner in their basement. With ransom dealings falling through and growing public attention around this case, Arquímedes is informed that he was no longer under military protection.
In August 1985, Arquímedes and Maguila are arrested when they collect the ransom. Subsequently, police raided the Puccio home, secured Bollini de Prado’s release and arrested most of family members. This case drew great media attention, and this family gained the name of the “Puccio Clan”.
The prosecuting offers Arquímedes a deal: if Arquímedes confesses to being the mastermind behind the kidnappings, his family will not be indicted as accomplices. He refuses and claimes that his actions complied with higher military orders.

title: XOXO
tagline: Eat. Sleep. Rave. Repeat.
overview: XOXO follows six strangers whose lives collide in one frenetic, dream-chasing, hopelessly romantic night.
plot:
XOXO is a 2016 American music drama film directed by Christopher Louie, a music video director who wrote the story, from a screenplay by Dylan Meyer. Produced for Netflix by Prettybird, with Joe Russell, Louie, Daniel Shafer and Max Leitman as producers and the DJ Pete Tong as producer and music supervisor, it stars Graham Phillips, Sarah Hyland, Brett DelBuono, Hayley Kiyoko, Colin Woodell, Chris D'Elia, Ryan Hansen and Ione Skye, with Ian Anthony Dale, Brianne Howey and Henry Zaga.

The film follows six strangers whose lives intersect during a single night at XOXO, a huge fictional electronic dance music festival in the desert. Ethan Shaw (Phillips), a young bedroom DJ whose track "All I Ever Wanted" has exploded on YouTube, is offered a make-or-break slot at the festival by way of his best friend and manager Tariq (DelBuono), but he has only hours to get there. Things go wrong at once: a festivalgoer passes Tariq a hallucinogen with a kiss and he disappears into a wild trip, Ethan's name is missing from the lists, and a cynical star DJ, Avilo (Hansen), tries to lure him into a dubious collaboration. Krystal (Hyland), a romantic raver, hopes to meet Jordan (Zaga), a date she found online, but crosses paths with Ethan instead. Shanni (Kiyoko) and Ray (Woodell), a couple facing a long-distance future because she is moving to New York, try to sneak into the sold-out event through a sewer tunnel. Neil (D'Elia), a former DJ who now drives a party bus that breaks down on the highway, must confront Avilo, the man he blames for ruining his career, while the festival's founder Anders (Dale) wanders through offering advice. By the climactic set, each problem is resolved and Ethan finally gets his chance.

In 2015 Netflix announced the casting and that it would produce and distribute the film. To give the EDM setting authenticity, scenes were shot at three real music festivals. XOXO premiered on Netflix on 26 August 2016 after a one-week run at the Laemmle Royal in Los Angeles. Reviews were mixed, with a 71% Rotten Tomatoes approval rating from a small sample. The Hollywood Reporter found it so silly it was almost charming, praising Damián Acevedo's neon cinematography and the soundtrack, and Consequence of Sound called it sweet but lacking any real perspective on EDM culture, while The Village Voice wrote that, though predictable, it rewards viewers willing to give in to its rhythms.

title: Mother's Day

overview: Intersecting stories with different moms collide on Mother's Day.
plot:
As Mother's Day nears, a group of seemingly-unconnected people in Atlanta come to terms with their relationships with their mothers.
Sandy is a divorced mother of two sons, Mikey and Peter, whose ex-husband, Henry, has recently married a younger woman, Tina. Still getting used to this, she meets Bradley, a former Marine, in the supermarket. Bradley's wife Dana, a Marine Lieutenant, died a year previously, leaving him with their two daughters, Vicky and Rachel.
Kristin, adopted from birth, has her own daughter, Katie, and mulls over marrying the father of her child, Zack. She considers her life incomplete and her friend Jesse encourages her to search for her birth mother. Jesse also happens to be Sandy's best friend.
Jesse is married and has a son, Tanner, with Russell, who is Indian. Her sister Gabi is married to her wife Max and has a son, Charlie. When their racist, homophobic parents, Earl and Florence, unexpectedly show up, they have to come to terms with who their daughters are and the partners they have chosen.
As she's in Atlanta promoting her latest book, Miranda, an accomplished author and television personality, gets a surprise visit from Kristin, who is her daughter who she was forced to give her up for adoption at birth, as she was very young. Their making up leads to Kristin asking Zach to marry her on air and marrying on the same day, so Miranda can participate.
Sandy, an interior designer, hopes to land a job designing the stage for Miranda’s new talk show, but numerous circumstances cause her to miss the design meeting. A frustrated Sandy causes a scene expressing all the reasons she was late in front of Miranda, who is left curious and asks to meet with Sandy. While Sandy tries to pitch her stage design, Miranda asks about Sandy’s personal life and her blunt and amusing answers impress Miranda enough to give her the designer job.
Jesse and Gabi's parents ambush them and their partners on their camper-van, and with Russell's mom's help through Skype, force him to make up with Jesse. Later on, the families including his mom, who flies in from Vegas, celebrate Mother's Day with a picnic in the park.
Sandy and Bradley meet again by chance in the hospital. She's there because of her younger son's asthma attack, he because of a mishap in the Mother's Day party he was throwing which ended with his going to the hospital for a broken leg. Helping her get unstuck from a vending machine, combined with his daughters' encouragement, Bradley finally starts to see her in a positive light.

title: Mission: Impossible - Fallout
tagline: Some missions are not a choice.
overview: When an IMF mission ends badly, the world is faced with dire consequences. As Ethan Hunt takes it upon himself to fulfill his original briefing, the CIA begin to question his loyalty and his motives. plot:
Mission: Impossible - Fallout is a 2018 action spy film directed by Christopher McQuarrie and produced by Paramount Pictures. The movie marks the sixth installment in the Mission: Impossible film series.

The story begins with Ethan Hunt (Tom Cruise) and his team, including Benji Dunn (Simon Pegg), Luther Stickell (Ving Rhames), and Ilsa Faust (Rebecca Ferguson), on a mission to neutralize a threat from the terrorist group, The Apostles. However, things take a turn when they discover that the Apostles are actually working for August Walker (Henry Cavill), an American CIA operative.

As Ethan delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a plot by August to sell nuclear materials to the highest bidder. Meanwhile, Ilsa is revealed to be working undercover as a double agent, feeding information to The Apostles while secretly working with Ethan's team.

The stakes escalate when Ethan and his team are ambushed by The Apostles in Paris, resulting in Luther being killed. The team then flees to Istanbul, where they discover that August has stolen the plutonium from the nuclear facility, intending to sell it to a terrorist organization.

Ethan and Ilsa embark on a perilous journey across Europe, following a trail of clues and encountering various obstacles along the way. They visit Morocco, Austria, and Norway, all while being pursued by The Apostles and August's henchmen.

As the story unfolds, Ethan and Ilsa grow closer, but their relationship is complicated by Ilsa's loyalty to her country and her allegiance to Ethan's team. Meanwhile, August's true intentions are revealed, and Ethan must confront him in a thrilling showdown.

The film's climax features an intense sequence of action-packed set pieces, including a HALO (high-altitude, low-opening) skydive jump by Ethan and Ilsa, as well as a high-speed car chase through the streets of Paris. The final confrontation between Ethan and August takes place at a nuclear facility in Norway, where Ethan must use his skills to disable the plutonium's delivery system.

In the end, Ethan successfully prevents the sale of the plutonium, but not before Ilsa is mortally wounded by one of August's henchmen. As Ethan holds her dying body, he realizes that their relationship has become a central part of his mission. The film concludes with Ethan and his team escaping, while Ilsa passes away in Ethan's arms.

Throughout the movie, Tom Cruise performs many of his own stunts, which adds to the film's sense of realism and authenticity. The action sequences are expertly choreographed, and the cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the beauty of various locations around the world.

Overall, Mission: Impossible - Fallout is a thrilling and entertaining spy thriller that delivers on its promise of high-octane action and suspenseful storytelling.

title: The Man Who Knew Infinity
tagline: What does it take to prove the impossible?
overview: Growing up poor in Madras, India, Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar earns admittance to Cambridge University during WWI, where he becomes a pioneer in mathematical theories with the guidance of his professor, G.H. Hardy.
plot:
The Man Who Knew Infinity is a 2016 biographical drama film that tells the story of Srinivasa Ramanujan, an Indian mathematician who made groundbreaking contributions to mathematics. 

At its core, The Man Who Knew Infinity explores themes of identity, belonging, and the struggle for recognition in a predominantly Western-dominated field. The film delves into Ramanujan's journey as he navigates his humble beginnings in India and finds himself drawn to the world of mathematics, which becomes an escape from the societal expectations placed upon him.

The movie also touches on the theme of mentorship and the complex relationships between teachers and students. Ramanujan's relationship with G.H. Hardy, a British mathematician who recognizes his talent, is particularly poignant as it highlights the tension between cultural differences and intellectual curiosity.

Furthermore, The Man Who Knew Infinity grapples with the idea of genius and its consequences. Ramanujan's extraordinary mathematical abilities are both celebrated and exploited by those around him, leading to a sense of disconnection and isolation that he struggles to overcome.

Ultimately, the film is a powerful exploration of what it means to be seen and understood in a world that often values conformity over individuality. Through Ramanujan's story, The Man Who Knew Infinity sheds light on the experiences of marginalized communities and the importance of embracing diversity in pursuit of knowledge and understanding.

title: The Con Is On
tagline: And it won't be their last
overview: In an effort to avoid paying off a massive gambling debt to a notorious mobster in England, a couple flees to Los Angeles and hatch a jewel theft plot.
plot:
The Con Is On, developed under the title The Brits Are Coming, is a 2018 heist comedy directed by James Oakley, who co-wrote it with Alex Michaelides. Uma Thurman and Tim Roth play a pair of British con artists, with Maggie Q, Sofía Vergara, Alice Eve, Parker Posey, Crispin Glover and Stephen Fry in supporting roles.

Harriet "Harry" Fox and her husband Peter are London grifters; Harry gambles, and Peter drinks and uses cocaine. After they lose a large sum connected to a botched deal, they owe money to Irina, a dangerous gangster, and they flee to Los Angeles to hide and plan their next move. There they meet Sidney, an old friend who is a corrupt priest with a sideline in shady jobs. He offers them work transporting a shipment of opium, but he also tips off Irina about the price on their heads. Peter learns that Irina's grudge is personal: she has feelings for Harry and despises him.

Hiding in a luxury Beverly Hills hotel, Peter runs into his ex-wife Jacky. She is now married to Gabriel, a film director who is cheating on her with both Gina, a relative of Jacky's, and Vivienne, a fiery actress demanding that he leave his wife. Jacky's blue gemstone ring, worth about £5 million, gives the Foxes an idea: they will steal it and use it to pay off Irina. They have a forger make a copy so they can swap the rings at a dinner party at Jacky and Gabriel's mansion, but a drunken Gabriel and Vivienne ruin the plan. When Irina tracks them to the hotel, the couple hide at the mansion, where Harry poses as a dog whisperer. Gabriel wins Best Director at an awards show and declares Vivienne his true love in his acceptance speech, which causes a furious fight at home. Jacky throws the ring away, and it lands in Harry's wine glass. After a shootout with Irina and her henchman, Harry wounds the gangster and hands her a ring; at the airport, Harry realizes the rings were mixed up. The couple board a flight to Brazil, penniless but free of their debt.

Casting took place in 2015. Although the story is set in Los Angeles, it was shot in Manhattan and Yonkers, New York. Lionsgate released the film in limited theaters and on video on demand on May 4, 2018. Reviews were poor, and none of the six critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes gave it a positive review. The Los Angeles Times enjoyed its stylish first half, its martini-dry dialogue and Thurman's comic turn but disliked the rest. RogerEbert.com gave it one and a half stars.

After opening it, the alien inmate is revealed to be a Martian named J'onn J'onnz who Lex plans to use against the League. He tells J'onn that the Legion are heroes and the League is evil.
Back at the Hall of Justice, Cyborg begins to question what he should do to be a better member. In the Hall of Justice, he notices J'onn disguised at Batman, creating a false mission alert about the Metropolis power station being in danger. When the League arrive at the power station, Cyborg sees that the station seems perfectly safe while the rest of the League can see the danger. This is because J'onn used his telepathy to make the fake mission alert look as real as possible as they evacuate Lois Lane and the workers alongside stopping other "problems" to the power plant. After the League launch the Nuketron reactor core into space, they immediately realize the only damage present is the damage they caused and the public turns against them for destroying the power station. The United Nations and General Sam Lane sentence the League to be banished into space.
This, however, turns out to be Lex's plan all along and the Legion then begin to divide which parts of the world they will control. This results in J'onn questioning the affiliation of the Legion. While disguised as Black Manta, he discovers that Lex plans to dispose of him once his usefulness expires. In space, Sinestro uses the Father Box to send the League to a black hole and Cyborg's robot assistant Cy-Bot is destroyed.
The real Cyborg is still in the Hall of Justice trying to find out why the League saw the power station in danger while he didn't. He soon finds the microchip J'onn used to hack the computer, but Sinestro finds and battles Cyborg. Just when it seems like Sinestro gained the upper hand, J'onn arrives and uses his telepathy to control him. J'onn explains how the Legion tricked him and how he tricked the League into turning themselves against the public and that his telepathy was ineffective on inorganic beings, explaining why it didn't work on Cyborg, whose brain was half-machine. J'onn sides with Cyborg and has Sinestro bring back the rest of the League.
As the Legion attacks the city, the League split up to battle them.

title: The Condemned 2
tagline: The world's deadliest game is back online
overview: A former bounty hunter who finds himself on the run as part of a revamped Condemned tournament, in which convicts are forced to fight each other to the death as part of a game that's broadcast to the public.
plot:
The Condemned 2, also released as The Condemned 2: Desert Prey, is a 2015 American action film directed by Roel Reiné and produced by WWE Studios. Professional wrestler Randy Orton stars as the bounty hunter Will Tanner, with Eric Roberts as his father Frank, Wes Studi, Steven Michael Quezada and Bill Stinchcomb. Written by Alan McElroy and shot in New Mexico, it is a standalone sequel to The Condemned (2007), which starred Steve Austin, and shares only its general theme of people forced into a deadly game for the entertainment of gamblers. Lionsgate released it in a handful of theaters and on video on demand on 6 November 2015.

Will Tanner leads a team of tough, skilled bounty hunters in the family business founded by his father. Their mission is to capture Cyrus Merrick, a criminal entrepreneur who runs illegal gambling on life-and-death contests. When the team finds him, he is presiding over a wager on which of two abducted homeless men will die first from poison. In the violent confrontation that follows, Merrick is killed rather than captured, and the authorities let Will go free only on condition that he leave bounty hunting for good, a decision that infuriates his father.

Will tries to start over, but Merrick's surviving right-hand man has other plans. He organizes a new high-stakes game in which Will himself becomes the prey: his former colleagues are blackmailed into trying to kill him, each attack captured by drones and broadcast to wealthy spectators placing bets in a secret casino. Hunted across the desert, Will must rely on his skills and instincts to survive while trying to understand who is behind the game. With the help of his father and an intelligence specialist, he fights his way toward the man running the operation, who eventually enters the game himself as another contestant in a final kill-or-be-killed showdown.

The film received negative reviews. Dennis Harvey of Variety called it a belated, barely related sequel generic enough to make the forgettable 2007 original look like an oasis of cinematic personality, criticizing its clichéd dialogue, unremarkable stunts and failure to make use of Orton's imposing physique, though he noted the scenery-chewing performances of Roberts and Quezada.

title: Pitch Perfect 3
tagline: Last Call Pitches
overview: After the highs of winning the world championships, the Bellas find themselves split apart and discovering there aren't job prospects for making music with your mouth. But when they get the chance to reunite for an overseas USO tour, this group of awesome nerds will come together to make some music, and some questionable decisions, one last time.
plot:
Pitch Perfect 3 is a musical comedy film directed by Elizabeth Banks and written by Kay Cannon. The movie takes place three years after the events of Pitch Perfect 2, with the Bellas facing an uncertain future.

The story begins with the Bellas struggling to find their place in the world without their iconic competition circuit. The group's leader, Aubrey Posen (Anna Camp), is trying to navigate her post-Bella life, while also dealing with the pressure of being a former champion. Meanwhile, Emily Junk (Hailee Steinfeld) and Chloe Beale (Brittany Snow) are trying to find their own musical identities.

The Bellas receive an offer from a wealthy investor, Jonathon Grouse (John Lithgow), who wants to use their music as a way to boost his failing business. The group reluctantly agrees to perform at the World Championship of A cappella in China, but things take a turn when they discover that the competition is being held on a US Navy ship.

As the Bellas prepare for the competition, they face various challenges, including Aubrey's struggles with leadership and Emily's desire to pursue a solo career. The group also meets a new rival, Evermoist (a cappella group from China), who are determined to take down the Bellas.

Throughout the movie, the Bellas undergo rigorous training to prepare for the competition, led by their new coach, Gail Abernathy-McKadden (Elizabeth Banks). The group also faces personal struggles, including Aubrey's relationship issues and Emily's feelings of inadequacy.

As the World Championship approaches, the Bellas face off against Evermoist in an epic battle of a cappella. The competition is fierce, but the Bellas ultimately come out on top, thanks to their hard work and dedication.

In the end, the Bellas are hailed as champions, and Aubrey finally finds her place in the world. Emily pursues her solo career, while Chloe finds love with a fellow musician. The movie ends on a high note, with the Bellas performing a final show-stopping number that showcases their talents.

Overall, Pitch Perfect 3 is a heartwarming and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, perseverance, and finding one's place in the world. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and catchy musical numbers, it's a must-see for fans of the Pitch Perfect franchise.

title: Pet
tagline: If You Love Something, Never Let It Go.
overview: A man bumps into an old crush and becomes obsessed. After several failed attempts at winning her over, he kidnaps her and holds her captive underneath the animal shelter where he works.
plot:
Pet is a 2016 psychological thriller film directed by Carles Torrens and written by Jeremy Slater, who had sold the script in 2007. It stars Dominic Monaghan as Seth, Ksenia Solo as Holly, Jennette McCurdy as Claire, Nathan Parsons as Eric and Da'Vone McDonald as Nate.

Seth, a painfully introverted man who works at an animal control center, becomes obsessed with Holly, a waitress and former high school classmate, after seeing her writing in a journal on a bus. Encouraged by Nate, a security guard at work, he studies her online profiles and asks her out, but she rejects him. When he follows her to the bar where her ex-boyfriend Eric works and refuses to accept her rejection, a scuffle breaks out, and Seth steals her journal, which he reads obsessively. In an abandoned wing of the shelter he finds a hidden room, builds a steel cage, then breaks into Holly's apartment and kidnaps her.

Seth tells the caged Holly that he loves her and has imprisoned her to "save" her. From the journal he has learned that Holly's friend Claire had an affair with Eric, and that Holly, in a rage, crashed their car into a truck and then stabbed the injured Claire with a shard of glass, a death blamed on the accident. Since then Holly has committed a series of gruesome murders and recorded them in her journal, and Seth has found a purpose in stopping her. The two engage in psychological games, with Seth insisting she kills out of guilt and Holly answering that she kills for pleasure. When the suspicious Nate discovers Holly, she distracts him so Seth can overpower him, and at her urging Seth kills Nate and disposes of the body. Holly then persuades Seth to prove his love by cutting off his finger, seizes his knife, threatens suicide unless he frees her, and slits his throat. Some time later, Holly is back with Eric and has published her journal entries as fiction through a vanity press. Discovering that Eric is cheating again, she spares him and instead visits a warehouse where Seth, still alive but horribly mutilated, is kept in a cage, thanking him for absorbing her murderous impulses.

Pet premiered at South by Southwest on March 11, 2016, and was released in nine US theaters on December 2, 2016, by Orion Pictures and Samuel Goldwyn Films, grossing just $8,004. Reviews were mixed, praising its subversive themes and lead performances but criticizing implausible twists; Rotten Tomatoes reported 56% approval and Metacritic a score of 48.

title: Our Times
tagline: Back to the youthful days!
overview: Office worker Truly Lin goes on a journey through her memories. 20 years ago, she had a crush on the most popular guy in school. Taiyu, a ruffian and a bully, is in love with the campus belle. Truly teams up with Taiyu to tear the golden couple apart and help each other to get the ones they love.
plot:
Our Times (Chinese: 我的少女時代) is a 2015 Taiwanese teen romantic comedy-drama and the feature directorial debut of Frankie Chen, who had previously worked in television drama. It stars Vivian Sung as the schoolgirl Lin Truly, Darren Wang as Hsu Tai-yu, the school's notorious gang leader, Dino Lee as Ouyang Fei-fan, the most popular boy in school, and Dewi Chien as Tao Min-min, with Joe Chen and Jerry Yan as the adult Truly and Tai-yu. Set largely in the 1990s, the film is a nostalgic look at first love and adolescence.

In the present day, Lin Truly is an overworked office employee whose sincerity makes her the target of ridicule from younger colleagues. Listening to an old cassette of a song by Andy Lau, she recalls her high school years, when she was an ordinary girl who idolized Lau and had a crush on Ouyang. When she naively passes on a threatening chain letter to several people, including the school bully Hsu Tai-yu, who is then hit by a car, Tai-yu discovers she sent it and forces her to become his errand girl.

After discovering that Ouyang is secretly dating Min-min, the school's most popular girl, on whom Tai-yu has a crush, Truly forms an alliance with Tai-yu to break the couple up. She learns that Tai-yu and Ouyang were once close friends and that a tragedy turned Tai-yu into a gangster, and she persuades him to become his old self again. As the two study together, defend each other against an unfair school administrator and lead a student protest, their friendship slowly turns into love, but misunderstandings and Tai-yu's health problems separate them before they can confess their feelings. Years later, a chance encounter with Andy Lau leads the adult Truly back to the boy who once promised her that Lau would sing for her.

The film gained wide popularity across Asia, and its theme song, "A Little Happiness" by Hebe Tien, became the first video by a Chinese-language singer to reach 100 million views on YouTube.

Our Times grossed about 84.4 million dollars worldwide, with mainland China its largest market, making it a major commercial success across Asia. Critical response was lukewarm: the South China Morning Post found it excessively saccharine, while the Taipei Times praised Sung's performance and the film's period detail.

title: Forsaken
tagline: Redemption.
overview: John Henry returns to his hometown in hopes of repairing his relationship with his estranged father, but a local gang is terrorizing the town. John Henry is the only one who can stop them, however he has abandoned both his gun and reputation as a fearless quick-draw killer.
plot:
Forsaken is a 2015 Canadian revisionist Western directed by Jon Cassar from a screenplay by Brad Mirman. It stars Kiefer Sutherland and his father Donald Sutherland, who share leading roles in a film for the first time, along with Brian Cox, Michael Wincott, Aaron Poole and Demi Moore. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2015 and was released in February 2016.

In 1872, John Henry Clayton, a former gunslinger haunted by his past, returns to his hometown in Wyoming after more than ten years of drifting since fighting in the American Civil War. He learns from his father, the stern Reverend Samuel Clayton, that his mother died years earlier. The two men are estranged: the reverend is ashamed of the violent reputation his son earned after the war, and John Henry has lost his faith because of the atrocities he witnessed. He has vowed never to use a gun again and tries to atone by helping his father work the family farm.

John Henry also reunites with his former sweetheart, Mary Alice, who married another man and has a son after he failed to return. Meanwhile the town is being terrorized by a gang working for the ruthless businessman James McCurdy, who is forcing local farmers to sell their land because the railroad is coming. McCurdy recognizes John Henry as a potential threat, and his gang includes the reckless Frank Tillman and "Gentleman" Dave Turner, an elegant gunfighter with his own code of honor who regards John Henry with wary respect. As McCurdy's men grow more violent toward the farmers and John Henry endures their humiliation without fighting back, he is pushed closer to breaking his vow, and the conflict with his father and the gang builds toward a reckoning.

The film received mixed reviews, with a 40 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 55. Several critics appreciated the scenes between the two Sutherlands and the film's classic, unhurried style, while others found the story familiar. Glenn Kenny of RogerEbert.com gave it three out of four stars, writing that it had a solid story and told it without waste.

title: Southbound
tagline: One way in, no way out.
overview: The film contains five stories set on desolate stretches of a desert highway. Two men on the run from their past, a band on its way to a gig, a man struggling to get home, a brother in search of his long-lost sister and a family on vacation are forced to confront their worst fears and darkest secrets in these interwoven tales.
plot:
Southbound is a 2015 American horror anthology made by the directing collective Radio Silence with Roxanne Benjamin, David Bruckner and Patrick Horvath, whose five linked stories unfold along a lonely desert highway watched over by mysterious floating creatures. The cast includes Fabianne Therese, Larry Fessenden, Kate Beahan, Zoe Cooper and Gerald Downey.

In "The Way Out", two men, Mitch and Jack, flee the creatures but keep returning to the same gas station; Jack is killed, and Mitch, convinced he deserves his fate, enters a motel room that becomes his own home, where an apparition of his daughter, Katherine, forever slips away from him. In "Siren", Sadie, Ava and Kim, members of a touring band, break down in the desert and accept a ride from an eccentric couple, whose dinner, prayers and strange medicine draw Sadie's friends into a cult ritual; still haunted by the death of a former bandmate, Sadie escapes and runs into the road, where she is struck by a car.

In "The Accident", the driver, Lucas, distracted by a phone call, calls 911 but cannot say where he is. Voices on the line guide him to an abandoned hospital and talk him through gruesome surgery that kills Sadie, then mock him before letting him leave with clean clothes and a new car. In "Jailbreak", Danny storms a bar called The Trap with a shotgun, searching for his sister, Jesse; its regulars are demons, and he forces the bartender to lead him to Jesse, who is working as a tattoo artist and insists she stays by choice. Danny drags her away into the desert, where she admits that she killed their parents, abandons him to the demons and drives off. In "The Way In", a family spends a last weekend together before their daughter, Jem, leaves for college, when three masked men break in. They kill the mother after revealing a secret about the father, Daryl, and then Daryl himself, showing him a photograph of Katherine; unmasked, they are Mitch and Jack. Jem fights back but is killed, and as the ground opens and the creatures rise, Mitch and Jack escape onto the highway, closing the loop.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 16, 2015, and The Orchard released it in U.S. theaters on February 5, 2016. It drew 81% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 58.

title: Guardians
tagline: Squad of Soviet Superheroes
overview: During the Cold War, an organization called "Patriot" created a super-hero squad, which includes members of multiple soviet republics. For years, the heroes had to hide their identities, but in hard times they must show themselves again.
plot:
Guardians (Russian: Zashchitniki) is a 2017 Russian superhero film directed by Sarik Andreasyan. Anton Pampushnyy, Sanzhar Madiyev, Sebastien Sisak and Alina Lanina play a team of Soviet superheroes, with Valeriya Shkirando as Major Elena Larina and Stanislav Shirin as the villain Kuratov. The team was created during the Cold War and includes representatives of different nationalities of the Soviet Union, each with special abilities linked to the elements. The film was released in Russia in February 2017.

During the Cold War, a secret organisation called Patriot genetically modifies selected individuals to create superhumans capable of defending the Soviet Union. The resulting team consists of Arsus, who can transform into a powerful bear-man; Khan, who moves at superhuman speed and fights with twin curved blades; Ler, who can control earth and stone; and Xenia, who can become invisible when in contact with water. The project succeeds where a rival programme fails, prompting the rival scientist, Professor August Kuratov, to flee and continue his experiments in secret. When soldiers attempt to arrest him, Kuratov destroys the Patriot laboratory in an explosion and is drenched in chemicals, which he survives by rebuilding his body as a cyborg able to generate electricity and control machines. He also creates an army of clones.

After the explosion, the four heroes go into hiding for decades. In the present day, a group of combat robots taking part in a military exercise suddenly turns on its operators and kills them. The Ministry of Defence revives Patriot under Major Larina, who tracks down the surviving heroes and persuades them to reunite. Kuratov, now determined to prove his genius to the world, seizes control of military technology and launches an attack on Moscow, and the Guardians must learn to work together again and rediscover their powers in order to stop him.

The film was conceived as a Russian answer to American superhero franchises, presenting a multinational team drawn from the former Soviet republics, and it relies heavily on computer-generated effects.

Guardians received overwhelmingly negative reviews and was widely panned in Russian media for its script, effects and acting, with only about 27 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It debuted at the top of the Russian box office, but its takings fell quickly and it is regarded as a box-office bomb, with some publications listing it among the worst films ever made.

title: The Promise
tagline: Empires fall. Love survives.
overview: Set during the last days of the Ottoman Empire, a love triangle develops between Mikael, a brilliant medical student, the beautiful and sophisticated artist Ana, and Chris, a renowned American journalist based in Paris.
plot:
The Promise is a 2016 American epic historical war drama film directed by Terry George, who co-wrote the screenplay with Robin Swicord. Set in the final years of the Ottoman Empire, it stars Oscar Isaac, Charlotte Le Bon and Christian Bale in a love triangle that unfolds immediately before and during the Armenian genocide, with Shohreh Aghdashloo, Angela Sarafyan, Marwan Kenzari and Jean Reno. Its budget was donated by the Armenian-American businessman Kirk Kerkorian.

Mikael Boghosian, an apothecary in the Armenian village of Siroun in southern Anatolia, becomes engaged to Maral, the daughter of a wealthy neighbor, and uses her dowry to pay for medical school in Constantinople. There he befriends Emre, the son of a senior Ottoman official, and meets Ana Khesarian, a Paris-raised Armenian involved with Chris Myers, an American reporter for the Associated Press. Mikael falls in love with Ana as the First World War begins.

Emre helps Mikael obtain a student exemption from military service, but when Mikael tries to save his uncle during the mass arrests of Armenians in April 1915, he is seized and sent to a forced-labor camp, while Emre is punished with conscription. Mikael escapes and returns home to find the Armenian community under attack. At his family's urging he marries Maral and hides with her in the mountains, where she becomes pregnant. Seeking help, he finds Ana and Chris at a nearby Red Cross mission, but on their way back to Siroun, they discover that the villagers, including Mikael's wife, have been massacred.

Chris is arrested as a spy and sentenced to death, but is freed through Emre's help and the intervention of the American ambassador, Henry Morgenthau; Emre is executed for aiding him. Mikael, Ana and a group of orphans join thousands of Armenians who make a stand against the Ottoman army on Musa Dagh, until a French warship evacuates them. As the refugees row to the ship, Ana is thrown into the water by an artillery barrage and drowns, while Mikael saves his young cousin Yeva. Years later in Watertown, Massachusetts, Mikael, who adopted Yeva, gives a toast at her wedding before the orphans, now grown.

The Promise premiered at the 2016 Toronto International Film Festival and was released in the United States on April 21, 2017, near the anniversary of the genocide. It received mixed reviews, with critics feeling the love triangle overshadowed the history. It grossed only about $12 million against a $90 million budget.

title: Coco
tagline: The celebration of a lifetime
overview: Despite his family’s baffling generations-old ban on music, Miguel dreams of becoming an accomplished musician like his idol, Ernesto de la Cruz. Desperate to prove his talent, Miguel finds himself in the stunning and colorful Land of the Dead following a mysterious chain of events. plot:
Coco is a beautifully crafted animated film that pays homage to Mexican culture, traditions, and history. The movie follows the story of Miguel Rivera, a young boy who dreams of becoming a musician like his idol, Ernesto de la Cruz.

Miguel lives with his family in a small town in Mexico, where music is an integral part of their daily lives. However, Miguel's family has a long-standing ban on music due to a past tragedy that led to the death of his great-great-grandfather, Papá. According to legend, Papá was a famous musician who abandoned his family and left them with nothing.

On the Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos), Miguel decides to sneak out of the house to fulfill his dream of becoming a musician. He steals his family's most prized possession, a magical guitar that supposedly belonged to Ernesto de la Cruz, and sets off on an adventure to find him.

As Miguel travels through the Land of the Dead, he meets various characters who are trapped between worlds, including his deceased relatives and a charming trickster named Héctor. Together, they embark on a journey to uncover the truth about Papá's past and the reason behind the family's ban on music.

Throughout their adventure, Miguel learns valuable lessons about the importance of family, tradition, and following one's dreams. He also discovers that his great-great-grandfather was not the musician he thought he was, but rather a complex individual who made sacrifices for his family.

As the story unfolds, Miguel must confront his own identity and the expectations placed upon him by his family. In the end, he finds a way to honor his ancestors while still pursuing his passion for music.

Coco is a heartwarming film that celebrates Mexican culture and traditions, while also exploring universal themes of identity, family, and the power of music. The animation is stunning, with vibrant colors and intricate details that bring the Land of the Dead to life. The characters are well-developed and relatable, making it easy for audiences of all ages to become invested in their stories.

Overall, Coco is a beautifully crafted film that will leave you smiling, laughing, and maybe even shedding a tear or two. It's a must-see for anyone who loves animation, music, or just great storytelling in general.

title: Bad Cat
tagline: Stop behaving like a human!
overview: A foul-mouthed cat and its gang cross paths with humans.
plot:
Shero is a crass and short-tempered tabby cat, owned by a man named Tank. He sends his associates, Rifki the seagull and Riza the rat to obtain liquor for a barbecue that night. Another cat, Blackie, informs Shero about an attractive Siamese cat named Princess in a nearby apartment. When Princess's cartoonist owner leaves for work, Shero and Blackie sneak into the apartment to seduce her. Princess panics, triggering a series of accidents that lead to her death. The cartoonist returns home, finds Princess dead, and furiously attacks Shero and Blackie. Blackie is killed while Shero fights the cartoonist, and they both tumble out the window, resulting in the cartoonist's death. On his way back home, Shero meets a kitten named Taco, who claims to be Shero's illegitimate son. Shero rejects Taco and goes to steal fish from Hazel, Tank's landlady. She threatens Tank with eviction unless he can cover months of unpaid rent by the next day. Enraged, Tank ejects Shero from his home and blocks every possible entrance. While smoking and sulking, Shero witnesses a beautiful Angora cat named Misscat being harassed by a pair of dogs and rescues her by beating her assailants. Shero attempts to seduce Misscat but is turned down and told to meet her again on the same rooftop that night. Meanwhile, the brainless cadaver of the cartoonist is revived by an ambulance defibrillator. The cartoonist hijacks the ambulance and begins hunting for Shero.
Shero gets a bouquet for Misscat. Meanwhile, the cartoonist finds the two dogs and forces them to lead him to Shero. Taco witnesses this transaction and follows them. Shero and Misscat meet to prepare to make love, but they are captured and tied up by the dogs and the cartoonist. Before the cartoonist can electrocute Shero, Taco appears and frees Shero, who fights the cartoonist and throws him off the building and into a dumpster, along with the dogs. Shero brushes Taco off again, and Taco reveals that his mother, Mimosa, who was Shero's past mate, is dead. Shero and Taco bond after a brief exchange of fists. Taco helps Shero attempt to obtain liquor from the local grocer. However, the cartoonist, after hijacking a garbage truck, kidnaps Taco during the mission, forcing Shero to chase him. Shero rescues Taco as the garbage truck plunges into the sea, and he once more kills the cartoonist in an underwater fight. As Shero and Taco return home, Hazel chases off Misscat and installs barbed wire to further prevent Shero's entry. The cartoonist's body is lifted from the sea by a rescue team and revived once more with power wires.
After Rifki and Riza's latest attempt to retrieve liquor fails, Riza proposes to Shero that they can all get what they want by robbing a bank. The cartoonist is apprehended by the police, but he hijacks a police car when the bank robbery is reported. As Shero and the group make their getaway, Taco takes a bullet for Shero from the cartoonist.

title: Barbie in Rock 'N Royals
tagline: Raise Your Voice!
overview: When royal Princess Courtney trades places with famous rock star Erika, two worlds collide while both learn to appreciate new friends and experiences.
plot:
Barbie in Rock 'N Royals is a 2015 American-Canadian computer-animated musical film and the 30th entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Karen J. Lloyd from a screenplay by Marsha Griffin, it was produced by Mattel Playground Productions with animation by Rainmaker Entertainment and music by Gabriel Mann and Rebecca Kneubuhl, and was released direct to video by Universal in the United States on 8 September 2015. Running 84 minutes, it was the last Barbie film in which Barbie plays a character with a different name, and, like Barbie: The Princess and the Popstar, it turns on a princess and a pop star trading places.

Barbie stars as Princess Courtney, a modern royal heading to an island summer camp for the first time. On the island are two rival camps: Camp Royalty, for young princes and princesses, and Camp Pop, for aspiring musicians. A registration mix-up swaps Courtney's name with that of Erika Juno (Chiara Zanni), a famous rock star who has cancelled her tour hoping to make real friends at Camp Pop, so the princess lands among the musicians and the singer among the royals. The camp heads, the stern Lady Anne (Nicole Oliver) of Camp Royalty and Finn Oxford (Michael Dobson) of Camp Pop, share an old rivalry. When Lady Anne hears Erika sing, she fakes a computer failure to block the swap and challenges Finn to a sing-off, with the losing camp to close for good and surrender its land to the winner.

While the two girls learn to fit into unfamiliar worlds and make unexpected friends, Erika overhears Lady Anne's assistant, Clive, revealing the stakes and admitting he has bribed one of the judges, Svetlana Petranova of Camp Arabesque. The other judges are rock legend Allegra James and Prince Reginald of Thistlebrook. Learning that one camp will be lost, the campers of both sides decide to perform together rather than compete. Allegra and the prince abstain, and Svetlana names Camp Royalty the winner, but Finn and Lady Anne overrule the result, agreeing that rock and royalty can mix, and plan to merge the camps the next summer, while Courtney and Erika form a band with their friends called Rock 'N Royals.

Kelly Sheridan voices Courtney and Svetlana, with Bethany Brown, Alessandro Juliani and Kira Tozer among the cast. The songs include "What If I Shine" and the end-credits single "Raise Our Voices". The film's British launch was accompanied by a singing competition promoted with the girl group Little Mix and Nickelodeon.

title: Devil's Gate
tagline: Every family has its secrets.
overview: Set in the small town of Devil's Gate, North Dakota, the film examines the disappearance of a local woman and her young son. Schull plays an FBI agent who helps the local sheriff search for answers. Partnering with a deputy , they track down the missing woman's husband and find that nothing is as it seems.
plot:
Devil's Gate is a 2017 American supernatural horror and science fiction film directed by Clay Staub in his feature debut, from a screenplay he wrote with Peter Aperlo. Amanda Schull stars as FBI Special Agent Daria Francis, with Shawn Ashmore as Deputy Colt Salter, Milo Ventimiglia as the farmer Jackson Pritchard, Bridget Regan as his wife Maria, Jonathan Frakes as Sheriff Gruenwell, and Javier Botet. In some territories it was released as Abduction.

In the small farming town of Devil's Gate, North Dakota, Daria arrives to investigate the disappearance of Maria Pritchard and her young son Jonah. The sheriff wants her to leave Jackson, the boy's ill-tempered and devout father, alone, but she enlists the friendly Colt, and after Maria's sister and mother describe Jackson's worsening temper and Jonah's sketchbook turns up full of disturbing drawings, the pair drive out to the remote Pritchard farm. They find it newly booby-trapped, with a stranded motorist's car outside and Maria's car hidden in the barn. After a standoff, Daria handcuffs Jackson, then discovers what he is keeping in his cellar: a strange humanoid creature locked in a cage. Jackson insists it is a demon like those that took his family, and that he means to trade it for them.

Their phones and car die, and an unnatural lightning storm forces them back into the house. Maria reappears and accuses Jackson of giving Jonah to the beings, whom he had prayed to as angels when the boy fell ill. Daria comes to realize that the visitors are aliens who are colonizing Earth because their own world is dying, replacing people with copies, and that Jackson himself has been replaced. Jonah is the first naturally born human-alien hybrid. One of the beings kills Colt, and when Jonah is returned in a flash of light, Jackson prepares to shoot him, only for Maria to kill Jackson first. The authorities insist on a story that leaves out the aliens, and some time later Jonah shows his mother a hidden collection of the discs used to summon the beings, telling her that it is time for the harvest.

The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on 24 April 2017 and was released by IFC Midnight in January 2018. Reviews were mostly negative, with a 38% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Critics noted competent effects and photography, and The Village Voice called Staub a formidable director of action, but most found the dialogue weak and the story derivative.

title: Siren
tagline: No Man Can Resist Her. All Men Should.
overview: A bachelor party becomes a savage fight for survival when the groomsmen unwittingly unleash a fabled predator upon the festivities.
plot:
Siren (stylized as SiREN) is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by Gregg Bishop and written by Ben Collins and Luke Piotrowski. The first spin-off of the V/H/S anthology franchise, it is a feature-length expansion of "Amateur Night," David Bruckner's segment from V/H/S (2012), with Hannah Fierman reprising her role as the creature Lily. Chase Williamson stars as Jonah, with Justin Welborn, Michael Aaron Milligan and Hayes Mercure. Unlike its predecessor, the film is told in a conventional narrative style rather than as found footage. It received a limited theatrical release on 2 December 2016.

The film opens years in the past, as a mystic and a sheriff investigate a séance in a church that has ended in the deaths of everyone present. The creature summoned during the ritual, which takes the form of a young girl, kills the sheriff, and the mystic places a shackle around her ankle to control her.

In the present, Jonah is about to get married, and his brother Mac and friends Rand and Elliot take him out for his bachelor party. Disappointed by a seedy strip club, they are approached by a stranger who leads them to a secret underground club in the countryside. Its owner, the charismatic Mr. Nyx, turns out to be the mystic from the prologue. When Jonah asks for an experience that will not compromise his loyalty to his fiancée, Nyx sends him to a private room where a captive young woman, Lily, sings to him from behind glass. Her song puts him into a trance in which he relives every sexual experience of his life. Believing she is a trafficking victim, Jonah and his friends help her escape, only to discover that she is the monstrous creature from the opening scene. Lily, who has formed a dangerous fixation on Jonah, follows him through the night, killing anyone who stands in her way, while Nyx and his men pursue the group to reclaim his prized possession.

Siren received mixed reviews, with a 65 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 54. Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times called it, for the most part, a clever and confident expansion of a terrific short that stings less but still packs plenty of poison, while other critics found it less effective than Bruckner's original segment.

title: The Star
tagline: It takes many tails to tell the greatest story ever.
overview: A small but brave donkey and his animal friends become the unsung heroes of the greatest story ever told, the first Christmas.
plot:
The Star, also known as The Star: The Story of the First Christmas, is a 2017 American animated comedy retelling the Nativity of Jesus from the perspective of the animals, directed by Timothy Reckart and written by Carlos Kotkin from a story by Kotkin and Simon Moore. It features the voices of Steven Yeun, Gina Rodriguez, Zachary Levi, Keegan-Michael Key, Aidy Bryant, Kelly Clarkson, Kristin Chenoweth, Tracy Morgan, Tyler Perry and Oprah Winfrey. It was produced by Sony Pictures Animation and released by Sony Pictures Releasing on November 17, 2017.

In Nazareth, Mary is visited by an angel who tells her she will bear the Messiah, as a new star begins to glow in the sky. Six months later, a young donkey tired of turning a mill wheel dreams of joining a royal caravan and feeling important. Helped by an older donkey, he escapes from his owner, a miller, and, injured, takes refuge at the home of the newlywed Mary and Joseph. Mary names him Boaz, or Bo, and nurses him, while Joseph comes to accept her pregnancy after a vision of his own. Bo and his friend Dave, a wisecracking dove, plan to slip away, but Mary's kindness keeps them there for months.

Meanwhile, the three wise men arrive at the palace of King Herod with their talkative camels, Felix, Cyrus and Deborah. On learning that their gifts are for a newborn king, Herod sends a brutal hunter and his two fearsome dogs, Thaddeus and Rufus, to find and kill the child. When Mary and Joseph set out for Bethlehem for the census, Bo realizes that they are in danger and sets out with Dave to warn them, joined by Ruth, a cheerful sheep who left her flock to follow the star. After a chaotic marketplace chase, Joseph, unaware of the threat, sends Bo away. Bo finds the royal caravan but realizes Mary matters more and returns.

In Bethlehem, where there is no room at the inn, the miller recaptures Bo and ties him in a stable, where the star's light has been shining onto the manger for months. Realizing that this is where the baby is meant to be born, they help Bo escape. He brings Mary and Joseph to the stable, while his friends rally the camels and Ruth's flock to defeat the hunter, who falls to his death. Jesus is born, the shepherds and wise men arrive, and Joseph buys Bo from the miller.

The Star grossed about $63 million worldwide against a $20 million budget. Reviews were mixed, though audiences gave it an "A" CinemaScore. Mariah Carey's song "The Star" was nominated for a Golden Globe for Best Original Song.

title: Why Him?
tagline: Of all the guys his daughter could have chosen...
overview: A dad forms a bitter rivalry with his daughter's young rich boyfriend.
plot:
Stanford student Stephanie Fleming invites her partner Laird Mayhew over to "Netflix and chill". Meanwhile, back home in Grand Rapids, Stephanie's dad Ned is celebrating his 55th birthday with friends and family at an Applebee's. During a slideshow presentation in his honor, Stephanie drops in via webcam to congratulate him, when suddenly Laird walks in on her and flashes the camera.
After picking them up at the airport, Stephanie drives her family – parents Ned and Barb and younger brother Scotty – to Laird's Silicon Valley villa to meet him. She explains to Ned that Laird is the CEO of a video game company, which has made him extremely wealthy. Laird gives the family a tour of his house, complete with curse words and inappropriate comments about Barb. He then reveals a large tattoo of the Flemings' Christmas card on his back, complete with "Happy Holidays" written underneath. In the living room is a tank with a moose filled completely with its urine. The basement has a bowling alley that Laird built with a mural of Ned, posed in a "crotch-chop" position.
Ned talks to Stephanie about Laird's behavior and she asks him to give him a chance. Later, as Laird goes with Ned for a walk in the woods outside his house, he asks Ned for his blessing to propose to Stephanie. Ned is quick to say no, which completely blindsides Laird, who had been confident that Ned would say yes. Laird promises to win him over.
As the family gathers in Laird's living room for Christmas Eve, Laird reveals that he bought Ned's struggling printing company as a gift to remove all his debts. Instead of expressing gratitude, Ned punches Laird in the face and they begin to fight, which culminates in Laird falling into the moose tank, which subsequently breaks and leaves Scotty briefly trapped under the moose. Stephanie and Barb are both angry at their partner's behaviors, and the Flemings leave Laird's home.
On Christmas Day, the Flemings are celebrating without Stephanie. They are surprised when Laird's helicopter arrives with Stephanie. She is still mad at both Ned and Laird for their behavior and refuses to talk to either of them. Ned and Laird talk and Laird gets Ned's blessing to propose to Stephanie. However, she declines the proposal saying she is not ready to get married, but she wants them to continue dating.
Later during the party, Ned and Scotty approach Laird with a new business idea, since they are all part of the same company now. Scotty suggests they sell the same toilets Laird has in his home since they would be very profitable. Laird likes the idea and agrees. The couples then dance together as music plays, with Ned referring to Laird as "son".
Scotty, Ned, and Laird eventually turn the printing company into a toilet factory and become profitable. Stephanie uses the Fleming-Mayhew conglomerate to help underdeveloped countries with their sewage projects. Finally, Laird has what he always wanted, to be part of a family.

title: Lumberjack Man
tagline: Welcome to Summer Camp.
overview: As the staff of Good Friends Church Camp prepares for a spring break filled with "Fun Under the Son", a demon logger rises from his sap boiler to wreak his vengeance and feast on flapjacks soaked in the blood of his victims.
plot:
Lumberjack Man is a 2015 American comedy slasher film written and directed by Josh Bear. Michael Madsen stars as Dr. Peter Shirtcliff, with Ciara Flynn, Jarrett King, Brina Palencia and Alex Dobrenko among the cast. The film was part of After Dark Films' 2015 "8 Films to Die For" lineup, a series of low-budget genre releases.

Teenagers and staff arrive for their annual retreat at the Good Friends Church Camp, unaware that a monstrous threat has awakened nearby. In an abandoned log cabin close to the campgrounds, an undead lumberjack rises from the grave. Armed with axes, a saw and a rolling griddle loaded with giant flapjacks, he begins stalking the campers, killing them and using their blood as syrup for his pancakes. Shirtcliff, an eccentric expert, tries to warn the head park ranger, LuAnn Potts, of the danger, but she dismisses his story as absurd, especially when he links it to the history of an award-winning instant pancake brand created by a man named J.T. Jeppson. As Shirtcliff heads to the camp to save the young people, LuAnn begins examining old newspaper clippings and police reports and starts to believe something is wrong. The killer attacks her, but retreats when she throws syrup at him.

At the camp, the campers and counselors are killed one by one around the mess hall until only a few remain, including Faith, Reggie and the cook, while a cowardly counselor who abandons the others meets a gruesome end. Shirtcliff arrives and reveals the true story behind the creature and the Jeppson pancake fortune. In 1892, Jeppson, while hunting in the woods, was lured by a delicious aroma to the cabin of Nehemiah Easterday, a reclusive man who each year, on the day before Lent, cooked his family's secret pancake recipe. The secret of what happened between the two men explains the origin of the Lumberjack Man and his murderous appetite, and the survivors must find a way to stop him.

The film received generally poor reviews. Ari Drew of Dread Central gave it three stars, finding it fun but lacking in writing and technical polish, while a writer for Slasher.Club called it a nonsensical, ultimately bad film whose occasional charm was undone by terrible characters. Its gleefully silly premise nonetheless gave it some appeal among fans of comedic horror.

title: Digimon Adventure tri. Part 1: Reunion
original_title: デジモンアドベンチャー tri. 第１章「再会」
overview: After years of inactivity, the DigiDestined regroup with their Digimon to save their world, but have the years changed their characters too much?
plot:
Digimon Adventure tri. Part 1: Reunion (Japanese: Saikai) is a 2015 Japanese animated adventure film produced by Toei Animation, the first of six films in the Digimon Adventure tri. series created to celebrate the fifteenth anniversary of the Digimon franchise. Directed by Keitaro Motonaga from a screenplay by Yūko Kakihara, with character designs by Atsuya Uki, it serves as a direct sequel to the television series Digimon Adventure and Digimon Adventure 02 and follows the original eight DigiDestined during their high school years. The project was announced in 2014 as a television series and was reconceived in May 2015 as a theatrical film series.

Set in 2005, six years after the first adventure, the film finds Tai Kamiya restless and without direction: his friends have drifted apart, he cannot gather them for one of his soccer games, and he has no plans for the future. When a Kuwagamon tears through Odaiba, Tai races to the scene, and Agumon arrives to digivolve and fight back as the battle spreads to the airport. Watching the destruction and the injured bystanders, Tai is shaken by the realization that the DigiDestined's battles cause real harm. A new connection to the Digital World is letting through infected Digimon more powerful than before, and the children of the second series appear to have been overwhelmed. Supported by a government task force aided by Gennai, the group reunites, including Mimi, who returns from America, but Tai clashes with Matt, who insists that only they can protect people. When the Royal Knight Alphamon attacks, apparently hunting a mysterious new DigiDestined named Meiko Mochizuki and her partner Meicoomon, Matt pulls Tai out of his paralysis and their partners combine into Omnimon, yet Tai hesitates at the decisive moment and Alphamon escapes, while the enigmatic Hackmon watches from the shadows.

Reunion opened in Japanese theaters on 21 November 2015 in a limited release, and was simulcast outside Japan by Crunchyroll in episodic form on the same day. It grossed about ¥230 million in Japan. An English dub distributed by Eleven Arts premiered at a Fathom Events screening in North America on 15 September 2016. Den of Geek's Shamus Kelley called it a model for how continuations of famous franchises should be made, praising its faithful characters and Tai's arc about responsibility, though he wished the female characters had more to do.

title: Harmony
tagline: This is the way the world ends...
overview: Set in a future world. Japan has created a great medical technology that controls ethics, health, and social interaction to create a perfect world. Three young girls attempt to stand up to this by committing suicide, but it doesn't work. Years later, Tuan, one of the girls who attempted suicide must prevent a crisis that threatens this "perfect" world.
plot:
Harmony is a 2015 Japanese animated science fiction film directed by Michael Arias and Takashi Nakamura and produced by Studio 4°C, with a screenplay by Kōji Yamamoto. It is based on the novel of the same name by Project Itoh and was the second of three anime features adapted from his novels, following The Empire of Corpses and preceding Genocidal Organ. Miyuki Sawashiro voices the protagonist, Tuan Kirie, and Reina Ueda voices her friend Miach Mihie.

In the future, after a nuclear cataclysm called the Maelstrom and the civil wars that followed nearly wiped out humanity, a seeming utopia has been established. Across national borders, society is overseen by the Admedistration, and citizens' bodies are monitored by WatchMe medical nanotechnology, all devoted to preventing disease and extending life. Crime and illness have largely vanished, and people live under a powerful ethic of welfare and mutual consideration. As teenagers in Japan, Tuan, Miach and their friend Cian Reikado reject this order, which they feel smothers them with kindness and denies any real autonomy, and attempt suicide together, committing the crime of rejecting life itself. Miach, the fiercest critic of the system, apparently dies, while Tuan and Cian are saved at the last moment.

Thirteen years later, Tuan works as a senior inspector for the World Health Organization, investigating illegal gene therapy around the world while still holding on to her old ideals and taking pleasure in mistreating her own body. When she meets Cian again and they recall their pact and the loss of Miach, a wave of murders and suicides suddenly breaks out, apparently driven through the very networks meant to protect people. Tuan's investigation leads her to follow the clues left by her old friend, and she must uncover the truth behind the supposedly perfect world and the meaning of the word harmony, then decide what kind of world she wants to create.

The film was released in Japan on November 13, 2015, taking over the date originally set for Genocidal Organ, which had been delayed. Funimation licensed it and gave it a two-day theatrical engagement in the United States on May 17 and 18, 2016. A four-volume manga adaptation by Fumi Minato ran in Newtype from 2015 to 2019. Critics praised its contemplative passages and minimalist sound design but faulted the stilted, monologue-heavy script and plain visuals; Anime News Network's Nick Creamer called it talk-heavy and visually uninspired.

title: Even Lambs Have Teeth
tagline: Revenge can be a bitch.
overview: Two young women terrorized by a group of small town psychos seek revenge on their tormentors.
plot:
Even Lambs Have Teeth is a Canadian-French rape-and-revenge thriller of 2015 written and directed by Terry Miles. It stars Kirsten Prout as Sloan and Tiera Skovbye as Katie, two young women who strike back at the trafficking ring that abducted them, with Garrett Black, Jameson Parker, Darren Mann, Michael Karl Richards, Patrick Gilmore as Boris and Craig March as the local sheriff.

Fresh out of college, Katie and Sloan plan to spend a month working on a rural organic farm before a trip to New York City. Katie's uncle, an FBI agent, sees them off at the bus station and asks for a coded text message each day to prove they are safe. While they wait, two charming young men, Lucas and Jed, offer them a lift to the farm; Sloan talks a reluctant Katie into accepting. Instead the boys detour to Jed's family home, where their mother serves the girls drugged food. They wake in their underwear, chained inside storage containers in the woods, prisoners of a sex-exploitation ring run by Boris, and are assaulted by the sheriff and other local men. Boris uses Katie's phone to send a reassuring message, unaware that the code must change daily.

Sensing that something is wrong, the uncle drives to the town. The sheriff tries to calm him and then warns Boris, who orders Jed to get rid of the girls. A restaurant worker, however, remembers seeing them leave in a blue truck, and the uncle traces it to Boris. Meanwhile Katie kills one of their abusers by biting into his throat, takes his keys and frees Sloan, and the pair escape in the sheriff's own patrol car. After arming themselves at a hardware store, they ambush Boris at home, force him to name his accomplices and kill him, then hunt down the rest of the ring one by one in increasingly inventive ways. Later, as the friends finally leave for New York, the uncle assures Katie's mother that they will be fine, while at the airport a stranger with an organic-farm sign greets a new pair of young travellers.

The film premiered at the Mile High Horror Film Festival in October 2015 and was later released on DVD and on demand. Bloody Disgusting's Patrick Cooper praised its balance of human horror, dark comedy and violent revenge.

title: Marauders
tagline: The rich will pay
overview: An untraceable group of elite bank robbers is chased by a suicidal FBI agent who uncovers a deeper purpose behind the robbery-homicides.
plot:
Marauders is a 2016 American crime thriller directed by Steven C. Miller and written by Michael Cody and Chris Sivertson. Christopher Meloni stars as an FBI agent investigating a string of violent bank robberies that appear aimed squarely at a ruthless banking executive played by Bruce Willis, with Dave Bautista and Adrian Grenier co-starring.

In Cincinnati, four masked men take $3 million from a branch of Hubert National Bank, and their leader executes the manager, Steven Hutchinson. FBI Special Agent Jonathan Montgomery leads a joint investigation with the city police, and a fingerprint at the scene belongs to TJ Jackson, an Army Ranger officially killed in 2011 when his unit supposedly went rogue and kidnapped Alexander Hubert for ransom, leaving his brother Jeffrey sole heir to Hubert International. The stolen cash turns up donated to a city mission. A second raid empties safe deposit boxes belonging to Hubert and Ohio Senator Cook, and David Dagley, a member of Hubert's security team and the Rangers' former commanding officer, is lured to the bank and stabbed to death. Evidence of a secret affair between Hubert and Cook reaches Montgomery as the robbers push him toward Hubert's corruption. During a third, bloody heist at the main branch one robber is killed. A stolen file then exposes the truth: Hubert and Cook had fed the Rangers false intelligence about a terrorist threat in Costa Rica so that Alexander would die, and a Special Forces team, unaware of the deception, wiped out the unit. TJ survived thanks to Wells, then a Special Forces sniper. As Hubert's assets are frozen and he prepares to flee, TJ is arrested, and Montgomery's colleague, FBI Special Agent Wells, is revealed as the robbers' leader, avenging the massacre alongside other veterans of the attack. Detective Mims, consumed by guilt and facing his wife's terminal cancer, tracks Wells down and begs to return the money, and Wells kills him. Later, in Tijuana, Montgomery finds Wells about to kill Hubert and stabs Hubert himself, letting Wells go.

Meloni plays Montgomery, with Willis as Hubert, Bautista as FBI agent Stockwell, Grenier as Wells, Texas Battle as TJ and Johnathon Schaech as Mims. Financed by Emmett/Furla/Oasis Films, it was shot in Cincinnati from September to October 2015, and Lionsgate Premiere released it on July 1, 2016. Reviews were poor, with 22% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics called it a by-the-numbers B-movie with a convoluted plot and a rote performance from Willis.

title: Ford v Ferrari
tagline: They took the American dream for a ride
overview: American car designer Carroll Shelby and the British-born driver Ken Miles work together to battle corporate interference, the laws of physics, and their own personal demons to build a revolutionary race car for Ford Motor Company and take on the dominating race cars of Enzo Ferrari at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in France in 1966.
plot:
Ford v Ferrari is a biographical sports drama film directed by James Mangold, released in 2019 by 20th Century Fox. The movie tells the story of the rivalry between car designer Carroll Shelby and driver Ken Miles, who join forces to take down the dominant Ferrari team at the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

The film begins with a young Carroll Shelby (played by Christian Bale), an American racing driver who returns from World War II as a paraplegic. Despite his physical limitations, Shelby is determined to return to racing and becomes involved in the development of the Ford GT40, a car designed to challenge Ferrari's dominance at Le Mans.

Shelby meets Ken Miles (played by Matt Damon), an Australian-born driver who has been hired by Ford to compete against Ferrari. Miles is initially hesitant to join forces with Shelby, but eventually warms up to his unorthodox methods and the two form a strong partnership.

As the story unfolds, we see the development of the GT40, which becomes a symbol of American ingenuity and determination. The film also explores the personal struggles of both Shelby and Miles, including their relationships with their families and their own demons.

The plot thickens as the 24 Hours of Le Mans approaches, and Shelby and Miles prepare to take on Ferrari's dominant team led by Enzo Ferrari (played by Remo Girone). The tension builds as the two teams engage in a series of intense racing battles, both on and off the track.

In the climactic final act, Shelby and Miles face off against Ferrari at Le Mans, with the GT40 emerging victorious. However, the victory is bittersweet, as Shelby's health begins to decline, and he must come to terms with his own mortality.

The film ends with a poignant moment of reflection, as Shelby looks back on his life and the legacy of the GT40. The final shot is of the GT40 crossing the finish line at Le Mans, a testament to the power of determination and innovation.

Throughout the film, Mangold pays tribute to the real-life events that inspired the story, including the rivalry between Ford and Ferrari in the 1960s. The film features stunning racing sequences, impressive car designs, and outstanding performances from the cast.

Overall, Ford v Ferrari is a thrilling and emotionally resonant film that celebrates the spirit of American ingenuity and determination. With its strong performances, impressive car designs, and gripping storyline, it's no wonder that the film received widespread critical acclaim and earned several awards and nominations.
