plot:
Sword Master (Chinese: 三少爺的劍) is a 2016 Chinese-Hong Kong 3D martial arts film directed by Derek Yee and produced by Tsui Hark. A remake of the 1977 Shaw Brothers film Death Duel, in which Yee starred, it is based on a wuxia novel by Gu Long. Lin Gengxin stars as Hsieh Shao-feng, known as the Third Master, with Peter Ho as the swordsman Yen Shisan, Jiang Yiyan, Jiang Mengjie and Norman Chui. The film premiered at the Rome Film Festival and the Golden Horse Film Festival before its release on 2 December 2016.

Yen Shisan, a tattooed master swordsman and assassin, has long lived in the shadow of Hsieh Shao-feng, the legendary Third Master of the Supreme Sword Manor. Mu-Yung Chiu-ti, who claims to be Shao-feng's jilted bride, hires Yen to kill him. Yen declines the contract but sets out anyway to face the only opponent who might defeat him. At the manor he is told by Shao-feng's father that the Third Master died thirty-six days earlier. Deprived of his rival and suffering from an incurable illness, Yen gives up the life of the sword and becomes a gravedigger, hoping to do some good in the time he has left. Meanwhile, the villainous Divine Might clan seizes the chance to challenge the manor for supremacy in the martial world, now that no one there seems able to stand against them.

Elsewhere, a drunken stranger arrives at a brothel, drinks away all his money and is forced to work there as a servant. Refusing to give his name, he is nicknamed Ah-chi, or "Useless Chi." He defends Hsiao Li, a lowly prostitute who is being cheated by her customers, and the two form a bond. His kindness gradually draws him back into the conflicts of the martial world, as his true identity and the reason he abandoned his former life come to light. His path eventually converges with that of Yen Shisan, and the two greatest swordsmen of their generation must confront the Divine Might clan, Mu-Yung Chiu-ti's schemes and, finally, each other.

Sword Master grossed about $14.7 million worldwide, including around 100 million yuan in China. Reviewers praised its visual style and choreography but felt the story, which closely follows the 1977 original, was overly convoluted, and that its digital effects sometimes overwhelmed the swordplay, which marked a return to the genre for Yee, whose career had begun as a Shaw Brothers actor.

title: The Spirit of Christmas
tagline: This holiday could be the start of a new beginning.
overview: A woman falls in love with a man who is somewhat unavailable.
plot:
The Spirit of Christmas is a 2015 American romantic fantasy television film directed by David Jackson from a screenplay by Tracy Andreen. Produced by MarVista Entertainment, with Andrea Ajemian as producer, music by Claude Foisy and cinematography by Michael Negrin, it was developed under the working title Hollygrove and filmed in Wrentham, Massachusetts. Running about 91 minutes, it stars Jen Lilley and Thomas Beaudoin and premiered in the 2015 holiday season on the Lifetime network, blending a Christmas romance with a ghost story and a murder mystery.

Lilley plays Kate Jordan, a dedicated Boston lawyer whose devotion to work has left her with no lasting relationships and who has not really celebrated Christmas since her mother's death. Her boss gives her twelve days to close a deal: she is sent to Vermont to appraise the Hollygrove Inn so that it can be sold, a job she hopes will win her a promotion. On arrival she finds the caretaker, Walter Rafferty (Robert Walsh), uncooperative; he explains that the prospective buyer fled because a spirit lives in the house and disapproves of its sale, and that the inn cannot take guests because of the ghost. Kate soon meets the handsome Daniel Forsythe (Beaudoin), the owner of the mansion, who has been scaring off buyers. Murdered ninety-five years earlier, Daniel returns to the inn in bodily form for twelve days every Christmas, but he remembers neither who killed him nor why.

Kate puts the sale aside to help him. The two get off to a rocky start, with Daniel locking her out of the house and tossing blankets out after her, but they gradually warm to each other, and he even finds himself pressed into tending bar at a holiday party. As the days pass, they uncover the reason for his murder and the identity of the killer, and they fall in love, forcing Daniel to make a choice about his feelings before his time runs out. The supporting cast includes Bates Wilder as Sheriff Noah Bell, Kati Salowsky and Joanna Herrington.

Though it attracted less attention than many holiday television films on its release, the film has drawn admirers since. Writing for MovieWeb in 2022, Gissane Sophia called it a top-tier holiday film that had slipped under too many radars, praising the slow-burn romance between two jaded, heartbroken people, the leads' chemistry, Beaudoin's sardonic, brooding Daniel and the way the romance develops through solving the mystery, and arguing that it deserved cult status.

title: LEGO Marvel Super Heroes: Avengers Reassembled!

overview: The Avengers are forced to “party” with Ultron when he seeks to disassemble the team by taking control of Iron Man’s armor and enact a nefarious scheme to take over the world.
plot:
LEGO Marvel Super Heroes: Avengers Reassembled! is a 2015 American computer-animated television special based on Lego's Marvel Super Heroes toy line and featuring Marvel Comics' Avengers. Directed by Rob Silvestri and written by Mark Hoffmeier, it was produced by Arc Productions, with Jill Wilfert and Jason Cosler as executive producers alongside Marvel's Alan Fine, Dan Buckley, Jeph Loeb and Joe Quesada. Running about 22 minutes, it serves as a comedic spin-off of Avengers: Age of Ultron. The voice cast includes Mick Wingert as Iron Man, Roger Craig Smith as Captain America, Travis Willingham as Thor and Yellowjacket, Fred Tatasciore as the Hulk, Laura Bailey as Black Widow, Troy Baker as Hawkeye, JP Karliak as Vision and Baron Strucker, Jim Meskimen as Ultron, Grant George as Ant-Man, Ben Diskin as Spider-Man, Eric Bauza as Iron Spider and Bumper Robinson as Falcon.

As the Avengers prepare for a party at Avengers Tower, the team notices that Iron Man is behaving strangely. They soon discover that the villain Ultron has taken control of Tony Stark and his armor, turning him into a puppet as part of a scheme to take over the world. After causing chaos in the tower, the possessed Iron Man flies off, and the heroes give chase, learning that Ultron has joined forces with Yellowjacket and Hydra, led by Baron Strucker, to destroy them. Captain America, the Hulk, Thor, Vision, Black Widow and Hawkeye set out to free their teammate, with help from Spider-Man, Iron Spider and Ant-Man. Thor enters Stark's mind and learns that he must shock him to break Ultron's hold, and with a jolt of thunder he restores Iron Man to the team. Meanwhile, Spider-Man and Iron Spider capture Yellowjacket and extract information about the villains' plans. Returning to the tower, the reunited Avengers find Ultron wreaking havoc; he assembles his robot minions into a giant version of himself to finish them off, but Ant-Man shrinks down, gets inside Ultron's head and forces him to fall apart. The special ends with the team welcoming its newest member, Falcon.

The special premiered on Disney XD on 16 November 2015. Bubbleblabber gave it 5.5 out of 10, finding it less funny and gag-heavy than Lego's Star Wars parodies such as Droid Tales and its film-inspired dialogue grating, but noting that fans of cameos would enjoy the appearances of Spider-Man's allies, Falcon, Ant-Man and his nemesis Yellowjacket.

title: Battle of the Sexes
tagline: He made a bet. She made history.
overview: The true story of the 1973 tennis match between World number one Billie Jean King and ex-champ and serial hustler Bobby Riggs.
plot:
Battle of the Sexes is a 2017 biographical sports comedy-drama directed by Valerie Faris and Jonathan Dayton and written by Simon Beaufoy, loosely based on the famous 1973 tennis match between Billie Jean King and Bobby Riggs. Emma Stone stars as King and Steve Carell as Riggs, with Andrea Riseborough as Marilyn Barnett, Sarah Silverman as Gladys Heldman, Austin Stowell as Larry King, Bill Pullman as Jack Kramer, Alan Cumming as Ted Tinling, Elisabeth Shue as Priscilla Riggs and Jessica McNamee as Margaret Court.

In 1970, Billie Jean King and her manager Gladys Heldman confront promoter Jack Kramer, who has organized a tournament offering women one-eighth of the men's prize money despite equal ticket sales. When Kramer refuses to change the terms, King and eight other players break away to form their own tour, which eventually leads to the creation of the Women's Tennis Association. Exhausted by the constant travel and promotion, King, who is married to Larry, begins a secret romance with her hairdresser, Marilyn Barnett.

Meanwhile Bobby Riggs, a former men's champion now in his fifties, struggles with a gambling addiction that is straining his marriage to his wealthy wife, Priscilla. Looking for a comeback and a big payday, he comes up with the idea of a match against the best female player, boasting that even at 55 he can beat any woman. King turns him down, but Margaret Court, who has overtaken her as world number one, accepts and is easily defeated. Determined to prove a point for women's tennis and equality, King agrees to face Riggs on her own terms. As the spectacle-driven match approaches, King trains relentlessly while Riggs turns the event into a media circus, and the whole country tunes in to see the outcome.

The film examines sexism, gender equality and King's private struggle with her sexuality, presenting the match as a turning point in the history of women's sport.

Battle of the Sexes premiered at the Telluride Film Festival and was released by Fox Searchlight on September 22, 2017. It grossed 18 million dollars but received positive reviews, with 84 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 73, and Stone and Carell both received Golden Globe nominations.

title: The Limehouse Golem
tagline: Before the ripper, fear had another name.
overview: A series of murders has shaken the community to the point where people believe that only a legendary creature from dark times – the mythical Golem – must be responsible.
plot:
A series of murders has shaken the community of Limehouse in the docklands of Victorian London. Journalists dub the murderer the Golem, after the Jewish legend. When music-hall star Elizabeth Cree is accused of poisoning her husband, John, on the same night as the last Golem murder, Inspector John Kildare discovers evidence linking John Cree to the murders and wants to solve the cases before Elizabeth is hanged.
Kildare finds a diary written by the Golem of the crimes, handwritten in a printed copy of Thomas De Quincey's essay "On Murder Considered as one of the Fine Arts", in a collected volume in the British Museum Library Reading Room. He deduces that the Golem must be one of the four men who were in the library on the date of the last entry: Dan Leno, Karl Marx, George Gissing and John Cree. Kildare acquires handwriting samples of the other three men, while listening to Elizabeth's story about how she was the daughter of an unmarried mother and went from sewing sail-cloths at the docks to becoming a star.
When Elizabeth's abusive mother died, she was befriended by Dan Leno and fell in with his music-hall troupe, performing comic songs while dressed as a man. Her act quickly becomes second in popularity only to Leno, but she aspires to become a dramatic actor. She is wooed by John Cree, a struggling playwright. Her fellow performer, Aveline Ortega (María Valverde), becomes jealous since she herself is interested in John, and sabotages Elizabeth's first dramatic role.
Elizabeth is entrapped by the theatre's owner, a man known as 'Uncle' (Eddie Marsan) and is forced to pose nude for photographs and to beat him for his sexual gratification. She tells John, who offers to marry her and keep her safe. Elizabeth accepts and Kildare notes that Uncle died suddenly only days later, leaving the theatre to Dan Leno. John's career stalls, and he grows bitter toward Elizabeth, who supports him financially, but is only interested in what he can do for her career. She hires Aveline as a maid and facilitates an affair between Aveline and John so that she will not have to keep sleeping with him. The two remain estranged until John Cree's poisoning.
Kildare finds a handwritten copy of the play written by Cree before his death on the day Elizabeth is to be hanged. He finds it to be a match with the diary and gets an hour's postponement to her sentence, hoping that revealing John Cree's crimes will cause her sentence to be commuted. Kildare instructs her to write a statement, but she writes the confession "I am the Golem", her handwriting matching the diary. Kildare realises that she is the true Golem rather than her husband. She killed 'Uncle' and began committing murders as the Golem to make a lasting name for herself, poisoning her husband when he found evidence.

plot:
L.O.R.D.: Legend of Ravaging Dynasties is a 2016 Chinese animated motion-capture action fantasy adventure film written and directed by Guo Jingming. Produced by Le Vision Pictures, which handled distribution in Greater China, it opened on 30 September 2016 in 3D and IMAX 3D, while Lionsgate released it the same day in the United Kingdom and Ireland, Australia and New Zealand, and the United States and Canada. Le Vision said Lionsgate saw the film's appeal to young adult audiences, comparing it to the studio's Hunger Games and Twilight franchises. A sequel premiered on the streaming platform Tencent Video on 4 December 2020 and later reached Netflix.

The film is set on the Odin Mainland, divided into four countries, each protected by soul masters who wield supernatural soul powers; the seven mightiest are known as the Noble Lords. In the Aslan Empire, the realm of the water element, Qi Ling (Cheney Chen), who has worked as a busboy at an inn since childhood, tames the legendary soul beast Ice Fang during a clash between soul masters. Yin Chen (Kris Wu), the Seventh Lord, arrives on the orders of the Silver Priest (Roy Wang) to take Qi Ling as his disciple, and guides him toward the Grave of the Souls, where he must find his soul weapon.

Impatient, Qi Ling ignores his master's instructions and enters the Grave with Tianshu You Hua (Lin Yun) and Guishan Lian Quan (Fan Bingbing), drawing himself into the Upcoming Storm, a contest of soul powers among the lords. Meanwhile a conspiracy long hidden within the Aslan Empire begins to surface. While searching for his disciple, Yin Chen learns that his own former master, Gilgamesh, the former First Lord, may still be alive, and risks everything to find him. At the same time the Corroders You Ming (William Chan) and Thalia (Amber Kuo) are ordered by the Silver Priest to kill Guishan Lian Quan and her brother, Feng Hun (Yan Yikuan), setting lords and disciples against one another in a battle over truth and honor.

The film opened strongly, earning about $29.2 million in its first weekend across four markets, almost all of it from China, where it benefited from the National Day holiday and placed second behind I Belonged to You. Poor word of mouth and competition from Operation Mekong caused takings to fall sharply after its opening day, and it finished with about $53.8 million, $53.6 million of it from China.

title: Sing Street
tagline: Boy meets girl. Girl unimpressed. Boy starts band.
overview: A boy growing up in Dublin during the 1980s escapes his strained family life by starting a band to impress the mysterious girl he likes.
plot:
In 1985, 15-year-old Conor Lalor lives in inner-city South Dublin with his parents, Robert and Penny, and two older siblings, Brendan and Ann. Since his parents constantly argue, Conor writes music as a way to cope with his troubled home life. Due to recent financial difficulties, Robert and Penny announce that Conor will be transferred from his private school to Synge Street, a public Christian Brothers school.
On his first day at Synge Street, Conor is reprimanded by Brother Baxter, the stern school principal, for not wearing the mandatory black shoes, despite Conor's pleas that he cannot afford new shoes. After Baxter orders him to remove his brown shoes, Conor paints the shoes black. An encounter with school bully Barry introduces Conor to Darren, a budding entrepreneur. Conor then meets and becomes smitten with Raphina, a 16-year-old aspiring model who lives across the street from the school. In an effort to impress Raphina, he decides to form a band and recruits her for a music video. Darren agrees to manage his band and introduces him to multi-instrumentalist Eamon.
They are soon joined by keyboardist Ngig, drummer Larry and bassist Garry, naming their band Sing Street. The band practises in Eamon's living room, playing covers until Brendan, a music enthusiast, encourages Conor to develop the band's own style. Conor writes original songs with Eamon, describing themselves as "futurists". Sing Street films their first music video wearing outlandish costumes; Raphina acts as ingénue and makeup artist. Conor wears makeup to school the next day, and Baxter forcibly removes it.
Raphina gives Conor the nickname "Cosmo", which she says is more in keeping with his new band's image. She tells him about her plans to leave for London soon with her older boyfriend, Evan, with whom she has an on-and-off relationship. After spending the day filming a music video for a new song, Conor and Raphina kiss. At school, he stands up to Barry.
As Conor and Raphina grow closer, he takes her out to Dalkey Island in his grandfather's motor cruiser. There, they view the car ferry leaving Dún Laoghaire for the United Kingdom. Meanwhile, Robert and Penny inform the family that they are getting legally separated and selling the house, as Penny has fallen in love with her boss and plans to move in with him, while Robert intends to get himself an apartment.
Sing Street prepares to film a Back to the Future-inspired music video for their new song in the school gym, but Conor is disheartened when Raphina fails to show up, only to find that she has left for London without telling him. A few days later, Raphina returns to Dublin, explaining to Conor that Evan abandoned her in London after they had a fight. When Raphina laments that her life now involves "hanging out with a 15-year-old schoolboy", Conor distances himself from her.
An opportunity arises for the band to play at an end-of-term dance at school.

plot:
Rafael "Rafe" Khatchadorian lives in a middle-class home with his mother Jules, his rebellious younger sister Georgia, and Jules' lazy, child-hating boyfriend (later fiancé) Carl, who goes by the nickname Bear. Rafe has an overactive imagination and is very passionate about his artistic talent and has a friend named Leo who supports his antics.
Though Rafe is not enthusiastic about starting his first day at Hills Village Middle School, he's reminded it's his last option, as he's been kicked out of the other two in the area already. It does not go as he hoped, as he discovers Principal Ken Dwight and Vice-Principal Ida Stricker are even worse than the bullies and the school is filled with rules that are unjustified and unlawful.
After Dwight destroys Rafe's sketchbook by dissolving it in a bucket of acid for drawing a picture of Dwight in his sketchbook teasing him, Rafe and his friend Leo come up with a plan to start a massive "insurrection" against Principal Dwight and Stricker, by breaking every rule in the rule book.
They unleash several pranks on Principal Dwight, Stricker, and the school staff, including putting sticky notes all over the school, filling the teacher's lounge with plastic balls, dyeing Principal Dwight's hair pink, and turning the school's trophy case into a fish tank. He refers to this plan as "Operation: Rules Aren't For Everyone", or R.A.F.E.
As the annual B.L.A.A.R. (BaseLine Assessment of Academic Readiness) test is coming up, Dwight sees an opportunity to improve his school's results (and thereby his own annual bonus) by eliminating Rafe's seemingly underperforming class from the test. Rafe, and the whole class, are suspended for the pranks the day before the test. In addition, Rafe's teacher, Mr. Teller, is fired as Principal Dwight suspects his involvement. Dwight then offers Rafe a deal to let his class take the fall and he'll be the only one not suspended. However, Rafe deliberately sets off the sprinkler system, and Dwight immediately expels him.
Jeanne Galleta, the president of the AV club and Rafe's love interest, shows Rafe that Dwight put fake evidence in their lockers in order to stop their class from taking the B.L.A.A.R. test. Rafe devises a plan to stop the test and expose Dwight and Stricker along with Jeanne, Leo, Georgia, Gus, Miller, and his suspended class. The next day, both Dwight and Stricker are fired after Teller and Superintendent Hwang receive the evidence and decide to press charges on both of them.
As Dwight walks out, he is pranked with green hair dye in his hat. Jules breaks up with Bear after finding out his true nature, and Rafe is reenrolled into HVMS (with Mr. Teller also reinstated) and says goodbye to Leo (now revealed to be Rafe's imagination, a grief manifested flashback of his late younger brother who tragically died from cancer prior to the events of the film), thereby finally coming to terms with Leo's death.

title: Allied
tagline: The enemy is listening.
overview: In 1942, an intelligence officer in North Africa encounters a female French Resistance fighter on a deadly mission behind enemy lines. When they reunite in London, their relationship is tested by the pressures of war.
plot:
Allied is a 2016 spy thriller film directed by Robert Zemeckis, starring Brad Pitt and Marion Cotillard.

The movie begins with Max Vatan (Brad Pitt), a French Resistance fighter who has just returned from World War II. He is married to Hadley (Emily Blunt), an American socialite, in a loveless marriage of convenience. The couple's relationship is strained due to the fact that they are not truly in love.

One day, Max receives a message from his former lover, Marianne Beausejour (Marion Cotillard), who was also involved with him during the war. She has been working for the French Resistance and has information about a German spy ring operating in Paris. Max is initially hesitant to get involved again, but eventually agrees to meet with Marianne.

During their meeting, Max and Marianne rekindle their romance, and he becomes embroiled in her work with the Resistance. As they spend more time together, Max begins to suspect that Marianne may be working for the Germans, using him as a pawn in her game of espionage.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that Marianne was indeed working for the Germans, but not in the way Max initially thought. She had been sent to Paris to gather intelligence on the German spy ring, and she had used Max's cover to gain access to their inner circle.

Max becomes increasingly entangled in Marianne's web of deceit, and he begins to question his own loyalties and motivations. He also starts to develop feelings for Hadley again, but ultimately realizes that his heart belongs to Marianne.

The plot thickens as Max discovers the true extent of Marianne's deception. She had been using him to gather information on the German spy ring, and she had manipulated him into doing her bidding. Max is torn between his love for Marianne and his duty to Hadley and the Resistance.

In the end, Max makes a choice that will change the course of his life forever. He decides to expose Marianne's true intentions and bring her to justice, rather than continuing to play along with her game. The movie ends with Max walking away from Marianne, leaving their complicated past behind him.

Throughout the film, Zemeckis explores themes of love, loyalty, and deception. The movie is a complex web of intrigue and espionage, with multiple twists and turns that keep the viewer guessing until the very end.

title: First Man
tagline: One giant leap into the unknown
overview: A look at the life of the astronaut, Neil Armstrong, and the legendary space mission that led him to become the first man to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969.
plot:
First Man is a 2018 American biographical drama directed by Damien Chazelle from a screenplay by Josh Singer, based on James R. Hansen's 2005 biography First Man: The Life of Neil A. Armstrong. It covers the years leading to the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969 and the toll they took on Armstrong, his family and his colleagues. First announced in 2003 with Clint Eastwood attached to direct, the project was revived with Chazelle, Ryan Gosling and Singer by 2015, and filming began in Atlanta in November 2017. It premiered at the Venice Film Festival on August 29, 2018, and Universal Pictures released it in the United States on October 12.

In 1961, test pilot Neil Armstrong narrowly lands an X-15 that bounces off the atmosphere, while at home his two-year-old daughter, Karen, is dying of a brain tumor. After her death, he applies for Project Gemini and moves to Houston with his wife, Janet, and son Rick as one of NASA's second group of astronauts, befriending Elliot See and Ed White as the United States trails the Soviet Union in the Space Race. He is given command of Gemini 8 with David Scott; after docking with an Agena target, a malfunction sends the capsule into a violent spin, and Armstrong, close to blacking out, regains control and aborts the mission. See dies in a jet crash before the flight, and in 1967 White and the rest of the Apollo 1 crew are killed in a launch-pad fire.

plot:
No Time to Die is a 2021 spy thriller and the twenty-fifth James Bond film produced by Eon Productions, the fifth and final film to star Daniel Craig as Bond. Directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga, who wrote the screenplay with Neal Purvis, Robert Wade and Phoebe Waller-Bridge, it co-stars Rami Malek as Lyutsifer Safin, Léa Seydoux as Madeleine Swann, Lashana Lynch as the new 007 Nomi, Ana de Armas as Paloma, and returning cast members Ralph Fiennes, Naomie Harris, Ben Whishaw, Jeffrey Wright, Rory Kinnear and Christoph Waltz.

After an ambush in Italy convinces him that Madeleine has betrayed him, Bond leaves her and retires from MI6. Five years later, he is living quietly in Jamaica when his old CIA friend Felix Leiter asks him to help rescue a kidnapped scientist, Valdo Obruchev, who has been taken from a secret MI6 laboratory along with Project Heracles, a bioweapon of DNA-targeted nanobots that can be programmed to kill only people with a specific DNA.

Bond infiltrates a SPECTRE gathering in Cuba with the agent Paloma, but the plot is far larger than it appears: the nanobots kill the assembled SPECTRE members instead of Bond, and Bond learns that Obruchev is working for Safin, a man whose family was murdered by Madeleine's father on Blofeld's orders. As Felix is betrayed and killed, Bond is drawn back into the world he left, crossing paths with Nomi, confronting the imprisoned Blofeld and reconnecting with Madeleine, who has a young daughter. Safin, operating from a hidden island base, plans to unleash Heracles on millions, and Bond must stop him at a devastating personal cost.

The film closes the arc of Craig's Bond, emphasizing family, love and sacrifice, and features a theme song performed by Billie Eilish and a score by Hans Zimmer.

Delayed repeatedly by the COVID-19 pandemic, No Time to Die premiered at London's Royal Albert Hall on 28 September 2021. It grossed over 774 million dollars, the fourth-highest gross of 2021, and received generally positive reviews, with a Metacritic score of 68, winning the Academy Award for Best Original Song.

plot:
I Am Dragon (Russian: On – drakon, "He's a Dragon"), released in Germany as Dragon: Love Is a Scary Tale, is a 2015 Russian 3D romantic fantasy adventure written and directed by Indar Dzhendubaev and produced by Timur Bekmambetov's company Bazelevs. Loosely based on The Ritual, a 1996 fantasy novel by Marina and Sergey Dyachenko, it is set in an invented world blending Kievan Rus' with Scandinavian, Celtic and Eastern traditions. Maria Poezzhaeva and Matvey Lykov play the leads. After a Moscow premiere on November 24, 2015, Bazelevs Distribution released it in Russia on December 3, 2015.

For generations villagers appeased a fearsome dragon by offering it maidens, until a knight whose beloved had been taken slew the beast; afterward the sacrificial rite became a wedding ceremony. Years later Princess Miroslava, or Mira, whose father and sister Yaroslava consider her childish, is placed on a boat in her bridal gown and drawn across the water toward Igor, the Dragon Slayer's grandson. As his people sing the old ritual song, a dragon, long thought dead, snatches her away to its island. In a cave she meets a guardian creature and a young man who cannot recall his name; she calls him Arman, then learns that he is the dragon himself, living as a human but sometimes changing against his will and losing control.

Arman explains that he chose to remain human until the Dragon Slayer killed his father, when grief turned him into a dragon carrying the memories of his ancestors. He hides in the cave whenever he senses a transformation, but the wedding song had changed him too quickly. Mira teaches him to live as a person and they fall in love, while an enchantment, which reveals the island only to those loved by someone there, keeps the timid Igor lost in fog. Learning she plans to flee, Arman reveals that dragons burned the captured maidens and that new dragons were born from their ashes, and he sends her home. On her second wedding day Mira realizes she loves him, abandons Igor and sings the song. The dragon seizes her, but her fearless declaration of love lets Arman master his dragon form, and years later they live on the island with their daughter.

Reviews were mixed, with praise from Film.ru and The Hollywood Reporter's Russian critic and scorn from the Russian Gazette. It earned only about $1.7 million in Russia against an $18 million budget, but its success in China made it the top-grossing Russian film internationally in 2016.

title: The Eyes of My Mother

plot:
Francisca and her parents live on a farm where they raise animals. A trained surgeon, Francisca's mother teaches her how to remove eyeballs from farm animals, as well as the legend of St. Francis of Assisi. One day, Charlie, a door-to-door salesman, asks to use the bathroom. Against her better judgment, Francisca's mother lets him into the house. Charlie draws a gun and takes Francisca's mother into the bathroom. When her father comes home, he finds Charlie bludgeoning his wife's body in the tub. He knocks Charlie out and chains him up in the barn. Francisca and her father bury her mother in the backyard. Francisca visits Charlie and he explains the thrill of killing others. When he asks Francisca if she plans to kill him, she reacts with confusion, proclaiming that Charlie is her only friend and that she will take care of him. She then removes Charlie's eyes and vocal cords, bags them, and puts them in the refrigerator.
Years later, Francisca's father dies, and the now adult Francisca preserves his body. At a bar, Francisca meets a young woman named Kimiko, whom she takes home. Kimiko asks about Francisca's mother; when Francisca explains that her mother was murdered, Kimiko offers condolences, and Francisca kisses her. Francisca then jokes that she killed her father. A frightened Kimiko tries to leave, but Francisca murders her before dismembering her and placing her bagged organs in the refrigerator. Afterward, she bathes Charlie, still chained up in the barn, and brings him inside to sleep in her bed with her. Charlie attempts to escape, but she catches him and repeatedly stabs him. She tells him that he was right; killing someone "feels amazing". She places his organs into bags and keeps them in her refrigerator, just as she had done to Kimiko.
Now distraught at being completely alone, Francisca wanders the woods until she reaches a highway and catches a ride with a woman named Lucy and her infant son Antonio back home. Francisca becomes enamored of Antonio, and upon reaching her house, asks Lucy if she can hold him. When Lucy agrees, she thanks Lucy for the "gift" and rushes out of the car with Antonio. Lucy frantically pursues her, but Francisca stabs her, removes her eyes and vocal cords, and keeps her chained up in the barn like she had done to Charlie, subsequently spending the next few years raising Antonio as her own son.
When Antonio reaches late childhood, he becomes curious about the barn, which Francisca has forbidden him to enter. He enters the barn as Francisca is asleep one night and is terrified at the sight of a blinded, chained Lucy, groaning unintelligibly and reaching for him. Antonio asks Francisca about the woman in the barn, but she claims to not know what he is referring to. Lucy later escapes the barn and blindly makes her way to a road where a trucker finds her. After discovering Lucy missing, Francisca digs up her mother's remains and cradles the corpse as she speaks to it, expressing how much she misses her.

Nickelodeon's Ho Ho Holiday Special is a 2015 American Christmas comedy television special produced by Nickelodeon Productions. Directed by Jonathan Judge, who wrote it with Kevin Kopelow, the hour-long special was filmed at Paramount Studios in November 2015 and premiered on Nickelodeon in early December 2015. It brings together a large ensemble of the young stars of the network's live-action series of the time, including The Thundermans, Nicky, Ricky, Dicky & Dawn, Henry Danger, Bella and the Bulldogs, Game Shakers, 100 Things to Do Before High School and School of Rock, in a mix of comedy sketches and musical numbers about holiday customs held together by a larger wraparound story.

An announcer opens the show by promising a cast too big to name, but one sure to include every viewer's favourite Nickelodeon star. Two of Santa's elves, Jingles (Tony Cavalero) and Tinsel (Kelly Perine), take a break from their Christmas preparations to tell holiday stories. In the main storyline, Jack Griffo of The Thundermans is invited by the President of the United States to spend Christmas with the First Family at the White House, but accepts instead an invitation from fellow Nickelodeon stars to a Christmas party at a mansion. As the stars sing their way through the evening, strange things begin to happen, and they discover that they are trapped inside until after Christmas.

The trapped guests must survive a series of festive challenges in a parody of the Saw horror films, such as cracking open countless nuts to find a key, escaping a room filling with eggnog and eating an entire gingerbread house. Interspersed with the main story are sketches in which other Nickelodeon actors play themselves or characters, including a game show spoof starring Jace Norman and an opening that parodies the title sequence of South Park, with Breanna Yde and Lizzy Greene singing and Kira Kosarin mumbling through dental braces in the manner of Kenny McCormick. In the end, the villain behind the traps is revealed to be Rico Rodriguez, who imprisoned the stars in revenge for never answering his letters asking them to sing a song with him, letters that in fact were never sent.

The Disaster Artist is a 2017 American biographical comedy-drama directed and co-produced by James Franco, who also stars. Scott Neustadter and Michael H. Weber wrote the screenplay, based on the 2013 non-fiction book by Greg Sestero and Tom Bissell. The film recounts the unlikely friendship between aspiring actors Tommy Wiseau and Greg Sestero that led to the making of Wiseau's 2003 film The Room, widely considered one of the worst films ever made. James Franco plays Wiseau and his brother Dave Franco plays Sestero, with Seth Rogen, Alison Brie, Ari Graynor and Josh Hutcherson in supporting roles.

In San Francisco in 1998, nineteen-year-old Greg meets Tommy in an acting class after Tommy delivers a bizarre and fearless rendition of a scene from A Streetcar Named Desire. Greg admires his lack of inhibition, even though Tommy is deeply secretive: he seems to have unlimited money, refuses to reveal his age or the origin of his wealth, and claims to come from New Orleans despite an unmistakably European accent. At Tommy's suggestion, the two move to Los Angeles to chase acting careers.

Greg finds an agent and begins dating a woman named Amber, while Tommy is turned away by every agent, teacher and casting director he approaches. When Greg's prospects also fade, Tommy decides to write, finance, direct and star in his own film, a melodrama about a love triangle between a banker named Johnny, his fiancée Lisa and his best friend Mark, played by Greg. The production descends into chaos as Tommy insists on shooting on both film and digital cameras, struggles to remember his lines, alienates his crew and treats his cast harshly, straining his friendship with Greg. The story ends at the premiere of The Room, where the audience's laughter turns what Tommy intended as a serious drama into an unexpected cult phenomenon.

The film is a comedy about outsider ambition and friendship that treats Wiseau with both humour and affection, and its closing credits compare recreated scenes with the original footage.

The Disaster Artist premiered at the South by Southwest festival in March 2017 and was widely praised, especially for James Franco's performance. He won the Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy, and the screenplay received an Academy Award nomination for Best Adapted Screenplay.

title: Your Name.
tagline: It was almost like seeing something out of a dream, nothing more or less than a breathtaking view.
overview: High schoolers Mitsuha and Taki are complete strangers living separate lives. But one night, they suddenly switch places. Mitsuha wakes up in Taki’s body, and he in hers. This bizarre occurrence continues to happen randomly, and the two must adjust their lives around each other.
plot:
Your Name (Japanese: 君の名は。, Hepburn: Kimi no Na wa) is a 2016 Japanese animated romantic fantasy film written and directed by Makoto Shinkai, produced by CoMix Wave Films and distributed by Toho. Ryunosuke Kamiki and Mone Kamishiraishi voice the leads, with Ryo Narita, Aoi Yūki, Nobunaga Shimazaki and Masami Nagasawa. It is the first of what critics have called Shinkai's "disaster trilogy," followed by Weathering with You (2019) and Suzume (2022), films that share themes inspired by Japan's frequent natural disasters. The soundtrack was composed by the rock band Radwimps.

Mitsuha Miyamizu is a high school girl living in Itomori, a small rural town in the mountains of Gifu Prefecture, where her family runs the local Shinto shrine. Bored with country life, she wishes to be reborn as a boy in Tokyo. Soon afterward she begins intermittently switching bodies with Taki Tachibana, a high school boy who works part-time at a restaurant in Tokyo. On certain days each wakes up in the other's body and must live through the day as the other person, returning to normal after sleep. They establish rules and communicate through notes, phone diaries and writing on their skin.

While in Taki's body, Mitsuha helps him win a date with his coworker Miki Okudera, and Taki, as Mitsuha, makes her more popular at school and visits a sacred site in a mountain crater with her grandmother and younger sister, where they leave an offering of ritual sake. Mitsuha mentions that a comet is expected to pass close to Earth during the town's autumn festival. When the body swaps suddenly stop, Taki sets out to find Mitsuha in person, armed only with his memories of the town's landscape, and makes a shocking discovery about Itomori and the comet that reveals the two were separated by more than distance. His search turns into a desperate race to change the past.

Your Name received widespread acclaim for its animation, story, music and emotional power. It became a cultural phenomenon in Japan and was for several years the highest-grossing anime film worldwide, earning more than $380 million. It won the Los Angeles Film Critics Association Award for Best Animated Film and the Japan Academy Prize for Best Screenplay, among many other honors.

title: The Snowman
tagline: Soon the first snow will come, and then he will kill again.
overview: Detective Harry Hole investigates the disappearance of a woman whose pink scarf is found wrapped around an ominous looking snowman.
plot:
The Snowman is a 2017 psychological thriller film directed by Tomas Alfredson and written by Peter Straughan, Hossein Amini and Søren Sveistrup, based on Jo Nesbø's 2007 novel of the same name. It stars Michael Fassbender, Rebecca Ferguson, Charlotte Gainsbourg, Val Kilmer and J. K. Simmons, and follows the Oslo police inspector Harry Hole as he hunts a serial killer who leaves snowmen at his crime scenes.

In a prologue, a boy's mother, Sarah, is assaulted at their remote cabin by his abusive father, a married police officer named Jonas. Chasing him in her car, she lets go of the wheel and crashes into a lake; the boy escapes, but she stays in her seat and sinks. Years later, Harry, an alcoholic inspector reeling from his break-up with Rakel, whose son, Oleg, he loves as his own, receives a letter signed with a child's drawing of a snowman. He joins new recruit Katrine Bratt in investigating the disappearance of Birte Becker, a wife and mother, outside whose home stands a snowman. Katrine, who has taken police files without permission, suspects links between several disappearances and a case from nine years earlier investigated by the alcoholic inspector Gert Rafto. After the pair visit Sylvia Otterson at her farm, a masked figure beheads her, and her head is found atop a snowman.

Katrine suspects the corrupt businessman Arve Støp. In Bergen, Harry learns that Rafto died of an apparently self-inflicted gunshot and that Katrine is his daughter. The victims are found to have visited the clinic of Dr. Vetlesen, who runs Støp's high-class prostitution ring, but Vetlesen is found shot dead with the remains of two missing persons, and Katrine is suspended. Trying to trap Støp, she is drugged by a masked attacker who cuts off her finger to wipe her tablet, and she is found dead in a car marked with a snowman. Harry discovers that Rakel's new boyfriend, the cosmetic surgeon Mathias, had consulted with Becker's husband. Mathias, revealed as the boy from the prologue who targets mothers he judges unfit, kidnaps Rakel and Oleg. Harry saves Rakel, losing a finger, and pursues Mathias onto a frozen lake, where Mathias shoots him but falls through the ice and drowns. Harry, fitted with a metal prosthetic finger, volunteers for a new case.

Shot in Norway, London and Sweden, the film was released by Universal Pictures in October 2017 and grossed $43.1 million on a $35 million budget. Critics panned its incoherent story, giving it 7% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Belzebuth
tagline: Don't stop praying
overview: While leading a police investigation of a massacre in a public school at the border of Mexico and U.S.A, special Agent Emanuel Ritter links this strange case to the coming and rising of the ancient demon Belzebuth. But in order to stop the trail of upcoming infanticides, Ritter shall have to confront himself before dealing with the forces of good and evil.
plot:
Belzebuth is a 2017 Mexican supernatural horror film directed by Emilio Portes, who co-wrote the screenplay. Joaquín Cosío stars as the police detective Emmanuel Ritter, with Tobin Bell, Tate Ellington, José Sefami and Yunuen Pardo in supporting roles. The film, which features dialogue in both Spanish and English, was completed in 2017 and released in January 2019.

The film opens in a hospital, where Ritter and his wife are celebrating the birth of their son. After Ritter leaves in response to a call from work, the baby is taken to the nursery. A nurse beginning her shift locks the nursery door, takes out a scalpel and murders Ritter's son and every other newborn in the room before slitting her own throat, all before anyone can break in to stop her.

Years later, Ritter remains traumatized and emotionally closed off, unable to come to terms with his son's death, haunted by the loss. He is called to investigate a mass shooting at an elementary school, which turns out to be one of a series of horrific massacres of children in the region, carried out by seemingly ordinary people who appear to have been overtaken by some outside force. Joined by Ivan Franco, an investigator who specializes in paranormal cases, Ritter begins to suspect that the killings are linked and that they share a supernatural cause. Their inquiry leads them to Vasilio Canavas, an excommunicated priest played by Bell, who may hold the key to understanding the evil behind the murders. As the investigation deepens, Ritter is drawn into a confrontation with a demonic force that appears to be targeting the children for a specific purpose, and he must face his own grief and loss of faith in order to stop it.

Belzebuth drew attention as an ambitious Mexican genre production combining a police procedural with demonic-possession horror, and for Bell's casting, which recalled his role as Jigsaw in the Saw series. It received generally favorable reviews, with 80 percent of 15 critics' reviews on Rotten Tomatoes being positive. Reviewers frequently singled out its shocking hospital prologue and its blend of crime-thriller and religious-horror conventions.

title: Misconduct
tagline: Ambition can be deadly
overview: An ambitious lawyer finds himself caught in a power struggle between a corrupt pharmaceutical executive and his firm’s senior partner. When the case takes a deadly turn, he must race to uncover the truth before he loses everything.
plot:
Arthur Denning is the owner of a major pharmaceutical firm. He is very controlling of his girlfriend Emily Hynes, and she is physically intimidated by his security guards. She is abducted, and Denning is sent photos of her bruised face. He is ordered to go to an art gallery with the ransom. When a man approaches him, Denning attacks him, but learns that he was the gallery owner.
Before her abduction, Hynes reaches out to her ex-boyfriend Ben Cahill. She hints at Denning's abuse and shares some dirt that she has on him. At her apartment, she shows Cahill some files that she has stolen from Denning's laptop that reveal his criminal behavior during drug trials. She soon convinces a stranger to beat her up for the photo that she sends to Denning.
Cahill uses the information from Hynes to pitch a class-action lawsuit to his boss Charles Abrams that he files against Denning. That evening, Cahill is stunned to find Hynes dead in her apartment. With a bottle of pills in her hand and a lethal cocktail of drugs in her system, her death is suspicious but possibly just a suicide. Cahill decides to leave the scene without reporting it to the police and tries to cover his tracks, secretly telling only his wife about it.
At a preliminary deposition to the lawsuit, Denning suddenly settles the suit for $400 million, provided that the stolen documents are returned to him. Before long, Hynes's body is found in Cahill's home. Convinced that he is being framed, he confronts Denning, who is amused at Cahill's passion, but assures him that he had nothing to do with it.
A hitman kidnaps Cahill and his wife Charlotte (Eve), but Cahill overpowers and kills him. When he inspects the hitman's files, he realizes that the villain is actually his boss. Abrams has been colluding with Denning for years, deliberately losing all of the cases that his clients brought against the pharmaceutical magnate. The settlement was all just an elaborate way of protecting Denning from criminal liability.
Cahill submits the hitman's files to the police, who arrest Abrams. Before he can be taken into custody, however, Abrams grabs an officer's gun and kills himself.
As Cahill packs for a move to a new house, he notices that some of his wife's clothing smells like Hynes's perfume. He asks her what happened between the two of them. Charlotte confesses that she confronted Hynes about her involvement with her husband. They had an argument in which Charlotte hit Hynes, causing her to fall and hit her head. Although Charlotte is a nurse, she did not help her and stages the scene for the police.

title: Taylor Swift: The 1989 World Tour - Live
original_title: Taylor Swift: The 1989 World Tour - Live
tagline: She lost him, but she found herself. And somehow that was everything.
overview: Filmed in front of 76,000 fans at the ANZ Stadium in Sydney, Australia, "The 1989 World Tour Live" captures Taylor Swift's entire performance while also mixing in behind-the-scene, rehearsal, and special guest footage from her 1989 Tour.
plot:
The 1989 World Tour Live is a 2015 American concert film by the singer-songwriter Taylor Swift, documenting her fourth concert tour, the 1989 World Tour, staged in support of her fifth studio album, 1989 (2014), her first record marketed as pop rather than country. Directed by Jonas Åkerlund and produced in partnership with Apple Music, the film was shot at the show of 28 November 2015 at ANZ Stadium in Sydney, Australia, and also includes behind-the-scenes footage and appearances by special guests from shows in North America and Europe. Its release marked Swift's first collaboration with Apple, coming months after she pulled her catalog from Spotify over its payment model and after Apple agreed to pay artists during the free trial period of its streaming service.

The concert opens with black-and-white projections of street scenes as Swift rises from beneath the stage to sing "Welcome to New York," followed by "New Romantics" and "Blank Space," and an industrial rock version of "I Knew You Were Trouble." The set moves through "I Wish You Would," a Singin' in the Rain-inspired staging of "How You Get the Girl" with dancers twirling neon umbrellas, and "I Know Places," in which masked dancers chase her through moving doors. Swift introduces "Clean" by sharing lessons from her personal life and performs a synth-driven "Love Story" on an elevated platform that sweeps around the stadium. Later highlights include "Style," "This Love," "Bad Blood" in a black leather suit, a rock rendition of "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together" on electric guitar, a piano mashup of "Enchanted" and "Wildest Dreams," and "Out of the Woods" beneath giant paper planes, before the show closes with "Shake It Off" on a platform above the crowd amid fireworks and confetti.

The tour began in Tokyo on 5 May 2015 and ended in Melbourne on 12 December, spanning 85 shows. It was the highest-grossing tour of 2015, selling more than 2.27 million tickets and grossing over 250 million dollars, and critics praised Swift's stage presence and connection with her audience, while her parade of celebrity guests drew wide comment. Announced on 13 December 2015, the film premiered exclusively on Apple Music on 20 December 2015 and remained on the service until 22 May 2020; footage from it was also used in the music video for "New Romantics."

title: Snatched
tagline: Mess with me, mess with my mother.
overview: When her boyfriend dumps Emily, a spontaneous woman in her 30s, she persuades her ultra-cautious mom to accompany her on a vacation to Ecuador. plot:
Recently fired from her job and dumped by her rock musician boyfriend, Emily Middleton is determined to enjoy a previously planned non-refundable trip to Ecuador. Learning of her relationship status from social media, her mother, Linda, tells her to come home in order to move on, where she reunites with her agoraphobic brother, Jeffrey. Initially refusing, Linda agrees to go on the trip with her daughter.
In Ecuador, after they check into the upscale hotel, Emily meets a handsome man named James at the hotel bar, and they begin a relationship. After one night of drinking and dancing with James, Emily and her mother take a sightseeing day trip with him. During their ride, a white van rams James' Jeep and the masked men abduct Emily and Linda. James escapes, but Linda suspects he was in on the kidnapping plot from the start. Emily awakens inside a cell and begins to panic, while Linda tries to calm herself by reading men's magazines. The leader, Hector Morgado, contacts Jeffrey and demands $100,000 in ransom money. Morgado then has his nephew take both women away from the kidnappers' hideout to another location. They manage to escape from their captors' car and stow away into a passing truck. As it drives away, Emily kills the leader's nephew who is chasing them by pounding his head with a shovel. The truck's driver then stops his truck and leaves them both in the middle of the jungle.
They find a phone at a nearby bar, where they call the U.S. State Department officer Morgan Russell, saying that they are in peril, and Morgan advises them to go to the US Embassy in Bogotá, Colombia. They meet a rugged-looking American named Roger Simmons. He agrees to help them find the consulate. After the three share a meal, Morgado and his men track them down. Morgado is about to kill them both as revenge for his only nephew's death, but Linda distracts him while Emily retrieves a nearby spear gun with which to threaten him. As she retrieves it, she accidentally fires it, killing Morgado's only son. They manage to escape with Simmons onto a boat. Soon, however, they are forced off the boat when the captain detects another boat nearby that is looking for the two women.
Meanwhile, Jeffrey, learning that his mother and sister have been kidnapped, calls Morgan at the State Department, saying he will join forces with the agents in order to find his mother and sister. Morgan reluctantly agrees. In Colombia, Emily, Linda, and Simmons hike through the jungle until Simmons falls to his death from a cliff. Later, Emily passes out from the effects of a tapeworm infestation. After a local village doctor removes the tapeworm from her body, Morgado and his men track them down again. They spot a zip line and decide to use it to escape. Unfortunately, the zip line is good for only one person. Linda forces Emily to leave her behind and is recaptured.
Emily safely arrives at the US Consulate.

The Straw Hat Pirates' arrival on Nebulandia is also a part of Kōmei's plan.
plot:
One Piece: Adventure of Nebulandia is a 2015 Japanese animated television special based on the One Piece manga and anime and produced by Toei Animation. Directed by Konosuke Uda, the original series director of the One Piece anime, from a screenplay by Atsuhiro Tomioka, it was broadcast on 19 December 2015 in the Saturday Premium slot as the sixth One Piece special in that slot, following Episode of Sabo earlier that year. Unlike specials that retell manga arcs, it is an original story, and it brings back the Foxy Pirates, the crew the Straw Hats defeated in the anime's Davy Back Fight arc, with new members. It was released on Blu-ray and DVD in March 2016.

Sailing in the New World, Monkey D. Luffy and the Straw Hat Pirates are challenged by Captain Foxy to a Davy Back Fight rematch. The contest is a trap devised by Kōmei, a brilliant strategist who has recently joined Foxy's crew. During an eating contest, Zoro and Sanji consume a strange mushroom that saps their strength and turns them into good-for-nothings, and the pair are captured and carried away. Chasing their friends, the Straw Hats reach Nebulandia, an island shrouded in a mist formed from sea water that, like seastone, neutralises the powers of Devil Fruit users. Their arrival is exactly what Kōmei planned.

Kōmei is in fact a vice admiral of the Navy and a special operations strategist who infiltrated the Foxy Pirates by deliberately losing to them. Having lost his home town to pirates as a child, he despises them and dreams of proving that ordinary people without powers can defeat Devil Fruit users through cunning, thereby changing the Navy itself. Luffy is forced into an uneasy alliance with his old Davy Back rival Foxy for the rescue. Using the island's terrain and a series of traps, especially the pitfalls he favours, Kōmei captures Robin, Franky and Usopp, but Brook and Chopper, searching for an antidote to the mushroom, foil his attempt to seize Luffy. In the final battle, Kōmei floods his base with sea water to weaken Luffy, but Foxy's Slow-Slow Beam and a pitfall turn the tables, and Luffy defeats him with a decisive blow.

The regular voice cast returns, led by Mayumi Tanaka as Luffy, Kazuya Nakai as Zoro and Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji, with Toshio Shimada as Foxy. Ichikawa Ennosuke voices Kōmei, a role he modelled on the Three Kingdoms strategist Zhuge Liang, while Hoka Kinoshita plays another new crew member who is secretly a Navy officer.

title: The Love Witch
tagline: She loved men... to death
overview: A modern-day witch uses spells and magic to get men to fall in love with her, with deadly consequences.
plot:
The Love Witch is a 2016 American campy horror comedy film written and directed by Anna Biller. The film is a loving homage to 1960s Technicolor films, particularly those of Roger Corman and Russ Meyer.

At its core, The Love Witch explores the theme of toxic masculinity and the objectification of women in society. The main character, Elaine, is a modern-day witch who uses magic to seduce men, only to ultimately destroy them with her charms. However, as the film progresses, it becomes clear that Elaine's actions are motivated by a deep-seated desire for validation and acceptance from men.

The film also critiques the societal norms of the 1960s, particularly those related to beauty standards and femininity. The characters in the film embody the idealized feminine roles of the time, with Elaine being the ultimate femme fatale. However, as the story unfolds, it becomes clear that these roles are suffocating and limiting for women.

Furthermore, The Love Witch is a commentary on the commodification of sex and the ways in which women's bodies are objectified and exploited for male pleasure. Elaine's magic is a metaphor for the ways in which women are forced to use their bodies as objects of desire in order to survive.

Throughout the film, Biller uses vibrant colors, lush costumes, and over-the-top performances to create a sense of nostalgia and campiness. However, beneath its playful surface, The Love Witch is a biting critique of patriarchal society and the ways in which women are forced to navigate a world that is hostile to their desires and agency.

Ultimately, The Love Witch is a film about female empowerment and the importance of self-love and acceptance. Elaine's journey is one of self-discovery and growth, as she learns to reject the toxic norms of society and forge her own path.

plot:
One Piece Film: Gold is a Japanese animated adventure film based on the popular manga and anime series "One Piece" created by Eiichiro Oda. The film was produced by Toei Animation and directed by Kiyoshi Matsuda.

The story takes place after the events of the Dressrosa Arc in the One Piece manga and anime series. Monkey D. Luffy, the main protagonist, is on a quest to find the legendary treasure known as "One Piece" that will grant him the title of Pirate King. Luffy's crew, the Straw Hat Pirates, are also searching for the treasure.

The film begins with Luffy and his crew arriving in the city of Gold Town, where they meet a young boy named Trafalgar Law, who is on a mission to find the legendary "Gold" that will grant him immense power. Law is revealed to be the son of Shanks, one of the Seven Warlords of the Sea, and has inherited his father's powers.

As Luffy and his crew search for the treasure, they become entangled in a conflict between Law and the World Government, who seek to capture Law and use his powers for their own gain. The Straw Hats soon discover that the "Gold" is actually a powerful artifact known as the "Will of D." which has the power to grant immense strength and abilities.

Throughout the film, Luffy and his crew face numerous challenges and battles against the World Government's agents, including the ruthless Admiral Kizaru. Along the way, they also meet new allies, such as Trafalgar Law's sister, Boa Hancock, who becomes a valuable member of the Straw Hats.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that the "Gold" is actually a powerful artifact created by the ancient civilization known as the "Poneglyphs." The Poneglyphs were said to hold the secrets of the world and the location of the One Piece treasure. However, the World Government seeks to use the "Will of D." for their own gain, leading to a climactic battle between Luffy and Law.

In the end, Luffy and his crew successfully defeat the World Government's agents and claim the "Gold," which is revealed to be a powerful artifact that holds the secrets of the world. The film concludes with Luffy and his crew setting sail once again, determined to find the One Piece treasure and become the Pirate King.

Overall, One Piece Film: Gold is an action-packed adventure film that explores themes of power, friendship, and the pursuit of one's dreams. With its stunning animation and engaging storyline, it is a must-see for fans of the One Piece series.

title: Planetarium
tagline: You never know what's about to change...
overview: In 1930s France, two sisters who are thought to be able to communicate with ghosts meet a visionary producer while performing in Paris.
plot:
In the late 1930s, two American sisters, Laura and Kate Barlow, travel to France where they perform séances at cabarets with Laura hosting the session and Kate channeling the spirits. A public performance of theirs is seen by French film producer Andre Korben. Impressed by their act, he books them for a private session and is moved by the spirit that visits him.
Feeling stifled by the lack of innovation in the French film industry, Korben convinces investors and his team to film a séance as it happens. Unfortunately for Korben, the reels look ridiculous. But the director is drawn to Laura, who, despite not being a spiritualist, has a face that photographs well. The film team conceives of a conventional script in which Laura plays a medium who channels the spirit of a widower's wife and the three become locked in a love triangle with the widower unsure if he is falling in love with his former wife or the medium.
Laura and Kate move in with Korben, who is generous and kind to them. However, he continues to hold private séances with Kate, much to Laura's displeasure. (She fears, rightly, that Korben's interest in the spirit world is sexual.) Eventually, Laura is forced to leave for the coast to continue filming. Korben takes Kate to a metaphysical scientist and films their sessions together.
On the coast, Laura realizes that the rise of anti-semitism means the tides are turning against Korben. Rumours that he once performed in porn abound; and someone writes that she is a Jew's whore on her mirror. When Korben and Kate arrive to reunite with Laura, Korben shows his producers and investors the film of him and Kate which shows nothing. The director walks off the film and blames the money Korben has wasted chasing ghosts as an excuse. Meanwhile, Kate falls ill and reveals that she hasn't been faking but really can see ghosts. She believes this is because she is dying. Kate has leukemia, which is a death sentence at the time.
Korben is jailed for his wasted investments and the trial strips him of his French citizenship.
Years later, Kate is dead; and Korben has been sent to a death camp in "the East". Laura runs into Eva, an actress she once knew, who helps her get a part in a film working with her former director. No longer involved with spiritualism or Korben, Laura's film career in Nazi era France is assured.

title: I, Daniel Blake
tagline: My name is Daniel Blake. I am a man, not a dog.
overview: A middle aged carpenter, who requires state welfare after injuring himself, is joined by a single mother in a similar scenario.
plot:
Daniel Blake, a widowed 59-year-old joiner from Newcastle, has had a heart attack. Though his doctor has not allowed him to return to work, he is deemed fit to do so after a Work Capability Assessment and is denied Employment and Support Allowance. Daniel is frustrated to learn that his doctor was not contacted about this decision and thus applies for an appeal, a process Daniel finds difficult because he must complete forms online and is not computer literate.
Daniel befriends Katie Morgan, a single mother, after she is sanctioned for arriving late to her Jobcentre appointment. Katie and her children have just moved to Newcastle from a homeless shelter in London, as there is no affordable accommodation. Daniel helps the family by repairing objects, teaching them how to heat rooms without electricity, and crafting wooden toys for the children.
During a food bank visit, Katie breaks down crying, having become overwhelmed by hunger due to feeding her children instead of herself. After she is caught shoplifting at a supermarket, a security guard secretly offers Katie work as a prostitute. Daniel surprises her at the brothel where she goes to work and begs her to give up the job, but Katie tearfully insists she has no other way to feed her children.
As a condition for receiving Jobseeker's Allowance, Daniel must keep looking for work. He refuses a job at a garden centre because his doctor will not allow him to work yet. When his work coach tells him he must work harder to find a job or be sanctioned, Daniel spray paints "I, Daniel Blake, demand my appeal date before I starve" on the side of the building. Daniel earns the support of bystanders, including other people claiming benefits, but is arrested and cautioned by the police.
Daniel sells most of his belongings and becomes a recluse but is pulled out of his depression by Katie's daughter, Daisy, who brings him a homemade meal to repay Daniel for his kindness. On the day of Daniel's appeal, Katie accompanies him to the tribunal, where a welfare adviser tells Daniel that his case looks promising. Upon seeing the judge and doctor who will decide his fate, Daniel becomes anxious and excuses himself to use the toilet, where he suffers another heart attack and dies.
Later, Katie reads a eulogy at his public health funeral, including a speech he had intended to read at his appeal. The speech describes his feelings about how the welfare system failed him, and states, "I am not a blip on a computer screen or a national insurance number, I am a man."

title: Toni Erdmann
tagline: Life is just passing by...
overview: Without warning a father comes to visit his daughter abroad. He believes that she lost her humor and therefore surprises her with a rampage of jokes.
plot:
Winfried Conradi is a divorced music teacher from Aachen with a passion for bizarre pranks involving several fake personas. Following the death of his beloved dog, he decides to reconnect with his daughter, Ines, who is pursuing a career in business consulting. Ines is working in Bucharest, Romania, on an outsourcing project in the oil industry. Consumed by her work, she seems to have little time for her family.
Winfried spontaneously travels to Bucharest and waits for Ines in the lobby of an office complex. After several hours, she finally appears, accompanied by several of her client's board members and on the way to a meeting. Winfried puts on sunglasses and fake teeth as a playful disguise, and approaches the group from the side while hiding behind a newspaper. Ines ignores him, but meets with him briefly after work and invites him to a business reception at the US Embassy.
In the evening, Winfried and Ines attend the reception, where they meet Henneberg, a German oil company CEO with whom Ines wishes to secure a consulting contract. Ines tries to gain Henneberg's attention, but Henneberg seems more interested in her father. Winfried tells Henneberg that he has hired a replacement daughter because Ines is always busy. To Ines's surprise, Henneberg invites Winfried and Ines for drinks, along with his entourage. At the bar, Henneberg once again brushes Ines aside and makes fun of Winfried.
After several days, Ines and Winfried are struggling to get along. Stressed out from work, Ines oversleeps, missing a planned rendezvous with clients, and blames her father for not waking her up. Feeling alienated and unwanted, he leaves in a taxi for the airport. Ines continues with her work as normal, and several days later arranges to meet two female friends at a bar. While Ines and her friends are chatting, a man approaches and introduces himself as "Toni Erdmann". The man is clearly Winfried in a wig and false teeth, but Ines does not let on. Her two friends politely engage "Erdmann" in conversation; he explains that he is a "life coach" and consultant visiting Bucharest to attend the funeral of his friend's turtle.
Ines is increasingly frustrated and unfulfilled in her work and personal life, but continues to encounter "Erdmann" sporadically at parties or outside her office. At first Ines is angry with her father, and accuses him of trying to "ruin" her, but as time goes on she comes to see the value of her father's interventions in her life, and plays along with the ruse. "Erdmann" accompanies her on a night out with her work friends, and eventually even accompanies her to a business meeting. In turn, "Erdmann" takes Ines to a Romanian family's Easter party, where he forces her into a reluctant performance of Whitney Houston's "Greatest Love of All". After singing, Ines promptly rushes off.
Back at her flat, Ines is preparing to host a business team-building brunch to celebrate her birthday.

title: After the Storm
overview: Ryota is an unpopular writer although he won a literary award 15 years ago. Now, Ryota works as a private detective. He is divorced from his ex-wife Kyoko and he has an 11-year-old son Shingo. His mother Yoshiko lives alone at her apartment. One day, Ryota, his ex-wife Kyoko, and son Shingo gather at Yoshiko's apartment. A typhoon passes and the family must stay there all night long.
plot:
After the Storm (Japanese: 海よりもまだ深く, Umi yori mo Mada Fukaku, "Even Deeper than the Sea") is a 2016 Japanese family drama film written, directed and edited by Hirokazu Kore-eda. Hiroshi Abe stars as a failed novelist, with Kirin Kiki as his mother, Yoko Maki as his former wife and Taiyo Yoshizawa as his son. It premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2016 Cannes Film Festival and was released in Japan on May 21, 2016.

Ryota once won a minor literary prize for his only novel, and still clings to the idea that he is a serious writer. In reality, he works at a small private detective agency, where he sometimes supplements his income by blackmailing the people he is hired to investigate, and squanders his money on gambling, leaving him unable to pay child support. He turns down an offer to write for a manga series, considering it beneath him, while telling people he is researching his next book.

Since the recent death of Ryota's father, a gambler like his son, his widowed mother, Yoshiko, lives alone and seems to be moving on, taking up hobbies with other elderly women. Ryota visits her frequently. His sister, Chinatsu, suspects his motives, and he in turn suspects that she is sponging off their mother. When Ryota goes to an old hiding place where his mother used to conceal money from his father, he finds only cardboard and a teasing note from his sister.

Meanwhile, Ryota's former wife, Kyoko, has lost patience with his excuses, and threatens to stop his monthly visits with their young son, Shingo, unless he pays what he owes. Ryota, jealous of Kyoko's new boyfriend, fears that her remarriage would cost him his relationship with his son. During one of his visits with Shingo, a typhoon strikes, and Ryota, Kyoko and the boy are forced to spend the night at his mother's apartment. As the storm rages, Kyoko tells Ryota that their marriage is truly over, explaining that adults cannot live on love alone and that he never acted like a family man when it mattered. Accepting this, Ryota takes Shingo out into the storm to shelter in a playground structure, as he once did with his own father, and the two share a rare moment of connection. In the morning, the storm has passed, and they go their separate ways.

After the Storm received critical acclaim, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 96% approval and a consensus praising its timeless observations on parental responsibility, personal bonds and forgiveness.

title: Dunkirk
tagline: Survival is Victory
overview: The story of the miraculous evacuation of Allied soldiers from Belgium, Britain, Canada and France, who were cut off and surrounded by the German army from the beaches and harbour of Dunkirk between May 26th and June 4th 1940 during World War II.
plot:
Dunkirk is a 2017 war drama film directed by Christopher Nolan, produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, and distributed by Warner Bros. The film is set during World War II and tells the story of the Dunkirk evacuation, also known as the Miracle of Dunkirk.

The film begins on May 26, 1940, with a dramatic sequence showing the German army's invasion of France. The British Expeditionary Force (BEF), led by General Lord Gort, is trapped in Dunkirk, a coastal town in northern France. As the Germans close in, the BEF is surrounded and outnumbered.

The story then shifts to three main plot threads: the evacuation of Allied soldiers from Dunkirk, the rescue efforts by the Royal Air Force (RAF), and the experiences of a young British soldier named Tommy (Fionn Whitehead). The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, with each thread intersecting and overlapping at various points.

The evacuation of Allied soldiers from Dunkirk is depicted as a chaotic and desperate effort. Thousands of soldiers are stranded on the beaches of Dunkirk, with no clear way to escape. The British Navy, led by Admiral Bertram Ramsay (Kenneth Branagh), launches a massive rescue operation, with ships and boats converging on the beach to evacuate the soldiers.

Meanwhile, the RAF is engaged in a fierce dogfight with German aircraft, trying to protect the evacuation fleet from enemy attack. The film's aerial sequences are intense and suspenseful, showcasing the bravery and skill of the RAF pilots.

Tommy, who has been separated from his family during the evacuation, finds himself on the beach, struggling to survive amidst the chaos. He joins a group of other soldiers, including Mr. Dawson (Mark Rylance), a civilian who is helping to evacuate the soldiers. As they try to escape, Tommy and Mr. Dawson face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, enemy fire, and personal losses.

As the evacuation continues, the film's narrative builds towards a dramatic climax. The British Navy launches a final push to clear the beach of German forces, while the RAF provides cover with its aircraft. The soldiers are finally able to escape, but not before many have lost their lives or been separated from their loved ones.

The film ends with Tommy, who has survived the evacuation, watching as the last of the ships depart from Dunkirk. He is reunited with his family, who had been searching for him throughout the ordeal. The final shot is of a small boat, which is revealed to be carrying Mr. Dawson's body, symbolizing the sacrifice and bravery of those who helped evacuate the soldiers.

Throughout the film, Nolan uses innovative cinematography and editing techniques to create a sense of tension and urgency. The film's score, composed by Hans Zimmer, adds to the emotional impact of the story. Overall, Dunkirk is a powerful and moving tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of those who fought in World War II.

tagline: Can you forget your past... no matter how dark it is?
overview: On a dark night, the Japanese police is raided by a spy. Different countries' intelligence agencies - such as England's MI6, Germany's BDN, and America's CIA - as well as the FBI's secret files are going to be taken, but public safety officers lead by Tooru Amuro arrive just in time. The spy steals a car and escapes. The next day, Conan and his friends go to a newly-remodeled aquarium in Tokyo. Under the main attraction, a Ferris wheel, Conan finds an attractive woman alone and injured. Her left and right eyes are different colors.
plot:
A Black Organization spy, codenamed Curaçao, infiltrates the NPA Security Bureau Office, stealing the NOC list of MI6, BND, CSIS, FBI and CIA agents working undercover in the Black Organization. Yuya Kazami, an officer of the Public Security Bureau, catches her red handed and Curaçao is forced to run away. Rei Furuya, also known as Bourbon, attempts to stop her from escaping and later engages in a car chase on the Rainbow Bridge, with Akai Shuichi joining later. The car chase ends up causing a havoc, and Akai decides to shoot the tire of Curaçao's vehicle, causing the car to crash and fall off the bridge. Curaçao escapes from the car as it is falling and lands in the water. She later surfaces at Tohto Aquarium near the crash site.
The next day, the Detective Boys discover Curaçao at Tohto Aquarium. She is suffering from amnesia and her phone is broken as a result of the car crash the day prior. Conan retrieves the broken phone and takes photos of Curaçao, sends the photos to Ran, who, in turn, sends them to the Tokyo Metropolitan Police, then hands the phone to Dr. Agasa so he can recover the data on it. The Detective Boys then decide to stay with Curaçao to help her regain her memory. After noticing Curaçao's perfect aiming skills while playing darts and her swift act of saving Genta from falling from high a place, Haibara and Conan notice that Curaçao is not an ordinary woman, and Haibara herself gets a sense that Curaçao is likely to be another Black Organization agent. The Bureau becomes aware that Curaçao appears to react to certain events in the Tohto Aquarium, and decides to take her back to the Aquarium. The same night, the Black Organization, who arrived by the Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey, knocks out the electricity for the entire aquarium and plan to intercept Curaçao when the Ferris wheel reaches the top. After Curaçao regains her memory by looking at the specific color patterns of the projected lights like she did earlier before, Yuya Kazami, who boarded the Ferris wheel with her, is knocked unconscious by her and she escapes.
