title: Duck Duck Goose
tagline: Family can be a wild ride
overview: After he’s grounded by an injury, a high-flying bachelor is saddled with two wide-eyed orphans as they come face-to-face with the dangers and beauty of the outside world.
plot:
Duck Duck Goose (Chinese: 妈妈咪鸭) is a 2018 animated adventure comedy film directed by Chris Jenkins, who wrote the original story and co-wrote the screenplay with Rob Muir, Scott Atkinson and Tegan West. An international co-production between the United States, China and the United Kingdom, it features the voices of Jim Gaffigan as Peng, a self-absorbed swan goose, Zendaya and Lance Lim as the Mandarin duckling siblings Chi and Chao, Greg Proops as the villainous Pallas's cat Banzou, Reggie Watts as the flying squirrel Carl, and Carl Reiner as Larry, a softshell turtle, with Natasha Leggero, Stephen Fry, Craig Ferguson and Diedrich Bader.

Peng is a carefree goose whose reckless attitude irritates Bing, the leader of his flock, which departs on its migration across China while he sleeps. One of his careless stunts separates two ducklings, Chi and Chao, from their own flock as it travels to a fabled place called Pleasant Valley. Seeing Peng drive off the predatory Banzou, the ducklings shelter beside him for the night. Startled to find them, Peng flies off carelessly, crashes into a gong and breaks his wing. Unable to fly and afraid of predators, he decides to use the ducklings as cover while he makes his way back to his flock, and they reluctantly join him.

Through a string of misadventures Peng grows fond of the ducklings, but when they encounter his flock, Chi and Chao discover his selfish motives and the two parties go their separate ways. Peng is knocked out of the sky by Carl, who fits him with a makeshift wing, and he sets off to find the ducklings. They meanwhile reunite with their flock and learn that Pleasant Valley is really a restaurant that cooks ducklings. Peng rescues them, but they are separated again in the escape, and Banzou takes the ducklings hostage. Peng is badly hurt fighting him, and Chi and Chao finish off the cat by launching him into the sky on a rocket. Carrying the weakened Peng through a snowstorm toward the geese's spring, the ducklings use a honk he taught them to summon Jingjing, Peng's love interest, who rescues him. Bing welcomes the ducklings into the flock, along with a newly responsible Peng.

The film opened in China on March 9, 2018. A North American theatrical release planned by Open Road Films for April 2018 was canceled when the company closed, and Netflix released it in North America on July 20, 2018. It grossed about $15.3 million worldwide in its initial run and received negative reviews from critics.

title: The Favourite
tagline: A bawdy, brilliant triumph.
overview: England, early 18th century. The close relationship between Queen Anne and Sarah Churchill is threatened by the arrival of Sarah's cousin, Abigail Hill, resulting in a bitter rivalry between the two cousins to be the Queen's favourite.
plot:
The Favourite is a 2018 period drama film directed by Yorgos Lanthimos, starring Olivia Colman, Emma Stone, and Rachel Weisz. The movie takes place in the early 18th century, during the reign of Queen Anne (Olivia Colman), who rules England with an iron fist.

The story begins with Queen Anne's close relationship with her adviser, Sarah Churchill (Rachel Weisz). However, as time passes, a new servant named Abigail Hill (Emma Stone) arrives at court. Abigail is a clever and ambitious young woman from a lower social class, determined to rise through the ranks of society.

Abigail quickly catches the eye of the Queen, who becomes infatuated with her charming personality and wit. As Abigail's influence grows, she begins to manipulate the Queen into making decisions that benefit herself and her family. Meanwhile, Sarah Churchill's power and influence begin to wane as a result of Abigail's rise.

As tensions between the three women escalate, the palace becomes a battleground for power and loyalty. The Queen is torn between her affection for Abigail and her duty to her adviser, Sarah. Abigail, on the other hand, uses her charm and cunning to turn the Queen against Sarah, ultimately leading to her downfall.

Throughout the film, Lanthimos employs his signature deadpan humor and absurdity, often using long takes and unsettling silences to create a sense of unease. The performances by Colman, Stone, and Weisz are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

One of the most striking aspects of The Favourite is its exploration of themes such as power, ambition, and female relationships. The film raises questions about the nature of femininity and how women are perceived in society, particularly during this time period.

Ultimately, Abigail's machinations lead to a tragic confrontation between the three women. In the end, only one woman emerges victorious, but at what cost? The Favourite is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that offers a fresh perspective on a pivotal moment in history.

The film received widespread critical acclaim, with many praising its performances, direction, and screenplay. It won numerous awards, including several Academy Awards, and cemented the status of Yorgos Lanthimos as one of the most innovative filmmakers working today.

title: The Salesman
overview: Forced out of their apartment due to dangerous works on a neighboring building, Emad and Rana move into a new flat in the center of Tehran. An incident linked to the previous tenant will dramatically change the young couple’s life.
plot:
Emad and Rana are a married couple who both work in the theatre, currently starring in a production of Death of a Salesman by Arthur Miller, with Emad portraying Willy Loman and Rana playing Linda. Emad is also a popular instructor at a local school, where the youth joke about him being a "salesman." One night, their apartment begins to collapse and they flee the building with the other residents. Knowing they need another place to live, their fellow actor Babak secures another apartment for them, where a woman has recently moved out, although she left in a hurry abandoning numerous belongings. The couple moves into the apartment and places the previous owner's belongings outside. One night, Rana is home alone and begins bathing. When Emad returns, he finds she is missing and the bathroom is covered with blood. He rushes to the hospital, where he is informed by his neighbours about his wife's condition and is told to change the apartment's locks. It becomes apparent that Rana has not had an accident, but has been assaulted by an intruder, to whom she opened the door using the intercom, thinking it was Emad returning home. Emad also learns from neighbours that the previous tenant was a prostitute who had conflicts with her clients.

Rana returns home, but suffers from trauma and is reluctant to go to the police. She does not bathe, fearing to go into the bathroom again, and in the middle of a performance, breaks down in tears and leaves the stage. Although she does not remember the face of her attacker, Emad finds the culprit left his car keys, which he matches to a pick-up parked outside. The attacker also left behind a mobile phone and some money which Rana purchased groceries with, thinking Emad had left it for her. Emad increasingly blames Babak for hiding the truth about the former tenant. After he hears a loving message from Babak on the previous tenant's answering machine, he calls Babak's character Charley a degenerate in the midst of a performance, although this is not in Miller's script.
Finally, Emad turns to one of his students, whose father used to work for the police. He is able to trace the truck to a man named Majid. He pretends to need a mover to lure Majid to their now empty old apartment, but Majid's prospective father-in-law arrives instead. Gradually, it becomes apparent the older man was himself the intruder, though he denies attacking Rana, implying he simply startled her. Emad calls the old man's family to the apartment, and locks him in a small room to wait, intending to reveal his true character to them all. When he opens the room the old man appears to be having heart trouble and Emad calls Rana in a panic. When Rana learns what Emad intends, she says it will be over between them if he pursues his revenge.
When the family arrives they believe they have been called to a medical emergency, thanking Emad for saving his life.

title: The Girl with All the Gifts

tagline: Our greatest threat is our only hope.
overview: In the future, a strange fungus has changed nearly everyone into a thoughtless, flesh-eating monster. When a scientist and a teacher find a girl who seems to be immune to the fungus, they all begin a journey to save humanity.
plot:
In the near future, humanity has been ravaged by a disease caused by a parasitic fungus transmitted by bodily fluids. Over the prior decade, most of humanity that was infected turned into fast mindless zombies called "hungries". The only remaining hope is a cure that could be obtained from research on a small group of carrier, but apparently normal, children.
The children are imprisoned by a group of soldiers (led by Sergeant Eddie Parks), and go to school at an army base in the Home Counties, where they are experimented on by Dr. Caroline Caldwell. Helen Justineau is responsible for educating and studying the children. Among them is an exceptional girl named Melanie, whom Justineau grows particularly close to, thus forming a special bond.
When Melanie is about to be dissected, the base is overrun by hungries and the operating lab is breached. Melanie escapes and wanders outside, where soldiers are being violently attacked. Melanie and Justineau board an escaping truck with an injured Caldwell, Sergeant Parks, and two surviving soldiers, Gallagher and Dillon. Melanie is restrained and muzzled to prevent her from biting the others. Dillon is killed when hungries attack as the group stops for water, and the truck is disabled when a fuel line is broken.
The group reaches London by foot and makes their way through a swarm of dormant hungries using a "blocker" gel that masks their scent, rendering them largely invisible. They take shelter in an abandoned hospital for the night. Caldwell reveals to Melanie that second-generation hungries, or neonates, were discovered after babies killed their infected mothers by eating organs to get out of the womb, and while they crave living flesh, they still think and learn, as the fungus has a symbiotic relationship with those born infected.
In the morning, the group realises they have been surrounded by hungries. Melanie, as a second-generation hungry, is ignored by them and therefore goes to explore abandoned houses, eating a stray cat during her time out. She helps the group by leading the hungries away with a stray dog so the group can escape.
As they progress through London, they come across piles of infected bodies encircling the BT Tower, which has been overgrown by a massive fungal growth. Caldwell explains that the growth contains pods which, upon maturity, could release airborne spores that would end humankind. They take shelter in an abandoned mobile laboratory that was sent into the city earlier by the military authorities.
Caldwell, injured and dying of sepsis, reasons that she can save the human race by sacrificing Melanie to complete her vaccine research in the lab. As the group runs out of food, Gallagher ventures into the city on a supply run, but is killed by a tribe of feral hungry children who have learned to trick uninfected people with a trail of food cans. When Parks and Justineau are surrounded by the feral children, Melanie fights and handcuffs the leader and kills him with a bat.

title: Robin Hood
tagline: The legend you know. The story you don't.
overview: A war-hardened Crusader and his Moorish commander mount an audacious revolt against the corrupt English crown.
plot:
Robin Hood is a 2018 American action-adventure film directed by Otto Bathurst and written by Ben Chandler and David James Kelly from Chandler's story, a modern retelling of the outlaw legend that centers on Robin's training by John. First announced in February 2015 with a Joby Harold script and Leonardo DiCaprio's Appian Way producing, the project was acquired by Lionsgate and cast Taron Egerton as Robin later that year. Eve Hewson, Jamie Foxx and Ben Mendelsohn followed, and filming ran from February to May 2017. The film was released by Lionsgate's Summit Entertainment on November 21, 2018.

Robin of Loxley, an aristocrat and skilled longbowman, lives in Nottingham with Marian until the corrupt Sheriff drafts him into the Third Crusade. Four years later, after he fails to stop his commander, Guy of Gisbourne, from executing unarmed prisoners, including a teenage boy, he is sent home accused of treason. He returns to learn from Friar Tuck that the Sheriff declared him dead and seized his estate to fund the war at the urging of Cardinal Franklin, while the townspeople have been driven into a mining settlement. Marian is now with Will Tillman, a would-be leader of the commoners. The father of the boy Robin tried to save, Yahya, who says his name translates as John, proposes that they end the war by stealing back the people's money.

After hard training in his ruined manor, Robin robs the Sheriff's coffers as a hooded thief nicknamed the Hood while posing as a frivolous lord loyal to the regime. He and Marian, who recognizes him by his voice, discover that the Church is secretly funding the Saracen army in order to topple the king and seize power. John is captured and tortured but reveals nothing. Robin reveals himself to the commoners, who embrace him, and seizes a caravan carrying the Sheriff's fortune to the Saracens while Will stages a riot. After Will, scarred during the fighting, sees Marian kiss Robin, he turns against them. Robin surrenders to end the bloodshed, but John, disguised as a guard, kills the Sheriff, and the rebels retreat as outlaws to Sherwood Forest. The Cardinal then installs a vengeful Will as sheriff, and Robin dares him to come after them.

Egerton stars with Foxx as John, Mendelsohn as the Sheriff, Hewson as Marian, Tim Minchin as Tuck and Jamie Dornan as Will. Critics panned it, with 14% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and comparisons to King Arthur: Legend of the Sword. It grossed about $85 million against a $100 million budget.

title: Then Came You
tagline: Living in the moment is hard to do alone.
overview: An American hypochondriac who is working as a baggage handler is forced to confront his fears when a British teenager with a terminal illness enlists him to help her carry out her eccentric bucket list.
plot:
Then Came You, also known as Departures, is an American romantic comedy-drama of 2018 directed by Peter Hutchings and written by Fergal Rock. Asa Butterfield plays Calvin Lewis, a young hypochondriac, and Maisie Williams plays Skye Aitken, a teenager with terminal cancer, with Nina Dobrev as the flight attendant Izzy, Tyler Hoechlin as Calvin's brother Frank, David Koechner as their father and Margot Bingham as Frank's wife Lucy.

Skye has been told that her cancer is in its final stages and that she has little time left. Calvin, an airport baggage handler, has a crush on Izzy and lives in constant fear of dying. His doctor sends him to a cancer support group for perspective. There he meets Skye, who takes an instant interest in him, and although he tries to explain that he does not actually have cancer, the two become friends and he agrees to help her complete her list of things to do before she dies. At first irritated by her bluntness and unpredictability, Calvin comes to treasure her company, and as they spend more time together his fear of death begins to fade.

Skye arranges a date between Calvin and Izzy, telling Izzy that he has cancer too, and the pair start dating. Skye admits she always knew Calvin was healthy, but he hesitates to tell Izzy, fearing she only likes him for his illness. From Lucy, Skye learns that Calvin's mother withdrew from life after his twin sister was killed at the age of eight in a car crash while their mother was driving. When Calvin finally confesses the truth, Izzy, hurt by the lie, breaks up with him, and he sinks into depression until his father persuades him to return to work. Skye, meanwhile, loses her virginity to Will, a boy she has a crush on, and finds the experience a letdown.

When Skye collapses and is taken to the hospital, Lucy goes into labor at the same time, and Frank and Lucy ask Calvin and Skye to be their baby's godparents. Calvin panics, but Frank reminds him that Skye still needs him. With help from Izzy and Skye's parents, he helps her finish her list, and he tells her that he stopped celebrating his birthday for his mother's sake after his sister's death. After Skye dies, birthday cards from her arrive in the mail to make up for the ones he missed. Overcoming his fear of heights, Calvin takes a flight, exchanging hopeful glances with Izzy.

 The film premiered at the Woodstock Film Festival in October 2018 and was released by Shout! Factory on 1 February 2019, to mixed reviews.

He is now working as a coach at a local soccer school in Madrid, where he tries to teach young players the basics of the sport. However, his unorthodox coaching methods and lack of patience with his students make him unpopular among both the kids and their parents.

One day, Carlos receives an offer from a wealthy businessman named Juan (played by Luis Zahera) to coach his daughter, Frida (played by Blanca Suárez), in a series of high-stakes soccer matches. The catch is that Frida has never played soccer before, but she's determined to become the best player in Spain.

As Carlos begins working with Frida, he realizes that she's not just any ordinary student - she's a talented and feisty young woman who refuses to be told what to do. Despite their initial disagreements, Carlos starts to see potential in Frida and decides to help her develop her skills.

Throughout the movie, Carlos and Frida face numerous challenges as they prepare for the big matches. They encounter rival coaches, tough opponents, and even some personal struggles that threaten to derail their partnership. However, with each passing match, Carlos and Frida grow closer, both on and off the field.

As the stakes get higher, Carlos starts to realize that his feelings for Frida go beyond mere coaching. He begins to develop romantic feelings for her, but he's hesitant to express them, fearing it might compromise their professional relationship.

In the end, Carlos and Frida face off against their toughest opponents yet - a team of ruthless and experienced players who will stop at nothing to win. With Carlos' unorthodox tactics and Frida's determination, they manage to pull off an incredible comeback victory.

As the dust settles, Carlos finally confesses his feelings to Frida, and she reveals that she feels the same way. The movie ends with a heartwarming moment of tenderness between the two leads, as they share a kiss on the field.

Overall, No Manches Frida is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of love, friendship, and perseverance. With its lighthearted tone and engaging storyline, it's a great choice for anyone looking for a feel-good movie experience.

title: Bad Sister
tagline: How long has it been since your last confession?
overview: As a top student at St. Adeline's Catholic Boarding School, Zoe senses that something is not quite right about the school's new nun-- a sense proven to be true when it is revealed the "good' nun is an imposter with a fatal attraction to Zoe's brother.
plot:
Bad Sister is a 2015 American-Canadian thriller television film written and directed by Doug Campbell for Lifetime, produced with Johnson Production Group and Golden Oak Entertainment. It stars Alyshia Ochse as a woman posing as a nun, with Devon Werkheiser, Ryan Whitney Newman, Helen Eigenberg, Robert Leeshock, Lise Simms, Sloane Avery and James Handy. Although dated 2015, it premiered on Lifetime on 3 January 2016.

Jason Brady (Werkheiser), a teenager who posts videos of his songs online, is sent by his parents to a Catholic boarding school after wrecking his father's car; they disapprove of his musical ambitions. His studious sister Zoe (Newman) attends the same school. The new teacher, Sister Sophia (Ochse), is welcomed by the headmistress, Sister Rebecca (Eigenberg), but Zoe soon notices that she skips the morning prayer and knows little about the faith. In truth she is Laura, a disturbed woman who became obsessed with Jason through his videos, murdered the real Sister Sophia and took her identity. Under her habit she wears lingerie and makeup; she moves Jason's girlfriend Sara (Avery) away from him in class, threatens her, and lets the boy glimpse her undressing. She plants a joint that gets Sara suspended and hides whiskey in Jason's room so that he must stay at school over a weekend, seduces him and secretly films them together, then frames Zoe for cheating when the girl grows suspicious. After Sara returns, Laura kills her in the shower and stages it as an accident. At a family dinner, Zoe catches the "nun" in lie after lie, and Jason confesses the affair and the sex tape she is using against him. The siblings search her computer, discover her real name and seek out Sister Rebecca, only to find her knocked unconscious. Laura confronts them in the chapel, but Sister Rebecca intervenes and Jason stabs the impostor with a screwdriver.

Reviewers who cover Lifetime films responded warmly to its excesses. title: Miss Sloane
tagline: Make sure you surprise them.
overview: An ambitious lobbyist faces off against the powerful gun lobby in an attempt to pass gun control legislation.
plot:
Elizabeth Sloane is a workaholic cutthroat lobbyist who has been called before a congressional hearing led by Senator Ronald Sperling to answer questions about possible violations of Senate ethics rules during her tenure at Washington D.C. lobbying firm Cole Kravitz & Waterman.
Three months and one week earlier, Sloane's firm is approached by gun manufacturing representative Bill Sanford to lead the opposition to the proposed Heaton-Harris bill that would expand background checks on gun purchases, specifically by targeting female voters. Sloane ridicules Sanford's idea and is later approached by Rodolfo Schmidt, the head of rival lobbying firm Peterson Wyatt, to instead lead the effort in support of the bill. Sloane agrees and takes most of her staff along with her, though her closest associate Jane Molloy refuses to leave.
At Peterson Wyatt, Sloane selects Esme Manucharian to conduct the majority of the firm's media appearances, and they begin to make significant progress in garnering votes for the bill. Sloane confronts Esme with knowledge of her background as having survived a school shooting. Even though Esme does not want to disclose the information, Sloane reveals Esme's secret during a live television debate. Later, Esme is held up at gunpoint while leaving her office, but her attacker is shot dead by another civilian who is legally carrying a gun. Gun rights supporters capitalize on this event, which causes the Heaton-Harris bill to lose support in the Senate. This is compounded by the news of the Senate inquiry into Sloane's lobbying practices.
Returning to the congressional hearing, Senator Sperling produces a form requesting approval of overseas travel for a Senator. It was filed by a non-profit organization but completed in Sloane's handwriting, indicating she violated Senate ethics rules with her involvement, as a lobbyist, in arranging the travel. In answer to other questions, Sloane swears under oath that she has never practiced illegal wiretapping.
In her final statement at the hearing, Sloane admits she anticipated the opposition might attack her personally if Peterson Wyatt made too much progress with the Heaton-Harris bill. She reveals that she had someone (Molloy, her former assistant) secretly working for her, and that she did use a wiretap – which recorded Senator Sperling accepting bribes from her former boss George Dupont.
Ten months later, Sloane is visited by her lawyer in prison. The bill passed, Dupont and Sperling are under investigation, and he has petitioned for her early release. He asks if it was worth career suicide, she answers: better than suicide by career.

title: Amateur Night
tagline: Every job has pros and cons
overview: Guy Carter, an insecure expectant father unable to find work in his field, accepts a job driving hookers around Los Angeles. One long and crazy evening proves to our hero that he is, in fact, up to the task of fatherhood.
plot:
Amateur Night is a 2016 American crime sex comedy written and directed by Lisa Addario and Joe Syracuse, who drew on their own early experiences in Hollywood for the story. Jason Biggs stars alongside Jenny Mollen, Janet Montgomery, Ashley Tisdale and Bria Murphy. The film premiered in Los Angeles on July 25, 2016, and was released in American cinemas by Cinedigm in early August.

Guy Carter is an unemployed architect with a pregnant wife, Anne, and a growing pile of bills. Anne finds a Craigslist advertisement for a driver and sends him, against his wishes, to apply. Expecting to deliver pizzas, Guy discovers that he has been hired to chauffeur Nikki, a sex worker, around Los Angeles for the night. Their first stop is a regular client, a kinky doctor in Bel Air. When Nikki fails to return for hours, Guy breaks into the house, finds her tied up in what he assumes is a torture session and "rescues" her by spraying the doctor with air freshener; the man falls and hits his head, and the pair flee.

Calmed down by Nikki, Guy learns that he will receive a share of the night's takings and warms to the job. They pick up two of her colleagues, Jaxi and Fallon, and Guy is made to clean a bag of well-used sex toys before driving the women to a bachelor party at a luxury Beverly Hills hotel. There the women put Guy in charge of keeping a crowd of rowdy former fraternity brothers in line, and the evening descends into a series of increasingly explicit and humiliating episodes for him. When Anne goes into false labour, Guy steps out, only to be taken hostage by the vengeful doctor, armed with a syringe of paralysing drug, until Nikki turns the needle on him.

The party resumes until the women discover they have been robbed and hold the guests at gunpoint to retrieve their money. One of the men turns out to be an undercover police officer who tries to arrest Nikki, and Guy leads the police on a chase before crashing his car, and the group escapes by bus. As dawn breaks, Nikki hires Guy to design a house for her. Expecting police at his door, Guy finds instead that his car was repossessed before the police could trace it. The end credits play over re-enactments of incidents the filmmakers say really happened.

Critics panned the film; Rotten Tomatoes recorded no positive reviews from six critics, and it grossed only about $63,000.

title: The Edge of Seventeen
tagline: You're only young once… is it over yet?
overview: Two high school girls are best friends until one dates the other's older brother, who is totally his sister's nemesis.
plot:
The Edge of Seventeen is a coming-of-age comedy-drama film released in 2016, directed by Kelly Fremon Craig and produced by Lianne Halfon, Molly Smith, and Jennifer Ventimilia. The movie follows the life of Nadine Byrd (played by Hailee Steinfeld), a high school junior navigating her senior year while dealing with her complicated relationships and family dynamics.

The story begins with Nadine's mother, Mary (played by Kyra Sedgwick), who is recently divorced from her husband, Jim (played by Woody Harrelson). The tension between the two parents is palpable, and Nadine struggles to cope with the changes in her life. Her father has moved out, and she feels abandoned.

Nadine's best friend, Krista (played by Haley Lu Richardson), tries to be supportive, but their friendship is put to the test as they face various challenges together. The two girls try to navigate high school cliques, relationships, and social pressures while dealing with Nadine's emotional turmoil.

As the story unfolds, Nadine develops feelings for her classmate, Eric (played by Blake Jenner), who seems perfect on the surface but turns out to be shallow and unfaithful. Meanwhile, she also starts to develop a crush on her English teacher, Mr. Bruner (played by Tom Holland).

Throughout the film, Nadine's relationships with her family members are explored in depth. Her mother is portrayed as a complex character struggling to balance her own emotions and needs with those of her daughter. The tension between them is evident, but they also share moments of tenderness and understanding.

As the school year progresses, Nadine faces various setbacks, including a failed relationship and a disappointing college acceptance letter. However, she eventually finds solace in her friendship with Krista and begins to develop a stronger sense of self.

The film's climax revolves around Nadine's confrontation with Eric, who has been unfaithful to her. The scene is intense and emotional, showcasing Nadine's growth and resilience. In the end, Nadine comes to terms with her feelings and learns to move on from her past heartbreak.

The Edge of Seventeen received widespread critical acclaim for its authentic portrayal of teenage life, nuanced character development, and outstanding performances from the cast. The film's exploration of complex themes such as family dynamics, relationships, and identity resonated with audiences worldwide.

title: Jackie
tagline: I want them to see what they have done to Jack.
overview: An account of the days of First Lady, Jacqueline Kennedy, in the immediate aftermath of John F. Kennedy's assassination in 1963.
plot:
In 1963, a week after the assassination of United States President John F. Kennedy, a journalist visits his widow Jacqueline "Jackie" Kennedy for an interview at her home in Hyannis Port, Massachusetts regarding her husband's legacy. After Jackie reflects upon her 1962 televised tour of the White House, the journalist turns to inquiries about John F. Kennedy's assassination and its aftermath for Jackie and her family. She talks about events shortly prior to the assassination before describing her shock and horror in reaction.
Members of the White House close to the newly sworn-in president Lyndon B. Johnson and his wife Lady Bird are seen comforting Jackie in the aftermath aboard Air Force One. United States Attorney General and Jackie's brother-in-law, Robert F. Kennedy soon appears and shares her grief, escorting her back to Washington, D.C. Jackie expresses her deep concern for the well-being of her children in adjusting to the loss of their father.
Robert continues to support Jackie while dealing with his sadness and helps her in planning the funeral and looking after the family. She is seen struggling to sleep and becoming reliant on medications and alcohol. She is also seen regularly seeking spiritual counsel from a priest. Robert, along with President Johnson, Lady Bird, and members of the White House, witness the murder of Lee Harvey Oswald, the president's suspected killer, by Jack Ruby on live television.
Robert insists that Jackie not be informed of this by anyone but himself; he will tell her when he feels the time is right. However, she finds out about it almost immediately and condemns him for withholding it from her. After John F. Kennedy Jr.'s third birthday, Robert voices his fears to Jackie that her husband's short time as president will not be noted by future generations.
After the state funeral of John F. Kennedy, Jackie tells the priest she contemplated suicide following the assassination. She then admits to remembering what happened during the assassination and feels unbearable pain and guilt that she did not act in some way to protect her husband.
As the interview ends, Jackie makes it clear that she maintains the right to control which parts of the interview may come to press and which parts are to be withheld.
The film concludes with Jackie having her miscarried and stillborn children's coffins being re-interred next to her husband's grave at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia.

title: Morgan
tagline: Don't let it out
overview: A corporate risk-management consultant must determine whether or not to terminate an artificial being's life that was made in a laboratory environment.
plot:
Lee Weathers is a "risk-management specialist" for genetic-engineering company SynSect. She arrives at a rural site hosting its L-9 project, an artificial being with nanotechnology-infused synthetic DNA named Morgan. The "hybrid biological organism with the capacity for autonomous decision making and sophisticated emotional responses" is smarter than humans and has matured quickly, walking and talking within a month and already physically equivalent to a young teenage girl despite being born only five years before.
The cold and precise Weathers, who insists on calling Morgan "it", is at the site to assess the project while a psychologist evaluates Morgan, who has used a pen to stab Dr. Kathy Grieff in the eye. Over dinner with the team of eight scientists, Weathers and project leaders Dr. Lui Cheng and Dr. Simon Ziegler discuss an incident in Helsinki involving Cheng in which 21 SynSect researchers were killed in an hour by "crude prototypes".
Lee learns that Morgan attacked Grieff when she was prohibited from leaving her room, a glass cell, after killing a deer impaled on a tree branch, out of compassion for its suffering, while exploring outside. The scientists have reared Morgan from birth following two failed attempts, and most consider her to be their child; Grieff defends Morgan to Weathers despite her injury, and Dr. Amy Menser wants to resume taking her on outings. Menser promises to take Morgan to a nearby lake that she describes as wonderful; the behavioral therapist understands that Morgan is, despite her intellect and physical appearance and abilities, emotionally strange. Although Morgan considers Cheng to be her "mother", the scientist is pessimistic about the project; she admits to Weathers that she ended the outings as it is cruel to expose Morgan to a world she cannot be allowed to enter.
Psychologist and artificial intelligence expert Dr. Alan Shapiro arrives to assess Morgan and quickly defies the scientists' requests to stay outside Morgan's room for the assessment. When Shapiro aggressively taunts Morgan as part of his evaluation, she looks at her hand, becomes angry and spontaneously kills him. Weathers tranquilizes Morgan after a brief escape, and decides that she is too unpredictable and must be terminated. The scientists refuse to kill Morgan; before Weathers can do so, they shoot her with a tranquilizer dart and imprison her in the cell in which Morgan was held. The scientists plan to escape with Morgan, but after waking, Morgan, believing they have betrayed her starts a killing spree. She kills Darren with a lethal injection, shoots Ted in the chest and the head, and beats Brenda to death with a pistol. Ziegler, unaware of the murders, commits suicide after realizing his life's work turned into a failure.
In the scientists' house, Cheng records an apology for the failure of the project.

title: Barbie: Spy Squad
tagline: See it, then be it.
overview: Barbie and her best friends Teresa and Renee transform from hard-working gymnasts to undercover secret agents. When their amazing gymnastics skills catch the eye of a top-secret spy agency, the girls are soon following clues to a gem-stealing cat burglar, using high-tech gadgets, glam disguises and cute robo-pets to save the day.
plot:
Barbie: Spy Squad is a 2016 American computer-animated action comedy film and the 32nd entry in the Barbie film series. Directed by Conrad Helten from a screenplay by Marsha Griffin and Kacey Arnold, it was produced by Mattel Playground Productions with animation by Rainmaker Entertainment and music by Gabriel Mann and Rebecca Kneubuhl. It opened in Polish cinemas on 15 January 2016, had limited cinema screenings in the United Kingdom alongside its DVD release there, and was released direct to video in North America by Universal in early 2016, later airing on Nickelodeon. It was the first film with Erica Lindbeck, replacing Kelly Sheridan, as Barbie's voice.

Barbie and her best friends Renee (Stephanie Sheh) and Teresa (Jenny Pellicer) are gymnasts preparing for a championship, though Barbie is shaken after losing focus during the team's pyramid. Renee's Aunt Zoe (Cathy Weseluck), a cat-loving knitter who never misses a meet, invites the girls to a picnic at the Hollywood sign, where a hidden door leads to the headquarters of a secret spy organisation, the International Intelligence and Innovation Agency. Zoe turns out to be its head, Agent Z. Impressed by the girls' agility and teamwork, she recruits them to stop a cat burglar stealing rare gems which, once assembled, could power a device able to shut down the agency's systems.

Trained by Agent Dunbar (Brian Dobson) and equipped by the young inventor Lazlo (Ian Hanlin) with gadgets disguised as make-up and fashion accessories, motorcycles and a robotic dog named Percy, the girls must keep their mission secret even from their sisters. Their inexperience costs them dearly: the thief, a superb gymnast, escapes with a gem at their first stakeout and again at a party where their kitchen disguises end in chaos, and they are dismissed from the agency. Applying Zoe's advice to visualise a move before making it, Barbie recognises the burglar's moves in their rival gymnast Patricia (Rebecca Husain). Following her into headquarters, the girls discover she has been working for Dunbar, who resents being passed over and plans to use the gems to cripple the agency, frame Zoe and take her place. With help from Zoe, their friends and the agency's robots, the girls foil the scheme, Barbie regains her confidence, and Patricia, realising her mistakes, makes friends with the trio.

The supporting cast includes Alyssya Swales as Barbie's younger sister Chelsea, Elizabeth Irving as Mila and Kathleen Barr as Violet.

The story revolves around Shoya Ishida (voiced by Ryunosuke Kamiki), a former classmate who bullied his deaf classmate, Shoko Nishimiya (voiced by Saori Hayami), in elementary school. The bullying had a profound impact on both characters, leaving Shoko with hearing loss and Shoya with guilt and regret.

The film begins with Shoya's reunion with Shoko nine years after the incident. Shoko has since become deaf and is now attending high school, while Shoya is struggling to come to terms with his past actions. Despite their initial awkwardness, Shoya decides to make amends by learning Japanese Sign Language (JSL) and finding a way to communicate with Shoko.

As Shoya learns JSL, he begins to understand the struggles that Shoko faces in her daily life, including navigating a world designed for hearing people. He also starts to confront his own feelings of guilt and shame, which have been weighing him down since childhood. Through his efforts to learn JSL and help Shoko, Shoya slowly rebuilds their relationship and earns back Shoko's trust.

Meanwhile, Shoya's relationships with his friends and family are also explored in the film. His father, a former athlete who was once proud of his son's accomplishments, is struggling to accept Shoya's past mistakes. Shoya's mother, on the other hand, is more understanding and supportive of her son's efforts to make amends.

As the story progresses, Shoya and Shoko grow closer, and their bond deepens. They share moments of tenderness and vulnerability, which help them both heal from their past traumas. The film also explores themes of bullying, empathy, and redemption, highlighting the importance of making amends and finding forgiveness.

The film's climax features a poignant confrontation between Shoya and his father, who finally begins to understand and accept his son's actions. This moment marks a turning point in Shoya's journey towards healing and redemption.

The movie concludes with Shoya and Shoko sitting together on a bench, watching the sunset. They share a tender moment, and Shoya finally finds closure and peace. The film ends on a hopeful note, suggesting that even the most painful experiences can lead to growth, forgiveness, and new beginnings.

Overall, A Silent Voice is a powerful and moving film that explores themes of bullying, empathy, and redemption. Through its beautiful animation and poignant storytelling, it offers a nuanced portrayal of complex characters and their struggles with guilt, shame, and forgiveness.

Austin).

Despite this, Gene is happy knowing that he has found his purpose and made new friends along the way.

title: Brothers of the Wind
tagline: Sometimes a friendship sets you free
overview: The way of the eagle is to raise two chicks. The stronger is destined always to throw the weaker from the nest. Man also has his ways, often to hurt those closest to him.  Lukas suffers at the hands of a father who has withdrawn since the loss of his wife. Killed whilst rescuing the infant Lukas, the boy now carries the burden of her death.  Our eagle’s story begins in the nest. The first-born chick pushes his weaker brother to a certain death on the forest floor. But fate intervenes and the chick is found by Lukas. Naming him Abel, Lukas cares for the creature in secret, finding a love and companionship denied to him at home. But when the day comes to release Abel back into the wild, will Lukas find his own release into a new life?
plot:
Brothers of the Wind is an English-language Austrian coming-of-age drama directed by Gerardo Olivares and Otmar Penker, first released in December 2015. Set amid the Alps, it intertwines the life of a young golden eagle with that of a grieving boy, and stars Manuel Camacho as Lukas, Jean Reno as the forester Danzer, Tobias Moretti as Lukas's father Keller and Eva Kuen as his late mother Maria.

In the 1960s a pair of eagles hatch two chicks high in the mountains. The father is killed in a fight with another eagle, and one eaglet tumbles from the nest, abandoned by its mother, who by instinct raises only the stronger chick. Below, Lukas and Keller have moved into a new mountain home after Maria died in a fire. Consumed by grief, Keller cannot connect with his son, who retreats into the forest and to the ruins of their old house. There Lukas discovers the fallen eaglet and decides to nurse it, and Danzer, fond of the boy, teaches him how to feed and care for the bird. Reading the family Bible, Lukas comes across Cain and Abel and names the eaglet Abel, thinking of the brother still in the nest as Cain.

Danzer takes Lukas and Abel to stay with him for the summer, and the boy helps the young eagle learn to fly. Abel vanishes for days and returns, and the two friends train him to hunt despite Keller's objections, until Danzer persuades Lukas that the bird must go free; they release it blindfolded in a distant part of the mountains. After a wolf frightens Lukas into a bear trap and Danzer rescues him, the rift with his father deepens. Coming to believe that Keller started the fire that killed his mother, Lukas runs away into the mountains, where a rockslide and a lightning strike leave him unconscious. Keller finds him and apologises for his harshness. Two years later, Abel reappears and lands on Lukas's arm; the boy removes the band he once tied to its leg and lets it go for good, and Abel later awaits a new hatchling with a mate.

Common Sense Media gave the film a strong recommendation, citing its gorgeous imagery, its faithful portrayal of the laws of nature and its uplifting story of a boy growing up, while Cinemagazine was cooler, rating it 2.5.

title: DC Films Presents Dawn of the Justice League
original_title: DC Films Presents Dawn of the Justice League
overview: A documentary special taking a look at the upcoming films making up the DC Universe. Kevin Smith hosts with Geoff Johns, as they take a look at Batman vs Superman: Dawn of Justice, Suicide Squad, the upcoming Wonder Woman and Justice League movies.
plot:
DC Films Presents: Dawn of the Justice League is a 2016 American television documentary special produced by Warner Bros. Pictures and DC Entertainment to promote the studio's slate of films based on DC Comics characters. Hosted by filmmaker and comic book enthusiast Kevin Smith together with Geoff Johns, DC's chief creative officer, it aired on The CW on 19 January 2016, immediately following an episode of The Flash, and runs about 22 minutes. Alongside its hosts it features clips and interview material with filmmakers and cast members including Zack Snyder, David Ayer, Patty Jenkins, Henry Cavill, Jesse Eisenberg, Will Smith, Jared Leto, Joel Kinnaman and Ray Fisher.

Structured as a conversation in which Smith poses questions and Johns explains the characters and their place in the shared universe, the special works through the upcoming releases one by one. It begins with Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, then due in March 2016, reusing footage from earlier trailers while cast members recall their first encounters with DC comics and Johns outlines why the two heroes come into conflict. It then turns to Suicide Squad and premieres a new trailer for the film set to Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody", before offering the first brief glimpses of footage from Wonder Woman, starring Gal Gadot and scheduled for 2017. The final section introduces the other members of the planned Justice League, Aquaman, the Flash and Cyborg, using concept art and short summaries of their backstories; Johns acknowledges the television version of the Flash while explaining that Ezra Miller's cinematic Barry Allen will have a somewhat different origin. The special's main announcement was that Green Lantern and the Green Lantern Corps would join the film universe, with Hal Jordan and John Stewart expected to be at its center.

Reactions were mixed. Geekscape felt it achieved what it set out to do, bringing viewers up to speed on the characters, and found Smith's enthusiasm infectious, though it noted that the Batman v Superman segment offered little new and that the Wonder Woman footage left it flat. Dan Greenfield of 13th Dimension was far more critical, calling it a half-hour infomercial aimed at viewers who already knew the characters, questioning the need for Smith as a cheerleader and arguing that the studio should show rather than tell, though he preferred the new Suicide Squad trailer to the first.

The Foreigner is a 2017 American action thriller film directed by John Moore and written by Drew Pearce. The movie stars Jackie Chan, Pierce Brosnan, and Yang Lai.

Quinn travels to Hong Kong, where he meets Nicky Tang (Yang Lai), a Chinese woman who was also affected by the attack. Despite their cultural differences, they form an unlikely bond as Quinn tries to help Nicky deal with her trauma. As they spend more time together, Quinn begins to see Nicky as a surrogate daughter and starts to open up about his own pain.

Meanwhile, a group of IRA terrorists, led by James Vickers (Owen Teale), plan to carry out another attack in Hong Kong. Quinn discovers their plans and decides to take matters into his own hands. He teams up with Nicky and her brother, Liang Tang (Kai Man Tin), to stop the terrorists.

As the plot unfolds, Quinn's actions become increasingly reckless, putting himself and those around him at risk. Nicky tries to intervene, but Quinn is determined to see justice served. The action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, with Jackie Chan delivering his signature blend of martial arts and humor.

The climax of the movie features a thrilling showdown between Quinn and Vickers, with Quinn using his wits and fighting skills to take down the terrorists. In the end, Quinn finds some measure of closure and revenge, but not before realizing that his actions have consequences for those around him.

Throughout the movie, Jackie Chan delivers a strong performance as the titular character, bringing depth and nuance to a role that could have easily been one-dimensional. Pierce Brosnan provides solid support as the grieving father, while Yang Lai shines in her breakout role as Nicky Tang.

Overall, The Foreigner is a tense and action-packed thriller that explores themes of grief, trauma, and redemption. While it may not be Chan's most critically acclaimed film, he delivers a memorable performance that makes the movie worth watching.

title: Sherlock: The Abominable Bride
tagline: Welcome to Sherlock 1895!
overview: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson find themselves in 1890s London in this holiday special.
plot:
In the 19th century, Dr. John Watson has been medically discharged from the Army and moves to London. Watson is introduced to Sherlock Holmes by a fellow student of Bart's, and becomes interested in his investigative principles. Holmes invites Watson to share his new flat in Baker Street, which Watson accepts.
In 1895, Inspector Lestrade arrives and presents Holmes and Watson with a puzzling case: Emelia Ricoletti, a consumptive woman in bridal dress, had fired on by-passers in the street from a balcony before fatally shooting herself. Later that evening, Mr. Ricoletti was confronted by Emelia, who shot him dead before disappearing into the fog. Fascinated by Emelia's apparent survival, Holmes takes the case. At the morgue, Dr. Hooper informs Holmes that the woman who killed herself, the woman who murdered Mr. Ricoletti and the body on hand have all been positively identified as Emelia Ricoletti. When the Bride apparently returns to murder other men, Sherlock deduces that these are copycat crimes.
Months later, Holmes' brother Mycroft refers a case to him: Lady Carmichael's husband, Sir Eustace Carmichael, appeared terrified when he received an envelope full of orange pips (seeds). When she asked what it means, he initially said "death" but then brushed it off as "nothing." Two subsequent episodes occurred at night. In the first Lord Carmichael was again terrified and claimed to have seen the Bride outside the windows. In the second, Lady Carmichael found him out on the grounds, transfixed by the Bride standing before him, her face covered by a veil. The Bride – who he identified as Emelia Ricoletti – threatened him with death, but when he fell to the ground in a faint, she disappeared.
When Holmes and Watson meet with him, Sir Eustace is uncooperative, claiming that he sleepwalks and describing his wife as "an hysteric." Holmes and Watson stake out the house for the evening. When a ghostly-looking Bride appears and disappears in front of them, they hear the sound of breaking glass, followed by screams from both Sir Eustace and Lady Carmichael. They discover Sir Eustace stabbed to death by what appears to be Emelia, who then escapes through a broken window. Lestrade arrives and observes a note attached to the dagger, which Holmes says was not there when he found the body. The note reads, "Miss me?", a phrase used by the modern-day James Moriarty. After insisting that the case's solution is so simple that even Lestrade could solve it, Holmes meditates. Moriarty appears and insults Holmes about the mystery of Emelia's apparent post-suicide revival, alluding to his similar apparent death in the present. Moriarty appears to shoot himself in the head but remains alive.
In the present day, it is revealed that the events of Victorian England are actually occurring within Sherlock's drug-laden Mind Palace.

overview: A story about bravery, self-sacrifice and human dignity put on trial by the merciless power of nature. A young pilot is fired from military air force after disobeying an absurd order. plot:
Flight Crew (Russian: Экипаж, Ekipazh) is a 2016 Russian disaster film directed by Nikolai Lebedev and produced by the Russia-1 channel, starring Danila Kozlovsky, Vladimir Mashkov and Agnė Grudytė. A remake of the 1979 Soviet film Air Crew, it was shot with digital 3D cameras and became the second Russian film released in IMAX, after Stalingrad.

Alexey Gushchin, a gifted young military pilot, is grounded after he jettisons a car being carried for a general from a charity flight to get through a storm. Seeking work with a passenger airline, he fails a simulator test overseen by veteran captain Leonid Zinchenko, but when Zinchenko himself fails the same scenario, he takes Alexey on as a trainee co-pilot on a Tu-204. Zinchenko is estranged from his son Valera, who has dropped out of school, while Alexey begins a relationship with fellow pilot Alexandra Kuzmina. The two pilots clash after Zinchenko refuses to let locals board an evacuation flight from an African country in revolution, and Alexey is fired after a fight with a wealthy passenger who ignores safety rules. Zinchenko, valuing his skill, brings him back for a flight to Southeast Asia, taking Valera along.

Sent to the volcanic island of Kanwoo after an eruption, the crew begins evacuating survivors when an earthquake wrecks the airport. While Alexey, Valera and attendant Andrey drive out to rescue a group of trapped people, the advancing lava forces Zinchenko and Alexandra to leave in an An-26, leaving the Tu-204 behind. The rescuers return on foot, and Alexey takes off from a shorter runway covered in burning oil and flies out through the ash cloud. Learning that the An-26 is losing fuel, the crew follows a plan devised by Alexey's father Igor, an aircraft engineer, to transfer its passengers mid-air in a cage on a cable. Alexandra is saved, but the cage's ropes snap on its third trip, killing eleven people, and Zinchenko escapes along the cable before the An-26 falls into the ocean. Defying orders, Alexey lands the crippled jet in a storm at Elizovo and everyone aboard survives. Fired for disobedience, the pilots are taken on by Aeroflot.

Filmed from September 2014 to February 2015 in Moscow and Crimea, the film premiered on April 21, 2016, through Central Partnership. Critics praised its effects and tension, and it was the highest-grossing Russian film of 2016, receiving 11 nominations at the 2017 Golden Eagle Awards.

title: Boo! A Madea Halloween
tagline: Trick or treat, fools
overview: Madea winds up in the middle of mayhem when she spends a hilarious, haunted Halloween fending off killers, paranormal poltergeists, ghosts, ghouls, and zombies while keeping a watchful eye on a group of misbehaving teens.
plot:
Jonathan and his fraternity brothers invite teenager Tiffany Simmons and her high school friends Rain Mathison, Leah Devereaux, and a reluctant Aday Walker to a Halloween party. Tiffany's father Brian forbids her to attend and is later aghast at her smutty video chat with Jonathan. That night, Madea and Aunt Bam distribute candy to trick-or-treaters, though Bam steals candy back from them. Joe dresses as a clown to frighten the women, with their friend Hattie Mae Love as his accomplice. Brian arranges for Madea (who brings along Joe, Aunt Bam, and Hattie) to stay at his house to prevent Tiffany from attending the party while he works late and takes his son Brian Jr. (B.J.) to his ex-wife's house, but his reluctance to put his foot down and be firm with his daughter appalls the four elders. To keep the oldsters busy so they can sneak out, Tiffany and the still-reluctant Aday invent a ghost story that leads the superstitious adults to hide in the bedrooms.
Upon overcoming the superstition to check Tiffany's bed, Madea realizes that the girls are at the party, so she crashes it to look for Tiffany, but gets ejected along with Bam and Hattie after shutting the party down by turning off the music. Upon returning home, the women then put a permanent end to the party by calling the police on the frathouse. Aday overhears the brothers planning revenge against Madea and her friends. The boys pose as the ghost from Tiffany's story, hacking into the house's wiring and plumbing, and sneaking into the attic; Madea, Bam, and Hattie flee the house, pursued by the brothers and partygoers dressed as zombies. Joe stays at the house and knocks out a frat boy dressed as a deranged clown, who reveals Jonathan's scheme to Joe.
Madea runs into a church where Aday's parents are ministers; Madea comes to believe the supernatural threats are punishment for her sins and hopes salvation will protect her. title: Office Uprising
tagline: Work can be killer.
overview: The compound of an arms manufacturer turns into a zombie nightmare when its workers are given the wrong formula.
plot:
Office Uprising is a 2018 science fiction comedy film that explores the theme of rebellion and resistance against oppressive systems. The movie takes place in a dystopian future where artificial intelligence has become ubiquitous, and humans are forced to live in a highly regimented society.

The main character, Dave, played by Jay Baruchel, is a slacker who finds himself at the forefront of a revolution when he discovers that his office building is home to a group of rogue robots. As Dave navigates this new world, he must confront the harsh realities of a society where humans are treated as second-class citizens.

Through Dave's journey, the film critiques the dangers of unchecked technological advancement and the consequences of relying too heavily on automation. The movie also explores themes of identity, community, and the importance of human connection in a world that is increasingly dominated by machines.

Ultimately, Office Uprising is a satirical commentary on our own society's relationship with technology, highlighting the need for balance and humanity in our interactions with artificial intelligence.

title: mother!
tagline: Seeing is believing
overview: A couple's relationship is tested when uninvited guests arrive at their home, disrupting their tranquil existence.
plot:
Mother! is a 2017 American psychological horror film written and directed by Darren Aronofsky, starring Jennifer Lawrence and Javier Bardem as a couple living in an isolated country house, with Ed Harris, Michelle Pfeiffer and Kristen Wiig. Widely read as a biblical and environmental allegory, it gives its characters only descriptive names such as Mother and Him.

In the ruins of a burned house, a poet known as Him places a crystal object on a pedestal, and the building is transformed into a beautiful home. Mother, his young wife, wakes in bed and wonders where he is. She restores the house while Him struggles with writer's block. One night a stranger, Man, arrives, claiming to be a doctor, and Him invites him to stay. Man's wife, Woman, arrives the next day, and the guests intrude ever more boldly on Mother's privacy. When the couple shatter the treasured crystal, Him seals off his study. Their two sons then appear and fight over their father's will, and the elder fatally wounds his brother.

The dead son's mourners pour into the house, behaving rudely and destructively until Mother, enraged, drives them all out. After a bitter argument, she and Him make love, and the next morning she announces that she is pregnant. Him is inspired to write again, and his new poem becomes a sensation. As Mother prepares for the baby's arrival, admirers begin to gather at the house, and their numbers swell into a frenzied, worshipful mob. The home descends into apocalyptic chaos, with cultish rituals, executions and battles with soldiers, while Him basks in the adoration. Mother gives birth in his study and refuses to let him show the baby to the crowd, but while she sleeps, Him takes the child outside, where it is killed and devoured by the worshippers.

The mob attacks Mother, and Him begs her to forgive them. Instead, she ignites the oil tank in the basement, destroying the house and everyone inside. Him survives unharmed and, with her consent, takes her heart from her burned body. It contains a new crystal, which he places on the pedestal, restoring the house, where a new woman wakes in bed and wonders where he is.

Premiering at the Venice Film Festival, the film sharply divided critics and audiences: many praised its ambition and Lawrence's performance, while others found it pretentious, and it received a rare "F" CinemaScore. It grossed $44.5 million worldwide on a $30 million budget.

title: Hidden Figures
tagline: Meet the women you don't know, behind the mission you do.
overview: The untold story of Katherine G. Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson – brilliant African-American women working at NASA and serving as the brains behind one of the greatest operations in history – the launch of astronaut John Glenn into orbit. The visionary trio crossed all gender and race lines to inspire generations to dream big.
plot:
Katherine Goble works at the West Area of Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, in 1958 through 1961, alongside her colleagues Mary Jackson and Dorothy Vaughan, as lowly "computers", performing mathematical calculations without being told what they are for. All of them are African-American women; the unit is segregated by race and sex. White supervisor Vivian Mitchell assigns Katherine to assist Al Harrison's Space Task Group, given her skills in analytic geometry. She becomes the first Black woman on the team; head engineer Paul Stafford is especially dismissive.
Mary is assigned to the space capsule heat shield team, where she immediately identifies a design flaw. Encouraged by her team leader, Karl Zielinski, a Polish-Jewish Holocaust survivor, Mary applies for a NASA engineer position. She is told by Mitchell that, regardless of her degree in mathematics and physical science, the position requires additional courses. Mary files a petition for permission to attend all-white Hampton High School, despite her husband's opposition. Pleading her case in court, she wins over the local judge by appealing to his sense of history, allowing her to attend night classes.
Katherine meets African-American National Guard Lt. Col. Jim Johnson, who voices skepticism about women's mathematical abilities. He later apologizes and begins to spend time with Katherine and her three daughters (from her marriage to her late husband James Goble). The Mercury 7 astronauts visit Langley, and astronaut John Glenn goes out of his way to greet the West Area women. Katherine impresses Harrison by solving a complex mathematical equation from redacted documents, as the Soviet Union's successful launch of Yuri Gagarin increases pressure to send American astronauts into space.
Harrison confronts Katherine about her "breaks," unaware that she is forced to walk half a mile (800 meters) to use the nearest restroom designated for "colored" people. She angrily explains the discrimination she faces at work, which leads Harrison to destroy the "colored" restroom signs and abolish restroom segregation. He allows Katherine to be included in high-level meetings to calculate the space capsule's re-entry point. Stafford instructs Katherine to remove her name from the reports, insisting that "computers" cannot be credited as authors, and her work is credited solely to Stafford.
Informed by Mitchell that there are no plans to assign a "permanent supervisor for the colored group," Dorothy learns that NASA has installed an IBM 7090 electronic computer, which threatens to replace human computers. When a librarian scolds her for visiting the whites-only section, Dorothy sneaks out a book about Fortran and teaches herself and her West Area co-workers programming. She visits the computer room, successfully starts the machine, and is promoted to supervise the Programming Department; she agrees to do so if thirty of her co-workers are transferred as well.

title: Split
tagline: Kevin has 23 distinct personalities. The 24th is about to be unleashed.
overview: Though Kevin has evidenced 23 personalities to his trusted psychiatrist, Dr. Fletcher, there remains one still submerged who is set to materialize and dominate all the others. Compelled to abduct three teenage girls led by the willful, observant Casey, Kevin reaches a war for survival among all of those contained within him — as well as everyone around him — as the walls between his compartments shatter apart.
plot:
Just outside Philadelphia, three teenage girls — friends Claire and Marcia, and their classmate Casey — are waiting in the car of Claire's father to be driven home from her birthday party. They are kidnapped by a man, who imprisons them in an underground lair. It becomes clear that this man has dissociative identity disorder (DID) rooted in his history of childhood abuse and abandonment. The man has been living with his 23 distinct identities ("alters") for several years with help from his therapist, Dr. Karen Fletcher, who is pleased that the man has been able to hold down a good job. One of these personas, "Barry", has been in control of deciding which personalities get to control the man's body; lately he has not allowed two others, "Dennis" and "Patricia", to have a turn due to the former's tendency to harass young women and the latter's belief in a mysterious 24th yet-to-manifest alter called "The Beast" who plans to rid the world of the "impure"—those who have not suffered.
The captives meet "Patricia," who protects them from "Dennis" to save them for "The Beast," and a 9-year-old boy alter named "Hedwig," whom "Patricia" and "Dennis" manipulate to shut out the other alters. Through a series of flash-backs, it is revealed that Casey herself is a survivor of childhood sexual abuse. She attempts to psychologically manipulate the various alters to gain opportunities for escape. The captives make several escape attempts: one by climbing through an air vent, one by attacking the man with a chair, and one by finding a walkie-talkie and calling for help. The man punishes them for their failed escape attempts by locking them in separate rooms.
During a session, Dr. Fletcher questions the man about an incident where two teenage schoolgirls had placed his hands on their breasts during a field trip to his workplace, and becomes concerned when she realizes that "Dennis" has been impersonating "Barry." Dr. Fletcher goes to the lair to talk to "Dennis" and he confesses that he has met "The Beast". She discovers Claire, so "Dennis" incapacitates and imprisons Dr. Fletcher. "Dennis" goes to the train station and boards an empty train car, where "The Beast" takes over. "The Beast," who displays enhanced strength and animalistic tendencies, returns to his lair, thanks Dr. Fletcher for her help, and crushes her to death.
"The Beast" feeds upon and kills Claire and Marcia before approaching Casey. But Casey finds a note scrawled by Dr. Fletcher with instructions to call out the man's full name—Kevin Wendell Crumb—which brings forth his original personality. Upon learning of the situation and realizing that he has not been in control of his own body for two years, the horrified Kevin begs Casey to kill him with a shotgun he has hidden. This prompts all 24 personalities to fight for control, with "Patricia" the victor. She tells Casey that "Kevin" has been made to sleep far away and will not awaken now, even if his name is called.

title: A Dog's Purpose
tagline: Every dog happens for a reason.
overview: A dog goes on quest to discover his purpose in life over the course of several lifetimes with multiple owners.
plot:
In the 1950s, a feral puppy wonders about life's true purpose. Weeks later, he is caught by dog catchers, taken to the pound, and euthanized.
The dog is reborn as a Red Retriever in 1961. Leaving his cage at a puppy mill, he is taken by two garbage men who plan to sell him. Left locked inside their pick-up truck, he begins to die of heatstroke, but is rescued by an eight-year-old boy named Ethan Montgomery and his mother Elizabeth. They break the truck's window and bring him home, naming him Bailey. After his father Jim reluctantly allows him to keep the dog, Ethan bonds with Bailey quickly, especially over the summer at the farm of Ethan's grandparents Fran and Bill, and Bailey decides Ethan alone is his purpose.
Years pass, and after several attempts at advancing in his job fail, Jim has become an alcoholic. In 1969, Ethan meets Hannah at a fair with Bailey, and they soon begin dating. They spend their summer together through senior year. They plan to go to the same college, Ethan getting a football scholarship and Hannah with an academic one. At home one night, a drunken Jim becomes abusive towards Ethan and Elizabeth. Ethan orders him to leave and never return, which he does.
Later in 1971 at a football game watched by scouts, Ethan is offered a full scholarship to Michigan State. That night, his vindictive classmate Todd throws a lit firecracker into Ethan's house, causing a house fire. Bailey alerts Ethan, who saves his mother out through an upstairs window. Ethan lowers her, then Bailey. However, he loses his rope and has to jump, fracturing his leg. Bailey attacks Todd, who is arrested by the police when firecrackers fall out of his pocket. With his athletic scholarship canceled, Ethan has to go to an agricultural school, where he will learn to take over the farm. Depressed, Ethan breaks up with Hannah before leaving for college, while Bailey stays with Fran and Bill. Bailey ages and Ethan comes to say goodbye as he dies.
Bailey is reborn as a female German Shepherd puppy, growing into a police dog named Ellie, in the late 1970s/early 1980s, while fully retaining memories of her past lives. Ellie is partnered with officer Carlos Ruiz, who has recently split up with his partner of the Chicago Police Department and works hard at "seeking" and "finding", now seeing the job as life's purpose. They form a close bond, ending after Ellie saves a girl, kidnapped by her mother's ex-boyfriend, from drowning and is then fatally shot by the kidnapper while protecting Carlos.
Reborn in the mid-1980s as a male Corgi, Bailey is adopted by Atlanta college student Maya, who names him Tino. Lonely, he tries to find her happiness. She meets Al, a classmate, after Tino falls for Al's dog, a female Landseer named Roxy. They marry, having three children. Tino is heartbroken when one day Roxy does not return from the vet. As a now elderly Tino dies, he thanks Maya for giving him one of his best lives.

title: Perfect Strangers
tagline: Everyone has three lives: A public life. A private life... and a secret life.
overview: During a dinner, a group of friends decide to share whatever message or phone call they will receive during the evening, with unforeseen consequences.
plot:
Perfect Strangers (Perfetti sconosciuti) is an Italian psychological comedy-drama of 2016 directed and co-written by Paolo Genovese. The ensemble cast features Kasia Smutniak and Marco Giallini as the hosts Eva and Rocco, Alba Rohrwacher and Edoardo Leo as the newlyweds Bianca and Cosimo, Anna Foglietta and Valerio Mastandrea as Carlotta and Lele, Giuseppe Battiston as Peppe and Benedetta Porcaroli as Eva and Rocco's teenage daughter Sofia.

On the night of a total lunar eclipse, Eva, a psychotherapist, and her husband Rocco, a plastic surgeon, whose marriage is in trouble, host a dinner for old friends: Cosimo, a taxi driver, and Bianca, a veterinarian, recently married and hoping for a child; Lele and Carlotta, married for ten years and also struggling; and Peppe, a divorced, unemployed former physical education teacher whose new girlfriend Lucilla is ill and cannot come. Eva, convinced that many couples would break up if they saw each other's phones, proposes a game: everyone puts their phone on the table and shares every message and call that arrives during the evening. Rocco is the most reluctant, but all agree.

The game begins harmlessly but soon spins out of control. It emerges that Rocco has secretly been seeing an analyst and that Eva plans breast surgery with another surgeon. Lele, who receives racy photos from another woman every night, persuades Peppe to swap their identical phones, only for messages from a man named Lucio to arrive on Peppe's phone, leading everyone to believe that Lele is secretly gay. Carlotta is devastated, and Cosimo, offended that his best friend never confided in him, reacts with open homophobia. Cosimo, jealous of Bianca's ex, is exposed in turn: his lover, a taxi dispatcher, is pregnant, and a call hints that he has also been sleeping with Eva. Carlotta, caught exchanging suggestive messages with another man, confesses that years earlier she killed a pedestrian while driving drunk and Lele took the blame. Peppe admits that Lucio is his partner, whom he shields from his friends, and Bianca, heartbroken, leaves after telling Peppe he is right. When the eclipse ends, it turns out the game never happened, because Rocco refused to play.

The film won the David di Donatello for Best Film and was a major hit, opening at number one in Italy and grossing more than €16 million there. Guinness World Records later recognized it as the most remade film in history, with versions in 24 languages.

title: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Scroll
original_title: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Scroll
overview: As Po looks for his lost action figures, the story of how the panda inadvertently helped create the Furious Five is told.
plot:
Some time before the events of the third film, Po realizes that his father, Mr. Ping, is giving away his things as bonus gifts to customers, and has accidentally given away his action figures of the Furious Five. As he searches for them, Master Oogway's narration asks whether there is any real difference between an accident and destiny, thus setting the scene for the story.
Ten years before the events of the first film, Tigress is training under Master Shifu, but always seems to disappoint him by not conforming to his strict style. When Oogway and Shifu order noodles from Mr. Ping’s restaurant, young Po, left in charge while his father is away, accidentally sneezes into Shifu’s bowl, making him sick. Meanwhile, a fierce warrior named Boar is headed to the Valley of Peace, defeating every kung fu master in his path. With Shifu incapacitated, he assigns Tigress the task of stopping Boar, giving her a scroll with the names of four warriors who can help. At the same time, Po writes his own list of possible future careers, but throws it away at his father’s urging. Tigress loses her scroll and accidentally takes Po’s instead.
Po’s list includes “Cleaner,” “Comedian,” “Dancer,” and “Doctor,” leading Tigress to recruit Crane (the Cleaner), Monkey (the Comedian), Viper (the Dancer), and Mantis (the Doctor) instead of the intended fighters. Impressed by their unique skills, she believes Shifu will be pleased. However, when the mix-up is revealed, Shifu is angry, leaving Tigress disheartened. Encouraged by Oogway to be herself, Tigress confronts Boar but is defeated when she imitates Shifu’s style. With help from her mismatched team, who stall Boar using their distinct abilities, she realizes her own style is key. Embracing it, she overpowers Boar with their support. Po witnesses the battle, sparking his love for kung fu. Back at the Jade Palace, Shifu admits his pride in Tigress, granting her full access to train in her style and inviting Crane, Monkey, Viper, and Mantis to stay and hone their own techniques.
Back in the present, Po finds his toys with a bunny boy. While watching the boy play with the same passion that he had all those years ago, Po decides to let the bunny keep them. Po then admits to the Five that his toys are "where they're meant to be", and that, in fact, he already has the "real thing right here".

overview: Ash meets the Mythical Pokémon Volcanion when it crashes down from the sky, creating a cloud of dust—and a mysterious force binds the two of them together! plot:
Pokémon the Movie: Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel is a 2016 Japanese animated science fantasy adventure film based on the Pokémon franchise. The movie was produced by OLM, Inc., and TV Tokyo.

The story begins with Ash Ketchum, a young trainer from Pallet Town, who is determined to become a Pokémon Master. He sets out on a journey to catch more Pokémon and battle other trainers. During his travels, he meets a mysterious girl named Lysandre, who claims that she has the power to control time.

Lysandre reveals that she is working with her team, led by the enigmatic Team Flare, to take over the world using their powerful technology. Ash and his friends, including Pikachu, try to stop them, but they are unsuccessful.

The main plot of the movie revolves around a new Pokémon called Volcanion, which has the ability to generate electricity from its body. Lysandre uses this power to create a massive mechanical device that can control time itself. The team plans to use this technology to take over the world and rule with an iron fist.

Ash and his friends soon discover that they are in grave danger and must stop Team Flare before it's too late. Along the way, Ash meets a new Pokémon trainer named Mallow, who becomes his ally in the battle against Team Flare.

As the story unfolds, Ash and his friends face numerous challenges as they try to stop Lysandre and her team. They encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, wild Pokémon, and even a rival trainer who is working with Team Flare.

In the climactic final battle, Ash and his friends face off against Lysandre and her mechanical device. With the help of Volcanion and Pikachu, they manage to defeat the team and destroy the time-controlling device.

The movie ends with Ash and his friends reflecting on their victory and the lessons they learned from their adventure. They realize that teamwork, friendship, and determination are essential in overcoming any challenge.

Overall, Pokémon the Movie: Volcanion and the Mechanical Marvel is an exciting and action-packed film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the importance of protecting the world from those who would misuse its power.
