title: Cult of Chucky
tagline: You may feel a little prick
overview: Confined to an asylum for the criminally insane, Nica Pierce is convinced that she, not Chucky, murdered her entire family. But when the psychiatrist introduces a new therapeutic "Good Guy" doll with a familiar face, a string of new, grisly deaths leads Nica to wonder if she isn't crazy after all.
plot:
Cult of Chucky is a 2017 American supernatural slasher film written and directed by Don Mancini, creator of the Child's Play franchise. The seventh film in the series and a direct sequel to Curse of Chucky (2013), it stars Fiona Dourif, Michael Therriault, Adam Hurtig, Alex Vincent and Jennifer Tilly, with Brad Dourif once again voicing Chucky. Shot in Winnipeg, Manitoba, in early 2017, it premiered at London's FrightFest in August and, like its predecessor, was released direct to video by Universal on October 3, 2017.

Andy Barclay, the original target of the killer doll, has spent years tormenting Chucky's severed but still living head. Nica Pierce, the paraplegic survivor of the previous film, has been institutionalised after Chucky framed her for the murder of her family, and she has come to believe that she was the killer and that the doll was a delusion. Her psychiatrist, the abusive Dr. Foley, transfers her to a medium-security asylum, where she meets fellow patients including Madeleine, who smothered her infant son, and Malcolm, a man with dissociative identity disorder. Foley introduces a Good Guy doll into group therapy, and Madeleine treats it as her baby.

Tiffany Valentine, guardian of Nica's niece Alice, visits to tell Nica that Alice has died and leaves behind another Good Guy doll. Soon patients begin to die, Malcolm starts calling himself "Charles", and Nica realises that her "delusions" were real. Andy, learning of the killings, deduces that Chucky has found a way to place his soul into several bodies at once, and gets himself committed to the same institution. Madeleine is killed by a doll she believes is her child, and Nica discovers that there are now three living Chucky dolls. They explain that Chucky has learned a voodoo spell allowing him to split his soul among multiple hosts, Alice having been one of them.

The dolls murder a nurse, and one of them transfers part of his soul into Nica, enabling her body to walk; in her new form she kills Foley. Andy destroys one doll with a gun he had hidden inside it, but Nica-Chucky locks him in his cell and escapes to join Tiffany, accompanied by a living Tiffany doll. In a post-credits scene, Andy's former foster sister Kyle arrives at his home to continue tormenting the head.

The film was well received for a late franchise entry, earning 81% on Rotten Tomatoes, and it was nominated for Best DVD or Blu-ray Release at the 44th Saturn Awards.

title: Fences
tagline: Some people build fences to keep people out, and other people build fences to keep people in.
overview: In 1950s Pittsburgh, a frustrated African-American father struggles with the constraints of poverty, racism, and his own inner demons as he tries to raise a family.
plot:
Fences is a 2016 American drama film directed by Denzel Washington, based on the Pulitzer Prize-winning play of the same name by August Wilson. The film stars Denzel Washington, Viola Davis, and Jovan Adepo.

The story takes place in 1957 Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, during the Civil Rights Movement. Troy Maxson (Denzel Washington), a former baseball player, is a complex and troubled man struggling to find his place in the world. He works as a bus driver for the Pittsburgh Transit Authority and lives with his wife, Rose (Viola Davis), and their son, Cory (Jovan Adepo).

Troy's life is marked by regret and unfulfilled dreams. He was once a promising baseball player but was cut from the Negro Leagues due to racism. This experience has left him bitter and resentful towards society. Troy's relationships with his family are strained, particularly with his son Cory, who he feels is not living up to his expectations.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Troy's past experiences have shaped his present. He struggles to connect with his son, who is trying to find his own way in life. Troy's wife Rose tries to hold their family together, but her efforts are often thwarted by Troy's anger and bitterness.

Meanwhile, Troy's friend and coworker, Bono (Mykelti Williamson), provides a different perspective on life. Bono is a more optimistic character who encourages Troy to let go of his past and find peace. However, Troy's inability to forgive himself and others holds him back from moving forward.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Cory announces that he wants to leave home and pursue a career in baseball. This news sets off a chain reaction of events that forces Troy to confront his own demons and re-evaluate his relationships with those around him.

In the end, Troy's past comes back to haunt him, and he is forced to face the consequences of his actions. The film concludes on a bittersweet note, as Troy finally begins to find some measure of peace and forgiveness, but not before realizing that it may be too late for some things.

Throughout the film, Denzel Washington delivers a powerful performance as Troy Maxson, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Viola Davis also shines in her supporting role as Rose, capturing the complexity and resilience of a woman who has been holding her family together for years.

Overall, Fences is a powerful exploration of the human condition, tackling themes of regret, forgiveness, and redemption. The film features outstanding performances from its cast and is a testament to Denzel Washington's skill as an actor and director.

title: Raw
tagline: What are you hungry for?
overview: In Justine’s family everyone is a vet and a vegetarian. At 16, she’s a gifted teen ready to take on her first year in vet school, where her older sister also studies. There, she gets no time to settle: hazing starts right away. Justine is forced to eat raw meat for the first time in her life. Unexpected consequences emerge as her true self begins to form.
plot:
Lifelong vegetarian Justine begins her first semester at veterinary school, the same one her older sister Alexia is attending and where their parents met. On her first night, she meets her roommate Adrien, who claims he's gay, and they are forced to partake in a week-long hazing ritual, welcoming the new students. They are brought to a party, where Alexia shows Justine old class photos of students bathed in blood, including one with their parents. The next morning, the new class is splattered with blood and is forced to eat raw rabbit kidneys. Justine refuses because of her vegetarianism, but Alexia forces her to eat one. Justine leaves with Adrien and later discovers an itchy rash all over her body. She consults a doctor, who diagnoses her with food poisoning and gives her cream for the rash.
The next day, Justine begins having cravings for meat, which makes her feel ashamed. After a failed attempt to steal a burger from the cafeteria, she and Adrien take a late-night trip to a gas station so no one will see her eating meat. Unsatisfied, she eats raw chicken in the morning, and later throws up a long bundle of her own hair she had been chewing on. That night, Alexia attempts to give her a bikini wax, but when Alexia tries to cut the wax off with sharp scissors, Justine kicks her away and Alexia accidentally cuts off her own finger. Alexia faints, and Justine picks up the finger, tastes the blood, and starts eating it. Alexia wakes up to find Justine doing this but later tells their parents that her dog, Quicky, ate it.
The next morning, Alexia takes Justine to a deserted road, where Alexia jumps in front of a car, causing the two people in it to crash into a tree. Alexia starts eating one of the passengers so that her sister will "learn"; Justine is dismayed. Despite this, Justine's craving for human meat grows and she starts lusting after Adrien. That night, she arrives at a party, where paint is thrown at her as part of another hazing ritual and she is forced to make out with a boy. While kissing, Justine bites the middle of his bottom lip off, leaving the other party guests shocked and disgusted. Justine returns to her dorm and takes a shower, where she picks a chunk of his lip out of her teeth and eats it. Justine confides in Adrien and they end up having sex, during which Justine tries to bite Adrien but instead bites her own arm until it bleeds profusely, seeming to orgasm while doing so.
At another party, Justine becomes extremely intoxicated and Alexia takes her to the morgue. The next day, everyone in school stares at Justine, some avoiding her. Adrien shows her a video where Justine is crawling on all fours, attempting to take a bite out of the arm of a corpse as Alexia eggs her on, to boos and cheers from a crowd of watching party guests. Justine confronts Alexia and fights her, eventually biting each other until they are pulled apart by other students. Justine helps Alexia up, and they walk each other back to their dorms.

title: The Florida Project
tagline: Welcome to a magical kingdom
overview: The story of a precocious six year-old and her ragtag group of friends whose summer break is filled with childhood wonder, possibility and a sense of adventure while the adults around them struggle with hard times.
plot:
Moonee, a six-year-old girl, lives with her young, single mother, Halley, at Magic Castle Inn and Suites, a budget motel in Kissimmee, Florida, near Walt Disney World. Moonee spends most of her summer days unsupervised and making mischief with her downstairs neighbor, Scooty (whom Halley is supposed to watch while his mother, Ashley, works as a waitress at a diner), and Dicky, who lives at the nearby Futureland Inn. After Stacy, a new Futureland resident, catches the trio spitting on her car, Dicky is grounded for a week, and Moonee and Scooty meet and befriend Stacy's granddaughter, Jancey, who lives with Stacy.
Halley has recently lost her job as a stripper after refusing to have sex with clients, but this now affects her eligibility for TANF benefits; she begins relying on food that Ashley obtains from work. Struggling to pay rent, Halley begins selling knockoff perfume to tourists in the parking lots of upscale hotels with Moonee's help. Meanwhile, Moonee and Scooty show Jancey around the neighborhood and teach her things, like how to get ice cream by begging for money. They regularly inconvenience Bobby, the Magic Castle's manager, once shutting off the motel's power. Despite this, he remains protective of them. Bobby's duties include preparing expense reports, ejecting drug dealers, and doing repairs; he sometimes enlists the help of his son, Jack, with whom he has a tenuous relationship.
After Dicky's family moves to New Orleans, Scooty finds a lighter in a box that Dicky's family left behind; he, Moonee, and Jancey start a fire at an abandoned condominium complex. Seeing the fire, Ashley figures out that Scooty was involved, and forbids him from hanging out with Moonee or Jancey; she also severs ties with Halley and Moonee.
Without the free food from Ashley, and with security guards beginning to bother her at the hotels, Halley's financial situation declines even further. She begins soliciting sex work online, keeping Moonee in the bathroom with loud music when she has a client over. When Halley steals a client's Disney World MagicBands to scalp them, he returns to demand them back. Bobby scares him off but applies restrictions on unregistered guests in Halley's room; he also warns her that he will evict her if she continues having clients over. In desperation, Halley approaches Ashley to apologize and ask for money. Ashley criticizes Halley for doing sex work and threatens to kill her if her son was ever exposed to Halley's prostitution; enraged, Halley viciously beats her in front of Scooty.
Soon afterward, DCF investigators show up and question Halley and Moonee separately about their lifestyle. In anticipation of another visit, Halley gives her weed to one of the housekeepers and has Moonee help clean their room. They go to a fancier hotel and have an extravagant meal, which Halley charges to a guest's room.

title: The Pirates of Somalia
overview: After an inspiring chance encounter with his idol, rookie journalist Jay Bahadur uproots his life and moves to Somalia looking for the story of a lifetime. Hooking up with a local fixer, he attempts to get embedded with the local Somali pirates, only to quickly find himself in over his head.
plot:
The Pirates of Somalia, released in the United Kingdom as Pirates of Somalia, is a 2017 American drama written and directed by Bryan Buckley and based on Jay Bahadur's bestselling 2011 book. Evan Peters stars as Bahadur, a novice Canadian journalist, with Al Pacino as his idol, the veteran correspondent Seymour Tolbin, Barkhad Abdi as his Somali fixer Abdi, and Melanie Griffith as his mother, Maria. It was formerly titled Dabka.

Fresh out of the University of Toronto, Jay Bahadur is struggling to break into journalism. Still living with his parents, he scrapes by conducting product surveys in supermarkets. His chance comes after an encounter with Tolbin, who encourages him to skip graduate school and pursue a bold assignment: travelling to Somalia to uncover the story behind the country's notorious pirates.

By reaching out to news outlets in Somalia, Jay connects with a local reporter, Mohamad Farole, whose family welcomes him and gives him a place to stay. He is assigned a minder, Abdirizak, known as Abdi, who explains that the men the outside world calls pirates see themselves as saviours of the sea, a kind of coast guard. From his window Jay watches the street leading to the market, where he notices Maryan, a woman who sells khat, the stimulant that serves as currency for interviews, and whose husband is himself one of the pirates.

Jay succeeds in interviewing two pirates, Boyah and Maryan's husband Garaad, but his reports go unpublished by his contact at CBC Radio, Avril Benoit, who tells him the network will pay only for an interview with hostages aboard a hijacked ship. Abdi tries to arrange access to the captive German freighter Victoria, anchored at Eyl, but after Jay pushes his contacts too hard the ship slips away overnight. Meanwhile, the hijacking of the Maersk Alabama and the ordeal of Captain Phillips unfold, and both Jay's father and his Somali hosts warn him that it is no longer safe for him to remain.

Back in Canada, Jay is welcomed home by his family and approached by a government agent seeking his insight into Somalia. Later, living in Kenya, he advises an official committee as his book about the pirates becomes a bestseller, arguing that Somalia needs recognition of its complex and honourable culture rather than warships off its coast.

The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 27, 2017, and was released by Echo Bridge on December 8, 2017, to mixed reviews, earning 63% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Sheep & Wolves
tagline: You can be whatever you want. The main thing is you remain yourself!
overview: In a magical faraway land, in a picturesque little village nestled among green meadows and rolling hills, lives a flock of carefree sheep. But their pastoral and stress-free life is interrupted when a pack of wolves sets up camp in the nearby ravine.
plot:
Sheep and Wolves (Russian: Volki i ovtsy. Be-e-e-zumnoe prevrashchenie) is a 2016 Russian 3D animated fantasy comedy directed by Andrey Galat and Maxim Volkov, their directorial debut, and produced by Wizart Animation with CTB Film Company. The studio's first original story, conceived by Volkov, draws on the fairy tale The Wolf and the Seven Young Goats and the idea of a wolf in sheep's clothing. Alexander Petrov voices the hero, Grey, and Elizaveta Boyarskaya his love interest, Bianca, in the Russian version, while Tom Felton and Ruby Rose take those roles in the English dub.

A pack of wolves settles in a ravine near a village of sheep. Its wise old leader, Magra, announces his retirement, and two candidates must fight to succeed him: the cruel, selfish Ragear and the carefree joker Grey, who is in love with Bianca. When Grey's immaturity leads Bianca to leave him, he visits a gypsy camp, where an eccentric hare named Mami gives him a potion he hopes will win her back. Instead it turns him into a ram. Knocked out while fleeing his former pack, he wakes in the sheep village in the care of Lyra, older sister of the lamb Shia, whom Grey had once spared. Grey struggles with his new form, offends the flock by biting during a tournament, but wins their friendship after protecting Lyra and Shia from two wolves.

Ragear murders Magra and seizes the pack, then learns of Grey's transformation and resolves to destroy the village. After a photograph seems to show Grey as a spy, he leaves the sheep, but Mami tells him of the coming attack and that he can become a wolf again by reaching a certain tree by noon. Grey instead returns to warn the flock and leads its defense, and the wolves are trapped in a flooding cave, from which Grey rescues them. Shia exposes Ragear as Magra's killer, and Grey challenges him. A potion brought by Mami and Bianca seems to fail, but after being buried under rocks Grey emerges as a wolf and sends Ragear over a waterfall to his death. Grey marries Bianca, wolves and sheep live together in peace, and Mami reveals that the potion was only spring water and that his change came from learning responsibility.

The film had a budget of about $3.4 million. It opened at number two in Russia on 1,892 screens and earned over 143 million rubles during a 19-week run. Russian reviews were warm, but critics elsewhere were largely negative, attacking its writing, pacing, characterization and lore while giving some praise to the animation.

title: Rememory
tagline: We are nothing more than the memories we keep.
overview: The widow of a wise professor stumbles upon one of his inventions that's able to record and play a person's memory.
plot:
Sam Bloom (Peter Dinklage) and his brother Dash (Matt Ellis) are driving in the night when their car collides with another, causing his brother’s death.
After a year, scientific pioneer Gordon Dunn (Martin Donovan) mysteriously dies. He has created a device that allows one to record memories and watch them. Bloom sets about trying to solve the murder using this memory machine, while also hoping to recover the memory of his brother's death to understand his final words. Bloom learns that Dunn’s device has a technical fault which causes recurring hallucinations for its users including him. Most of the users have been quite upset with Dunn, directly blaming him for their mental deterioration. He also finds out that Dunn and his wife Carolyn (Julia Ormond) were separated after they lost their only daughter in an accident. After a confrontation with one of his patients, Dunn realized how much pain his machine caused people and attempted to use it to erase his own painful memories. However, doing so resulted in his death when the machine sent him into synaptic failure.
Bloom re-watches his “accident memory” and realizes his brother was just singing song lyrics as he died. The real truth of his memory is realizing that the Dunns were in the other car and that their daughter was killed in the collision. Bloom had fled the scene after seeing the little girl dead, leaving his brother to take the fall. Bloom hands over his memory to Carolyn as a sort of confession apology. Time passes and it is unclear if she watches the memory glass, later she throws it into the sea with Dunn’s recordings as she watches her daughter playing on the water—a hallucination resulting from her own use of the memory device. A montage of the lives of everyone affected by the device is shown over the launch of the repaired memory device while a recording by Dunn plays describing the power of memories for a person.
Sam is last seen at the dock, with a completed model he had created of all of the test subjects, Carolyn, himself, and Dunn and throws it into the water, as a means of allowing himself to let go and move on.

title: Andron
tagline: Only one survives
overview: A group of people are plunged into a dark, claustrophobic maze, where they must fight to survive, as the outside world watches.
plot:
Andron, released internationally as Andròn: The Black Labyrinth, is an Italian-made, English-language dystopian science fiction action film written and directed by Francesco Cinquemani. Leo Howard and Gale Harold head an ensemble of young contestants that also includes Michelle Ryan, Antonia Campbell-Hughes, Jon Kortajarena, Margareth Madè and the Skunk Anansie singer Skin in her first acting role, with Alec Baldwin and Danny Glover in supporting parts. It was produced by Andrea Iervolino and Monika Bacardi for Ambi Pictures and shot in Italy and Malta.

Ten young people wake up in a dark underground maze with no idea how they got there and no memory even of their own names. As fragments of their past return, they are disturbed to find that they seem to come from different periods of history. Moving walls abruptly reshape the labyrinth, separating the group, crushing some of its members and bringing the survivors into contact with new people, while packs of heavily armoured fighters hunt them and a robotic voice announces each death. The captives gradually realize that they are contestants in the Redemption Games, a deadly contest from which only one can emerge alive. The year is 2154, a quarter of a century after a "Big Catastrophe" that killed billions and allowed nine corporations to take over the world and enslave most of humanity. The games are broadcast to pacify the suffering masses outside, who bet on the contestants' survival. Overseeing the show from a vast office is Adam, a television executive and puppet master who watches the action on screens and arbitrarily intervenes to liven things up, answering to his political master, Chancellor Gordon. As their numbers shrink, the survivors, among them Alexander and Julian, must work out the puzzle of where they are and try to find a way out of the labyrinth.

The film premiered at the Trieste Science+Fiction Festival on November 8, 2015, and Momentum Pictures gave it a limited release in the United States in June 2016. It was panned by critics and holds a Metacritic score of 16 out of 100. Dennis Harvey of Variety described it as a drab and dull recycling of The Hunger Games, The Maze Runner and Cube, with Baldwin and Glover barely concealing their disinterest, though he praised Gherardo Gossi's widescreen cinematography and Riccardo Eberspacher's score. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter found it boring, incoherent and derivative.

title: Death Wish
tagline: How Far Would You Go To Protect Your Family?
overview: A mild-mannered father is transformed into a killing machine after his family is torn apart by a violent act.
plot:
Death Wish is a 2018 American vigilante action thriller film directed by Eli Roth, written by Joe Carnahan and produced by Roger Birnbaum. A remake of the 1974 film and the sixth entry in the series, it stars Bruce Willis as Paul Kersey, a Chicago trauma surgeon, with Vincent D'Onofrio as his brother Frank, Elisabeth Shue as his wife Lucy, Camila Morrone as his daughter Jordan, Dean Norris and Kimberly Elise as the detectives Kevin Raines and Leonore Jackson, and Beau Knapp as Knox.

During a family dinner at a restaurant, a valet named Miguel secretly copies the Kerseys' address after overhearing their plans. While Paul is called away to the hospital, Lucy and Jordan come home to find three armed burglars, and in the struggle Lucy is fatally shot and Jordan is left in a coma. Frustrated by the slow police investigation, Paul takes a pistol that falls from a wounded gang member at the hospital and uses it to stop a carjacking. A video goes viral and the media dub him the "Grim Reaper", and after treating a boy hurt for refusing to deal drugs, Paul shoots the dealer known as the Ice Cream Man in broad daylight. Paul recognizes a dying Miguel on his operating table wearing a watch stolen from his home. Miguel's phone leads him to a liquor store that fences stolen goods, where the gunman Fish accidentally kills the owner while trying to shoot Paul. Fish names Joe as another robber before Paul kills him, and Joe, tortured at a body shop, reveals that a third man, Knox, killed Lucy. Paul kills Joe, then exchanges fire with Knox in a nightclub restroom, and both are wounded. Knox describes Paul to the police, and Paul learns that Jordan has woken from her coma. When Knox rides the hospital elevator with them a week later, Paul realizes that he will come after the family, and he legally buys guns. As Knox's crew attacks the house, Paul sends Jordan to hide and call the police, kills the intruders and uses a hidden rifle to kill Knox. The police accept his account after he suggests that he is finished with vigilantism. Months later, dropping Jordan off at New York University, Paul sees a thief snatch a bag and points a finger gun at him.

Shot in Chicago and Montreal from September 2016, the film was released by MGM on 2 March 2018, less than three weeks after the Parkland school shooting, which several critics noted. It grossed $55.9 million on a $30 million budget but received largely negative reviews, earning a 17% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

title: Only the Brave
tagline: It’s not what stands in front of you, it’s who stands beside you
overview: Members of the Granite Mountain Hotshots battle deadly wildfires to save an Arizona town.
plot:
Only the Brave is a 2017 American biographical drama film directed by Joseph Kosinski and written by Ken Nolan, Andrew Niccol, and Christopher McQuarrie. The film is based on the true story of the Granite Mountain Hotshots, an elite team of firefighters from Prescott, Arizona.

The movie begins with a flashback to 2008, where we see the formation of the Granite Mountain Hotshots, led by Brendan McDonough (Josh Brolin), a young and ambitious firefighter. The team is handpicked by their leader, Eric Marsh (Anders Holm), who has a vision for a elite firefighting unit that can tackle the most challenging blazes in Arizona.

As the story unfolds, we see the team come together, consisting of 20 firefighters from different backgrounds, all united by their passion for fighting fires. The team is trained to be self-sufficient and work together seamlessly, with each member having a specific role. They are equipped with state-of-the-art gear and a customized truck that becomes their mobile command center.

The film takes us through the team's rigorous training, where they learn to navigate treacherous terrain, build complex shelters, and develop strategies for tackling massive fires. We see the camaraderie and banter among the team members, as well as their personal struggles and relationships outside of work.

As the summer of 2013 approaches, the Granite Mountain Hotshots are deployed to fight a devastating wildfire in Yarnell Canyon, Arizona. The fire is intense and unpredictable, with flames reaching up to 100 feet high. The team is tasked with creating a firebreak to contain the blaze, but they soon realize that the fire is moving faster than expected.

The film's climax is one of the most intense and emotional scenes in recent memory. As the fire closes in on the team, they make a desperate last stand, using everything at their disposal to try and escape. The scene is both heart-wrenching and awe-inspiring, as we witness the bravery and sacrifice of the Granite Mountain Hotshots.

The movie ends with a somber tone, as we reflect on the tragic loss of life that occurred during the Yarnell Canyon fire. Brendan McDonough's voiceover provides context for the events leading up to the tragedy, while also highlighting the team's unwavering dedication to their craft and each other.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is breathtaking, capturing the vast expanse of Arizona's desert landscapes and the intensity of the wildfires. The performances by Josh Brolin, Miles Teller, and Jeff Bridges are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to the characters.

Overall, Only the Brave is a powerful tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of the Granite Mountain Hotshots. The film is both an emotional rollercoaster and a testament to the human spirit's capacity for courage and resilience in the face of adversity.

title: Life
tagline: Be careful what you search for
overview: The six-member crew of the International Space Station is tasked with studying a sample from Mars that may be the first proof of extra-terrestrial life, which proves more intelligent than ever expected.
plot:
Life is a 2017 American science fiction horror film directed by Daniel Espinosa and written by Rhett Reese and Paul Wernick. The movie stars Jake Gyllenhaal, Rebecca Ferguson, Ryan Reynolds, and Hiroyuki Sanada.

The story begins with the crew of the International Space Station (ISS), led by Captain Oram (Hiroyuki Sanada), who are on a mission to collect samples from Mars. During the journey, they discover a new species of alien life form that has been living in the Martian soil. The creature is small and appears to be harmless at first, but it quickly becomes clear that it's highly aggressive and deadly.

As the crew tries to understand the nature of the creature, they begin to experience strange occurrences on board the ISS. Equipment malfunctions, and some crew members start to act strangely, as if they're being controlled by an unknown force. It becomes apparent that the alien life form has infected one of the crew members, Dr. David Jordan (Jake Gyllenhaal), who is initially excited about the discovery but soon becomes a threat to the rest of the crew.

The crew tries to contain the situation, but it quickly spirals out of control. The creature grows at an alarming rate, and its behavior becomes increasingly erratic and violent. As the crew fights for survival, they realize that the alien life form is not just a simple organism - it's a highly adaptable and intelligent being that can evolve and mutate rapidly.

As the situation worsens, Captain Oram makes the difficult decision to quarantine Dr. Jordan in a separate section of the ISS, hoping to contain the infection. However, this only seems to make things worse, as the creature begins to break free from its restraints and wreak havoc on the rest of the crew.

In the end, it's up to Dr. Miranda North (Rebecca Ferguson), a microbiologist who was initially skeptical of the alien life form, to find a way to stop the creature before it's too late. She discovers that the creature is vulnerable to UV light, which she uses to create a makeshift solution to destroy it.

The movie ends with a tense and suspenseful climax as Dr. North faces off against the creature in a desperate bid to save the rest of the crew. In the end, she succeeds in destroying the alien life form, but not before it has claimed several lives and left the crew of the ISS forever changed by their encounter with the unknown.

Overall, Life is a tense and thrilling sci-fi horror movie that explores the dangers of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's use of practical effects to create the alien creature is impressive, and Jake Gyllenhaal delivers a standout performance as the increasingly unhinged Dr. Jordan.

title: Stronger
tagline: Strength Defines Us
overview: A victim of the Boston Marathon bombing in 2013 helps the police track down the killers while struggling to recover from devastating trauma.
plot:
Jeff Bauman is a well-intentioned but underachieving Boston native who works at the deli counter of a Costco and lives in a small two-bedroom apartment with his alcoholic mother, Patty. One day at the local bar, Jeff runs into his ex-girlfriend Erin, who is attracted to his kindness and charm, but finds herself constantly frustrated by his lack of commitment. After learning that Erin is running in the 2013 Boston Marathon to raise money for the hospital she works at, Jeff asks every patron in the bar to donate and then promises Erin he'll wait at the finish line for her with a big sign.
The day of the Marathon, Jeff scrambles to make it to the finish line on time, but reaches it before Erin does. As she approaches the finish line, a bomb goes off right where Jeff is standing. After being rushed to a hospital, both of Jeff's legs are amputated above the knee. When he regains consciousness, Jeff tells his brother that he saw the bomber before the explosion. Patty calls the FBI, where Jeff is able to give them a description of Tamerlan Tsarnaev. Local authorities capture Dzhokhar Tsarnaev days later, and Jeff is hailed as a hero.
Jeff struggles to adjust to his condition, as well as his newfound fame. Patty books several interviews and constantly surrounds Jeff with news reporters during his rehab sessions, to which Erin, who has since rekindled her relationship with Jeff, objects. Jeff and his family are invited by the Boston Bruins to Game 2 of the first round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs against the Chicago Blackhawks. The Bruins organization asks Jeff to wave the flag during the game's opening ceremony. The crowd at TD Garden triggers traumatic flashbacks for Jeff, and he breaks down in the elevator. Erin comforts him and insists he talk to his family about the fragility of his mental state and the impact his newfound exposure is having on it. Later that night, they make love for the first time since his injury.
Patty books Jeff an interview with Oprah Winfrey without telling him, causing Erin to speak up and tell Patty that the constant media attention is intensifying Jeff's PTSD. After an argument between Patty and Erin, Jeff finally admits that he doesn't want to do any more interviews. A disheartened Patty tells him that she only wishes for the world to see how amazing her son is. She soon begins enabling Jeff's worst tendencies, including his laziness and affinity for drinking. He begins missing physical therapy appointments due to long nights of drinking, usually with Patty. Erin, who has since moved in, finds Patty blacked out on the couch and an unconscious Jeff in a bathtub, covered in feces. The next day, she snaps at Patty for her selfishness and negligence before calling Jeff out for his self-pity and refusal to stand up to his mother. Erin storms off, leaving Jeff and Patty to drive home alone.
That night, Jeff blows off Erin to drink with his brothers at a bar.

title: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Justice League - Gotham City Breakout
original_title: LEGO DC Comics Super Heroes: Justice League - Gotham City Breakout
overview: The caped crusader reluctantly agrees to let Batgirl and Nightwing take him on a long overdue vacation from crime-fighting, while Superman and the Justice League watch over Gotham City.
plot:
Batman and Robin chase Penguin and Harley Quinn, and after defeating Harley and Poison Ivy, Batman leaves Robin with the defeated criminals and chases after a criminal who resembles a ninja. After cornering the criminal in an alleyway, Batman is able to deduce that he is Nightwing, who was attempting to lure Batman into a surprise birthday party. Batgirl, Robin and Nightwing reveal that as a present for Batman, they decided to take him on vacation. Superman is willing to temporarily replace Batman, believing that Gotham's criminals would be easy to defeat due to most lacking superpowers. The Justice League and Teen Titans are able to convince Batman to accept the vacation, while Robin stays behind to help Superman.
Meanwhile, at Arkham Asylum, Joker escapes by digging out with a spoon, and Batman figures out that Nightwing and Batgirl plan to have him visit the dojo of his former martial arts sensei, Madame Mantis. After a brief reunion battle with his former sensei, Batman discovers it was actually a disguised minion of Deathstroke. Batman, Batgirl, and Nightwing then find Deathstroke and follow him into a cave.
Meanwhile, in Gotham City, Superman finds out about Joker's escape and ignores Robin's warning about him. Unfortunately, this allows Joker to trick Superman into freeing Harley Quinn, Penguin, Poison Ivy and Scarecrow from Arkham. Superman calls Cyborg in hopes of gaining assistance to stop the escaped villains.
Batman, Nightwing, and Batgirl end up falling down a waterfall in the cave. Batman explains his past with Deathstroke. At the bottom of the waterfall, Batman, Nightwing, and Batgirl discover an underground kingdom of Trogowogs (a hidden underground race of short, green humanoids). They immediately attack Batman, who ultimately surrenders to Deathstroke when the latter threatens to kill Nightwing and Batgirl. They are then introduced to the Trogowog leader, Bane, who gained his position using a pink crystal known as the Psyche Stone.
Back in Gotham, Poison Ivy easily defeats Superman and Cyborg. Superman reluctantly summons Wonder Woman, but Poison Ivy stuns them with her pheromones. By the time the effect wears off, they have been taken to Joker's funhouse where they are doused with Scarecrow's fear gas and put them in molten Kryptonite and more pheromones to be boiled into soup. Robin notices this and goes to save the Justice League.
Back in the Trogowog kingdom, Batman, Nightwing and Batgirl are held in the dungeon, stripped of their utility belts and imprisoned with Madame Mantis and Trogowog prince Grungle (the only one not to fall victim to the Psyche Stone). Grungle reveals that the Trogowogs were once a peaceful and friendly race until Bane killed his father, imprisoned him, and used the Psyche Stone to make the Trogowogs more violent. Batman frees them with a brick separator, but they are recaptured and Batman reluctantly uses the Psyche Stone to learn the "Forbidden Move", which creates destructive chi projectiles.

title: Molly's Game
tagline: Deal with her.
overview: Molly Bloom, a young skier and former Olympic hopeful becomes a successful entrepreneur (and a target of an FBI investigation) when she establishes a high-stakes, international poker game.
plot:
Molly Bloom is a world-class mogul skier, trained from a young age by her overbearing father, until a career-ending injury during a qualifying event for the 2002 Winter Olympics. Postponing her law school plans, she moves to Los Angeles where, working as a bottle service waitress, she meets real estate developer Dean Keith. He hires her as his round-the-clock office manager, and soon orders her to run his weekly underground poker game at The Cobra Lounge. Molly learns how to appeal to the rich and famous players, particularly the movie star "Player X".
Frustrated by Molly's large tips, Dean fires her, but she poaches his players for her own lucrative and technically legal poker game. After the skilled but risk-averse Harlan Eustice loses a hand to hedge fund manager Brad Marion, a notoriously bad player, Harlan makes increasingly desperate bets on tilt until he owes Molly $1.2 million he cannot pay. Player X loans Harlan the money in exchange for half of his ongoing winnings, revealing that he has been staking Harlan for years. Bitter over Molly's disapproval and lack of romantic interest in him, Player X spitefully draws her players to another game, and her poker ring collapses.
Moving to New York City, Molly enlists models to recruit wealthy players as she establishes a new underground poker empire. With millions at stake, her dealer convinces her to take a percentage of the pot to offset potential losses, making the game an illegal gambling operation. When Brad's hedge fund is exposed as a Ponzi scheme, he points law enforcement to Molly, who pays $500,000 in restitution to his victims rather than testify. The stress of her high-stakes life takes a toll as she becomes addicted to drugs, and allows wealthy members of the Russian mafia to join her game.
Molly's driver introduces her to the Italian mafia, but she declines to let them extort her players. In retaliation, a gunman attacks Molly in her home, stealing the contents of her safe and threatening to kill her and her mother. Unwilling to go to a hospital, Molly spends two weeks recuperating alone in her apartment, only to learn the mobsters have been caught up in unrelated arrests. Douglas Downey, a player infatuated with Molly, warns her that he has been forced to inform on her to the FBI. Her game is raided while over $4 million is seized from her bank account, and a penniless Molly moves home with her mother.
Two years since running her last game, Molly has published a memoir to pay her debts, and is arrested by heavily armed FBI agents for her former inadvertent ties to organized crime. She meets with high-profile attorney Charlie Jaffey, who unexpectedly takes her case after realizing that she refused to work with the mob. Charlie negotiates for Molly to receive immunity and her seized funds in exchange for her hard drives, but Molly refuses to risk destroying her players' lives and tarnishing her own name.

title: Woman Walks Ahead
tagline: Defy your times
overview: Based on a true story, this riveting western follows a headstrong New York widow as she journeys west to meet Sioux chief Sitting Bull, facing off with an army officer intent on war with Native Americans.
plot:
Woman Walks Ahead is a biographical Western drama of 2017 directed by Susanna White and written by Steven Knight. Jessica Chastain plays Catherine Weldon, a character inspired by the real Caroline Weldon, a New York portrait painter who travels to the Dakotas in 1890 to paint Sitting Bull, played by Michael Greyeyes. Sam Rockwell appears as the army officer Colonel Silas Grove, Ciarán Hinds as the Indian agent James McLaughlin and Bill Camp as General Crook.

Recently widowed, Catherine writes to Sitting Bull through McLaughlin at Fort Yates, asking to make his portrait. The agent secretly destroys the letter and orders her detained. On the train the colonel advises her to go home. When she arrives, a passerby steals her trunk and art supplies, and at Fort Yates she is confined overnight; the colonel returns her stolen belongings and warns her that the recent fighting between the army and the Lakota is far from forgotten. Next morning Sitting Bull's nephew, an agency employee, takes her to him. Sitting Bull agrees to sit for $1,000, and she stays on the reservation. The colonel warns her not to raise the Lakota's hopes, since a treaty taking more of their land is about to be ratified and General Crook and the 7th Cavalry are on their way.

Sitting Bull first appears for the portrait in an ordinary suit, then changes into traditional buckskins at Catherine's request. Returning, they find the village empty: the people have seen a draft of the treaty, which would halve their rations and take their land, and suspecting Catherine of being a spy, have joined a Ghost Dance. Catherine buys all the food in town for the reservation and is beaten by townsmen for it. Recovering, she announces at a dinner with Crook that she will fight the treaty, and campaigns alongside Sitting Bull, whose arrival at the vote silences the chiefs bribed to testify falsely. The treaty is overwhelmingly rejected, but the colonel tells her this gives the army its pretext for war. Sitting Bull, foreseeing his death that winter, sees the finished portrait before the colonel warns him in Lakota of an arrest at dawn and carries Catherine off for her safety. During the arrest, a hidden sniper shoots Sitting Bull dead. Closing titles note the Wounded Knee massacre that followed and Catherine's lifelong advocacy.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2017 and was released by A24 and DirecTV Cinema in 2018. Reviews were mixed, praising the two leads.

title: The Meyerowitz Stories (New and Selected)
overview: An estranged family gathers together in New York for an event celebrating the artistic work of their father.
plot:
The Meyerowitz Stories (New and Selected) is a 2017 American comedy-drama written and directed by Noah Baumbach. Adam Sandler, Ben Stiller and Elizabeth Marvel star as the adult children of a self-absorbed artist played by Dustin Hoffman, with Emma Thompson as his fourth wife and Grace Van Patten as Sandler's daughter. The film competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival and was released in theaters and on Netflix in October 2017.

After separating from his wife, the unemployed musician Danny Meyerowitz moves in with his father, Harold, a retired Bard College art professor and sculptor, and Harold's fourth wife, Maureen, a pleasant but scatterbrained hippie. Danny is close to his daughter, Eliza, a freshman film student at Bard whose provocative short films embarrass the family. Danny's sister, Jean, lives a quiet, solitary life, while their younger half-brother, Matthew, is a successful financial adviser in Los Angeles.

Harold, who believes the art world has unjustly forgotten him, refuses to take part in a group faculty show at Bard. He and Danny attend a retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art for Harold's more successful contemporary, L.J. Shapiro, where Harold feels so uncomfortable that he runs off down the street, and Danny chases after him, cutting short a promising encounter with Shapiro's daughter, Loretta. In town on business, Matthew meets Harold for lunch and tries to persuade him to sell his Manhattan house and his sculptures, provoking resentment. When Harold suffers a serious health crisis and is hospitalized, the three siblings are forced to come together, confronting old grievances, their father's favoritism and the ways in which his ego has shaped their lives. Jean reveals a painful secret from her youth, Danny and Matthew finally air their rivalry, and the family prepares for the Bard exhibition honoring Harold's work.

The film received positive reviews, with a 92 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Baumbach's bittersweet view of family dynamics and the remarkable cast, and a Metacritic score of 79. Sandler's performance was especially praised as one of the best of his career. At Cannes the film also won the Palm Dog award for its canine performer.

title: Annabelle: Creation
tagline: You don't know the real story
overview: Several years after the tragic death of their little girl, a doll maker and his wife welcome a nun and several girls from a shuttered orphanage into their home, soon becoming the target of the doll maker's possessed creation—Annabelle.
plot:
Annabelle: Creation is a 2017 supernatural horror film directed by David F. Sandberg and written by Gary Dauberman. The movie serves as a prequel to the 2014 film Annabelle, which was also based on the popular doll.

The story begins in 1945, during World War II, at the Orphanage of Saint Agnes, where a young nun named Sister Charlotte (Linda Cropper) is tasked with caring for a group of orphaned children. The orphans are being cared for by the nuns, but they are struggling to cope with the trauma and loss they have experienced.

One day, a mysterious dollmaker named Samuel Mullins (Anthony LaPaglia) arrives at the orphanage, seeking refuge from his troubled past. He is haunted by the memory of his deceased wife, who was killed in a tragic accident involving one of her own dolls. Mullins becomes obsessed with creating the perfect doll, and he begins to work on a new doll that he believes will bring him peace.

As Mullins works on his doll, he becomes increasingly unhinged, and his behavior becomes erratic. The other nuns at the orphanage begin to suspect that something is wrong with him, but they are powerless to stop him. Meanwhile, Sister Charlotte begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences in the orphanage, which she attributes to the presence of evil spirits.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Mullins' doll has become a vessel for an ancient evil entity known as Annabelle, who was once a young girl named Annabelle Higgins. The doll is imbued with a malevolent spirit that feeds on fear and terror, and it begins to exert its influence over the other children at the orphanage.

As the situation spirals out of control, Sister Charlotte and the other nuns are forced to confront the evil entity head-on. In a desperate bid to save the children, they perform an exorcism on Annabelle, but the ritual goes horribly wrong, and the doll is left with a piece of her soul.

The movie ends with Mullins' descent into madness, as he becomes convinced that his doll has become a vessel for the evil entity. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Annabelle was not just a simple doll, but a key to unlocking an ancient evil that had been imprisoned for centuries.

Throughout the movie, the tension builds slowly, as the audience is left wondering what will happen next. The special effects are impressive, and the doll itself is terrifyingly realistic. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Anthony LaPaglia, who brings depth and nuance to his portrayal of Samuel Mullins.

Overall, Annabelle: Creation is a chilling and atmospheric horror movie that explores themes of trauma, grief, and the supernatural. While it may not be as scary as some other horror movies, it is a well-crafted and engaging film that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

overview: After finding an ad online for “video work,” Sara, a video artist whose primary focus is creating intimacy with lonely men, thinks she may have found the subject of her dreams. plot:
A prolific serial killer, using the name "Aaron" after a previous victim, undergoes a midlife crisis as his fortieth birthday approaches, finding himself dissatisfied with his killings. When his latest ad for a videographer lures YouTuber Sara to his remote cabin, Aaron changes his approach by admitting he is a serial killer who will let Sara live for the next 24 hours if she records a documentary on his life. Sara, doubting his revelation, agrees to film Aaron in the hopes that the video will popularize her unsuccessful web series about eccentric Craigslist clients.
Over the course of the day, Aaron struggles to intimidate Sara, who plays along with his various eccentricities. Sara eventually admits that she does not believe Aaron is truly a serial killer, whereupon Aaron informs her that he intends to conclude the documentary by having her kill him. He later stages a suicide attempt, much to her horror. As she prepares to leave, he convinces her to stay. The two have a conversation in which Aaron admits he is a virgin who has never kissed anyone. Surprised at this revelation, Sara offers to kiss him, to which he agrees.
Aaron brings Sara into the woods, where he gifts her the same heart-shaped locket he had given to his victim in the previous film, then shows her to an open grave he dug. He then proceeds to stab himself in the stomach before handing her the knife and imploring her to stab herself, hoping to conclude their film in the same manner as Romeo and Juliet. When she attempts to flee, he stabs her and drags her to the grave. Aaron approaches the camera and starts to give a closing monologue, but a still-alive Sara emerges from the grave and strikes him in the back of the head with a shovel before fleeing.
Afterwards, Sara is recorded in public by an unidentified individual whistling a tune heard in Aaron's videos. When Sara notices the individual filming her, the camera abruptly cuts away.

title: Train to Busan
tagline: Life-or-death survival begins.
overview: When a zombie virus pushes Korea into a state of emergency, those trapped on an express train to Busan must fight for their own survival.
plot:
Train to Busan is a 2016 South Korean post-apocalyptic horror film directed by Yeon Sang-ho. The movie takes place in a world where a mysterious virus has turned most of humanity into violent, zombie-like creatures.

The story begins with Seok-woo (played by Gong Yoo), a wealthy stockbroker who lives in Seoul with his wife Soo-an (played by Kim Su-an) and their young son Su-an. On the day of their daughter's birthday party, Seok-woo receives an unexpected phone call from his mother, who is bedridden with cancer, asking him to take care of her. Feeling guilty for not spending enough time with his family, Seok-woo decides to visit his mother in Busan.

As they board the KTX train to Busan, Seok-woo and Soo-an are unaware of the impending disaster that awaits them. The train is suddenly attacked by a group of zombies, who have been infected by the mysterious virus. The passengers and crew fight for survival as the train becomes a battleground.

Seok-woo's mother dies shortly after they arrive in Busan, but he continues on to find his daughter, who has gone missing. Along the way, he meets a young girl named Sung-gyeol (played by Kim Soo-an), who is also searching for her family. As they navigate through the treacherous streets of Busan, Seok-woo and Sung-gyeol form an unlikely bond.

As the train's passengers are picked off one by one, Seok-woo and Sung-gyeol discover that the virus has been caused by a mysterious outbreak in China. The government is trying to contain the outbreak, but it's too late, and the virus has spread globally.

The duo eventually boards a bus to escape the chaos, but they soon realize that the bus is also infested with zombies. In a desperate bid to survive, Seok-woo sacrifices himself to save Sung-gyeol by pushing her off the moving bus.

In the end, Sung-gyeol manages to find her way back to her father's office building in Seoul, where she finds him alive and well. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Sung-gyeol finally finding some sense of closure and reunion with her family.

Throughout the movie, Yeon Sang-ho explores themes of class struggle, social inequality, and the breakdown of society in the face of catastrophic disaster. The film's tense atmosphere and graphic violence make it a thrilling ride, but its thought-provoking commentary on human nature makes it more than just a mindless horror flick.

Overall, Train to Busan is a gripping and intense thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and social commentary, it's no wonder this movie has become a modern classic in the zombie genre.

title: Super Dark Times
overview: Teenagers Zach and Josh have been best friends their whole lives, but when a gruesome accident leads to a cover-up, the secret drives a wedge between them and propels them down a rabbit hole of escalating paranoia and violence.
plot:
In 1996, in Upstate New York, two teenage best friends, Zach and Josh, rate the girls in their yearbook. They find a common interest in Allison.
After school, the duo crosses the path of the universally-disliked Daryl and his eighth-grade friend Charlie. Later that week, the four boys meet up at Josh's house where they look through the possessions of Josh's brother, who is away in the military, and find a bag of marijuana and a katana.
Afterwards, the boys play with the sword in a secluded park area bordering the local cemetery and notice that Daryl has stolen the marijuana. After a tense argument, Josh and Daryl fight, resulting in Daryl being accidentally stabbed in the neck with the katana. Daryl runs from the scene but only makes it into the adjacent forest where he dies. The boys panic and hide both Daryl's body and the weapon.
At school, rumors circulate about Daryl's disappearance. Zach has nightmares and Josh doesn't attend classes. Zach wants to return to Daryl's burial site and attend Allison's upcoming party with Josh, who declines but goes to Allison's party separately where he shares his brother's weed. Zach, disturbed, leaves.
Another student, John, is found dead. Rumors speculate that he fell off a bridge. Zach suspects that Josh is responsible for John's death. He returns to Daryl's burial site and finds the katana missing and Daryl's corpse mutilated.
Zach goes to Josh's home and realizes Josh is with Allison. He tracks her to Meghan's house, where Josh has killed Meghan with the katana and tied Allison up. After Zach unties her, the former friends fight until a neighbor intervenes and subdues Josh, who is arrested, while Zach's fate is left unknown.
Months later, Allison has recovered and returns to school. A camera shot shows three parallel lines on the back of her neck.

title: The Autopsy of Jane Doe
tagline: Every body has a secret.
overview: Father and son coroners receive a mysterious unidentified corpse with no apparent cause of death. As they attempt to examine the "Jane Doe," they discover increasingly bizarre clues that hold the key to her terrifying secrets.
plot:
The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by André Øvredal from a screenplay by Øvredal and Joel Bergman. The movie stars Brian Cox, Anthony Mackie, and Hailee Steinfeld.

The story begins with the death of a young woman named Jane Doe, who is found dead in her apartment. Her body is discovered by her landlord, who calls the local coroner's office to report the incident. Dr. Aaron Hunt (Brian Cox) and his son, Corbin (Anthony Mackie), are called to perform an autopsy on Jane.

As they begin the examination, they notice that Jane's body appears to be in pristine condition, with no signs of trauma or injury. However, as they delve deeper into the autopsy, they start to uncover strange and inexplicable details about her life. They find a series of cryptic symbols etched into her skin, which seem to be some sort of code.

As the autopsy progresses, Corbin becomes increasingly unsettled by the strange occurrences surrounding Jane's body. He begins to suspect that something supernatural is at play, but his father is skeptical and dismissive of these concerns.

Despite their initial reservations, the doctors soon realize that they are dealing with a malevolent entity that has taken possession of Jane's body. The entity, which appears to be some sort of ancient being, begins to exert its influence over Corbin, causing him to experience terrifying hallucinations and visions.

As the night wears on, the situation becomes increasingly dire, and Corbin's grip on reality begins to slip. His father tries to intervene, but he is powerless against the entity's malevolent forces.

In a desperate bid to save his son, Dr. Hunt turns to an ancient ritual that may be able to banish the entity from Jane's body. However, this comes at a terrible cost, and Corbin is forced to confront the dark secrets of his family's past in order to survive.

The movie builds towards a shocking climax as Corbin faces off against the entity in a desperate bid for survival. In the end, only one of them will emerge victorious, and the consequences of their confrontation will be devastating.

Throughout the movie, Øvredal uses a slow-burning tension to build suspense and unease, creating a sense of creeping dread that permeates every frame. The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a masterclass in atmospheric horror, using the setting and the characters' interactions to create a sense of unease and uncertainty.

The movie's use of symbolism and metaphor adds depth and complexity to the narrative, exploring themes of grief, trauma, and the supernatural. The performances from Cox and Mackie are outstanding, bringing a sense of gravitas and intensity to their roles.

Overall, The Autopsy of Jane Doe is a chilling and unsettling horror movie that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

title: Vengeance: A Love Story
tagline: Beyond good and evil is Justice
overview: When a new friend is brutally assaulted, Detective John Droomor is put by chance in charge of the investigation. Although the evidence against the perpetrators seems overwhelming, there is nothing definitive in the case that guarantees justice is served, even more so if some people are willing to twist and betray it.
plot:
Vengeance: A Love Story is a 2017 American action thriller directed by former stuntman Johnny Martin from a screenplay by John Mankiewicz, a writer-producer of House of Cards. It is based on Joyce Carol Oates's 2003 novel Rape: A Love Story. Nicolas Cage stars as John Dromoor, a Niagara Falls police detective and Gulf War veteran, with Anna Hutchison as Teena Maguire, Talitha Bateman as her 12-year-old daughter, Bethie, Deborah Kara Unger as Teena's mother, Agnes, and Don Johnson as the defense attorney Jay Kirkpatrick.

The film opens with a bust that goes badly wrong, showing Dromoor's questionable judgment, and he drinks away his troubles in a bar where he meets Teena, a flirtatious single mother who quickly catches his interest. After a Fourth of July party, Teena and Bethie take a shortcut home through the dark woods, where Teena is gang-raped, beaten and left for dead in front of her daughter by a group of four meth addicts. Bethie makes her way back to the road and flags down a passing car, which happens to be driven by Dromoor.

While Teena recovers, Agnes takes on the care of both her daughter and granddaughter. Bethie identifies the attackers and a hearing is set to decide whether the case will go to trial. The defendants' families hire Kirkpatrick, a nationally renowned criminal defense lawyer, who turns the proceedings against the traumatized victim by attacking her sobriety, her parenting and her sex life, while the judge appears all too friendly with him. When the case seems lost and the men are set free, Dromoor, a lone wolf suffering from post-traumatic stress, refuses to accept the failure of the legal system and sets out on his own campaign of vigilante justice against the attackers on Teena's behalf, eventually confronting the lawyer and offering comfort to both Bethie and her mother.

The project had first been planned for production in Michigan around 2009 with Samuel L. Jackson, Dianne Wiest and Abigail Breslin attached, but stalled. Cage joined in February 2016 and was briefly announced as director before stepping back, and filming began that April. The film was released direct to video in the United Kingdom in March 2017 and by FilmRise in the United States on September 15, 2017. Reviews were negative: Michael Rechtshaffen of the Los Angeles Times called it ham-handed and cliché-ridden and found Cage's performance detached, while Flickering Myth criticized its overwrought acting and tidy, consequence-free ending.

title: Rendel
tagline: Revenge begets revenge.
overview: Rendel, a masked superhero, becomes blinded by his desire for revenge against a sinister criminal organization.
plot:
Rendel, also known as Rendel: Dark Vengeance, is a 2017 Finnish superhero action film written, produced and directed by Jesse Haaja and based on his own original character. It stars Kris Gummerus as Rendel, with Matti Onnismaa, Rami Rusinen and Renne Korppila in the other leading roles and Alina Tomnikov, Tero Salenius, Aake Kalliala, Anu Palevaara and Kristina Karjalainen in the supporting cast.

In the city of Mikkeli, a company called VALA has developed a lucrative vaccine without proper testing. VALA is a front for a criminal organization led by Pekka Erola, whose son Jarno, known as Rotikka, is one of its most violent enforcers. The gang's operations are being disrupted by a mysterious masked vigilante dressed in black, who leaves his victims marked with the name Rendel.

Through flashbacks, the film reveals the story of Rämö, a financial director and devoted family man. After refusing to invest in a scheme proposed by one of VALA's men, he loses his job and struggles to find work, until he is hired by VALA to handle paperwork. There he discovers that the vaccine, made from a tar-like substance that bonds permanently to skin, has not been properly tested and has caused numerous deaths. Fearing that Rämö will become a whistleblower, Erola sends Rotikka and his henchman to kill him. Rämö's wife and daughter are murdered, and he is beaten and left for dead, but he survives. Covering his face with the tar to create a mask and wearing the biker jacket his family gave him, he becomes Rendel, a dark avenger whose name comes from the Hungarian word for order. As his war against the organization escalates, VALA's leaders hire a team of foreign mercenaries to destroy him, while a mysterious woman named Marla offers him help.

The film combines brutal, stylized action with a dark revenge story set in a small Finnish city, offering an independently produced take on the superhero genre.

Rendel won the Best Action Movie award at the Feratum Film Festival in Mexico. A sequel, Rendel 2: Cycle of Revenge, was filmed in the Kainuu region in 2019, and an English-language continuation featuring Gummerus was later announced.

Votto has offered a large sum of money to discreetly rescue his abducted daughter, Nina. He gives Joe the address of a brothel for wealthy patrons sent via an anonymous text. Joe stakes out the brothel, kills several security guards and patrons, and rescues Nina. While Joe and Nina await Votto's arrival in a hotel room, the news reports that Votto has committed suicide. Police officers gain access to the room with the help of the desk clerk, kill the clerk, and take Nina. Joe escapes after killing an officer sent to kill him.

Arriving back at his home, Joe discovers that two agents have murdered his mother and have been waiting for him. He kills one agent and mortally wounds the other. As the agent is dying, he reveals that Votto and Governor Williams are pedophiles and child traffickers and that Nina is Williams's favorite. He explains that Williams is directing the authorities to cover up the trafficking. Joe drives to a lake in a forest to give his mother a water burial and fills his pockets with stones, with the intent of killing himself. As he sinks, he has a vision of Nina. Removing the stones from his pockets, he swims back to the surface.
Joe follows Williams to his country home and fights his way in, only to discover Williams with his throat slit. He searches the house and discovers Nina, who is seated at a dining room table, alongside a bloody straight razor. Although Joe has become increasingly upset, Nina reassures him that she is alright. title: Call Me by Your Name

overview: In 1980s Italy, a relationship begins between seventeen-year-old teenage Elio and the older adult man hired as his father's research assistant.
plot:
In the summer of 1983, Elio Perlman, a 17-year-old Jewish French-Italian boy, lives with his parents in rural Northern Italy. Elio's father, a professor of archaeology, invites a 24-year-old Jewish-American graduate student, Oliver, to live with the family over the summer and help with his academic paperwork. Elio, an introspective bookworm and musician, initially thinks he has little in common with Oliver, who appears confident and carefree. Elio spends much of the summer reading, playing piano, and hanging out with his childhood friends, Chiara and Marzia. During a volleyball match, Oliver touches Elio's back, but Elio brushes it off. Elio later finds himself jealous upon seeing Oliver kiss Chiara.
Elio and Oliver spend more time together, taking long walks into town, and accompanying Elio's father on an archaeological trip. Elio is increasingly drawn to Oliver, even sneaking into Oliver's room to smell his clothing. Elio eventually confesses his feelings to Oliver, who tells him they cannot discuss such things. Later, in a secluded spot, the two kiss for the first time. Oliver is reluctant to take things further, and they do not speak for several days.
Elio goes on a date with Marzia and the two have sex. Elio leaves a note for Oliver to end their silence. Oliver writes back, asking Elio to meet him at midnight. Elio agrees and they sleep together for the first time. Afterward, Oliver tells Elio, "Call me by your name and I'll call you by mine". The morning after, Elio is briefly conflicted about their encounter and takes out his sexual frustration by masturbating with a peach. When Oliver finds him, Elio cries about how little time he and Oliver have left together. Marzia confronts Elio after not hearing from him for three days. He responds indifferently, hurting her.
As the end of Oliver's stay approaches, Elio's parents, who appear aware of the bond between the two, recommend that he and Oliver visit Bergamo together before Oliver returns to the U.S. They spend three romantic days together. Heartbroken after Oliver's departure, Elio calls his mother to ask her to pick him up from the train station and take him home. Marzia is sympathetic to Elio's feelings and says she wants to remain friends. Elio's father, observing his unhappiness, tells him that the bond he had with Oliver was rare and that he envies Elio because he never had what Elio and Oliver had. He consoles Elio by advising him to keep his heart open for more joy and experiences rather than close himself off.
During Hanukkah, Oliver calls Elio's family to tell them he is engaged to be married to a woman he has been intermittently dating for a few years. Elio calls Oliver by his (Elio's) name and Oliver responds with his (Oliver's); Oliver says "[he] remember everything". After the call, Elio sits by the fireplace and stares into the flames, tearfully reflecting as his parents and staff prepare dinner.

title: The Irishman

plot:
In a nursing home, elderly Irish American World War II veteran Frank Sheeran narrates his time as a hitman for the Italian-American Mafia.
In 1950s Philadelphia, Sheeran works as a union delivery truck driver, where he starts selling some of the meat shipments to a local Philadelphia Italian American gangster known as "Skinny Razor," a member of the Philadelphia crime family headed by Angelo Bruno. After the delivery company accuses Sheeran of theft, union lawyer Bill Bufalino gets the case dismissed when Sheeran refuses to name his customers to the judge.
Bill introduces Sheeran to his cousin Russell Bufalino, head of his namesake crime family in Northeastern Pennsylvania. Sheeran begins to carry out jobs for him, as well as members of the South Philadelphia underworld, including "painting houses," a euphemism for contract killing.
Sheeran is soon introduced to Jimmy Hoffa, head of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, who has financial ties with the Northeastern Pennsylvania crime family. He is struggling to deal with fellow rising Teamster Anthony "Tony Pro" Provenzano, in addition to mounting pressure from the federal government. Hoffa becomes close with Sheeran and his family, especially his daughter Peggy; in turn Sheeran becomes his chief bodyguard.
After the 1960 election of John F. Kennedy, Bufalino is thrilled while Hoffa is furious. Kennedy's brother, Robert F. Kennedy, whom he appointed Attorney General, forms a "Get Hoffa" squad to bring down Hoffa, who is eventually arrested and convicted in 1964 for jury tampering.
While Hoffa is in prison, his replacement as Teamsters president, Frank "Fitz" Fitzsimmons, misuses the union's pension fund and gives interest-free loans to the Mafia. Hoffa's relationship with Tony Pro, himself arrested for extortion, also deteriorates beyond repair when Hoffa refuses to help restore his forfeited pension. Hoffa's sentence is commuted by President Richard Nixon in 1971, although he is forbidden from partaking in any Teamsters activities until 1980.
Despite his parole terms, Hoffa undertakes a plan to reclaim his power atop the Teamsters. His growing disrespect for other Teamster leaders and his intention to separate the union from the Mafia begin to worry Russell. During a dinner in Sheeran's honor in October 1973, Russell pleads with Sheeran to confront Hoffa and warn him that the heads of the crime families are displeased with his behavior. Hoffa then informs Sheeran that he "knows things" that Russell and the dons of other families are unaware of and claims that what he knows makes him untouchable, for if anything ever happened to him, they would all end up in prison.
In 1975, while on their way to the wedding of Bill's daughter, Russell reluctantly informs Sheeran that the dons have become fed up with Hoffa and have sanctioned his murder. Russell further informs Sheeran that he must serve as the triggerman, knowing he might otherwise try to warn or save Hoffa.

title: The Commuter
tagline: Lives are on the line
overview: A businessman, on his daily commute home, gets unwittingly caught up in a criminal conspiracy that threatens not only his life but the lives of those around him.
plot:
The Commuter is a 2018 action thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra, in his fourth collaboration with Liam Neeson, and written by Byron Willinger, Philip de Blasi and Ryan Engle. Neeson stars as a former policeman drawn into a murder conspiracy on his daily train ride, alongside Vera Farmiga, Patrick Wilson, Jonathan Banks, Florence Pugh and Sam Neill.

Michael MacCauley, a former NYPD officer turned insurance salesman, rides the same Hudson Line train between Tarrytown and Grand Central every day. Suddenly laid off and afraid to tell his wife, he confides in his former partner, Murphy, who is still on the force. On the ride home, a mysterious woman named Joanna offers him a "hypothetical" deal: find a passenger known as "Prynne," who has something that does not belong to them, for $100,000, starting with $25,000 hidden in the bathroom. Michael takes the money, but when he tries to get off, he is handed his wife's wedding ring as a warning. A commuter he asks for help is pushed under a bus, and Joanna reveals that his family is being held and that he must plant a GPS tracker on Prynne.

Michael's attempts to identify Prynne go wrong: the man he tags turns out to be an FBI agent, found dead soon after. Murphy tells him that Prynne is a key witness to the supposed suicide of city official Enrique Mendez, and Michael realizes that Prynne is to be killed and that he is being framed. He forces the passengers into the last car and kills another passenger, Oliver, who had been hired to murder Prynne. Prynne turns out to be Sofia, a teenage girl holding evidence against powerful people, who was being escorted to witness protection. When Michael refuses to kill her, Joanna detonates explosives to derail the train, but Michael uncouples the final car and saves most of the passengers. Police surround the car, believing he has taken hostages, and Murphy is sent in to negotiate, inadvertently revealing that he is the corrupt cop who killed Mendez. Michael removes Murphy's identifying tag, and snipers shoot Murphy. Sofia testifies, Michael's family is rescued, and he is offered his old job back. Later, he confronts Joanna on a train and prepares to arrest her.

Released by Lionsgate in the United States on January 12, 2018, The Commuter grossed $119.9 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, with critics comparing it to Non-Stop but praising Neeson's performance; Rotten Tomatoes reported 55% approval and Metacritic a score of 56.

title: The Shape of Water
tagline: A Fairy Tale for Troubled Times
overview: An other-worldly story, set against the backdrop of Cold War era America circa 1962, where a mute janitor working at a lab falls in love with an amphibious man being held captive there and devises a plan to help him escape.
plot:
In 1962, during the Cold War, Elisa Esposito works as a janitor in a secret government laboratory in Baltimore, Maryland. Found abandoned by the side of a river as an infant with scars on her neck, Elisa is mute and communicates through sign language. Her only friends are her closeted middle-aged neighbor Giles, an advertising illustrator, and her coworker Zelda.
Colonel Richard Strickland has captured a creature from a South American river and taken it to the facility for study, losing two fingers (which are unsuccessfully retransplanted) while interrogating it. Elisa discovers it is a humanoid amphibian, and bonds with the creature after visiting him in secret. Seeking an advantage in the Space Race, Strickland persuades General Frank Hoyt to vivisect the Amphibian Man to examine his respiratory system. Scientist Robert Hoffstetler, a Soviet spy, pleads with Strickland to keep him alive for further study, while being ordered by his handlers to kill the creature.
Giles reluctantly agrees to help Elisa free Amphibian Man after failing a work assignment and being rejected by a local restaurant manager whom he discovered was both racist and homophobic. Hoffstetler and Zelda also become involved in the plot and successfully get the Amphibian Man to Elisa's apartment. Elisa keeps him in her bathtub, planning to release him into a nearby canal when heavy rain allows access to the ocean. When Giles tries to stop the Amphibian Man from devouring one of his cats, his arm is slashed and the Amphibian Man flees. Elisa coaxes him back to her apartment and the creature touches Giles on his balding head and wounded arm. The next morning, Giles discovers his hair is regrowing and the wounds on his arm have healed. Elisa's infatuation with the Amphibian Man culminates in sexual intercourse.
General Hoyt gives Strickland an ultimatum to recover the Amphibian Man or his career will be over. Hoffstetler is told by his handlers he'll be extracted from the US in two days. The Amphibian Man's health begins to deteriorate.
Strickland follows Hoffstetler to a meeting with his handlers where Hoffstetler is shot. Strickland intervenes, shooting the handlers, then tortures the dying spy into revealing the Amphibian Man's whereabouts. Strickland confronts Zelda in her home and her husband reveals Elisa has the Amphibian Man. Zelda warns Elisa to release the creature before Strickland can arrive. He ransacks Elisa's apartment and finds evidence of the creature in the bathtub and a calendar note revealing where she plans to release him.

Elisa and Giles are bidding farewell to the creature at the canal when Strickland arrives, knocks Giles down, and shoots both the Amphibian Man and Elisa. Giles and Strickland fight while the Amphibian Man heals himself, then fatally slashes Strickland's throat. As the police arrive with Zelda, the Amphibian Man jumps into the canal with the unconscious Elisa and kisses her.
