title: Can You Ever Forgive Me?
tagline: Her greatest work will be her biggest crime.
overview: When a bestselling celebrity biographer is no longer able to get published because she has fallen out of step with current tastes, she turns her art form to deception.
plot:
In 1991, following the critical and commercial failure of her biography of Estée Lauder, author Lee Israel struggles with financial troubles, writer's block, and alcoholism. Her only friend is her cat, which has a health issue. Lee hopes to write a biography of comedian Fanny Brice, who died in 1951, but her literary agent, Marjorie, sharply rejects the idea, noting that Brice’s life no longer interests people. Marjorie bluntly adds that Lee is not remotely successful enough to act like she does, which is to say miserable and angry all the time.
With Marjorie unable to secure her an advance for a new book regardless of subject matter, Lee resorts to selling her possessions to cover her living expenses. She sells a personal letter she received long ago from Katharine Hepburn to Anna, a used bookstore merchant and autograph dealer. Lee begins spending time with old acquaintance Jack Hock after a chance encounter with him at a gay bar called Julius’, where he reveals he has been banned from all Duane Reade locations for shoplifting.
Lee visits a Manhattan library's special collections department to research Fanny Brice and discovers two letters typewritten by Brice. She removes one of them from the building, takes it to Anna's store, and shows it to her. Anna makes Lee an offer that is lower than what she was expecting, due to the letter's bland content. Lee returns home and uses a typewriter to add a postscript to the letter, then returns to the store where Anna, now amused by what "Fanny Brice" wrote "several decades ago", offers Lee $350. She also asks Lee for advice on whether her short stories are worth publishing, but Lee, who is socially phobic, replies cautiously. Lee uses some of the $350 to pay for her cat's treatment by a veterinarian.
Emboldened by her success with selling the Brice letter, Lee starts forging and selling letters supposedly written by deceased celebrities, incorporating intimate details to command high prices. Anna, a fan of Lee's biographies, tries to initiate a romantic relationship with Lee, while also hoping for Lee's input regarding her short stories, but Lee rebuffs her.
In some of Lee's forged letters, she has Noël Coward make references to his social life that reflects his homosexuality. Paul, a used-book dealer, buys one of them from Lee and sends it to a friend of his who knew Coward. The recipient doubts Coward would have risked his privacy and relays his suspicions to Paul, who warns others, leading to Lee's customers blacklisting her. Unable to sell more forgeries, she has Jack sell them on her behalf, since the customers do not know he has a connection to Lee. She also starts stealing authentic letters from libraries and archives for Jack to sell, replacing them with forged duplicates. While Lee is out of town committing one such theft, she lets Jack stay in her apartment. Jack spends the night with a young waiter from Julius’, when Lee's cat dies.

title: Thelma
tagline: Unleash Your True Self. Unleash Your True Power.
overview: A college student starts to experience extreme seizures. She soon learns that the violent episodes are a symptom of inexplicable abilities.
plot:
Thelma is a lonely and repressed young woman from an ultra-religious Christian family who has lived a sheltered life under the protection of her father, Trond, and disabled mother, Unni. She struggles to make friends and soon after moving to Oslo to attend university begins to experience unexplained psychogenic non-epileptic seizures. When she meets another student, Anja, she discovers that her feelings for Anja trigger uncontrollable psychokinetic powers. Thelma suffers much guilt over her feelings for Anja, and wishes she was not in love with her.
While undergoing a brain tomography test to find the cause of her seizures, she begins to think about Anja and as she focuses on her, Thelma's power is set in motion and she unconsciously and unwittingly makes Anja vanish into empty space. Distraught and confused by Anja's sudden disappearance, Thelma returns home and soon remembers that when she was a little girl, she had a baby brother. Once, when feeling neglected and jealous of the attention given to her younger sibling, and wishing him to be quiet and gone, she involuntarily caused him to teleport from his crib and reappear underneath the sofa. In a final tragic incident, she caused him to disappear from his bath, and he was found trapped below the ice of a frozen lake by her father. Traumatised, Thelma's mother tried to take her own life by jumping off a bridge, but instead the failed attempt left her paraplegic. Thelma had forgotten these events. Realising her utter distress, her parents tell her the truth, which is that she is somehow able to manifest whatever she deeply wants and that she inherited the same inexplicable ability from her grandmother (who blamed herself for the disappearance of Thelma's grandfather and was kept sedated in a psychiatric nursing home by Trond). Thelma perceives that her parents have a similar fate in mind for her as her grandmother. Though Trond expresses some misgivings about drugging Thelma, Unni tells him it is their responsibility to stop Thelma.
Earlier, while visiting Anja, Thelma had recalled how her father once held her hand over a lit candle until it almost burned so that she could feel what Hell's eternal fire was like. She causes the death of her father by telekinetically making him self-combust while out boating on the unfrozen lake. Thelma realises that her power can also restore life when she revives a small dead bird. She begins to understand that her supernatural ability is also a gift and uses it to heal her mother, making her able to walk again. Along with the realisation that she can summon her power, Thelma is able to finally control it, and brings Anja back to existence. She returns to college, now with Anja as her girlfriend.

title: Red Sparrow
tagline: Seduce. Deceive. Repeat.
overview: Prima ballerina, Dominika Egorova faces a bleak and uncertain future after she suffers an injury that ends her career. She soon turns to Sparrow School, a secret intelligence service that trains exceptional young people to use their minds and bodies as weapons. Dominika emerges as the most dangerous Sparrow after completing the sadistic training process. As she comes to terms with her new abilities, she meets a CIA agent who tries to convince her that he is the only person she can trust.
plot:
In modern-day Russia, famous ballerina Dominika Egorova supports her infirm mother. Her career abruptly ends after her dance partner injures her during a performance. After the Bolshoi cuts her off, Dominika's Uncle Ivan, the deputy director of the SVR, reveals that her ex-partner, Konstantin, and a rival dancer, Sonya, who were lovers, deliberately injured her. Dominika seeks retribution by ambushing them in the Bolshoi showers and beating them with her cane, injuring both. To avoid prosecution and receive financial support, she agrees to help Ivan. She is tasked with seducing Dimitri Ustinov, a Russian gangster, in exchange for her mother's continued medical care.
Meeting at a bar, the two go to her private hotel room, where Dimitri rapes her but is quickly interrupted and garroted by Sergei Matorin, an SVR operative authorized by Ivan. They flee to a safehouse and Ivan offers Dominika a choice: become an SVR operative, or be executed for witnessing Ustinov's assassination.
Nate Nash is a CIA operative working in Moscow. While meeting with a Russian mole code-named Marble in Gorky Park, they are confronted by the police. Nash creates a diversion to ensure his contact escapes unidentified while reaching the U.S. Embassy. Nash is reassigned to the U.S. but insists he is the only person Marble will work with. Since he cannot return to Russia, he is assigned to Budapest to reestablish contact with Marble, which the SVR also deduce.
Dominika is sent to State School 4, a brutal specialist training school for "Sparrows"—operatives capable of seducing their targets with sexpionage— where she's given the alias, Katya, and revealing her true identity and profession is forbidden. She excels in her training, despite some friction with her trainer, 'the Matron'. Against Matron's recommendation, Ivan and General Vladimir Korchnoi, a high-ranking official, decide that Dominika is ready for an assignment in Budapest—to gain Nash's trust and expose Marble's identity.
In Budapest, Dominika lives with fellow "sparrow" Marta, and is supervised by station chief Maxim Volontov. She makes contact with Nash, who quickly determines she is a Russian intelligence operative and attempts to convince her to defect.
Dominika inspects Marta's room and finds she has been assigned to buy classified intelligence from Stephanie Boucher, chief of staff to a U.S. Senator. When Ivan pressures her about her slow progress with Nash, Dominika claims to be helping Marta with Boucher as well.
Marta is brutally killed by Sergei Matorin after Dominika told her about the earlier incident with Ustinov. Dominika is then warned by Sergei that the same fate would befall her should she open her mouth about that again. She contacts Nash, agrees to become a double agent in exchange for protection for her and her mother, and has sex with him.

title: Ben 10 Generator Rex Heroes United
tagline: Two Heroes. One Epic Battle.
overview: Ben Tennyson falls through a wormhole and encounters Rex. The two heroes must unite against a foe that can absorb their powers.
plot:
Ben 10/Generator Rex: Heroes United is an animated crossover special uniting Ben 10: Ultimate Alien and Generator Rex, written by Man of Action, the creative team behind both series. Structured as a double-length episode of Generator Rex, covering the third and fourth episodes of its third season, it brings Ben Tennyson into Rex's universe and redraws him and his alien forms in that show's art style. It premiered at New York Comic Con 2011 before airing in a one-hour slot on Cartoon Network on November 25, 2011, the network's second crossover special after 2007's The Grim Adventures of the KND.

A mysterious rift opens over Manhattan, and Rex Salazar, a former agent of the peacekeeping organization Providence, arrives with Agent Six and Bobo. Something comes through: Ben, transformed into Humungousaur. Mistaking him for an EVO, a human mutated by rogue nanites, Rex fights him across the city as Ben shifts into Diamondhead, Lodestar and Rath, while a strange metallic creature that also emerged from the rift slips away. Back in human form, Ben is stunned that nobody knows him. The creature self-destructs in front of Six, leaving him in a coma, and Rex blames Ben. Doctor Holiday finds the creature was nanite-based but unlike any EVO. Ben escapes confinement as Big Chill, and he and Rex meet Caesar, who admits he created the creature, Alpha, to manufacture adaptable nanites, then banished it to another dimension after it became sentient and began seizing human bodies. Ben realizes Caesar sent it into the Null Void, the alien prison where it took a cyborg body before returning.

Alpha now aims to absorb EVOs and capture Rex's Omega Nanite, the key to its perfection. At the Bug Jar, a quarantined city of EVOs, Ben fights as XLR8, Four Arms and the new Shocksquatch, but Alpha copies the Ultimatrix and takes Rex's Omega Nanite, becoming the giant Alpha-Omega. Ben merges with Rex as Upgrade and together they compress Alpha into a dense sphere. Caesar recovers the Omega Nanite and opens a rift home for Ben, who, as Upchuck, swallows the compacted Alpha before leaving. Six recovers, Caesar restores Rex's nanite, and Alpha stirs in the Null Void, hinting at a return.

Daryl Sabara voices Rex, with Yuri Lowenthal as Ben, Wally Kurth as Six, Grey DeLisle as Holiday, John DiMaggio as Bobo, J. K. Simmons as White Knight, Michael Emerson as Alpha and Freddy Rodriguez as Caesar. Fans of both series embraced the special, which reached the iTunes top 100.

title: Denial
tagline: The whole world knows the Holocaust happened. Now she needs to prove it.
overview: Acclaimed writer and historian Deborah E. Lipstadt must battle for historical truth to prove the Holocaust actually occurred when David Irving, a renowned denier, sues her for libel.
plot:
Denial is a 2016 biographical drama film directed by Mick Jackson and written by David Hare, adapted from Deborah Lipstadt's 2005 book History on Trial: My Day in Court with a Holocaust Denier. It dramatizes Irving v Penguin Books Ltd, the libel case brought against Lipstadt by the Holocaust denier David Irving. Rachel Weisz stars as Lipstadt, with Timothy Spall as Irving, Tom Wilkinson as the barrister Richard Rampton, Andrew Scott as the solicitor Anthony Julius, Alex Jennings as Justice Charles Gray and Mark Gatiss as the historian Robert Jan van Pelt, with Jack Lowden and Caren Pistorius.

Lipstadt, an American professor of Holocaust studies, has a lecture disrupted by Irving, a British writer on Nazi Germany, who sues her and her publisher for libel in England over her description of him as a Holocaust denier. Because English libel law puts the burden of proof on the defendant, Lipstadt's team, headed by Julius and Rampton, must show that Irving deliberately lied about the Holocaust. Preparing the defense, Lipstadt and Rampton visit the site of Auschwitz, where van Pelt explains how the gas chambers operated. Lipstadt bristles at Rampton's seemingly irreverent manner, and her lawyers sideline her, believing her involvement would hurt the case, while British Jewish leaders urge her to settle. The team scores an early success by flattering Irving into accepting a trial before a judge rather than a jury he might sway. Representing himself, Irving tries to twist the evidence, and his claim that the gas chamber roofs had no holes for introducing Zyklon B ("no holes, no Holocaust") dominates the press. Lipstadt wants survivors to testify, but Julius fears Irving would humiliate them. Rampton wins her trust, then dismantles Irving in cross-examination, while historians such as Richard J. Evans expose the distortions in his work. At the close, Gray unsettles the defense by asking whether Irving can be lying if he sincerely believes his claims, but Rampton argues that Irving's antisemitism proves his falsifications were deliberate. Gray finds for the defense, and her lawyers remind her that her writing was the basis of the victory. Irving later claims on television that the trial largely went his way.

Shot in London and at the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum, Denial premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 11 September 2016. It received positive reviews, with an 82% Rotten Tomatoes rating that particularly praised Weisz's performance.

title: Hard Target 2
tagline: It's hunting season again...
overview: Forced into a deadly cat-and-mouse game, a disgraced mixed martial arts fighter is hunted through the jungles of Southeast Asia.
plot:
Hard Target 2 is a 2016 American action film directed by Roel Reiné, starring Scott Adkins with Robert Knepper, Temuera Morrison, Rhona Mitra and Ann Truong. Billed as a follow-up to the 1993 film Hard Target, in which Jean-Claude Van Damme played a drifter battling a human hunting operation in New Orleans, it has no narrative connection to the original and reworks its premise of people hunted for sport in a new setting.

Professional mixed martial arts fighter Wes Baylor faces Jonny Sutherland for a welterweight championship in Las Vegas. Angry at the judges' scoring, Baylor tries for a knockout and accidentally kills Sutherland in the ring. Consumed by guilt, he goes into self-imposed exile in Thailand. Six months later, he is still haunted by the tragedy and scraping by in underground fights when he attracts the attention of Jonah Aldrich, a wealthy man who offers him $1 million for a private bout in Myanmar.

On arrival, Baylor learns that there is no fight: he is to be the prey in a lethal hunt organized by Aldrich for a group of rich clients. He is given a water bottle and a money belt that secretly contains a GPS tracker. The hunters include Sofia, a bullfighter named Esparto, a video game designer, a sharpshooter, a Texan and his son Tobias, and Aldrich's right-hand man Madden, supported by a unit of corrupt soldiers. Baylor kills his first pursuer at a waterfall and then meets Tha, a local woman who agrees to guide him to the border. As Aldrich escalates the hunt with armed motorcycles and rocket launchers, Baylor and Tha fight back, picking off hunters one by one. They make their way through a minefield, where an explosion buys them time to hide in a cave in which Tha finds her missing brother, an earlier target of Aldrich's game who had managed to survive in hiding. Baylor then turns the tables on the remaining hunters for a final confrontation with Aldrich, finding a measure of redemption along the way.

The film was released direct to video in 2016. Reviewers frequently noted that it could not match the original, which had been made with a much larger budget by the acclaimed director John Woo, but many judged it a respectable addition to Adkins's catalogue. Critics at HighDef Digest and MMA Torch were particularly enthusiastic, praising the fight scenes, Reiné's slick visuals and the cast of villains surrounding Adkins's sympathetic hero.

title: Edge of Winter
tagline: Nothing is more dangerous than a father's love.
overview: When two brothers are stranded by a brutal winter storm with an unpredictable father they barely know, the boys begin to suspect their supposed protector may be their biggest threat.
plot:
Edge of Winter is a 2016 Canadian psychological thriller drama film directed and written by Rob Connolly and Kyle Mann. Joel Kinnaman stars as Elliot Baker, a recently divorced father whose anger gradually takes control of him while he is stranded with his two sons in the wilderness, with Tom Holland as his teenage son Bradley and Percy Hynes White as his younger son Caleb. Rossif Sutherland and Shiloh Fernandez play Luc and Richard, two hunters, and Rachelle Lefevre plays Karen. The film was produced by Kyle Mann and Jonathan Bronfman and shot in and around Sudbury, Ontario.

Elliot, who has just been fired for punching his boss, eagerly seizes a chance to spend time with his sons, Bradley and Caleb, when their mother drops them off for a visit. When the boys find his shotgun, he decides to turn the discovery into a bonding lesson in firearm safety and takes them to his old lumber yard in the snowy wilderness, but the trip is strained from the start; Elliot finds messages on Bradley's phone complaining about spending time with him and hides the phone. On the way home, with Bradley at the wheel because Elliot has been drinking, an argument between the brothers sends the car off the road, where it becomes stuck. During the night in the car, Caleb lets slip that their stepfather has been promoted and the family will soon be moving to London, and Elliot reacts with fury. Facing the risk of freezing or starving if they try to walk to the main road, they make for a hunting cabin, where Elliot rescues Bradley after he falls through the ice. Their uneasy refuge is disturbed when two hunters, Richard and Luc, arrive seeking shelter. Increasingly paranoid and desperate not to lose his sons, Elliot treats the strangers as a threat, and his behavior turns violent, leaving the boys to realize that the greatest danger they face may be their own father as they try to find a way to escape and bring help.

Edge of Winter received mixed reviews, with scores of 50% on both Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter praised Kinnaman's superb performance and the boys' quietly terrified reactions, while finding that the film ultimately succumbed to tired thriller conventions.

title: The Death of Stalin
tagline: In the Kremlin, no one can hear you scheme
overview: When dictator Joseph Stalin dies, his parasitic cronies square off in a frantic power struggle to become the next Soviet leader. As they bumble, brawl and back-stab their way to the top, the question remains — just who is running the government?
plot:
For 20 years, Stalin's NKVD security forces have imposed The Great Terror. Those on Stalin's list of 'enemy' names are arrested, exiled or shot.
On the night of 1 March 1953, Josef Stalin demands the director of Radio Moscow provide a recording of a live recital of Mozart's Piano Concerto No. 23 after the show has concluded. The director recalls the audience and orchestra and records the recreated concert. Pianist Maria Yudina, who hates the cruel dictator, only complies after being bribed and slips a note into the recording before it is couriered to Stalin.
Stalin is hosting a tense, but rowdy, gathering of Central Committee members at Kuntsevo Dacha. As Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov leaves, NKVD head Lavrentiy Beria reveals to Nikita Khrushchev and Deputy Chairman Georgy Malenkov that Molotov is to be part of the latest purge. The concert recording arrives and Maria's note, admonishing Stalin and wishing him dead, causes him to suffer a cerebral haemorrhage as he laughs at the note. Stalin's guards hear him fall in his office but fear disturbing him.
Stalin's housemaid discovers him unconscious the next morning and members of the Central Committee rush to the dacha. Beria finds Maria's note but only after Malenkov, Khrushchev, Lazar Kaganovich, Anastas Mikoyan, and Nikolai Bulganin arrive, does the Committee finally decide to send for medical help. The best doctors in Moscow have been arrested after the "Doctors' plot". When Stalin dies under the care of mediocre doctors, Beria orders the NKVD to relieve the Soviet Army of control of Moscow.
Beria and Khrushchev vie for the support of Molotov and of Stalin's children, Svetlana and her unstable, alcoholic brother Vasily. Beria removes Molotov's name from the impending purge and releases Polina Zhemchuzhina, Molotov's wife, from prison. The Committee names Malenkov, a puppet of Beria, as chairman. He hijacks Khrushchev's proposed reforms, such as releasing political prisoners and loosening clerical restrictions, relegating Khrushchev to planning Stalin's funeral.
Beria threatens Khrushchev with Maria's note, and Khrushchev reverses Beria's order to halt all transport into Moscow. When 1,500 arriving mourners are killed, the Committee wants to blame junior NKVD officers. In an effort to deflect blame, Beria threatens his colleagues with documents detailing their involvement in various purges.
Angered by the NKVD's takeover of security from the Army, Marshal Georgy Zhukov supports Khrushchev in launching a coup against Beria after Stalin's funeral. Khrushchev gets support from the rest of the Committee save Malenkov, and on Zhukov's orders the Army reclaims its posts from the NKVD. Zhukov, Kiril Moskalenko and Leonid Brezhnev storm a meeting of the Committee and arrest Beria.
Malenkov reluctantly signs Beria's death warrant. At Beria's emergency trial, Khrushchev finds him guilty of counter-revolutionary activities, sexual assault, and paedophilia.

title: Ocean's Eight
tagline: The plan is priceless.
overview: Debbie Ocean, a criminal mastermind, gathers a crew of female thieves to pull off the heist of the century at New York's annual Met Gala.
plot:
Ocean's Eight is a heist comedy-drama film released in 2018, directed by Gary Ross and written by Olivia Milch. The movie serves as a spin-off to the Ocean's franchise, with Sandra Bullock taking on the lead role of Debbie Ocean, the sister of Danny Ocean (played by George Clooney in the previous films).

The story begins with Debbie Ocean, who has just been released from prison after serving time for a crime she didn't commit. She sets out to plan and execute a massive heist at the Met Gala, one of the most prestigious events in New York City's social calendar.

Debbie assembles a team of eight women, each with their unique skills and expertise: Cate Blanchett as Lou, the tough-as-nails ex-con; Anne Hathaway as Daphne, a talented thief; Mindy Kaling as Amita, an expert hacker; Sarah Paulson as Tammy, a skilled pickpocket; Awkwafina as Constance, a street-smart thief; Rihanna as Nine Ball, a charismatic and deadly thief; Helena Bonham Carter as Rose, a quirky and artistic forger; and Richard Armitage as Claude Becker, the wealthy businessman who has hired Debbie to pull off the heist.

title: 1898: Our Last Men in the Philippines
tagline: There are men who want medals and men who want to come back.
overview: The Philippines, 1898. Fifty Spanish soldiers arrive in the small village of Baler to rebuild an outpost. Although the war against the Filipinos and their American allies is almost lost, as is the Spanish Empire, the garrison will endure a cruel siege for eleven months. They will be the last to surrender.
plot:
1898, Our Last Men in the Philippines (Spanish: 1898, Los últimos de Filipinas) is a 2016 Spanish war drama directed by Salvador Calvo. It dramatises the Siege of Baler of 1898 to 1899, in which a Spanish detachment held out for almost a year inside the church of San Luis Obispo de Tolosa against Filipino revolutionaries, unaware that the war had ended. The cast includes Luis Tosar, Javier Gutiérrez, Álvaro Cervantes, Karra Elejalde and Carlos Hipólito. It was released on December 2, 2016.

During the Philippine Revolution, rebels attack the Spanish garrison in the coastal town of Baler and kill most of its soldiers. A detachment of young recruits under Captain Enrique de las Morenas and Lieutenant Martín Cerezo is sent from Manila to reoccupy the town. They are welcomed by the parish priest, Brother Carmelo. Among the recruits is Carlos, a sensitive young man who dreams of studying art, and who begins to share the priest's opium.

News arrives that the United States has declared war on Spain and destroyed its fleet, cutting the garrison off from supplies. When the revolutionaries attack, the soldiers barricade themselves in the church. Months pass under siege as beriberi, caused by poor rations, kills many of them, including de las Morenas and Brother Carmelo, leaving the rigid Cerezo in command. One recruit deserts to the enemy and urges his comrades to give up a lost cause, and offers of peace, including newspapers reporting Spain's defeat, are dismissed by Cerezo as tricks.

The men grow desperate, and violence and paranoia spread. Carlos, suffering from withdrawal after his opium is discovered, is locked up. Even when a Spanish officer arrives with orders to surrender, Cerezo refuses to believe that Spain has lost its colonies. Carlos goes out to verify the news and learns from the Filipino commander that Spain has ceded the islands to the Americans, but Cerezo still holds out, and deserters are brutally punished.

Only when Cerezo reads a minor item in a newspaper about the posting of a friend, a detail no enemy could have invented, does he accept the truth. The garrison surrenders in June 1899, and the Filipino forces, impressed by their resistance, allow the survivors to leave with honour rather than as prisoners. Carlos, disillusioned, discards his drawings as the men depart.

The film was shortlisted as Spain's possible Academy Award submission. The Hollywood Reporter called it spectacular and striking, if not subtle.

title: Headshot
tagline: They should have killed him.
overview: A young man washes ashore, his memory gone - but his past comes back to haunt him after he is nursed back to health and his killing ability is needed when he takes on a powerful drug lord.
plot:
A comatose man of unknown identity and origin is being cared by Dr. Ailin in a rural hospital on a small island. The man eventually wakes up after two months with no clear memory of how he was injured or even his identity. He adopts the name Ishmael from Moby-Dick, which Ailin is reading. The man learns that he was found on the beach by a man named Romli.
Meanwhile, a mobster named Lee and his henchmen Rika and Besi violently eliminate a rival gang. One of the gang's survivors tells Lee about Ishmael and Lee sends the man to investigate. Ishmael and the thug have a brief altercation after the man threatens Ailin. Ailin travels to the mainland to seek better care for Ishmael, but her bus is stopped by Lee's men, who are looking for Ishmael (whom they call Abdi). They slaughter all the passengers except Ailin and a young girl, whom they abduct. Called by Ailin, Ishmael and Romli hurry to the scene of the bus attack. Ishmael kills a few of Lee's thugs, but Romli is also killed. An Interpol agent tells Ishmael about children abducted by Lee's syndicate and bred to be devoted smugglers and criminal enforcers; Ishmael was one of those children.
The agent is killed when a group of Lee's assassins attack the police station in an attempt to take out Ishmael/Abdi. Ishmael puts down the attackers instead and escapes. Ishmael must then go to war with the syndicate to save Ailin. While traveling, Ishmael encounters Besi near a well, and it is revealed that he, Besi and Rika trained together. Lee would put children in the well and starve them for a few days and the child, who killed all the others to get the food would be freed. Ishmael tries to persuade Besi to not be on Lee's side, but Besi refuses out of loyalty. They then begin to fight and Ishmael manages to gain the upper hand, killing Besi with a strong hit to the head. After Besi dies, Rika discovers his corpse and attacks Ishmael on the beach.
Ishmael eventually defeats Rika despite receiving multiple wounds from the latter, and it is revealed that Rika was the one who shot Ishmael and gave him amnesia in the first place. Rika takes advantage of the distraction and holds Ishmael at gunpoint, but she can't bring herself to shoot Ishmael again, where she instead shoots away from him, wasting her bullets. In the confusion, Ishmael accidentally mortally injures Rika by reflexively throwing a knife. After comforting Rika in her dying moments, Ishmael finds Lee's hideout, where he and Ailin meet each other during the chaos, with Ailin initially hostile to Ishmael due to their relationship resulting in her kidnapping. Ishmael manages to convince her and they mutually embrace.
However, Lee arrives and gets enraged that Ishmael killed both Besi and Rika, whom he had considered as his "favorite children". They then enter a brutal fight, with Lee gaining the upper hand due to his strength. However, Ishmael finally beats Lee outside, and impales him on the sharp branch of a tree trunk.

plot:
Ralph Breaks the Internet is a 2018 American animated comedy-adventure film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. The movie serves as a sequel to Wreck-It Ralph, released in 2012.

The story begins with Ralph (voiced by John C. Reilly), the lovable but destructive villain from the classic arcade game Fix-It Felix, who has become an unlikely hero after saving the arcade from an evil virus known as "Sugar Rush." To celebrate his victory, Ralph and his new friend Vanellope von Schweetz (voiced by Sarah Silverman) are invited to a high-tech gaming convention called Slaughter Race.

However, things take a turn when Ralph becomes fascinated with the world of online gaming and decides to explore the internet. He and Vanellope embark on a journey through various websites, including YouTube, eBay, and Amazon. Along the way, they encounter new characters, such as Shank (voiced by Gal Gadot), a tough-as-nails driver from the racing game Crash Bandicoot.

As Ralph delves deeper into the internet, he becomes increasingly obsessed with his online persona and the validation it provides. He starts to neglect his friendship with Vanellope and his responsibilities in the arcade. Meanwhile, Shank's true intentions are revealed, and she is determined to take down Ralph and claim the championship title for Crash Bandicoot.

As Ralph struggles to balance his online life with his real-life relationships, he must also confront the darker side of the internet. He discovers that the world of online gaming can be cruel and unforgiving, where players are often pitted against each other in a never-ending cycle of competition.

In the end, Ralph realizes that true friendship and connection cannot be found online but rather through shared experiences and genuine relationships. With Vanellope's help, he finds a way to reconcile his online persona with his real-life identity and saves the arcade from Shank's evil plans.

The movie features stunning animation, witty humor, and a talented voice cast. The film's exploration of the internet's impact on society is both thought-provoking and entertaining, making it a must-see for audiences of all ages. Overall, Ralph Breaks the Internet is a heartwarming and hilarious adventure that celebrates the power of friendship and the importance of staying true to oneself.

title: A Street Cat Named Bob
tagline: Sometimes it takes nine lives to save one
overview: James Bowen, a homeless busker and recovering drug addict, has his life transformed when he meets a stray ginger cat.
plot:
A Street Cat Named Bob is a 2016 British biographical drama directed by Roger Spottiswoode and written by Tim John and Maria Nation, based on James Bowen's memoirs A Street Cat Named Bob and The World According to Bob. Luke Treadaway stars as Bowen, with Ruta Gedmintas, Joanne Froggatt and Anthony Head, while Bob the cat plays himself in most scenes. The title is a play on A Streetcar Named Desire. The film premiered in London on 3 November 2016 and went on general release the following day.

James Bowen is a homeless former heroin addict busking on the streets of London and struggling to survive. After a near-fatal overdose, his support worker Val finds him a council flat and puts him on a methadone programme in the hope of getting him off the streets for good. On his first night in the flat, James discovers a ginger cat raiding his food. He assumes the cat belongs to someone nearby and tries to send him home, but the cat returns, this time with an infected wound on his leg. James's neighbour Betty, an animal lover, tells him about a charity veterinary clinic where she volunteers, and gives the cat the name Bob.

James spends what little money he has on Bob's treatment and then lets him go, but Bob refuses to leave and follows him onto the bus and into central London. The sight of a busker with a cat perched on his shoulders draws crowds, and James begins to earn more money than ever before, eventually becoming a well-known figure in the area and selling The Big Issue magazine. His friendship with Betty grows, and caring for Bob gives him the motivation to stay clean. But his path to recovery is not easy: he faces hostility from other vendors, trouble with authorities, the temptation of his old life and a painful attempt to reconcile with his estranged father, and he must undergo the ordeal of withdrawal from methadone to finally free himself from addiction.

The film was a success in the United Kingdom and won Best British Film at the National Film Awards UK in 2017. Critics praised Treadaway's performance and Bob's natural screen presence, though some found it sentimental. A Christmas sequel, A Gift from Bob, was released in 2020, after the real Bob had died earlier that year.

title: From a House on Willow Street
original_title: From a House on Willow Street
tagline: Evil has an address...
overview: After a young woman is kidnapped, her captors soon come to realize that in fact they may be the ones in danger and this young woman has a dark secret inside her.
plot:
Hazel, her boyfriend Ade, Ade's cousin James, and Mark plot to kidnap diamond heiress Katherine within the next six weeks. The expedited time frame worries Mark, who believes it may cause them to make mistakes. Hazel and Ade are adamant about the time frame, as Ade will soon go on trial for the accidental death of his brother George. They stress the importance of both the timing and the need for a flawless execution. Left with no other option, Mark agrees. Six weeks later, the four break into Katherine's house, encountering no resistance and finding the alarm already deactivated. After grabbing Katherine, they return to their headquarters in an abandoned warehouse and chain up Katherine. They are surprised by her dirty and sickly appearance but continue with their plan regardless.
Katherine warns them to let her go free and initially refuses to play along in making a ransom video. Hazel convinces her by promising the ordeal will end faster if she cooperates. However, the kidnappers can not contact her parents to make their demands. Hazel sends Ade and James back to Katherine's house to investigate. Less distracted, they realise the house is full of decaying food and smells horrible. James finds two dead, mutilated priests in the cellar, and Ade realises that Katherine's parents have been gruesomely murdered. Both are haunted by apparitions from their past. Worried they will be blamed for the murders, they flee the house after grabbing videotapes from the cellar. On the way back, Ade swerves to miss an apparition of George, and James is assaulted by his dead mother.
Back at the warehouse, Hazel and Mark are also haunted. Hazel sees her own dead mother, and Mark sees his dead daughter Sarah. James' condition steadily deteriorates, and the others leave him in a room to rest while they watch the videotapes. The first videotape is by Katherine and details the history of her house and its many unexplained deaths, including that of Hazel's mother. The others are annoyed that Hazel kept this detail quiet, but they continue watching. On the next videotape, a priest says a demon that feeds on grief is responsible for the deaths and has subsequently possessed Katherine. The demon has chosen this house because it is the furthest point in the world from a holy relic kept in the Vatican. Panicked by the demon's growing power, the priests attempt to immolate Katherine, but she kills everyone in the house.
Disturbed by the videotapes, Hazel, Ade, and Mark confront Katherine, who, as the demon, reveals that she only needs to possess two more people to be set free from hell. James, infected by his mother's apparition, attempts to infect the others. Katherine appeals to Mark, telling him that if he betrays Hazel and Ade, she will spare his soul and allow him to be with Sarah again. Mark frees Katherine from her chains and delivers the others to her. After hearing their anguished cries, he sacrifices himself to give them time to escape and becomes infected.

title: My Little Pony: Equestria Girls - Legend of Everfree

overview: When Canterlot Highschool goes on a trip to Camp Everfree, they’re surprised to find a magical force is causing strange things to happen around camp. plot:
The students of Canterlot High School attend a field trip to Camp Everfree, a nature camp owned by Gloriosa Daisy and her brother, Timber Spruce. During the bus ride, transfer student Twilight Sparkle has a nightmare of being overtaken by "Midnight Sparkle", a malevolent alter ego of herself produced while temporarily corrupted by Equestrian magic. Her friend Sunset Shimmer is supportive, relating to her own similar experience of transforming into a demon. Shortly upon arrival at the camp, Twilight develops telekinetic powers, which she worries is a sign of Midnight's lingering presence.
That night, Timber tells a campfire story about a forest spirit named Gaea Everfree being angered by the camp's construction and threatens to unleash a plague of natural disasters upon it. The next day, a sailboat crashes into a dock the campers are building to use as a fashion show runway. The terrified campers spot glittering gem dust that matches the description of Gaea's presence in Timber's story, convincing them that Gaea is real. Twilight, however, believes her magic to be responsible for the accident and distances herself from her friends.
Later, Twilight's friends begin developing superpowers which they can only use within the camp's boundaries (Rainbow Dash gains super speed, Fluttershy gets the ability to communicate with animals, Pinkie Pie can create explosions using sprinkles, Rarity can make diamonds out of thin air, and Applejack receives super strength). Now believing her magic is infecting her friends, Twilight prepares to run away from the camp. Sunset follows Twilight into the woods and, discovering her power of telepathic empathy, convinces her to stay. As Timber leads them back to the camp, Sunset notices gem dust falling from his pocket and suspects him of staging Gaea's attacks. She later overhears him arguing with Gloriosa about abandoning what Sunset assumes to be the camp. Remembering his earlier statements of longing for urban life, Sunset concludes that Timber means to shut the camp down by terrorizing the campers.
Sunset brings Twilight and Spike with her to investigate a nearby cave kept off-limits by Timber, where they find geodes infused with Equestrian magic. The three are confronted by Gloriosa, who reveals herself to be the true cause of the natural disasters. Sunset learns through her visions that Gloriosa, desperate to prevent the camp's closure, has been wearing the geodes as a necklace to harness their power, with the "disasters" resulting from her reckless attempts at using magic to improve the campers' experience; Timber, anticipating this, invented the story of Gaea Everfree to cover for her.
Gloriosa adds more geodes to the necklace and is completely corrupted by their power, taking on an appearance resembling Gaea. Crashing the campers' fashion show rehearsal, Gloriosa enacts her intent to "protect" them by trapping the camp in a bramble cage.

title: Don't Kill It
overview: Demon hunter, Jebediah Huntley teams up with an FBI agent to battle a supernatural force in the southern state of Mississippi.
plot:
Don't Kill It is a 2016 American comedy horror film directed and edited by Mike Mendez from a screenplay by Dan Berk and Robert Olsen. Dolph Lundgren stars as Jebediah Woodley, an eccentric demon hunter who travels to a small Mississippi town to destroy an ancient, murderous demon. Kristina Klebe, Tony Bentley, James Chalke, Billy Slaughter and Miles Doleac appear in supporting roles. The script was originally set in Alaska, but filming was moved to Mississippi for financial reasons, and the film was made for less than $1 million, part of it raised through crowdfunding on Indiegogo.

While hunting deer in southern Mississippi, a man named Gabriel follows his dog to a small golden box, which the dog opens. The animal begins to act strangely and attacks Gabriel, who is forced to shoot it. Gabriel returns home with the same black eyes and erratic behavior, murders his family and then begins killing his neighbors until he is shot dead by a neighbor named Marcus, who immediately develops black eyes himself and carries on the slaughter. The demon, it turns out, passes into whoever kills its current host.

Days later, Jebediah Woodley, a weathered demon hunter who has spent decades tracking this particular entity, hears about the killings on the radio and comes to town. At the same time, FBI agent Evelyn Pierce, who grew up in the area, has been sent to investigate the massacres as a possible case of domestic terrorism. Pierce and the local police chief dismiss Woodley's talk of demons and have him detained, but when the killings continue, Pierce is forced to accept that he is right. Woodley explains that the demon cannot simply be killed, since its killer becomes the next host, and that it must be trapped instead. As panic spreads and the townspeople start to turn on one another, Woodley and Pierce try to stop the demon without letting anyone kill it, a task that becomes increasingly difficult as it jumps from body to body.

The film played on the genre festival circuit before its release and was generally well received by horror critics, who enjoyed its sense of humor, its gory effects and Lundgren's relaxed, self-mocking turn as the gruff hunter.

title: An Ordinary Man
overview: A war criminal in hiding forms a relationship with his only connection to the outside world - his maid.
plot:
A war criminal is hiding in plain sight in an unnamed Balkan country. He is wanted internationally for ethnic cleansing and war crimes, but his country pretends his whereabouts to be unknown despite international pressures to turn him in. A retinue of loyalists watches over him and ensures his safety as he goes about his life in a city where his face is well known. He begins to form a relationship with his newly hired maid, Tanja, after he expresses loneliness to her. Initially treating her abusively, he gradually forms an awkward friendship with her. She is later revealed to be an agent who is hired to protect him. She reluctantly drives him to the cemetery in his home village. His driver, who had been waiting for them, kills her on the spot, and drives the General back to his apartment in the city. The last scene shows him awaiting his arrest, seated at his kitchen table, with a handgun and bullets laid out in front of him.
The character of the General is based on Ratko Mladić, who was ultimately sentenced to life in prison for war crimes committed in the Bosnian war.

title: Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House
original_title: Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House
overview: Just one enchanted jewel stands between earth and an army of evil spirits led by the devious ghoul, Phears. With the help of his new girlfriend and ghost pals, Max Doyle races to find the crystal and save the world.
plot:
Mostly Ghostly 3: One Night in Doom House, released as R.L. Stine's Mostly Ghostly: One Night in Doom House, is a 2016 American family fantasy horror comedy written and directed by Ron Oliver. It is the third feature film based on R. L. Stine's Mostly Ghostly book series, following Mostly Ghostly: Who Let the Ghosts Out? (2008) and Mostly Ghostly: Have You Met My Ghoulfriend? (2014), and was made by Universal 1440 Entertainment. To keep the characters at the same ages, the main roles were recast: Corey Fogelmanis plays Max Doyle, with Sophie Reynolds as Cammie, Blake Michael and Olivia Ryan Stern as the ghosts Nicky and Tara, Adam Tsekhman as Phears, Danny Trejo as Mr. Morgo and Jamie Kennedy as a television ghost hunter. Morgan Fairchild also appears.

Max is a teenage stage magician who shares his home with Nicky and Tara, two young ghosts who are counting on him to help them find their missing parents. To raise money for his girlfriend Cammie's school dance crew, he stages a public séance. The ghosts supply genuine spectral effects, but everyone assumes they are Max's tricks, and when the ghost of a French maid interrupts the show with information about Nicky and Tara's parents, the evening ends in embarrassment and Cammie breaks up with him. At the same time, his ghost friends complain that he treats them more like pets than friends.

Max turns for help to Simon Drake, the self-obsessed host of a ghost-hunting television show who is filming an episode in town, only to discover that he is a fraud. The evil ghost Phears, working with the sinister Mr. Morgo, takes possession of Drake as part of a new attempt to release an army of evil spirits on the world and plunge it into darkness. The key is a dark crystal that turns up in Max's house, which Max has tried to use to win Cammie back. Hampered by fame, family squabbles, a rich rival for Cammie's affections and an anxious dance choreographer, Max has to recover the jewel and rescue Nicky and Tara before Phears succeeds, in a showdown at a derelict mansion, the Doom House of the title.

The film was released directly on DVD, digital download and on demand on 6 September 2016. Common Sense Media described it as a low-budget, harmless fright-fest with nonstop action and over-the-top villains, enlivened by Kennedy's send-up of a reality television star, but lacking in depth.

title: Insidious: The Last Key
tagline: Fear comes home.
overview: Parapsychologist Elise Rainier and her team travel to Five Keys, NM, to investigate a man’s claim of a haunting. Terror soon strikes when Rainier realizes that the house he lives in was her family’s old home.
plot:
Insidious: The Last Key is a supernatural horror film directed by Adam Wingard and written by Leigh Whannell. The movie serves as the fourth installment in the Insidious franchise.

The story begins with Elise Rainier (Lin Shaye), a paranormal investigator, who has been institutionalized for her supposed mental illness due to her experiences with the spirit world. However, it is revealed that she was actually being held captive by a group of people who were trying to exploit her abilities.

Elise escapes from her captors and returns home, where she reunites with her friends Specs (Leigh Whannell) and Tucker (Angus Sampson). They inform Elise that her sister, Sally (Haley Murphy), has been experiencing terrifying visions and nightmares, which they believe are connected to their family's dark past.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that their family's history is filled with tragedy and loss. Their father, Josh (Derek Johnson), died under mysterious circumstances when Elise was a child, and their mother, Lorraine (Rose Byrne), has been struggling to cope with her grief ever since.

Elise decides to investigate the source of Sally's visions, which leads her to an abandoned asylum in New Orleans. There, she discovers that the asylum was once home to a malevolent spirit known as "The Key," which is responsible for the family's dark past.

As Elise delves deeper into the mystery, she realizes that The Key is connected to her own traumatic experiences and that it has been manipulating her sister's visions in an attempt to lure her back to the asylum. Elise must use her skills and knowledge of the spirit world to defeat The Key and free Sally from its grasp.

Throughout the movie, Elise faces numerous challenges and obstacles as she navigates the treacherous world of spirits and demons. She is aided by Specs and Tucker, who provide comedic relief and technical support throughout the investigation.

The climax of the movie features an intense showdown between Elise and The Key, which culminates in a dramatic confrontation that will determine the fate of Sally and the entire Rainier family.

Ultimately, Elise emerges victorious, but not without scars. She realizes that her experiences have left her with emotional baggage and that she must find a way to heal and move forward. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, as Elise begins to rebuild her life and reconnect with her sister.

Insidious: The Last Key received mixed reviews from critics, who praised the film's visuals and atmosphere but criticized its predictable plot and lack of originality. Despite this, the movie has developed a loyal fan base and is widely regarded as one of the best entries in the Insidious franchise.

title: Moonfall
tagline: Humanity will face the dark side of the Moon.
overview: A mysterious force knocks the moon from its orbit around Earth and sends it hurtling on a collision course with life as we know it.
plot:
"Moonfall" is a 2022 science fiction disaster film directed by Roland Emmerich, produced by Centropolis Entertainment, and written by Drew Pearce.

The movie follows two main storylines that eventually intersect. The first storyline revolves around Sam Bell (played by Patrick Wilson), an astronaut who wakes up on the Moon with no memory of how he got there or what happened to his crew. As he tries to piece together his past, he discovers a mysterious message from an unknown sender that sets him on a mission to prevent a catastrophic event.

The second storyline takes place in 2055, where we meet J.T. O'Grady (played by Halle Berry), the daughter of Sam Bell, who is now a renowned astrophysicist. She's recruited by a team of scientists and engineers, including her colleague Brian Harper (played by John Bradley), to prevent a massive asteroid from colliding with Earth.

As the story unfolds, we learn that the asteroid is not just any ordinary rock - it's actually a piece of the Moon that has broken off due to an unknown cataclysmic event. The team discovers that the Moon was once part of a larger celestial body called Kaltain, which was destroyed in a catastrophic collision with Earth millions of years ago.

The movie takes a thrilling turn as Sam Bell and J.T. O'Grady embark on a perilous journey to prevent the asteroid from colliding with Earth. Along the way, they encounter numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning equipment, and personal demons.

Throughout the film, Emmerich's signature style of explosive action sequences and heart-pumping suspense is on full display. The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Sam and J.T., as they work together to prevent the asteroid from destroying Earth.

While "Moonfall" received mixed reviews from critics, it has its fans who appreciate the film's over-the-top action sequences and thrilling plot twists. However, some viewers may find the pacing a bit uneven and the scientific explanations lacking in depth.

Overall, "Moonfall" is an entertaining sci-fi disaster film that will keep you on the edge of your seat. With its breakneck pace and mind-bending plot twists, it's sure to appeal to fans of Roland Emmerich's signature style.

title: Hotel Artemis
tagline: No guns. No cops. No killing the other patients.
overview: Los Angeles, June 21st, 2028. While the streets are being torn apart by riots, the Nurse, who runs a clandestine hospital for criminals in the penthouse of the Artemis, a closed old hotel, has a rough night dealing with troublemaker clients: thieves, assassins, someone from the past and the one who owns the place and the whole city.
plot:
On June 21, 2028, a riot breaks out in Los Angeles over the city's water privatization. Taking advantage of the chaos, professional criminal Sherman attempts a bank robbery that leaves half his team dead with his brother Lev and another accomplice critically wounded. During the robbery, Lev takes a fancy pen from a well-dressed bank customer (amongst gardeners and maids) who tells Lev he is making a terrible mistake. They escape to the nearby Hotel Artemis, an underground hospital funded by its criminal clientele, which is run by Jean "The Nurse" Thomas. Confined inside the hotel for 22 years by her severe agoraphobia and grief over the death of her son, Beau, Thomas adheres to the strict set of rules for the hospital, including "No weapons", "No non-members", and "No killing of other guests".
Sherman and Lev are admitted while their accomplice is forcibly ejected by Thomas' orderly, Everest. Lev, given the codename "Honolulu", undergoes the hotel's technologically advanced treatment, including robot-assisted surgery and 3D printed transplant organs. Thomas shows Sherman evidence that his brother Lev is a drug addict.
Sherman encounters the hotel's other guests: "Acapulco", an obnoxious arms dealer, and "Nice", an international assassin and old acquaintance. As the riot draws nearer, Thomas receives word that notorious crime lord Orian "The Wolf King" Franklin, who is also the owner of the Artemis, is en route with a Code Red. Thomas' preparations are complicated by the arrival of a wounded police officer named Morgan, a childhood friend of Thomas' late son, begging for help. Against Everest's warnings and Thomas' own rules, they admit Morgan.
Through aid from Nice, Sherman discovers the pen Lev stole is marked with the Wolf King's symbol and conceals diamonds worth over $18 million. The Wolf King has a strict policy of killing those who steal from him by drowning them in the ocean. Acapulco learns that Nice has been hired to kill the Wolf King; she incapacitates Acapulco and plants a bomb on the hotel's door lock power generator.
The wounded Wolf King arrives and is admitted, but his men and son Crosby must wait in the lobby's gated ante-room. Everest sneaks Morgan out of the hotel after finishing treatment of her wounds. Fearful of being discovered, Sherman prepares to fight the Wolf King's men until his brother is stable enough to move.
While administering to the Wolf King, Thomas discovers that he was responsible for her son's death. The police reported he died due to an overdose, instead of the truth, her son was killed after attempting to steal the Wolf King's car. The Wolf King paid the police to lie about her son's death and he used the tragedy to recruit Nurse Thomas to run Hotel Artemis. Thomas prepares to kill the Wolf King, but is diverted when Nice's bomb disrupts the power and Lev's life support. While Thomas struggles to save Lev, Nice kills the Wolf King.

title: What Happened to Monday
tagline: Seven sisters. One identity.
overview: In a world where families are limited to one child due to overpopulation, a set of identical septuplets must avoid being put to a long sleep by the government and dangerous infighting while investigating the disappearance of one of their own.
plot:
In a dystopian 2073, overpopulation has resulted in a strict one-child policy, enforced by the European Federation's Child Allocation Bureau. Any illegal children found by the C.A.B. are taken and placed in indefinite cryosleep.
After the death of his daughter during childbirth, Terrence Settman secretly raises his identical septuplet granddaughters. To conceal their existence, he names each child after a day of the week and trains them to live a shared life under a single identity, "Karen Settman". Each sister is allowed to go outside only on the day corresponding to her name to ensure their secret remains undiscovered.
One night, Monday fails to return home after work. The next day, Tuesday retraces her steps and discovers Monday received the promotion they were up for and met their co-worker Jerry at a bar. Before she can investigate further, C.A.B. agents detain her.
At the C.A.B. facility, Tuesday meets presidential candidate and head of the bureau Nicolette Cayman. Cayman reveals she is aware of the sisters' existence and dispatches C.A.B. agents to their apartment to eliminate them. The sisters manage to kill the agents, but Sunday is killed in the process. Learning the agents used Tuesday's severed eyeball to bypass the building's retinal scan, the sisters suspect Jerry may have disclosed their secret.
The next day, Wednesday leaves without disguising herself and confronts Jerry. He reveals that "Karen" received the promotion after transferring millions of euros to Cayman to fund her campaign. After a C.A.B. sniper kills Jerry, Wednesday flees his apartment.
The sisters remotely guide Wednesday to safety but are interrupted when C.A.B. agent Adrian Knowles arrives at their apartment, concerned about "Karen". Surmising that Adrian is in a relationship with one of them, Thursday convinces Saturday to accompany Adrian. At his apartment, Saturday, a virgin, learns which sister Adrian had been seeing. She covertly links their bracelets while sleeping with him, allowing Friday to hack into the C.A.B. surveillance system; the sisters believe they have found Monday in a holding cell. Meanwhile, C.A.B. agents corner and kill Wednesday. After Adrian leaves his apartment, C.A.B. agents arrive and kill Saturday after she tells her siblings Monday was dating Adrian. The sisters' apartment is raided simultaneously by a C.A.B. squad led by Joe, the bureau's head of security. Admitting that she cannot survive on her own, Friday sacrifices herself by detonating their apartment to allow Thursday to escape and rescue Monday.
After learning about the attack, Adrian rushes back to the sisters' apartment, where Thursday confronts him in his car and blames him for her sisters’ deaths. Adrian insists that he knew nothing about the sisters' existence and that he loves 'Karen' without knowing her true name Monday, and agrees to help rescue her.

title: Better Watch Out
tagline: You might be home but you're not alone
overview: On a quiet suburban street tucked within a 'safe neighborhood', a babysitter must defend a twelve-year-old boy from strangers breaking into the house, only to discover that this is far from a normal home invasion.
plot:
Better Watch Out, originally titled Safe Neighborhood, is a 2016 Christmas psychological horror film directed by Chris Peckover, who co-wrote the script with Zack Kahn. It stars Olivia DeJonge as the babysitter Ashley, Levi Miller as twelve-year-old Luke Lerner, Ed Oxenbould as Luke's friend Garrett, Aleks Mikic as Ashley's boyfriend Ricky, Dacre Montgomery as her ex-boyfriend Jeremy, and Patrick Warburton and Virginia Madsen as Luke's parents, Robert and Deandra Lerner.

At Christmas, seventeen-year-old Ashley babysits Luke, a precocious boy with a crush on her, who tries and fails to seduce her as they watch a horror film. Strange noises outside unnerve her, but they seem to come from Luke's best friend Garrett, who drops by. When a brick reading "U leave and U die" smashes through an upstairs window, Garrett panics, runs out the back and appears to be shot dead. Ashley and Luke hide, first in the attic, where he saves her from a dangerous fall, and then in his closet, as a masked figure with a shotgun enters. Recognizing the mask as Luke's, Ashley demands that the intruder remove it, revealing Garrett, and she realizes that Luke staged the attack to frighten her so he could play the hero. When she scolds him, Luke knocks her out. He ties her up with duct tape and makes her play truth or dare, and Ricky, lured by a text that Luke sent from her phone, arrives and senses something wrong. With Garrett holding him at gunpoint, Ricky is subdued and tied up next to Ashley. As Ashley cuts herself free with a piece of glass, Luke kills Ricky by dropping a paint can on him. She points the gun at Luke, but it is unloaded, and as she tries to reach carolers outside, Luke knocks her out again with the brick. Luke then gets Jeremy to write Ashley an apology note and hangs him from a tree, making the letter look like a suicide note. When a remorseful Garrett starts to free Ashley, Luke kills him, then stabs Ashley in the neck and arranges the scene to frame Jeremy before going to bed to await his parents, who call the police. Ashley, however, survives, having sealed her wound with duct tape, and she gives Luke the finger from her stretcher as he watches from his window.

Shot in Sydney in early 2016 on a $3 million budget, the film premiered at Fantastic Fest on 22 September 2016 and was released in the United States on 6 October 2017. Critics responded positively, giving it an 89% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praising the young cast, though it grossed only $188,756.

title: Mowgli: Legend of the Jungle
tagline: The greatest journey is finding where you belong
overview: A human child raised by wolves, must face off against a menacing tiger named Shere Khan, as well as his own origins.
plot:
In the jungles of India, the gigantic Indian python seer Kaa watches as Shere Khan, a sadistic Bengal tiger, breaks "jungle law" by killing a family of humans. The black panther Bagheera finds a surviving infant boy and takes him to Nisha and Vihaan's family of Indian wolves, but the child is spotted by Shere Khan's striped hyena assistant Tabaqui.
The "man-cub" is brought before the wolf council, where Bagheera strong-arms Baloo, a Himalayan brown bear, into serving as his fellow guardian. Shere Khan arrives to kill the child, but Akela, leader of the wolves, declares that the boy is under the pack's protection. Shere Khan warns that when Akela misses his prey, he will return to kill the boy.
The child, now known as Mowgli, is adopted by Nisha and raised by the wolves, Baloo and Bagheera. Years pass, and Mowgli encounters Shere Khan, who has antagonized the nearby "man-village" by killing and slaughtering their cattle. Mowgli falls into a tiger trap set by the villagers, but is saved by Hathi, an Indian elephant missing half a tusk.
That night, Bagheera reveals to Mowgli that he is human, but Mowgli is determined to complete "the Running" – the trial to earn full membership in the pack. Bagheera urges Mowgli to leave the jungle for the village, where he will be safe from Shere Khan; watching the village from afar, Mowgli learns of the existence of fire.
The next day, during the Running as Bagheera chases the young wolves to prove their skill, Mowgli uses his ability to climb and run upright to gain the lead. Desperate to keep him safe, Bagheera unfairly foils Mowgli. After stating to Mowgli that he let his guard down, an enraged Baloo angrily confronts and berates Bagheera for his actions. After running off, Mowgli is kidnapped by the Bandar-log tribe of monkeys and brought to Shere Khan. Baloo and Bagheera arrive to save him. They are overwhelmed by the monkeys and Mowgli is rescued by Kaa. After Baloo heals him, Bhoot, Mowgli's albino wolf friend, attempts to cheer Mowgli up, but Mowgli, furious that he hadn't completed the Running, angrily lashed out at him, causing Bhoot to run away in tears before Mowgli, who felt remorseful for hurting his friend's feelings, can apologize to him. Later, he goes to visit Kaa, who believes he can restore harmony to the jungle.
While hunting, the elderly Akela fails to bring down a water buffalo, leading Shere Khan to remind the pack they must now challenge him for the role of leader. As the wolves fight, Mowgli steals a burning branch from the village and repels Shere Khan and the challengers, but shames Akela who regrettably advises him to leave. Mowgli is soon captured by the villagers and John Lockwood, a British hunter. One night, Bagheera visits Mowgli and tells him that he must stay with the villagers and gain their trust as he once did to escape captivity himself.

title: Mary Magdalene
tagline: Her story will be told
overview: In the first century, free-spirited Mary Magdalene flees the marriage her family has arranged for her, finding refuge and a sense of purpose in a radical new movement led by the charismatic, rabble-rousing preacher named Jesus.
plot:
Mary Magdalene is a 2018 biographical drama film directed by Garth Davis and written by Roseanne Powell. The film tells the story of Mary Magdalene, one of Jesus' twelve apostles, and her journey from being a sinful woman to becoming a devoted follower of Christ.

The film begins with Mary (played by Rooney Mara) as a young woman living in Capernaum, a small fishing village on the shores of the Sea of Galilee. She is portrayed as a complex character, struggling with her own demons and feeling isolated from society due to her past mistakes. The story then shifts to Jesus' (played by Juno Temple) arrival in Capernaum, where Mary meets him and becomes drawn to his teachings.

As Mary spends more time with Jesus, she begins to see the world through new eyes and finds a sense of purpose and belonging. She is introduced as one of Jesus' twelve apostles, alongside other notable figures such as Peter (played by Yul Vazquez) and John (played by Louis Hunter). The film depicts their early days together, exploring the teachings of Jesus and witnessing his miracles.

However, Mary's past mistakes continue to haunt her. She is shown to have been involved with a group of men who were using her for their own gain, leading to her feelings of shame and guilt. Despite this, she finds solace in her relationship with Jesus, who accepts her unconditionally and helps her to confront her demons.

As the story unfolds, Mary becomes increasingly devoted to Jesus' teachings and is present at many key events in his life, including the Last Supper and the Crucifixion. The film's portrayal of these events is poignant and powerful, highlighting the depth of Mary's love for Jesus and her willingness to follow him even into death.

The film's climax features Mary standing by Jesus' side as he dies on the cross, a moment that has been depicted in many other films and artworks throughout history. However, this version offers a fresh perspective on the event, emphasizing Mary's role as a witness and follower of Jesus rather than simply a bystander.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of the natural world and the emotional intensity of the characters' experiences. The score by Jed Kurzel adds to the overall sense of drama and tension, perfectly capturing the mood of each scene.

Overall, Mary Magdalene offers a powerful and moving portrayal of one of Jesus' most devoted followers. By exploring her complex character and her journey towards redemption, the film provides a unique perspective on the life of Christ and his disciples.

title: Euphoria
tagline: It's never too late.
overview: The story of two sisters on a journey, where they try to get close to each other and approach the tough questions in life. Euphoria is a contemporary drama about responsibility and reconciliation, in a world where these concepts are gradually being lost.
plot:
Emilie (Eva Green) and Ines (Alicia Vikander) Thompson are two sisters with very different characters who live far apart and rarely see each other. Now Ines, an artist trying to cope with unfavourable reviews of her latest exhibition, has accepted Emilie's invitation to accompany her on a short trip to an unknown place in the heart of Europe. The hotel Emilie has chosen for the first few days of her stay is very luxurious, as is the restaurant where she plans to dine; she evasively explains to her sister that she has sold her flat because she wants to go back to studying. During dinner, she agrees to dance with a stranger, to whom she confides that she is convinced Ines is only with her because her career is on the decline, adding that she "has no more time to lie". She therefore rejects the man's advances on the grounds that she would like to have an adventure but that this is not possible for her; immediately afterwards she feels very uncomfortable, which she attributes to the champagne she has drunk.
Their destination, which Emilie describes as "the most beautiful place in the world", turns out to be an estate lost in the woods beyond an unspecified country border, where they are met by an elderly woman, Marina (Charlotte Rampling), who describes herself as Emilie's "personal companion". For the unsuspecting Ines, it is the moment of truth: Emilie reveals to her that she has cancer, has been undergoing unsuccessful treatment for three years, and has therefore chosen assisted suicide; the place to which she has taken her is actually an exclusive clinic where patients can spend their last six days in complete peace before taking their own lives by poisoning themselves after a simple ritual. Ines is distraught and cannot accept that Emilie has kept everything from her, but her sister bitterly claims that she did it because it was the only way she could accompany her on her final journey. In fact, during their stay, the two will repeatedly confront each other harshly about their conflicting life choices: Emilie has remained close to her mother, who fell into depression because of her separation from her husband, until her suicide; Ines soon distanced herself from her, accused her of weakness and victimhood, and did not even go to the funeral, building a nice career as an excuse for her constant absence and creating a kind of armour of rationality and self-preservation. At the clinic, the two women not only meet but also the charming Mr Daren (Charles Dance), also terminally ill, a wealthy playboy who is now an old man and organises a party on his last night, and Brian (Mark Stanley), a former footballer who has been paralysed and rendered impotent by a car accident and who, attracted to Emilie, spends a night with her, arousing her anger that he has decided to leave life behind despite his health.

title: Detroit
tagline: It's time we knew
overview: A police raid in Detroit in 1967 results in one of the largest citizens' uprisings in the history of the United States.
plot:
On July 23, 1967, the Detroit Police Department stage a raid on an unlicensed club during a celebration for some African American veterans returning from the Vietnam War. While suspects are being arrested, a mob forms and begins throwing rocks at the officers before looting nearby stores and starting fires, beginning the 12th Street Riot. With local authorities, elected representatives, and emergency services unable to maintain order, Governor George W. Romney authorizes the National Guard and President Lyndon B. Johnson authorizes Army paratroopers to enter Detroit to provide assistance. On the second day of rioting, officers Krauss and Flynn pursue a fleeing looter, and Krauss kills the man with a shotgun against orders, but is allowed to remain on duty while his superiors debate filing murder charges.
Seconds before The Dramatics, a black R&B vocal group, take the stage for a performance that they hope will lead to a recording contract with Motown, the police shut down the venue due to rioting outside. The bus the group gets on is attacked by rioters, and, in the ensuing chaos, they get split up. Larry, the lead singer, and his friend, Fred, rent a room in the nearby Algiers Motel—in a detached annex building—to get off the streets. They meet two young white women, Julie and Karen, who introduce them to Carl, Lee, Aubrey, and Michael. Carl and Lee stage a prank using a starter pistol, upsetting Julie and Karen, who go to the room of Greene, a Vietnam War veteran, while Larry and Fred return to their own room.
Melvin Dismukes, a private security guard, is at a grocery store near the Algiers to protect it from rioters. Some guardsmen pull up outside, and Carl decides to fire several blanks at the troops to frighten them. The shots are mistaken for a sniper attack, and members of the National Guard and the state and local police descend upon the Algiers annex to investigate. Krauss guns down a fleeing Carl immediately upon entering the building and plants a knife next to the body.
The task force lines up everyone they find in the annex against the wall, demanding to know who the sniper was. No weapon is found, but Krauss begins to terrorize and beat the suspects while interrogating them. Dismukes arrives and, although he does not like what he sees, does not challenge Krauss openly. As the situation spirals out of control, most of the state police and national guardsmen leave to avoid being associated with it, but no one intervenes or reports the abuse.
One by one, Krauss orders several suspects to be moved to different rooms and subjected to mock executions in order to terrify the others into confessing. Julie and Karen are taken to an upstairs room when Karen begins screaming, and Julie's clothes get torn off. Disgusted, one of the remaining Guardsman gets them released from custody.

title: A Cinderella Story: If the Shoe Fits
original_title: A Cinderella Story: If the Shoe Fits
tagline: A magical musical treat for the dreamer in all of us.
overview: A contemporary musical version of the classic Cinderella story in which the servant step daughter hope to compete in a musical competition for a famous pop star.
plot:
A Cinderella Story: If the Shoe Fits is a 2016 American musical teen comedy film directed by Michelle Johnston in her directorial debut, the fourth installment in the A Cinderella Story series. It stars Sofia Carson as Tessa, a young mechanic who secretly competes for the lead in a musical, Thomas Law as the star Reed West, and Jennifer Tilly as her stepmother, Divine, with Nicole Fortuin and David Ury.

Since her father's death, Tessa has lived with Divine and her stepsisters, Athena and Olympia. She goes along as their assistant to auditions at a luxury hotel for a musical based on Cinderella, directed by Freddie Marks and starring Reed, with whom she is instantly smitten. Freddie announces that auditions are open to everyone and that the actress cast as the lead will receive a recording contract. Tessa befriends Georgie, the show's make-up artist, and helps the stagehands repair a motorcycle for the production; Reed, seeing her work, takes her for a man. Inspired by the hotel staff's performances, Tessa decides to audition, and since her stepfamily forbids it, Georgie gives her a makeover and a fake identity. Her singing impresses Reed and Freddie, but when her stepfamily bursts into the dance audition, she flees, leaving a dance shoe behind.

Reed announces that whoever brings the matching shoe by midnight will win the role, and Divine orders Tessa to forge a copy for her daughters. Fixing the motorcycle, Tessa bonds with Reed and tells him about her father, then hands in her real shoe and wins the part under the stage name Bella Snow, secretly attending rehearsals. Told by Freddie that Reed is engaged to his co-star Harper Halston, she distances herself from him. Her stepsisters discover her secret and lock her away on opening day to steal the lead, but she escapes through an air vent. As chaos erupts onstage, Reed confronts Freddie for meddling and declares that he and Harper are only friends and that he loves someone else. Tessa appears without her disguise, the show succeeds, she receives her record contract and rejects Divine, and she and Reed ride off on the motorcycle she repaired.

The film was released digitally on August 2, 2016, alongside its soundtrack album from WaterTower Music, and on DVD that month. Its Freeform premiere in November 2016 drew 1.11 million viewers, and a Disney Channel airing in January 2017 drew 2.13 million. A Cinderella Story: Christmas Wish followed in 2019.
