overview: Brad and Dusty must deal with their intrusive fathers during the holidays.
plot:
Daddy's Home 2 is a 2017 American Christmas comedy film directed by Sean Anders and John Morris, and produced by Paramount Pictures.

The movie takes place two years after the events of the first film. Brad Whitaker (Will Ferrell) and Dusty Mayron (Mark Wahlberg) are still co-parenting their children, but they're struggling to balance their own relationships with their wives, Sara (Linda Cardellini) and Megan (Catherine Keener), respectively.

As Christmas approaches, the Whitakers and the Mayrons decide to spend the holiday together as a blended family. However, things quickly become complicated when Brad's estranged father, Don Whitaker (Mel Gibson), shows up unexpectedly with his own son, Ryan (Wes Bentley). Don is a gruff, old-school man who clashes with Dusty and the rest of the family.

As the two families try to come together for Christmas, they face various challenges. Brad and Dusty struggle to assert their authority as co-parents, while Sara and Megan try to keep the peace between their husbands. Meanwhile, Don's presence sparks tension among the group, particularly with Dusty, who feels like he's being replaced by his father.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Don's past, which reveal a complex and troubled relationship with Brad. We also learn more about Ryan, who is struggling to find his place in the world after serving in the military.

Throughout the film, the characters' relationships are put to the test as they navigate their differences and try to come together for Christmas. In the end, the Whitakers and Mayrons learn to put aside their differences and work together as a blended family.

One of the standout aspects of Daddy's Home 2 is its exploration of complex themes such as family dynamics, masculinity, and identity. The film tackles these issues with humor and heart, making it a relatable and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, Daddy's Home 2 is a fun and lighthearted holiday film that explores the ups and downs of blended families. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and heartfelt moments, it's a great addition to any Christmas movie marathon.

title: Ad Astra
tagline: The answers we seek are just outside our reach
overview: The near future, a time when both hope and hardships drive humanity to look to the stars and beyond. While a mysterious phenomenon menaces to destroy life on planet Earth, astronaut Roy McBride undertakes a mission across the immensity of space and its many perils to uncover the truth about a lost expedition that decades before boldly faced emptiness and silence in search of the unknown.
plot:
In the early 22nd century, mysterious cosmic-ray bursts emanating from Neptune cause power surges that threaten to destroy all life in the Solar System. Major Roy McBride is informed that the surge is antimatter in origin and may be connected to the Lima Project, a space station in orbit around Neptune, sent twenty-nine years earlier to search for intelligent life and fuelled by antimatter. Roy's father, Clifford McBride, was the project's leader, a man considered a hero in SpaceCom history. Contact was lost sixteen years into its mission. Roy agrees to travel to Mars to use the last active communications station unaffected by the bursts in an effort to contact Clifford aboard the Lima.
At the Moon SpaceCom base, Roy is told in secret by Colonel Pruitt that should he fail to make contact with the Lima Project, the station will have to be destroyed. Roy obtains passage to Mars on the cruiser Cepheus.
On the way to Mars the Cepheus attends a distress call from a research station, where the captain is killed. The ship continues to Mars but is hit by a surge as it is landing, Roy assumes command from the overwhelmed (but now in charge) First Officer, and calmly lands the ship. After securing himself in the underground SpaceCom complex, Roy begins recording officially pre-written voice messages and transmitting them to the Lima Project in hopes that his father will respond. Following several failed attempts, Roy ends up ignoring the official message and sends a personal message to his father stating that he hopes he will see him one day. Roy is then told he will be returning to Earth as his 'personal connection' makes him unsuitable for further service.
Roy is visited by facility director Helen Lantos, who reveals that her parents were Lima Project team members. She shows him classified footage revealing that Clifford's team mutinied and attempted to return to Earth, causing him to shut off their life-support systems; her parents were among those killed. She also states that the Cepheus is carrying a nuclear weapon and has now been requisitioned for a secret 'seek and destroy' mission without Roy. Seeing that the 'hero' story was fabricated to hide the truth, Roy decides that he should deal with his father. Lantos facilitates Roy getting to the rocket as it prepares to depart.
Roy climbs aboard as the rocket takes off and is immediately discovered by the crew, who are unintentionally killed in the confrontation. During the 79-day journey to Neptune, a solitary Roy reflects on his relationship with his father and with his estranged wife, Eve. He finally arrives at the station and plants the nuclear bomb before encountering Clifford, the sole survivor of the Lima Project. Clifford explains that the surges are coming from an antimatter meltdown caused by the mutiny. He also admits to Roy that he never really cared about his family and does not consider Earth his home.

title: Disobedience

overview: A woman learns about the death of her Orthodox Jewish father, a rabbi. She returns home and has romantic feelings rekindled for her best childhood friend, who is now married to her cousin.
plot:
New York photographer Ronit Krushka, known as Ronnie in the United States, returns to her childhood home in North London after her father, the old Rav, succumbs to pneumonia. Ronit is uncomfortable seeing everyone again since she was banished from the community for behaving in a manner not conforming to Orthodox culture.
Ronit is shocked to learn that her childhood friends Dovid, a chosen disciple of her father, and Esti, are now married. Dovid invites Ronit to stay with them. They attend Shabbat dinner at her uncle Moshe's house where she is questioned by the guests about changing her name, and they tell her she should get married, because that is what is right. Ronit tells them if she had stayed in London she probably would have been married off, but she would have been suicidal.
Ronit visits Moshe at his office to discuss the disposition of her father's house and discovers her father has left all of his possessions to the synagogue. Ronit and Esti run into each other on the street while Ronit is on her way to visit her father's house. While inspecting items left in the house, Ronit becomes frustrated and expresses that she wishes to cut her trip short and return to the United States. Upset, Esti tenderly kisses Ronit, who initially resists before reciprocating. Esti confesses to having asked Ronit to be notified of her father's death out of a desire to see her again. She also reveals her unhappiness with her life choices, taken based on the Rav's advice and her strong belief in HaShem. It is revealed that Ronit and Esti were caught in a romantic tryst when they were younger, leading Ronit to leave the United Kingdom; neither has been with another woman since and Esti admits being attracted to only women.
On the way home, they stop at a nearby park and kiss again, but are spotted by a couple from the congregation. The next day Esti, who works as a teacher at the local Jewish school, is called into the headmistress' office after the couple deliver a complaint about what they saw. Meanwhile, Dovid is asked to take over the Rav's duties. Ronit tells Esti she is leaving London, and the two of them sneak away to a hotel room in central London for passionate sex.
When Esti arrives home, she turns down Dovid when he tries to initiate intimacy. She later tells him the truth about her feelings for Ronit, causing him to leave. Esti later purchases a pregnancy test and discovers she is pregnant. The next morning, Dovid calls Ronit and says that Esti is missing. They spend the day looking for her and, when they return home, Esti has come back; she asks Dovid for her freedom, stating that she wants to give her unborn child a chance to decide whether or not to be part of their community.
Ronit and Esti attend the Rav's hesped (eulogy gathering), which is to be given by Dovid. Under the guise of addressing the congregation, he releases Esti from their marriage and then publicly turns down the offer of becoming the congregation's new spiritual guide.

title: Don't Knock Twice

overview: A mother desperate to reconnect with her troubled daughter becomes embroiled in the urban legend of a demonic witch.
plot:
In Wales, Jessica "Jess" Webb-Thomas, an American sculptor and former drug addict, meets with her estranged daughter Chloe (from Jess's prior marriage and sent to foster care due to the former's drug addiction) and invites her to come live with her and her second husband, Ben Thomas. Chloe declines. That night, Chloe goes out with her friend Danny to a house where legend says a witch lived. The two knock twice on the door and leave. Danny starts experiencing paranormal occurrences and is later dragged away by an unseen force. When the demonic spirit frightens Chloe, she accepts Jess' offer and moves in with her.
Chloe is initially hostile to her family. Strange events unfold, beginning when Chloe finds a human molar in her carrot and coriander soup. Jess suffers from a nightmare about an old woman crying in her house. In her nightmare, the woman looks at Jess and says "Przepraszam" ("I'm sorry" in Polish), before slitting her own throat. Jess tells Chloe about her dream and, finding this description familiar, Chloe tells her about Mary Aminov, a supposed witch that used to live next door. After her death by suicide, an urban legend started that she would come and get you if you knocked twice on her door. While sculpting, Jess's model Tira is disturbed by Chloe's presence and leaves. Chloe believes to be haunted by Baba Yaga, a demonic witch from Slavic folklore.
Chloe slowly warms up to her mother. One day, Jess discovers her workshop in shambles with "She's mine" scrawled on the floor. That night, the two are terrorized by the witch. The next day, a portal opens and Chloe is almost dragged inside but is saved by Jess. They meet with Tira, who says that Mary was never a witch. Because Chloe helped spread the false rumor of witchcraft, Mary's spirit wants revenge. Chloe flees in panic, convinced that the disappearances were her fault. She is found and returned to the foster home. Jess goes to retrieve her and has an epiphany that the true culprit of the disappearances was not Mary but Detective Boardman. Chloe is taken by the witch.
Jess breaks into Mary's abandoned house, injuring her foot on an old nail. She is caught and sent to the police station, but not before knocking twice at the door. When she is alone in her prison cell, she is taken through the same portal. She wanders into a cave where she finds a cage with Chloe in it. Jess gets her out and Baba Yaga pursues them; meanwhile, Boardman arrives at the witch's home. The pair are able to escape through the front door, but Boardman is dragged inside by the witch.
Ben returns home and is confronted by a mysterious figure in their bedroom. Jess and Chloe arrive home but find Ben missing. Tira is shown leaving the property covered in blood with Ben's dead body in the trunk of her car. The "Slave of Baba Yaga" symbol is shown on her chest.

title: Cage Dive
tagline: First you find the sharks. Then they find you.
overview: Three friends from California are filming an audition tape for an extreme reality game show. They document their journey to Australia where they will be doing their most dangerous activity.... Shark Cage Diving. A catastrophic turn of events leaves them in baited water full of Great White Sharks, turning their recording into a blood chilling diary of survival... and death.
plot:
Open Water 3: Cage Dive is a 2017 Australian found-footage survival horror film written and directed by Gerald Rascionato. Presented as a mockumentary about supposedly true events, it follows three American tourists recording an audition tape for an extreme reality show when their shark cage diving boat capsizes. The cast includes Joel Hogan, Megan Peta Hill and Pete Valley. Although billed as the third Open Water film, it is a standalone story linked to the earlier entries only by theme.

A news report from October 2015 describes a capsized shark diving boat off Australia and a search for three missing passengers from Laguna Beach, California. A week later a diver finds an underwater camera lodged in a reef, its memory card intact, and posts the footage online. The recordings show brothers Josh and Jeff and Jeff's girlfriend, Megan, arriving in Sydney to stay with the brothers' cousin Greg before flying to Adelaide for their dive, and reveal that Megan is secretly having an affair with Josh. During the excursion, as the three enter the cage, a rogue wave overturns the boat. They escape to the surface amid wounded passengers, and sharks soon kill several people nearby.

Drifting for hours, the trio clings to tangled life preservers while Jeff, who has a heart condition and needs regular medication, weakens. That night they find an inflatable emergency raft with supplies, and Josh rescues an unconscious, hypothermic woman from floating debris. During an argument Megan and Josh accidentally fire a flare inside the raft, which burns, killing the woman. The quarrel exposes the affair, and soon afterward a shark drags Megan under. The next morning Jeff taunts Josh about Megan's death until he loses consciousness from his heart condition, and Josh eventually lets his brother's body sink. With the camera battery nearly exhausted, Josh films a rescue helicopter in the distance, but as he waves and shouts, the camera captures a great white rising beneath him, and the footage ends as he is pulled under.

Lionsgate acquired the independent production in early 2017 and rebranded it as part of the Open Water series after the success of Open Water 2: Adrift, releasing it across multiple platforms on August 11, 2017. It bears similarities to 47 Meters Down, another 2017 film about a cage dive gone wrong. It received a 25% score on Rotten Tomatoes from eight critics, although Starburst Magazine reviewed it positively.

title: Maleficent: Mistress of Evil
tagline: Go beyond the fairy tale
overview: Maleficent and her goddaughter Aurora begin to question the complex family ties that bind them as they are pulled in different directions by impending nuptials, unexpected allies, and dark new forces at play.
plot:
Maleficent: Mistress of Evil is a 2019 American dark fantasy film directed by Michelle MacLaren, written by Michelle MacLaren and Christina Hodson, and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The film serves as a sequel to the 2014 film Maleficent.

The story begins with Princess Aurora (Ella Balinska) now a young woman, preparing for her wedding to Prince Philip (Benedict Walker). However, Maleficent (Angelina Jolie), who has been watching over Aurora from afar, senses that something is amiss. She discovers that the royal family's advisor, King Stefan (Harris Dickinson), plans to use dark magic to ensure his daughter's happiness and secure the throne.

Maleficent sets out to stop the wedding, knowing that it will lead to a catastrophic outcome for all of them. Along the way, she meets Morgan (Jemaine Clement), a powerful sorcerer who claims to be her long-lost brother. As they journey together, Maleficent learns more about her past and the reason behind her curse.

Meanwhile, Prince Philip's mother, Queen Grimhilde (Lesley Manville), is revealed to be the one responsible for casting the original curse on Aurora as a child. The queen's true intentions are to use Aurora's blood to gain ultimate power and control over the kingdom.

As Maleficent navigates her complicated past and confronts her enemies, she must also face her own morality and the consequences of her actions. Alongside Morgan, she forms an unlikely alliance with the fairy godmother, who helps them in their quest to stop the wedding and save Aurora from a terrible fate.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Maleficent and Queen Grimhilde, with the two powerful women engaging in a magical duel that will determine the future of the kingdom. In the end, Maleficent emerges victorious, but not without scars and a newfound understanding of her own strength and vulnerability.

Throughout the film, Angelina Jolie's performance as Maleficent is both captivating and nuanced, bringing depth to the character's complexities. The supporting cast delivers solid performances, particularly Ella Balinska as Aurora, who shines in her breakout role.

Overall, Maleficent: Mistress of Evil offers a thrilling and emotionally resonant sequel that expands on the original story while introducing new characters and themes. With its stunning visuals, engaging storyline, and strong performances, this film is sure to delight fans of fantasy and adventure movies alike.

title: Christopher Robin
tagline: Don't underestimate the value of doing nothing.
overview: Christopher Robin, the boy who had countless adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood, has grown up and lost his way. Now it’s up to his spirited and loveable stuffed animals, Winnie The Pooh, Tigger, Piglet, and the rest of the gang, to rekindle their friendship and remind him of endless days of childlike wonder and make-believe, when doing nothing was the very best something.
plot:
Christopher Robin is a 2018 American fantasy drama film directed by Marc Forster and produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie is based on the Winnie-the-Pooh stories created by A.A. Milne.

The story begins with Christopher Robin (played by Ewan McGregor), now a grown man, who has lost touch with his childhood imagination and the magical world of Winnie-the-Pooh. He is struggling to find meaning in his life as a successful businessman, but feels unfulfilled and disconnected from his past.

One day, while on vacation at the Hundred Acre Wood, Christopher Robin reunites with his old friends Pooh (voiced by Jim Cummings), Piglet (voiced by Nick Mohammed), Eeyore (voiced by Brad Garrett), Tigger (voiced by Jim Cummings), Rabbit (voiced by Peter Capaldi), Owl (voiced by Toby Jones), and Kanga (voiced by Nicole Scherzinger). The friends are delighted to see Christopher Robin again, but they also sense that he has lost his way.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Christopher Robin's adult life is marked by stress, anxiety, and a lack of creativity. He feels like he's losing himself in the process of becoming a successful businessman. Meanwhile, Pooh and the other animals are struggling to cope with the changing world around them, including the loss of their home due to urban development.

Through his interactions with his friends, Christopher Robin begins to rediscover the joys of childhood imagination and creativity. He starts to see the world through the eyes of a child again, and finds inspiration in the simple pleasures of life. The movie features stunning animation, bringing the beloved characters to life in a way that is both nostalgic and fresh.

As the story reaches its climax, Christopher Robin must confront his own fears and doubts in order to find his true purpose in life. With the help of his friends, he learns to let go of his adult responsibilities and rediscover the magic of childhood. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Christopher Robin returning home to his family, but this time with a renewed sense of wonder and imagination.

Throughout the film, there are also flashbacks that show Christopher Robin's childhood adventures in the Hundred Acre Wood, which serve as a reminder of the power of imagination and friendship. The movie features a talented voice cast, including Emily Blunt as Christopher Robin's wife, Jane, and Hayley Atwell as his mother.

Overall, Christopher Robin is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the importance of childhood imagination and creativity. It's a story about finding one's true purpose in life and rediscovering the magic of childhood through the power of friendship and imagination.

title: Aladdin

overview: A kindhearted street urchin named Aladdin embarks on a magical adventure after finding a lamp that releases a wisecracking genie while a power-hungry Grand Vizier vies for the same lamp that has the power to make their deepest wishes come true.
plot:
Aladdin is a 2019 American fantasy adventure film directed by Guy Ritchie and produced by Jerry Bruckheimer. The movie is a live-action remake of the 1992 animated film of the same name, which was based on the Middle Eastern folk tale "Aladdin's Wonderful Lamp".

The story begins in the bustling streets of Agrabah, where we meet our protagonist, Aladdin (played by Mena Massoud), a poor but kind-hearted street urchin who lives with his pet monkey, Abu. One day, while exploring the marketplace, Aladdin stumbles upon a mysterious cave where he finds a magic lamp containing the Genie (played by Will Smith). The Genie is an ancient being who has been trapped in the lamp for thousands of years and is eager to be released.

The Genie grants Aladdin three wishes, which he uses to become a prince to win the heart of Princess Jasmine (played by Naomi Scott), the beautiful daughter of the Sultan. However, their romance is threatened when the evil Jafar (played by Marwan Kenzari), the Royal Advisor, discovers that the magic lamp and its Genie are real.

As Aladdin navigates his new life as a prince, he must also confront the dark secrets of Agrabah's past and the true intentions of Jafar. The Genie, who has grown attached to Aladdin, becomes a valuable ally in the battle against Jafar.

Throughout the film, Ritchie's signature style is evident in the witty banter, clever wordplay, and fast-paced action sequences. The movie also features stunning visuals, with intricate sets and costumes that transport viewers to the vibrant world of Agrabah.

As the story unfolds, Aladdin must confront his own identity and the consequences of his wishes. In a thrilling climax, he faces off against Jafar in an epic battle to save the kingdom and win Jasmine's heart.

Ultimately, Aladdin emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. The film concludes with Aladdin and Jasmine sharing a romantic moment, while the Genie is finally able to rest in peace. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Aladdin embracing his true identity as a street urchin who has become a hero.

Overall, the 2019 live-action remake of Aladdin is a visually stunning and action-packed adventure that stays true to the spirit of the original tale while introducing new elements to captivate modern audiences.

title: The Lion King
tagline: The King has Returned.
overview: Simba idolizes his father, King Mufasa, and takes to heart his own royal destiny. But not everyone in the kingdom celebrates the new cub's arrival. Scar, Mufasa's brother—and former heir to the throne—has plans of his own. The battle for Pride Rock is ravaged with betrayal, tragedy and drama, ultimately resulting in Simba's exile. With help from a curious pair of newfound friends, Simba will have to figure out how to grow up and take back what is rightfully his.
plot:
The Lion King is a 2019 American musical drama film and a photorealistically animated remake of Disney's traditionally animated 1994 film. Directed by Jon Favreau and written by Jeff Nathanson, it was produced by Walt Disney Pictures and Fairview Entertainment. The voice cast includes Donald Glover as Simba, Beyoncé Knowles-Carter as Nala, Chiwetel Ejiofor as Scar, Seth Rogen and Billy Eichner as Pumbaa and Timon, John Oliver as Zazu, John Kani as Rafiki and Alfre Woodard as Sarabi, with James Earl Jones reprising his role as Mufasa.

In the Pride Lands, King Mufasa and Queen Sarabi present their newborn son Simba to the gathered animals, while Mufasa's younger brother Scar resentfully covets the throne. Mufasa teaches Simba about the responsibilities of a king and the "circle of life" that connects all living things. Scar tricks the curious cub into exploring a forbidden elephant graveyard, where Simba and his best friend Nala are chased by hyenas led by Shenzi before Mufasa, alerted by the hornbill Zazu, comes to their rescue. Scar then strikes a deal with the hyenas, promising them hunting rights in exchange for their help in killing Mufasa and Simba. He lures Simba into a gorge and has the hyenas drive a stampede of wildebeest toward him; Mufasa saves his son but is thrown to his death by Scar, who convinces Simba that he was to blame and urges him to run away and never return. Scar claims the throne and lets the hyenas into the Pride Lands. Rescued in the desert by the meerkat Timon and the warthog Pumbaa, Simba grows up carefree in their oasis, living by their motto "hakuna matata". Years later he is reunited with Nala, who tells him that the kingdom has fallen into drought and ruin under Scar's rule. Still burdened by guilt, Simba refuses to return, until the wise mandrill Rafiki and a vision of his father's spirit remind him of who he is, and he heads home to confront Scar and reclaim his place in the circle of life.

The film received mixed reviews, with many critics praising its visuals but faulting its lack of originality and near-identical retelling of the original; it holds a 52% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It nevertheless grossed more than $1.6 billion worldwide and broke several box-office records, including becoming the highest-grossing animated film of all time until 2024.

title: Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers
tagline: It's not a reboot. It's a comeback.
overview: Decades since their successful television series was canceled, Chip has succumbed to a life of suburban domesticity as an insurance salesman. Dale, meanwhile, has had CGI surgery and works the nostalgia convention circuit, desperate to relive his glory days. When a former cast mate mysteriously disappears, Chip and Dale must repair their broken friendship and take on their Rescue Rangers detective personas once again to save their friend’s life.
plot:
Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers is a 2022 American live-action and animated action-adventure comedy based on Disney's chipmunk duo and serving as a follow-up to the 1989 animated series of the same name. It was directed by Akiva Schaffer from a screenplay by Dan Gregor and Doug Mand. John Mulaney voices Chip and Andy Samberg voices Dale, with KiKi Layne, Will Arnett, Eric Bana, Seth Rogen and J. K. Simmons. It premiered at the El Capitan Theatre and was released on Disney+ on May 20, 2022.

In a world where humans and cartoon characters live side by side, Chip and Dale become best friends in elementary school and later move to Hollywood, where they rise from bit parts to stardom with the hit series Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers. When Dale is offered a solo spin-off, the pair fall out bitterly and the show is cancelled. Thirty years later, Chip is a cautious, jaded insurance salesman, while Dale, who has undergone "CGI surgery" to look three-dimensional, works the fan convention circuit.

Their old co-star Monterey Jack, deep in debt to the criminal Valley Gang because of his addiction to cheese, warns them of a ring that kidnaps cartoons, alters their appearance and forces them to star in cheap bootleg films overseas. When Monty disappears, the estranged chipmunks reluctantly reunite to find him, helped by Ellie Steckler, an eager police officer and devoted fan of their show.

Their investigation leads to the gang's leader, Sweet Pete, a grown-up, embittered Peter Pan who was cast aside by the industry when he aged, and his henchmen. The chipmunks trace the operation to a warehouse containing a machine for reshaping toons, and realise that someone in the police is working with Pete. During a chase at a fan convention Chip is captured, and Ellie discovers that her captain is in league with the villain.

Dale rallies their old co-stars Gadget and Zipper, now married with a large family, and stops the machine before it can be used on Chip. In the chaos, Pete is transformed into a monstrous amalgam of cartoon parts. Using a trick from one of their old episodes, the chipmunks trap him, and the FBI, led by Ugly Sonic, arrests the gang. When Dale survives a cannon blast thanks to a keepsake Chip once gave him, the friends reconcile, free Monty and the other captive toons and go on to make a successful reboot of their show.

Critics responded warmly, with 81% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and the film later won the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Television Movie.

title: The Return of Godzilla

overview: After a fishing boat is attacked, the sole surviving crew member realizes it is none other than a resurrected Godzilla. However, efforts to bring the story to light are suppressed by the Japanese government amid growing political tensions between the United States and the Soviet Union, who are both willing to bomb Japan to stop the monster.
plot:
The Return of Godzilla is a 1984 Japanese science fiction kaiju film directed by Kazuki Ōmori and produced by Tomoyuki Tanaka. It is the 15th film in the Godzilla franchise.

The movie begins with a series of mysterious earthquakes occurring around the world, which are later revealed to be caused by the return of Godzilla, also known as "Gigantis" or "Godzilla's Return". The story takes place two years after the events of Godzilla vs. Biollante (1989), where Godzilla is awakened from its slumber in the depths of the ocean.

The film starts with a series of strange occurrences happening around the world, including earthquakes and tidal waves. As the earthquakes intensify, it becomes clear that Godzilla has returned to wreak havoc on humanity. The Japanese government assembles a team of scientists and military personnel to deal with the crisis.

The main character, Dr. Yamane (played by Takeshi Kusao), is a renowned paleontologist who had previously studied Godzilla's DNA. He is recruited by the government to lead the team that will study and stop Godzilla. The team includes his daughter, Emiko (played by Yuriko Hoshi), a young scientist who has grown up studying her father's work.

As Godzilla begins its rampage across Japan, the team discovers that it is not just a mindless beast, but a creature with a complex intelligence and a desire to destroy humanity. The team also learns that Godzilla's return is linked to the discovery of a new species of giant lizard in the depths of the ocean.

The plot thickens as the team discovers that Godzilla's DNA has been altered by its encounter with a new species of giant lizard, which has given it enhanced strength and intelligence. This revelation raises questions about the nature of Godzilla's existence and whether it is truly a monster or a creature worthy of respect.

As the story unfolds, the team faces numerous challenges in trying to stop Godzilla. They use various tactics, including nuclear missiles and sonic devices, but nothing seems to work. The film builds towards an epic showdown between Godzilla and the team, which culminates in a dramatic confrontation on the streets of Tokyo.

In the end, Dr. Yamane comes up with a plan to use a device that can disrupt Godzilla's DNA, rendering it unable to reproduce. However, this plan is complicated by the fact that Emiko has fallen in love with Godzilla and wants to protect it. The film ends with a bittersweet conclusion, as Emiko sacrifices herself to save her father and the world from Godzilla.

The Return of Godzilla is a thought-provoking film that explores themes of nature vs. nurture, humanity's relationship with technology, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond our control. It is also a thrilling adventure that showcases Godzilla's iconic status as a symbol of Japanese popular culture.

title: Flower
tagline: Bad decisions. Good intentions.
overview: Rebellious, quick-witted Erica Vandross is a 17-year-old firecracker living with her single mom, Laurie, and her mom's new boyfriend, Bob, in L.A.'s San Fernando Valley. When Bob's mentally unbalanced son, Luke, arrives from rehab to live with the family, Erica finds her domestic and personal life overwhelmed. With Luke and her sidekicks Kala and Claudine in tow, Erica acts out by exposing a high school teacher's dark secret.
plot:
Flower is a 2017 American romantic comedy-drama directed by Max Winkler from a screenplay he wrote with Alex McAulay and Matt Spicer. Zoey Deutch stars as Erica Vandross, a brash and sexually curious seventeen-year-old, with Kathryn Hahn as her mother Laurie, Tim Heidecker as Laurie's boyfriend Bob, Joey Morgan as Bob's troubled son Luke, and Adam Scott as a former teacher. Dylan Gelula, Maya Eshet and Eric Edelstein complete the cast. The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2017 and was later released by The Orchard.

Erica and two friends run a reckless scheme in their Los Angeles suburb: Erica seduces older men while her friends secretly film the encounter, then the trio extort money by threatening to expose the men for involvement with a minor. Erica is saving the money to pay bail for her father, who is in jail awaiting trial for attempting to rob a casino. Her mother tolerates her behaviour but is frustrated that Erica refuses to warm to her new partner, Bob.

When Bob's son Luke, an anxious and emotionally fragile eighteen-year-old, returns from rehab and moves into the household, Erica first tries to provoke him but soon develops an unexpected friendship with him. At a bowling alley, Luke suffers a panic attack upon seeing Will Jordan, a former middle-school teacher he once accused of sexual abuse, a case that was dropped because of inconsistencies in his account. Shortly afterwards, Erica stops Luke from attempting suicide. Determined to punish the man she believes hurt him, Erica decides to make Will her group's next target, and Luke reluctantly agrees to help. As she pursues the teacher, however, the plan grows more dangerous and the truth about what happened between Will and Luke turns out to be more complicated than she assumed, forcing Erica to confront the consequences of her impulsive sense of justice.

The film moves between raunchy teen comedy and darker territory involving abuse, depression and family dysfunction, with the relationship between Erica and Luke at its centre.

Reviews were mixed. On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of about 48 percent; the consensus credits Deutch with bringing even a preposterously written character vividly to life, while finding the film's tonal shifts and treatment of its serious subject matter uneven.

The revolution ultimately leads to Dimitri being killed in an airstrike and Arkady being captured, ending the revolution. After several years, Arkady and his men believe that Dimitri has faked his death, so they torture a man for information on where Dimitri is hiding in London. Meanwhile, in London, former US military soldier Michael Knox visits his late best friend's house to attend the West Ham United football game with his niece, Danni. He had previously served in Afghanistan in an attack team alongside his best friend (who he explains "was like a brother") and was the only survivor of their last mission. Danni is grounded by her mother for delinquent behaviour, but Knox manages to fix the situation, and her mother gives her consent for Knox to take Danni to the football match.

Meanwhile, Arkady and his mercenaries covertly infiltrate the stadium, take over the control room, and initiate a lockdown of the entire stadium. Taking Superintendent Steve Thompson hostage, Arkady threatens Thompson into cooperating by threatening his family. Arkady then has his men blow up all transmission towers across the city to ensure that no communication will be made outside the stadium. Discovering Danni is missing from her seat, Knox seeks help from the cheeky stadium guard, Faisal Khan. Faisal reluctantly assists Knox to the control room. On their way, they run into one of Arkady's men posing as a guard near the lift, who ultimately attacks them, resulting in Knox killing him. Knox finds C-4 explosives in Andrei's jacket. He then uses the only working walkie-talkie to call the police about the situation, but Chief Commander Daniel Steed does not believe him and hangs up. After he kills two other men, Vlad and Anton, Knox brings the latter's body to a balcony and throws him down, smashing into concession stands and thereby summoning the police. Seeing this, Arkady and the other mercenaries infiltrate the news studio and kill the crew. Arkady forces a reporter to read a statement at gunpoint, demanding Dimitri's location, or they will blow up the stadium. As he finishes the statement, Arkady kills the reporter and two others on live television, which Danni's mum sees and prompts her to leave for the stadium. Steed is approached by Agent Cho, who explains that Dimitri fled Russia undercover, underwent plastic surgery, and was given amnesty in London. Cho says that he cannot meet the demands, as handing Dimitri to Arkady will plunge the entire Russian region into chaos, endangering millions. Arkady's team learns the background of Knox and Danni, and they decide to take Danni hostage.

title: Down a Dark Hall
tagline: Welcome to Blackwood. Where lost girls find their way.
overview: Kit, a troubled girl, is sent to the exclusive Blackwood boarding school, where she discovers that only four other female students have been admitted to learn the four pillars of knowledge under the ominous wing of the mysterious headmistress Madame Duret.
plot:
Kit Gordy, a difficult young girl, is sent to the mysterious Blackwood Boarding School after her delinquent behavior becomes too much for her school to handle. When she arrives at Blackwood, Kit meets eccentric headmistress Madame Duret and the school's only other students, four teenage girls with similar behavioral problems (Veronica, Ashley, Sierra, and Izzy). Technology is rarely used, and the girls can only phone their families in the domineering presence of the headmistress. The girls attend a variety of creative and intellectual classes, which begins to draw out unknown talents in them.
Sierra is the first to show a troubling obsession with her work, losing sleep, refusing to eat, and going into odd trances while creating amazing works of art. Ashley writes beautiful poetry and stories that deeply disturb her. Kit and Izzy slowly begin to experience the same bad side effects, saying it was like someone else was using their bodies. Only the belligerent Veronica shows no progress, much to Madame Duret's annoyance. During art class Kit notices that all of Sierra's paintings are signed "TC" and searches the school's library for answers. She realizes that Sierra is recreating paintings by the deceased artist Thomas Cole, and that the others are producing work from other dead geniuses.
Kit convinces Veronica to search the restricted areas of the school, where they come across old student records and more information on the people possessing the girls. When Madame Duret discovers Veronica alone she chains her up in an unused part of the school, explaining that the students are not merely vessels for the dead, but donors, unknowingly sacrificing themselves to be used to continue the careers of famous minds, whom she is able to commune with and channel into the girls' bodies. Kit calls the police and confronts the headmistress about everything. By now Sierra has already died from overwork, and Ashley jumps to her death to stop the possession taking over completely.
While struggling to free Veronica, Kit knocks over some candles, and fire quickly spreads throughout the old building. Izzy succumbs to the beauty of the flames, leaving only Kit and Veronica to escape. Madame Duret is eventually possessed by her former pupils and consumed by the fire. Kit passes out and meets her deceased father, who convinces her to stay and live. She wakes up in the back of an ambulance with her mother by her side.

plot:
Angel Has Fallen is a 2019 American action thriller film directed by Ric Roman Waugh and written by Jeff Nathanson. The movie stars Gerard Butler, Morgan Freeman, Jai Courtney, and Lance Reddick.

The story begins with Mike Banning (Gerard Butler), the former head of the Secret Service, who has retired to a quiet life in Virginia with his wife, Shannon (Molly R. Quinn). However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Shannon is kidnapped by a group of terrorists led by the ruthless and cunning assassin, Ortega (Lance Reddick).

As Mike frantically searches for his wife, he discovers that she has been taken to the White House, where President James Sawyer (Morgan Freeman) is hosting a high-profile event. The kidnappers demand that the President be killed in exchange for Shannon's safe return.

Mike soon realizes that Ortega is not just any ordinary terrorist but a former Secret Service agent who was thought to have been killed years ago. As Mike navigates the complex web of intrigue and deception, he must also confront his own demons and the personal costs of his past actions as a Secret Service agent.

As the story unfolds, Mike teams up with his old friend and fellow Secret Service agent, Tobin (Jai Courtney), to take down Ortega and rescue Shannon. Along the way, they encounter a range of characters, including a mysterious woman named Rachel (Pati Callahan) who may hold the key to unlocking the truth about Ortega's past.

As the plot thickens, Mike finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with Ortega, who will stop at nothing to achieve his goals. The action unfolds at breakneck speed, with Mike facing off against Ortega and his henchmen in a series of intense and suspenseful confrontations.

In the end, Mike is able to outsmart Ortega and rescue Shannon, but not before he suffers a serious injury that leaves him questioning his own mortality. As the movie concludes, Mike reflects on the personal costs of his actions as a Secret Service agent and the sacrifices he has made for his country.

Throughout the film, Gerard Butler delivers a strong performance as the rugged and charismatic Mike Banning, bringing depth and nuance to the character. Morgan Freeman provides a sense of gravitas and authority as the President, while Jai Courtney brings a youthful energy to the role of Tobin.

Overall, Angel Has Fallen is a tense and thrilling action movie that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats from start to finish. With its breakneck pace, intricate plot twists, and memorable performances, it's no wonder this film has become a fan favorite among action movie enthusiasts.

title: Mass
overview: Two couples meet for a painful and raw conversation in the aftermath of a violent tragedy.
plot:
Mass is a 2021 American drama film written and directed by Fran Kranz in his directorial debut. Reed Birney, Ann Dowd, Jason Isaacs and Martha Plimpton star as two couples who meet years after a school shooting in which the son of one couple killed the son of the other. Set almost entirely in one room, it premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 30, 2021, and was released by Bleecker Street on October 8, 2021.

Six years after a high school shooting, Jay and Gail Perry, whose son Evan was among those killed, agree to meet Richard and Linda, the parents of the teenage gunman, Hayden, who killed himself after the attack. Their meeting is arranged in a quiet back room of an Episcopal church, with a church worker nervously preparing the space. The couples have met before, during the legal proceedings that followed the shooting, when Jay and Gail spoke harshly to the other parents, and Jay has since become a public advocate for gun control.

After awkward small talk and memories of their sons as young children, the conversation turns to how the tragedy happened. Jay and Gail press for details of Hayden's upbringing beyond what the public already knows. Richard and Linda describe his growing depression after the family moved, his isolation, and the bullying he suffered, and they argue briefly over the influence of violent video games. While noting that schools and therapists failed to act on warning signs, they acknowledge their own guilt at not seeing what their son was becoming.

The talk grows heated. Jay and Gail admit they wanted Richard and Linda to suffer as much as the victims' families did. When the other couple reveal that Hayden had friends who were also bullied, one of whom had access to guns, Jay explodes, suggesting that Hayden was simply a psychopath, before breaking down as he describes how Evan died. Linda tells them about a notebook in which Hayden planned the attack, and explains that she and Richard held a funeral to mourn the boy they had loved before his crime.

When Linda asks to hear about Evan, Gail shares a happy memory of him at twelve and finally forgives Hayden and his parents, and the four hold hands in silence. As they leave, Linda returns to tell Gail how afraid she once was of Hayden. Jay is overcome by the sound of a choir rehearsing nearby. The film was acclaimed for its acting and writing, with 95% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and Dowd received a BAFTA nomination for Best Supporting Actress.

title: In the Fade
overview: Katja's life collapses after a senseless act impacts her. After a time of mourning and injustice, she seeks revenge.
plot:
In the Fade (German: Aus dem Nichts) is a 2017 German drama thriller written and directed by Fatih Akin. Diane Kruger stars as Katja Şekerci, a German woman whose Kurdish husband and young son are killed in a bombing carried out by neo-Nazis, with Denis Moschitto as her lawyer, Numan Acar as her husband, Johannes Krisch as the defense attorney and Ulrich Tukur. The film competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2017 Cannes Film Festival, where Kruger won the award for Best Actress, in her first major German-language role.

Nuri Şekerci, a Kurdish-German man who served time in prison for drug dealing and studied business while inside, now lives a happy life in Hamburg with his German wife, Katja, and their six-year-old son, Rocco, running a small office. One day Katja leaves Rocco with Nuri while she spends the afternoon with a friend. As she leaves, she warns a young blonde woman who has parked a new bicycle in front of the office that it might be stolen if she does not lock it. Returning that evening, Katja finds the street cordoned off: a nail bomb has exploded, killing Nuri and Rocco.

Katja tells the police about the woman with the bicycle and becomes convinced the attack was the work of neo-Nazis, but investigators focus on Nuri's past and possible links to drug traffickers. Overwhelmed by grief, Katja turns to drugs and attempts suicide, but she is stopped by news that suspects have been arrested: a young neo-Nazi couple, André and Edda Möller, whose own father reported his son to the police. The trial in the film's second part becomes a painful ordeal, as the defense attacks Katja's credibility because of her drug use and a Greek neo-Nazi provides the couple with an alibi. When the court acquits them for lack of evidence, Katja, abandoned by the justice system, follows the couple to Greece and contemplates taking justice into her own hands.

In the Fade received generally favorable reviews, with a 77 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus praised Kruger's ability to carry the film, though some felt it did not match her remarkable work. It won the Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film and was shortlisted for the Academy Award. The film was inspired in part by the murders committed by the National Socialist Underground in Germany.

title: Victoria & Abdul
tagline: History's most unlikely friendship.
overview: Queen Victoria strikes up an unlikely friendship with a young Indian clerk named Abdul Karim.
plot:
Abdul Karim, a young prison clerk from a Muslim, Urdu-speaking family in Agra, British India, is instructed to travel to Britain for Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee in 1888 to present her with a mohur, a gold coin that has been minted as a token of appreciation from British-ruled India.
The Queen, lonely and tired of her fawning courtiers, develops an interest in and then a friendship with Abdul. She spends time with him alone and gives him a bejewelled locket with her photograph. She promotes him to be her Munshi and asks him to teach her Urdu and the Quran. She in fact learns Urdu for 14 years. When Victoria discovers he is married, she has him bring his wife to England. His wife and his mother-in-law both wear black burqas, much to the consternation of the household—and the fascination of Victoria.
As Victoria's interest in India grows, she has the Durbar Room built at her Isle of Wight home of Osborne House for state functions. It is elaborately and intricately decorated, with a carpet from Agra, formal portraits of renowned Indians, a replica of the Peacock Throne and carvings by Bhai Ram Singh.
While Victoria treats Abdul as a son, his preferment is resented by her household and inner circle, including her son, Bertie, and the prime minister, Lord Salisbury. The household plots to undermine their relationship, hoping that Abdul will be sent home. When Victoria embarrasses herself by recounting Abdul's one-sided account of the Indian Rebellion of 1857 to the court, Victoria's faith and trust in him are shaken. She decides he must return to India, but soon changes her mind and asks him to stay.
The prime minister is adamant that the royal household must be rid of Abdul. They research his family background in India and present Victoria with a dossier showing that his family is more ordinary and poor than Abdul claimed. When Victoria insists that her doctor examine Abdul to learn why his wife has not become pregnant, he discovers that Abdul has gonorrhea. He expects the Queen will dismiss Abdul in disgust, but Victoria remains loyal to him, orders his medical treatment and admonishes her courtiers for plotting against him. She announces her intention to give Abdul a knighthood.
Eventually, the household decides that Victoria must break with Abdul. If not, they all will resign and have Victoria declared insane. When Victoria is told, she angrily summons her family and the entire household and demands that anyone who wishes to give up their place should step forward. When no-one does, she says she has decided against making Abdul a knight. She will instead include him in her next honours list as a Commander of the Royal Victorian Order.
When Victoria falls ill, she urges Abdul to return to India while she can still protect him and warns him that the court will turn on him after her death. Abdul insists that he will stay until her death.

title: Kill Switch
tagline: Worlds will collide
overview: A pilot battles to save his family and the planet after an experiment for unlimited energy goes wrong.
plot:
Kill Switch, also known as Redivider, is a 2017 science fiction film and the feature directorial debut of Tim Smit, from a screenplay by Charlie Kindinger and Omid Nooshin. Dan Stevens stars as Will Porter, a former NASA pilot turned physicist who is sent into a parallel world to undo the damage caused by tapping an unlimited source of quantum energy, and who must choose which of two Earths will survive. Bérénice Marlohe, Tygo Gernandt, Charity Wakefield, Bas Keijzer, Mike Libanon and Mike Reus co-star.

In the near future, Porter is recruited by Alterplex, a power company that has built an enormous tower drawing on limitless quantum energy. The energy comes from a mirror version of Earth known as "the Echo", which was never supposed to harbour life; a malfunction, however, created a true duplicate planet, populated and with a tower of its own. As the Alterplex tower siphons off its power, the Echo is plagued by strange gravitational anomalies and unexplained deaths, and the link between the worlds now threatens to destroy both within less than a day unless one of them is eliminated. Porter is dispatched into the Echo carrying a cube-shaped device called the Redivider, which he has been told will rebalance the flow of energy between the two universes and restore order. Once there, he discovers that the device is in fact a kill switch designed to annihilate the Echo, leaving him to decide which world must be sacrificed so the other can live. The Echo's armed forces are aware of his mission and hunt him, seeking to capture or kill him, while a band of anti-tower rebels wages its own war against the soldiers guarding the towers.

Stevens plays Porter, with Marlohe as Abigail Vos, Gernandt as Michael, Wakefield as Mia Porter, Gijs Scholten van Aschat as Reynard, Keijzer as Bektman, Libanon as Hugo and Reus as Dr. Klintsen. The casting of Stevens and Marlohe, with Smit directing, was announced in February 2016, and Aaron Ryder produced through FilmNation Entertainment; Don Diablo wrote, scored and performed the theme song, "Echoes". Saban Films acquired distribution rights in February 2017 and released the film theatrically on June 16, 2017, followed by a video-on-demand release from Lionsgate Home Entertainment on August 22. Critics were largely negative, giving it a 9% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31, and it earned only about $163,000 worldwide at the box office, with home video sales adding roughly $140,000.

title: Apostle
tagline: Your god can't help you.
overview: In 1905, a man travels to a remote island in search of his missing sister who has been kidnapped by a mysterious religious cult.
plot:
In 1905, Thomas Richardson travels to a remote Welsh island to rescue his sister, Jennifer, who has been kidnapped and held for ransom by a mysterious cult led by Malcolm Howe. Posing as a convert, Thomas encounters Howe, who founded the cult with two other convicts, Frank and Quinn. They claim that the barren island was rendered fertile through blood sacrifice. Thomas discovers Frank's son Jeremy and Quinn's daughter Ffion sneaking home after a tryst. He forces Jeremy to admit that Jennifer was kidnapped for ransom, as the cult does not have the resources to pay for the continuous animal sacrifices needed to maintain the island's fertility.
One of the newcomers attempts to assassinate Malcolm, but Thomas intervenes and is wounded. The same night, Malcolm parades Jennifer through the village, claiming she will be killed if her co-conspirator does not come forward. Thomas flees from an old woman who chases him, and escapes to a beach cave covered in markings, depicting a deity. Malcolm visits a barn where the old woman, who is in fact the island's deity, is imprisoned in tree roots; he reprimands her for appearing to Thomas before feeding her his blood, causing the vegetation imprisoning her to bloom. Thomas tells Malcolm's daughter Andrea that he was a Christian missionary who was persecuted in Beijing during the Boxer Rebellion for introducing Christianity to China, and lost his faith after his god failed to intervene. She takes him to a shack in a wheat field to hide.

title: Halloween
tagline: Face Your Fate.
overview: Laurie Strode comes to her final confrontation with Michael Myers, the masked figure who has haunted her since she narrowly escaped his killing spree on Halloween night four decades ago.
plot:
Halloween is a 2018 American slasher film directed by David Gordon Green, who co-wrote it with Jeff Fradley and Danny McBride. The eleventh installment in the Halloween series, it is a direct sequel to John Carpenter's 1978 original that disregards every other film in the franchise. Jamie Lee Curtis reprises her role as Laurie Strode, and James Jude Courtney plays Michael Myers, with Nick Castle returning to the role for a cameo; Judy Greer, Andi Matichak, Will Patton and Haluk Bilginer co-star.

On October 29, 2018, Michael, confined at Smith's Grove psychiatric hospital for four decades, is about to be transferred to another facility. True crime podcasters Aaron Korey and Dana Haines visit him. In Haddonfield, Laurie still lives in fear, drinking heavily inside her fortified house. Her daughter, Karen, was taken from her by the state at age twelve and remains estranged, while Laurie's granddaughter, Allyson, tries to stay close to her. On the night of October 30, the transfer bus crashes and Michael escapes. The next day he murders the podcasters at his sister Judith's grave, kills a mechanic for his overalls and recovers his mask.

That Halloween night, Allyson leaves a party after finding her boyfriend cheating; Michael kills her best friend. Laurie and Deputy Frank Hawkins, who arrested Michael in 1978, respond to the scene, and Laurie shoots Michael before he escapes. Karen and her husband, Ray, are taken to Laurie's house for protection. Hawkins subdues Michael and tries to kill him, but Michael's psychiatrist, Dr. Ranbir Sartain, who secretly arranged Michael's escape to study him in the wild, attacks Hawkins and drives toward Laurie's home with Michael and Allyson in the back seat. Michael wakes, kills Sartain, the officers guarding the house and Ray. In the final confrontation, he stabs Laurie and throws her from a balcony, but when he looks down her body has vanished, echoing their first encounter. Karen shoots him, and the three women trap him in the basement safe room and set the house on fire. A post-credits scene suggests Michael survived.

The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2018 and was released on October 19. It grossed $259.9 million worldwide. Critics responded favorably, with 79% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67, praising its return to basic but effective ingredients.

title: Bohemian Rhapsody

overview: Singer Freddie Mercury, guitarist Brian May, drummer Roger Taylor and bass guitarist John Deacon take the music world by storm when they form the rock 'n' roll band Queen in 1970. Hit songs become instant classics. When Mercury's increasingly wild lifestyle starts to spiral out of control, Queen soon faces its greatest challenge yet – finding a way to keep the band together amid the success and excess.
plot:
Bohemian Rhapsody is a biographical drama film that tells the story of the life of Queen's lead vocalist, Freddie Mercury. The film stars Rami Malek as Mercury and follows his journey from his early days as a musician to the band's rise to fame.

The film begins with Freddie Mercury (Rami Malek) growing up in Zanzibar, Tanzania, where he is born Farrokh Bulsara. He moves to India with his family at a young age and later attends art college in London, where he discovers his passion for music. Mercury forms a band called Ibex, which eventually becomes Queen.

The film then cuts to the early days of Queen, with Mercury meeting Brian May (Gwilym Lee) and Roger Taylor (Ben Hardy). The three musicians form a strong bond and begin to develop their unique sound. They are later joined by John Deacon (Joe Mazzello), who completes the classic lineup.

As Queen gains popularity, they start to tour and perform in front of large crowds. Mercury's charisma and stage presence quickly make him a fan favorite. The film depicts the band's struggles with fame, including their tumultuous relationship with their record label, EMI.

One of the most pivotal moments in the film is Queen's performance at Live Aid in 1985. The band takes the stage to perform "Bohemian Rhapsody," which becomes an instant classic. The film captures the energy and excitement of the event, as well as Mercury's emotional response to performing his iconic song.

Throughout the film, Malek delivers a critically acclaimed performance as Mercury, capturing the singer's flamboyant personality, wit, and vulnerability. The supporting cast, including Lucy Boynton as Mercury's girlfriend Mary Austin, also deliver strong performances.

As Queen's popularity continues to grow, Mercury becomes increasingly reclusive and struggles with his personal life. He is openly gay in a time when it was not widely accepted, which puts him at odds with his record label and the public.

The film's climax depicts Queen's performance at Live Aid, as well as their subsequent tour of Japan. The film ends with Mercury's final performance with Queen, which takes place on November 24, 1991, just months before his death from complications related to AIDS.

Overall, Bohemian Rhapsody is a triumphant and emotional tribute to Freddie Mercury's life and legacy. The film features stunning performances, impressive music sequences, and a gripping narrative that captures the highs and lows of Queen's incredible journey.

title: Sorry to Bother You

overview: In an alternate present-day version of Oakland, black telemarketer Cassius Green discovers a magical key to professional success – which propels him into a macabre universe.
plot:
In a dystopian near future, Cassius "Cash" Green and his artist girlfriend Detroit live in the garage of Cash's uncle Sergio. Struggling to pay rent, Cash gets a job as a telemarketer for RegalView. He struggles with customers until his older co-worker Langston teaches him how to use his "white voice" and adopt a blithe, affluent persona during calls, at which Cash excels.
Cash's co-worker Squeeze forms a union and recruits Cash, Detroit, and their friend Sal. When Cash participates in a protest, he expects to be fired but is instead promoted to an elite "Power Caller" position within the company. In the luxurious Power Caller suite, the lead Power Caller known as Mr. _______ tells Cash to always use his white voice. He learns that RegalView secretly sells military arms and cheap labor from the megacorporation WorryFree, through which employees sign lifetime contracts to work and be housed in factories, i.e. slave labor.
Though Cash is initially uncomfortable with the job, he is celebrated at work and can now afford a new apartment and a flashy car while paying off Sergio's house, keeping him from joining WorryFree in the process. Through his newfound success, he initially improves his relationship with Detroit and boosts his sex life significantly. He stops participating in the union push and Detroit quits her RegalView job to avoid conflicting loyalties between the two, while secretly participating in the Left Eye Faction, an anti-WorryFree activist group. She eventually breaks up with Cash, arguing that his immoral job has changed him, while he insists he has the right to be proud of his success.
As Cash is escorted through the union's picket line one morning, a picketer throws a can of soda at his head and injures him. Footage of the incident becomes a popular Internet meme, and even the woman who threw the can profits from it when she signs a sponsorship with the soda brand she threw. Cash attends Detroit's art exhibit and artistic performance uninvited, at which she uses a white voice of her own. He tries to stop the event, but that only motivates Detroit to kick him out, and she later has "everything but sex" with Squeeze.
Cash is invited to a debaucherous party with WorryFree CEO Steve Lift, where he is goaded into rapping for the predominantly white guests. Later, in a private meeting, Steve offers Cash a powdered substance which Cash snorts, believing it is cocaine. Cash looks for the bathroom but takes a wrong turn and discovers a shackled half-horse, half-human hybrid who begs him for help. Steve explains that WorryFree plans to make their workers stronger, more obedient, and more profitable by transforming them into human-horse "Equisapiens" through snorting a powder that modifies their DNA. Cash fears that he just ingested the substance, but Steve assures him it was cocaine. Cash refuses an offer of $100 million to become an Equisapien for five years to act as a false revolutionary figure to keep the employees in line.

plot:
Bumblebee is a 2018 American science fiction action film directed by Travis Knight and produced by Paramount Pictures. The movie takes place in 1987, during the height of the Transformers franchise's popularity.

The story begins with Charlie Watson (Hailee Steinfeld), a high school student who lives on the outskirts of a small town in California. Charlie is struggling to cope with her mother's death in a car accident and her father's absence due to his work as an oil rig worker. She spends most of her time alone, tinkering with cars and daydreaming about adventure.

One night, while out running from her troubles, Charlie stumbles upon a damaged Chevrolet Camaro that has crash-landed on the outskirts of town. As she approaches the car, it transforms into Bumblebee, an Autobot scout sent to Earth to protect its secrets from the Decepticons.

Initially, Charlie is frightened by the giant robot, but as she observes Bumblebee's behavior, she realizes that it is not a threat. Instead, she begins to form a bond with the Autobot, and they start to communicate through a series of beeps and chirps.

As Charlie spends more time with Bumblebee, she learns about its mission to find its long-lost friend, Jazz (Josh Duhamel), who has been captured by the Decepticons. The Autobots have sent Bumblebee to rescue Jazz, but it needs Charlie's help to navigate the human world and evade the Decepticon forces.

The plot thickens as Charlie becomes embroiled in a series of events that put her life at risk. She is pursued by the Decepticons, led by Shatter (Angus Macfadyen), who will stop at nothing to capture Bumblebee and exploit its advanced technology.

As Charlie and Bumblebee work together, they develop a strong bond, with Charlie learning about the Autobot's values of loyalty, friendship, and sacrifice. In return, Bumblebee learns about human emotions and experiences, which helps it to better understand its mission.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Charlie, Bumblebee, and the Decepticons. With the help of her father, who has been hiding a secret of his own, Charlie is able to outsmart the Decepticons and help Bumblebee rescue Jazz.

In the end, Charlie says goodbye to Bumblebee as it departs to continue its mission, but not before they share a heartfelt moment that leaves Charlie with a newfound sense of purpose and belonging. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest times, there is always the possibility for connection and redemption.

Overall, Bumblebee is a heartwarming and action-packed film that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and self-discovery. With its blend of humor, adventure, and sci-fi excitement, it has become a beloved entry in the Transformers franchise.

title: The Case for Christ
tagline: One man's journey to solve the biggest mystery of all times
overview: Based on the true story of an award-winning investigative journalist -- and avowed atheist -- who applies his well-honed journalistic and legal skills to disprove the newfound Christian faith of his wife... with unexpected, life-altering results.
plot:
In 1980, Lee Strobel is an atheist journalist and investigative reporter for the Chicago Tribune. He and his wife Leslie have a daughter named Alison and are expecting their second child. After getting a very special recognition, Lee and his family go out for dinner to celebrate, and Alison chokes on a piece of candy. One of the patrons, a nurse named Alfie, intervenes and saves Alison. She credits the event to God's will, which Leslie takes to heart.
Leslie and Alfie become friends and start attending a Christian church together. Irritated, Lee unsuccessfully tries to dissuade Leslie. Due to advice from his mentor, Lee sets out to find evidence that the resurrection of Jesus did not happen. Meanwhile, Leslie gives birth to a son, Kyle.
Lee starts gathering information and evidence. Next, he tries to prove that the witnesses were hypnotized, but a psychologist proves him wrong. Lee then tries to gather evidence that Jesus may have not actually died on the Cross, or was taken off, but again, a physician proves him wrong, saying Jesus had to have died on the Cross.
Meanwhile, Lee's estranged father tries to reconcile with him, but Lee brushes him off. His father dies soon after, and then Lee learns that his father truly loved him, which surprises Lee.
Simultaneously with Lee's pursuit to disprove the resurrection of Jesus, he is also investigating a case of the shooting of a police officer. At first, it looks like the convicted man is guilty and an informant for a gang, but Lee proves that the cop shot himself with a secret gun disguised as a pen, and the convict is freed.
Lee tries to get more evidence for his religious investigation, but his mentor explains that whether he chooses to believe or not believe, the last part of proving Jesus' real existence is faith. When a colleague gives him a speech, Lee decides to take the leap of faith and believe. When he tells Leslie about it, they have a happy reconciliation and pray together.

title: Show Dogs
tagline: Unleashed and undercover
overview: Max, a macho, solitary Rottweiler police dog is ordered to go undercover as a primped show dog in a prestigious Dog Show, along with his human partner, to avert a disaster from happening.
plot:
Show Dogs is a 2018 buddy cop comedy directed by Raja Gosnell from a screenplay by Max Botkin and Marc Hyman, mixing live action with talking animals. Filming began on November 28, 2016, at Pinewood Studio Wales in Great Britain, with further scenes shot on location in Las Vegas. The film was released in the United States on May 18, 2018, and reached DVD and Blu-ray that August.

Max, a tough Rottweiler serving as a police dog, tries to rescue Ling-Li, a baby giant panda that an animal smuggling ring is preparing to sell. In doing so he accidentally ruins an FBI sting run by his human partner, Frank, who blames the dog for letting the criminals escape. Forced to cooperate despite their mutual dislike, the two go undercover as a show dog and his handler at the prestigious Canini Invitational dog show in Las Vegas, hoping to unmask the smugglers from inside the competition.

Ludacris voices Max and Will Arnett plays Frank, with Natasha Lyonne as Mattie and Omar Chaparro as Señor Gabriel. The voice cast also includes Stanley Tucci as the Papillon Philippe, Jordin Sparks as Daisy, an Australian Shepherd, Gabriel Iglesias as the Pug Sprinkles, Shaquille O'Neal as the Komondor Karma, RuPaul as Persephone and Alan Cumming as Dante.

Reviews were negative. Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 16% approval rating and Metacritic a score of 31, although CinemaScore audiences awarded an A−. Christy Lemire gave it half a star, Peter Hartlaub gave it none, and Mark Kermode later named it the worst film of 2018, while The Hollywood Reporter was more forgiving of its self-aware script. Shortly after release, critics and parents' groups objected to a subplot in which Max must let a judge touch his genitals and is told to go to his "happy place", arguing that it normalized child grooming. Botkin said the script had been heavily rewritten by other writers, and the distributor Global Road Entertainment apologized, removed two scenes and sent a revised cut to theaters for the second weekend. The British Board of Film Classification considered the scene non-sexual and the US concerns a misinterpretation. Made for $5.5 million, the film grossed $40 million worldwide.

overview: After the tragic death of star volleyball player Caroline "Line" Found, a team of dispirited high school girls must band together under the guidance of their tough-love coach in hopes of winning the state championship!
plot:
Caroline "Line" Found is the star volleyball player on the Iowa City West High School volleyball team and well-loved by members of the community. With Line as the captain, the Trojans have been undefeated and everyone in the city has high hopes for them to win the championship against their long-time rival, City High. During a party at her house, Line sneaks off to visit her mother Ellyn, who is being treated for cancer in a hospital. Line is killed in a moped accident, leaving the entire community in mourning. At Line's wake, Ellyn insists on walking to her daughter's casket to pay her respects; Ellyn dies from cancer days after the wake, leaving her husband and Line's father Ernie grieving over the loss of his wife and his daughter.
The Trojans' coach, Kathy "Brez" Bresnahan, continues to hold volleyball practice. She asks Line's best friend, Kelley Fliehler, to return to the team, saying Line would have wanted them to continue. Kelley initially refuses, but Brez persuades her. The Trojans forfeited their most recent match and Kelley encourages the entire school to continue for Line.
West High struggles in practice and loses their first game badly, still discouraged by Line's death. Brez runs the team through grueling drills and names Kelley the new captain. Kelley initially struggles in the role, but improves as the weeks go by. The team begins to win and is motivated to win the state championship for Line. They need to win the fourteen remaining games to be eligible for the state championship, which they do.
Before the tournament begins, Kelley receives a gift from Line's father, that encourages her not just to play for Line, but to "Live Like Line". At West High, Kelley and boyfriend Alex paint the windows to read "Live Like Line". T-shirts with the catchphrase are given out to players, staff, and fans. The Trojans win the quarter-final game with ease, but struggle to win their semi-final game. They move on to the championship against City High, who are heavily favored to win. Before the game, Brez gives a tribute to Line, deciding not to have a moment of silence, but encourages the crowd to meet someone new, as Line always was kind to everyone. City takes the lead early, but West ties the score and forces the fifth and final set, which the Trojans win. As the crowd cheers, "Sweet Caroline" plays in honor of Line and Kelley holds Line's picture up high and proud.
During the closing credits, images, videos, and footage show the real life Caroline Found and her family, Kelley Fliehler, Kathy Bresnahan, and the Iowa West High volleyball team. On-screen subtitles show how Caroline Found's death inspired the real Iowa West High volleyball team to repeat their win for the 2011 Iowa State Championship. The Founds climbed Mount Monadnock. Over 4,000 students from across Iowa attended Line's funeral. Kathy "Brez" Bresnahan was voted National Coach of the Year for 2011; she retired from coaching in 2014 but remains in contact with the 2011 team.

title: Ghostbusters: Afterlife
tagline: Discover the past. Protect the future.
overview: When a single mom and her two kids arrive in a small town, they begin to discover their connection to the original Ghostbusters and the secret legacy their grandfather left behind.
plot:
Ghostbusters: Afterlife is a 2021 supernatural comedy film directed by Jason Reitman, written by Gil Kenan and Greg Russo, and produced by Ivan Reitman, Dan Aykroyd, and Chris Columbus. The movie serves as a direct sequel to the original Ghostbusters (1984) and Ghostbusters II (1989), ignoring the events of the 2016 reboot.

The story takes place in 2021, 30 years after the events of the first two films. We meet Callie Spengler (Carrie Coon), a single mother who lives on a farm with her son Trevor (Finn Wolfhard) and granddaughter Phoebe (Mckenna Grace). The family is struggling to cope with the loss of their father, Raymond Stantz (Dan Aykroyd), who was one of the original Ghostbusters.

One day, Callie receives an unexpected visit from a mysterious woman named Phoebe's grandmother, Janine Melnitz (Annie Potts), who reveals that she is Phoebe's mother and has been keeping her identity a secret. Janine informs Phoebe about her family's history as Ghostbusters and the reason for their disappearance.

As Phoebe begins to uncover the truth about her family's past, she discovers an old proton pack in the attic of her grandfather's house, which leads her on a journey to find the lost city of Stay Puft, where her father and his team were last seen. Along the way, she meets Trevor, who becomes her ally in uncovering the secrets of their family's legacy.

As they delve deeper into the mystery, Phoebe and Trevor encounter a new generation of Ghostbusters, led by Dr. Zoey Frankel (Mckenna Grace), who is determined to revive the original team's work. Together, they face off against a powerful entity known as Gozer, an ancient Sumerian deity that was defeated by the original Ghostbusters.

Throughout the film, Reitman pays homage to the original Ghostbusters while introducing new characters and themes. The movie explores the idea of legacy, family, and the power of tradition. The special effects are impressive, with a blend of practical and CGI elements that bring the supernatural world to life.

Overall, Ghostbusters: Afterlife is a heartwarming and entertaining film that honors the spirit of the original while introducing a new generation to the beloved franchise.
