title: Beach Rats
overview: An aimless teenager on the outer edges of Brooklyn struggles to escape his bleak home life and navigate questions of self-identity, as he balances his time between his delinquent friends, a potential new girlfriend, and older men he meets online.
plot:
Frankie is an aimless 19-year-old Brooklynite who spends his days hanging out and getting high with his macho friends as an escape from his troubled home life. His family includes his little sister and a mother who is mostly occupied with caring for his terminally ill father. At night, Frankie cruises Brooklyn Boys, a webcam site for gay men, but partially obscures his face with a hat.
When Frankie and his friends are at the Coney Island boardwalk watching fireworks, he catches the attentions of local girl Simone. Simone accompanies Frankie back to his place and tries to initiate sex with him, asking, "Am I pretty?" Frankie cannot perform and tries to make small talk instead, mocking and imitating her question. Insulted, Simone leaves. A few days later, Frankie and his friends are at the beach when they spot Simone with another guy. Frankie goes to apologize to Simone for his behavior the other night, and she tentatively forgives him. Meanwhile, Frankie uses the chat site to arrange hookups, particularly with older men as they are less likely to run into his friends and give away his double life. When a male partner asks about his penchant for older men, Frankie replies, "I don't really know what I like."
Frankie suffers a loss when his father succumbs to his terminal cancer. Frankie takes his father's pills, which he and his friends have been abusing. On a day out with Simone, Frankie casually asks her if she has ever made out with a girl. Simone replies she has, and makes an offhand comment that it is "hot" when girls make out, but when guys make out, it is "gay". That night, Frankie forces himself to have sex with her. Later, after a hookup with a gay man at a motel, Frankie is asked about his orientation. Frankie says he is not gay and reasons he has a girlfriend.
On a night out with his friends and Simone, they take drugs and party but when Frankie sees that the man from the motel works as a bartender he panics, he attempts to have sex with Simone but can't bring himself to do it and leaves her aggressively, he causes a fight on the dance floor and storms out. He meets up with an older man after. Much to his liking, when he gets home he is questioned by his mother for his behavior.
Frankie tries to apologize to Simone, who rejects him, telling him he needs to work on his personal issues and they stop seeing each other. Frankie runs into his friends on his way to meet with a guy his age named Jeremy. His friends, running out on their drug supply ask Frankie to come up with a plan and he tells them he uses a gay dating site to meet with men who have weed, his friends don't take him seriously but tag along with him when he tells them Jeremy is bringing weed with him. But when Jeremy meets them, he becomes wary of Frankie's crew and leaves. His friends insist that he finds another guy and they go back to Frankie's home, where he shows them the site and attempts to talk to men.

title: Lords of Chaos
tagline: Based on truth and lies
overview: A teenager's quest to launch Norwegian Black Metal in Oslo in the 1990s results in a very violent outcome.
plot:
Lords of Chaos is a 2018 biographical horror film directed by Jonas Åkerlund, who co-wrote the screenplay with Dennis Magnusson. Adapted from the 1998 book of the same name by Michael Moynihan and Didrik Søderlind, it offers a fictionalised account of the early 1990s Norwegian black metal scene, told from the perspective of guitarist Øystein "Euronymous" Aarseth, co-founder of the band Mayhem. Rory Culkin plays Euronymous, with Emory Cohen as Varg Vikernes, Jack Kilmer as Per "Dead" Ohlin, Sky Ferreira as Ann-Marit and Valter Skarsgård as the drummer Faust. Åkerlund was himself a former drummer of the Swedish band Bathory.

The story begins in 1984, when the young Euronymous forms Mayhem in Norway, recruiting bandmates and eventually the Swedish vocalist known as Dead. Dead's self-harm and macabre stage antics help build the band's extreme reputation. At one concert the group meets Kristian, a shy and awkward fan whom Euronymous initially treats with condescension, and Euronymous begins a relationship with Ann-Marit from the local metal community. When Dead takes his own life, Euronymous photographs the body rather than calling the police and turns the tragedy into part of the band's dark mythology.

Kristian reinvents himself as Varg Vikernes, the frontman of the one-man project Burzum, and gravitates toward Euronymous's record shop, Helvete, which becomes the centre of a small circle of musicians determined to prove they are the most extreme. What begins as provocative posturing escalates into real violence, including a series of church burnings and a murder, while a bitter rivalry develops between Euronymous, who cultivates an image he does not fully live up to, and the increasingly fanatical Varg. The conflict culminates in the 1993 killing of Euronymous.

The film presents its subjects as alienated young men caught up in their own myth-making, and it combines dark humour with brutally graphic depictions of violence, which drew criticism from some members of the real scene who disputed its accuracy.

Lords of Chaos premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in 2018. On Rotten Tomatoes about 73 percent of critics' reviews are positive, with the consensus describing it as a grimly compelling dramatisation of a music scene whose nihilistic aesthetic spilled over into real-life tragedy.

title: Fullmetal Alchemist
overview: Two alchemist brothers go on a quest for the Philosopher's Stone after an attempt to revive their dead mother goes horribly wrong.
plot:
Fullmetal Alchemist (Hagane no Renkinjutsushi) is a Japanese science fantasy action film of 2017 directed by Fumihiko Sori and adapted from Hiromu Arakawa's manga. Ryosuke Yamada stars as Edward Elric, with Atomu Mizuishi as his brother Alphonse, Tsubasa Honda as their friend Winry Rockbell, Dean Fujioka as Colonel Roy Mustang, Ryuta Sato as Maes Hughes and Yasuko Matsuyuki as Lust. Warner Bros. released it in Japan on 1 December 2017.

In the land of Amestris, Edward and Alphonse grow up in a rural town with their mother Trisha. When she dies of illness, the boys attempt the forbidden art of human transmutation to bring her back, and pay the price of equivalent exchange: Edward loses his left leg and Alphonse is pulled into the Gate of Truth. Edward gives up his right arm to recover his brother's soul and bind it to a suit of armor, and Winry's family fits him with automail prostheses. Recruited by Mustang, Edward becomes the youngest State Alchemist, the Fullmetal Alchemist, and the brothers begin searching for the legendary Philosopher's Stone that could restore their bodies.

Years later, Major General Hakuro introduces the teenage brothers to Shou Tucker, who earned his state license by creating a talking chimera. Tucker sends them to Dr. Tim Marcoh, a former stone-maker in hiding, who is killed by the assassin Lust. Returning to Tucker's home, the brothers discover that he has fused his little daughter Nina with the family dog to keep his credentials; they have him arrested, but not before he sows a bitter quarrel between them. Hughes finds something alarming in Marcoh's notes and is murdered by Lust's partner Envy.

Marcoh's research leads Edward to the secret Fifth Laboratory, where the now-deranged Tucker is holding Alphonse and Winry. There Edward learns that Philosopher's Stones are made from human lives and breaks down. Lust kills Tucker, revealing herself as a homunculus, and Hakuro, her ally, admits the military made stones from human captives; he unleashes an army of artificial Mannequin Soldiers powered by stones, which kill him. As the army destroys them, Mustang kills Lust and gives Edward the stone from her body, but the brothers refuse to use it to restore Alphonse. Instead Edward uses it to reach his brother's real body at the Gate of Truth and vows to find another way.

It was shot in Italy and Japan in 2016. Netflix released the film internationally in February 2018. Reviews were mixed, and two sequels followed in 2022.

title: Roma
tagline: There are periods in history that scar societies and moments in life that transform us as individuals.
overview: In 1970s Mexico City, two domestic workers help a mother of four while her husband is away for an extended period of time.
plot:
In 1970, Cleodegaria "Cleo" Gutiérrez is a Mixtec live-in maid in an upper-middle-class household in Mexico City's Colonia Roma neighborhood. The household consists of the mother, Sofía; the father, Antonio; their four school-aged children, Pepe, Sofi, Toño and Paco; and Sofía's mother, Teresa. Antonio, a medical doctor, often leaves for business conferences, but Sofía's distressed reactions to his absences suggest he is having an extramarital affair.
Meanwhile, Cleo believes she might be pregnant. She tells her boyfriend, Fermín, who pretends to be supportive but immediately abandons her at a movie theatre. She nervously reveals her news to Sofía, who provides emotional comfort and takes her to the hospital, confirming her pregnancy. Sofía then takes Cleo and the children to a family friend's hacienda for New Year celebrations. Recent tensions over land in the area arise, and a large forest fire erupts that the partygoers help extinguish.
Back in the city, Cleo sees Antonio and a young woman flirting on the street. She looks for Fermín, traveling to an impoverished district on the edge of the city, where she finds him training at a military-style camp run by Professor Zovek. Fermín denies that her baby is his, threatening to beat Cleo and their child if she talks to him again.

Cleo returns to the city, and the increasingly distraught Sofía tries unsuccessfully to conceal her husband's infidelity from their children. With the baby almost due, Teresa takes Cleo shopping for a crib downtown. Suddenly a student protest outside the store turns into the Corpus Christi massacre of 10 June 1971 as a paramilitary group, Los Halcones ("the Falcons"), attacks the protesters. The militants chase a student into the store and murder him. Fermín, appearing as one of Los Halcones, points a gun at Cleo and Teresa before wordlessly exiting. Then Cleo's water breaks. The violence in the streets slows traffic and her attempt to get to the hospital. When she arrives, Antonio briefly appears, reassures her, then makes an excuse to leave. She cries in agony as her baby girl is delivered stillborn.
Later, Sofía takes Cleo and the children on a family outing to the beaches at Tuxpan. Sofía tells her children that she and their father are separating and that the outing is giving him time to collect his belongings from their home. At the beach, a strong current almost drowns Sofi and Paco, but Cleo wades in and saves them, despite not knowing how to swim. Sofía and the children affirm their love for Cleo, all of them holding each other and crying, while Cleo confesses that she did not want her baby to be born. The group returns home to find the house reorganized, and Cleo prepares a load of clothes for washing.

title: The Nutcracker and the Four Realms
original_title: The Nutcracker and the Four Realms
tagline: Let the mystery unfold.
overview: When Clara’s mother leaves her a mysterious gift, she embarks on a journey to four secret realms—where she discovers her greatest strength could change the world.
plot:
The Nutcracker and the Four Realms is a 2018 American Christmas fantasy film directed by Lasse Hallström and Joe Johnston from a screenplay by Ashleigh Powell, retelling E. T. A. Hoffmann's 1816 tale The Nutcracker and the Mouse King and Tchaikovsky's 1892 ballet. It stars Mackenzie Foy as Clara Stahlbaum, Keira Knightley as the Sugar Plum Fairy, Jayden Fowora-Knight as Captain Philip Hoffman, Helen Mirren as Mother Ginger and Morgan Freeman as Drosselmeyer, with Eugenio Derbez, Matthew Macfadyen, Richard E. Grant and Misty Copeland. Johnston directed a month of reshoots after Hallström's principal photography at Pinewood Studios.

On Christmas Eve in Victorian London, Clara receives a locked egg-shaped box left to her by her late mother, Marie, with a note saying that everything she needs is inside. At the party of her godfather, the engineer Drosselmeyer, she follows a string bearing her name into a parallel world, where a mouse steals the key. With the help of Captain Philip, a nutcracker soldier, she reaches a palace and meets the regents of three realms: the Sugar Plum Fairy of the Land of Sweets, Shiver of the Land of Snowflakes and Hawthorne of the Land of Flowers, who say they are at war with Mother Ginger and the Fourth Realm. Clara learns that Marie created this world and was its queen, making Clara a princess, and that a machine Marie used to bring toys to life could defend the realms if activated with the key.

Clara and Philip retrieve the key from Mother Ginger, ignoring her warning, but the egg turns out to be a music box. The Sugar Plum Fairy then reveals her treachery: resentful at feeling abandoned by Marie, she uses the machine to create an army of toy soldiers to conquer all four realms and imprisons Clara and her allies. Finding a mirror inside the music box, Clara realizes she needed only herself. She escapes, wins Mother Ginger's help and reverses the machine, turning the Sugar Plum Fairy back into a doll. Clara returns to London, reconciles with her father and dances with him to the music box, which plays the first song he and Marie danced to.

Released by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures in November 2018, the film grossed $174 million worldwide but was a box office flop, with an estimated loss of $75-90 million. Critics found it lovely to look at but hollow, and it received 32% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Domestics
tagline: In the end, defend.
overview: A young husband and wife must fight to return home in a post-apocalyptic mid-western landscape ravaged by gangs.
plot:
The US Government conducts a catastrophic chemical weapons attack on the American populace to "reset" society. The surviving population of America divides into two groups. The Gangs, who name themselves Gamblers, Sheets, Plowboys, Nailers, and Cherries, control territory. The Domestics are unaffiliated with the Gangs and wish to live in peace rather than give in to violence. The story is interspersed with snippets from a talk show by DJ Crazy Al, who provides updates and commentaries about America.
Married couple Mark and Nina West, whose divorce was put on hold because of society's breakdown, travel to Nina's parents in Milwaukee. They rest in an abandoned house along the way, catching the attention of some Nailers. Two break in, prompting Mark to kill them. Later, while scavenging for supplies at a store, they are met by Nathan Wood and his son Steven, who save them from a group of pursuing Nailers. Nathan invites Mark and Nina to his home to meet his family for a meal. They accept, and encounter members of the Plowboys along the way. During the meal, Nathan tells Mark about a rumored new gang consisting of children.
The conversation takes a turn for the worse when Nathan informs Mark that they had eaten human flesh. A Nailer from the prior home invasion, having survived and followed them, holds Nathan's daughter hostage and demands a trade for Mark and Nina. Steven ambushes the Nailer and chaos ensues. Nina and Mark flee, leaving Nathan's family behind, where the Nailer kills Nathan's wife and daughter. Nathan kills the Nailer but swears revenge on the Wests. He calls his Plowboy contacts on his CB Radio. As they drive away, Mark and Nina get into a heated argument before Nina is shot and passes out.
The couple reach an abandoned house, unwittingly followed by Betsy, a deserter Cherry who is fascinated by Nina. Betsy had earlier killed her way out of the Plowboys' captivity. After treating Nina's wound, Mark looks for supplies in another house. When Nina awakens, she removes her wedding ring and contemplates leaving before finding Mark's notes pleading her to give their relationship another chance. She then finds a box of records and a bottle of alcohol, puts on her favorite Heavy Metal record and begins dancing.
Mark encounters William Cunningham, a flamboyant madman. He discovers William has captured Nathan and Steven, who has caught up to them. William holds him at gunpoint and forces him to fight a large slave. While fighting, Mark is thrown into William, and takes the opportunity to kill him then free the slave. Nathan decides to forgive Mark and depart with Steven, ending his quest for vengeance.

title: UFO
tagline: Sightings are never a coincidence. The cover-up ends here.
overview: A college student, who sees a UFO, uses his exceptional math skills to investigate the sighting with his friends while the FBI follows closely behind.
plot:
UFO is a 2018 American science fiction film written and directed by Ryan Eslinger. Alex Sharp stars as a gifted mathematics student determined to prove that an alien craft has visited Earth, with Gillian Anderson as his professor, David Strathairn as a federal official, and Ella Purnell. Unusually for the genre, its story turns on mathematics and physics rather than spectacle. Sony released it directly to video on September 4, 2018, promoting it with a trailer on UFO Day.

Derek Echevaro, a student at the University of Cincinnati, has been haunted since childhood by what he believes was a UFO sighting. In 2017 an unidentified object briefly hovers over Cincinnati's international airport, disrupting air traffic control radio. The authorities first describe it as a drone and later as a Gulfstream jet, but Derek's calculations prove both explanations impossible. Analysing the interference, he finds that it encodes the fine-structure constant, a fundamental number of physics, broken into chunks of digits.

When a mysterious program starts running on his computer, Derek reformats the signal into binary, and his obsession increasingly strains his relationships with his friends and roommates, Lee and Natalie. His work comes to the attention of Franklin Ahls, a senior official of a secret FBI committee on aerial phenomena, who is leading a team of scientists in Ohio trying to cover up the incident and decode the signal, which he believes comes from an advanced civilisation.

Sensing that time is short, Derek asks his professor, Dr. Rebecca Hendricks, for help. Sceptical at first, she joins him in analysing mobile phone disruptions recorded during the incident, but they realise that a unit of measurement is missing from their calculations. During a lecture on eigenvalues, Hendricks realises that the missing unit is 21 centimetres, the wavelength of radiation emitted by neutral hydrogen, which allows the signal to be read as coordinates.

Borrowing Lee's car, Derek drives to the location and briefly sees the craft, which sends out a new signal before vanishing. He is seized by armed agents and taken to Ahls, who confirms that the visitors used the fine-structure constant to establish a shared mathematical language and that the new message, more complex, appears to describe their location in three dimensions. Ahls confirms that humanity is not alone and invites Derek to help refine the calculations. Reviews were muted, Starburst giving it five out of ten.

title: Rampage
tagline: Big meets bigger
overview: Primatologist Davis Okoye shares an unshakable bond with George, the extraordinarily intelligent, silverback gorilla who has been in his care since birth.  But a rogue genetic experiment gone awry mutates this gentle ape into a raging creature of enormous size.  To make matters worse, it’s soon discovered there are other similarly altered animals.  As these newly created alpha predators tear across North America, destroying everything in their path, Okoye teams with a discredited genetic engineer to secure an antidote, fighting his way through an ever-changing battlefield, not only to halt a global catastrophe but to save the fearsome creature that was once his friend.
plot:
Rampage is a 2018 science fiction monster film directed by Brad Peeters and written by Ryan Condal. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Naomie Harris, Malin Åkerman, Jake Lacy, and Jeffrey Dean Morgan.

The story begins with Davis Okoye (Dwayne Johnson), a primatologist who works at the San Diego Zoo. He is particularly close to his genetically engineered gorilla, George, whom he has raised since childhood. However, their peaceful life is disrupted when a biotech company called UAC (United Animal Corporation) announces its plans to create genetically modified super-soldiers using DNA from various animals.

The CEO of UAC, Robert K. Ross (Jeffrey Dean Morgan), reveals that the company's goal is to create an army of super-intelligent and powerful creatures to fight in a war against China. The plan involves injecting DNA from different species into various animals, making them stronger and more aggressive.

As the story unfolds, Davis discovers that UAC has been secretly experimenting on his gorilla, George, without his knowledge or consent. When he confronts Ross, he is met with hostility and eventually loses control of George, who escapes and wreaks havoc on San Diego.

Meanwhile, a genetically modified wolf named Ruby (Naomie Harris) and an elephant named Ralph (Jake Lacy) also escape from UAC's facility. The three creatures, including George, begin to terrorize the city, causing destruction and chaos.

As Davis tries to find a way to stop his creations, he teams up with Dr. Kate Caldwell (Malin Åkerman), a geneticist who helped create the super-soldiers. Together, they embark on a mission to find a cure for George's DNA and prevent further destruction.

Throughout the movie, Davis struggles with his feelings of guilt and responsibility towards George, whom he considers a friend. He also grapples with the consequences of playing God and creating life forms that are beyond human control.

As the story reaches its climax, Davis and Kate devise a plan to use a virus to reverse the effects of the DNA injection on George and the other creatures. In the final battle, Davis confronts Ross and his team, who have been using the super-soldiers for their own gain.

In the end, Davis is able to stop George and the other creatures from causing further destruction, but not before they wreak havoc on San Diego. The movie concludes with Davis reflecting on the consequences of his actions and the importance of responsible scientific research.

Overall, Rampage is an action-packed monster film that explores themes of responsibility, friendship, and the dangers of playing God. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a cult classic among fans of science fiction and monster movies.

title: Iron Mask
overview: Commissioned to map the Far East territories of the Russian Empire, cartographer Jonathan Green sets off on a long journey of unbelievable adventures—making breath-taking discoveries and meeting mysterious creatures, Chinese princesses, deadly masters of oriental martial arts, and even the King of Dragons.
plot:
Iron Mask, released in Russia as Тайна печати дракона (The Mystery of the Dragon Seal) and in China as 龙牌之谜, and also known as Viy 2: Journey to China, is a fantasy adventure of 2019 directed by Oleg Stepchenko, sequel to the 2014 film Viy. Jason Flemyng returns as the English cartographer Jonathan Green and Charles Dance as Lord Dudley, joined by Jackie Chan as the White Wizard Master Et Al, Arnold Schwarzenegger as James Hook, the warden of the Tower of London, Helen Yao as his daughter Chen-Lan, Anna Churina as Jonathan's beloved Emma and Rutger Hauer as an ambassador.

In ancient China, White Wizards guard a magical dragon whose eyelashes yield a tea that cures any illness. Some turn greedy, becoming Black Wizards who stop trimming the lashes to harvest more tea, sending the dragon into a deep sleep. Et Al is exiled to the Tower of London, and his daughter Chen-Lan to a Russian prison. There she meets Jonathan, jailed because Tsar Peter the Great, who commissioned his last map, has been replaced by an impostor while the real tsar is held in the Tower alongside Et Al. Released through family influence but sent to map Russia's Far East so that he cannot expose the fraud, Jonathan takes Chen-Lan along as his assistant, mistaking her for a boy, and she agrees to guide him to China.

In London, Peter and Et Al alert Emma to their presence through one of Jonathan's letters and stage an escape; Et Al stays behind to fight Hook, giving Peter a magical medallion to lead him to his daughter, and Peter and Emma stow away on a ship bound for China. At the dragon's tower, Jonathan finds the Black Wizards' leader, a two-faced queen who has taken Chen-Lan's appearance, oppressing the townspeople and faking control of the dragon with tricks. Jonathan is caught spying, and he and Emma are about to be executed when Cossack allies wreck the queen's mechanical dragon. Chen-Lan revives the real dragon and duels the queen, who falls to her death once Jonathan sees through her disguise. Chen-Lan takes the throne, and Et Al, pardoned, travels to China with Hook.

Shot in 2015-2017 and delayed by censorship approval, the film opened in China on 16 August 2019. It was panned, scoring 22% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Schwarzenegger received a Golden Raspberry nomination for Worst Supporting Actor.

title: Mortal Engines
tagline: Some scars never heal
overview: Many thousands of years in the future, Earth’s cities roam the globe on huge wheels, devouring each other in a struggle for ever diminishing resources. On one of these massive traction cities, the old London, Tom Natsworthy has an unexpected encounter with a mysterious young woman from the wastelands who will change the course of his life forever.
plot:
Mortal Engines is a 2018 science fantasy adventure film directed by Christian Rivers and written by Fran Walsh, Philippa Boyens, and Peter Jackson. The movie is set in a post-apocalyptic world where cities are on wheels and roam the land, preying on smaller towns to sustain themselves.

In the year 2256, London is one of the largest and most powerful mobile cities, known as Cogtopolis. The city is ruled by the tyrannical Mayor, who controls its citizens through a complex system of gears and machinery. The story follows Hester Shaw (Hera Hilmar), a young woman with a prosthetic leg, who seeks revenge against the man responsible for her father's death.

Hester's father was killed by the leader of the city, Thaddeus Valentine (Robert Sheehan), who is also the inventor of the "mangler" - a machine that can crush and devour smaller cities. Hester sets out on a perilous journey to find Valentine, accompanied by her friend Anubis (Jorge Lendeborg Jr.), a skilled engineer.

As they travel across the land, they encounter other mobile cities, including New London, which is ruled by the ruthless Mayor of London, and the nomadic tribes that live outside the city walls. The group also meets Shangdu, a Chinese city that has been destroyed by Valentine's mangler.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Hester and Anubis discover that Valentine is planning to destroy all the smaller cities in order to create a new world order. They must use their skills and ingenuity to stop him and save the world from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the action unfolds at a breakneck pace, with thrilling chases and battles between the mobile cities. The special effects are impressive, bringing the post-apocalyptic world to life in stunning detail.

One of the standout aspects of Mortal Engines is its unique world-building. The concept of mobile cities roaming the land is both fascinating and terrifying, and the movie does an excellent job of exploring the consequences of such a society. The characters are also well-developed, with Hester being a particularly compelling protagonist.

The ending of the movie sets up a potential sequel, as Hester and Anubis face off against Valentine in a final showdown. However, the conclusion is bittersweet, leaving some questions unanswered and setting the stage for further adventures in this richly imagined world.

Overall, Mortal Engines is an exciting and visually stunning film that will appeal to fans of science fiction and adventure movies. With its unique world-building and compelling characters, it's a must-see for anyone looking for a thrilling ride.

title: Napping Princess
original_title: ひるね姫 ～知らないワタシの物語～
tagline: There's a reason why I can see in dreams
overview: Japan, 2020, a few days before the opening of the Tokyo Olympics. Although she should be studying for her final exams, Kokone, a schoolgirl who lives in a small town with her widowed father, a mysterious and talented mechanic, falls asleep often, anywhere, anytime, entering, over and over, a dream-world where a squad of fantastic motorized contraptions fights against magic, a world close to reality where she will find out the keys of her true past.
plot:
In a near-future Japan, Kokone Morikawa has strange dreams of the fantastical realm called Heartland while taking naps. In these dreams, Heartland is a society entirely revolving around cars; the King's castle is a car factory, and his subjects all come to it to make a constant stream of new cars. His daughter, Ancien (who appears as a younger Kokone), has a "magic tablet" computer she uses to give life to various machines: notably, a blue toy dog named Joy, and a motorcycle named Heart. The king disapproves of Ancien bringing Heart to life, however, and confiscates her tablet and Heart and orders Ancien to be confined to her tower. Additionally, the society of Heartland is under threat from a gigantic monster of molten metal called the Colossus. The king builds giant robots to face the Colossus. Ancien, spying a motorcycle-driving subject of the king's named Peach, decides to ally with him and seek to defeat the Colossus together with him, while the king's chief adviser Bewan plots against the king and Ancien alike.
In normal Japan, Kokone is finishing up her school term, considering where to go to college, and reconnecting with old friend Morio who has returned from Tokyo from his first year in college. Kokone lives with her single father Momotarō; her mother perished in an accident while Kokone was still young, and Kokone complains that her father never told her much about her mother. Momotarō is an eccentric car mechanic and has a jacket similar to Peach's, a blue stuffed dog, a motorcycle, and a cracked tablet, all similar to the ones seen in Kokone's dreams. The situation takes a turn for the worse when Momotarō is unceremoniously arrested three days prior to the 2020 Tokyo Olympics and accused of stealing the car company Shijima Motors' secrets. A suited figure who looks identical to the Heartland king's evil adviser visits the Morikawa home, and is overheard to be searching for both the tablet and Kokone. Via text message from jail, Momotarō warns his daughter not to trust the adviser, who is named Watanabe. The message includes a picture of a younger Momotarō, his wife, and Watanabe. With Morio's help, Kokone evades Watanabe and his men and recovers the stolen tablet and bear doll, driving away in the family's motorcycle. They also discover a business card for Isshin Shijima, the chairman of Shijima Motors, and consider visiting him for help after Kokone is told that her mother, Ikumi, was the daughter of the chairman. The two take a nap in the motorcycle, visit Heartland where they dream of the motorcycle soaring through the sky, and are surprised to find on waking up that the motorcycle has driven itself to Osaka overnight before running out of gas. Kokone's attempts to contact her father via the tablet seemingly fail, but surprisingly enough, the "magic" seems to work in the real world when a request to the tablet's e-Heart chat for train tickets results in an attendant giving them paid-for Shinkansen tickets to Tokyo.

title: A Ghost Story
tagline: It's all about time.
overview: Recently deceased, a white-sheeted ghost returns to his suburban home to console his bereft wife, only to find that in his spectral state he has become unstuck in time, forced to watch passively as the life he knew and the woman he loves slowly slip away.
plot:
A Ghost Story is an American supernatural drama of 2017 written and directed by David Lowery, following a man who dies and lingers as a ghost in the house he shared with his wife. Casey Affleck plays the husband, C, who spends most of the film beneath a white sheet, with Rooney Mara as his wife M and Will Oldham as a party guest credited as the Prognosticator.

M tells C, a musician, that as a child she moved often and used to hide little notes in every home she left. C resists her wish to move and on the night he finally gives in they are woken by a loud bang they cannot explain. Soon after, C is killed in a car crash . At the hospital M draws a sheet over his body and leaves; C rises as a ghost, still draped in the sheet and invisible to the living. Ignoring a doorway of light, he walks home. There he watches M grieve, eating a whole pie until she is sick, and slowly move on. In the house next door he notices another sheeted ghost which says it is waiting for someone but can no longer remember who. When M starts seeing another man, C makes books tumble from a shelf, one falling open at Virginia Woolf's story "A Haunted House". Before she moves out, M writes a note, tucks it into a crack in the woodwork and paints over it, and C tries to scratch it free.

Time slips past. A Spanish-speaking mother and her two children move in, and C drives them out by smashing a photograph and dishes. At a party held by later tenants, a man holds forth on the futility of creative effort since the universe will end. The house falls derelict and is bulldozed before C can reach the note; the neighbouring ghost decides that its loved ones are not coming and vanishes from beneath its sheet. A skyscraper rises on the site, and C leaps from its balcony into a futuristic city, only to land on the same spot in the nineteenth century, where pioneers begin building a home; its youngest child hides a note under a rock while humming C's song before the family is killed. Back in the house, C watches himself and M arrive, reliving their life until he causes the mysterious bang himself by slumping onto the piano. After his earlier ghostly self watches M leave for the last time, C finally prises out her note, reads it, and vanishes, his empty sheet dropping to the floor.

Premiering at the Sundance Film Festival and released by A24 in July 2017, the film earned just under $2 million worldwide but was widely acclaimed, with 91% on Rotten Tomatoes, winning three prizes at Deauville.

title: Wonder Wheel
tagline: Come along for the ride.
overview: The story of four characters whose lives intertwine amid the hustle and bustle of the Coney Island amusement park in the 1950s: Ginny, an emotionally volatile former actress now working as a waitress in a clam house; Humpty, Ginny’s rough-hewn carousel operator husband; Mickey, a handsome young lifeguard who dreams of becoming a playwright; and Carolina, Humpty’s long-estranged daughter, who is now hiding out from gangsters at her father’s apartment.
plot:
Wonder Wheel is an American period drama of 2017 written and directed by Woody Allen, set on Coney Island in the early 1950s. Kate Winslet stars as Ginny Rannell, a former actress working as a waitress, with Jim Belushi as her husband Humpty, a recovering alcoholic who runs the carousel, Juno Temple as his daughter Carolina, Justin Timberlake as the lifeguard and narrator Mickey Rubin and Tony Sirico and Steve Schirripa as the gangsters Angelo and Nick.

Mickey, an aspiring playwright, narrates to the audience. Carolina turns up on the boardwalk looking for her stepmother Ginny, who works at a clam bar, and asks to move in. Humpty had disowned her for marrying Frank, a mobster, but she explains that she has testified to the FBI about mob activity and believes Frank wants her dead. Humpty lets her stay if she saves for college, and Ginny gets her a waitressing job. When the gangsters come asking, the couple deny seeing her.

Ginny, whose own infidelity ended her happy first marriage, is miserable with the loud-mouthed Humpty and with life on the boardwalk, and her son Richie keeps setting fires. She begins an affair with Mickey, who is drawn to her maturity and sees her as someone to rescue. Humpty, softened by his daughter's presence, pays for her night classes. When Mickey happens to meet Carolina, he is captivated by her story and becomes torn between the two women. Ginny steals to buy Mickey an expensive watch, which he refuses, and grows jealous of his interest in Carolina. Carolina's unsuspecting boss tells the gangsters she has gone to a Brooklyn pizzeria with Mickey. Ginny phones the restaurant to warn her but, seeing a chance to be rid of her rival, hangs up without speaking. That night Mickey confesses his feelings and his affair, and Carolina walks off alone, followed by the mobsters' car. She never comes home. Discovering that Ginny made the silent call, Mickey confronts her; drinking and dressed in one of her old stage costumes, she holds out a knife and begs him to kill her, but he walks away. Humpty, drinking again after the police find no trace of his daughter, tells Ginny he needs her, but she coldly refuses his invitation to join a fishing trip with his friends' wives.

title: A Fantastic Woman
tagline: My name is Marina Vidal. Do you have any problem with that?
overview: Marina's life is thrown into turmoil following the death of her partner. Mourning the loss of the man she loved, she finds herself under intense scrutiny from those with no regard for her privacy.
plot:
Marina is a young trans woman living in Santiago, Chile. She works as a singer and a waitress and is in a relationship with an older man named Orlando. They have recently moved in together, and on Marina's birthday, Orlando gives her a note promising tickets to a famous resort as a gift. However, Orlando wakes up in the middle of the night feeling unwell and stumbles down a flight of stairs. Marina takes him to the hospital, but he dies of a brain aneurysm.
Marina contacts Orlando's brother, Gabo, and is later picked up by the police. The officers call her 'sir' after checking her old ID card and demand an explanation for her sudden departure from the hospital. Gabo arrives and speaks to Marina with enough familiarity to convince the police of her innocence. He lets her take Orlando's car home.
Orlando's ex-wife, Sonia, contacts Marina to arrange a time for her to drop off Orlando's car. While working, Marina is visited by a detective named Adriana, who works on cases that include sexual assault. Adriana suggests that Orlando was paying Marina as a sex worker rather than the two dating. She also thinks Marina may have caused Orlando's bruises while defending herself from a violent encounter. The detective tells Marina she will be waiting to meet with her after work-- she does not go.
Marina returns home, where she is comforted by Orlando's dog, Diabla. Orlando's son, Bruno, arrives the next morning and harasses Marina with personal questions. Marina takes the car to be washed and "sees" Orlando, which disturbs her. She then meets Sonia in a car park and hands over the car. Sonia becomes upset and asks Marina to hand over the flat as soon as possible. She tells Marina not to go to the funeral.
She goes to meet detective Adriana who insists a physical exam must be performed because Marina did not meet with her after work the day prior. When Marina tries to refuse the exam, the detective warns that doing so will result in an investigation being opened against her. She is forced to be photographed nude to check for any signs of bruising or injury.
Gabo calls Marina and tells her that Orlando will be cremated, and he wants her to have some of the ashes. Marina prepares to move out of Orlando's apartment and discovers Bruno has taken Diabla.
Wanda, her sister, and Gastón, Wanda's partner, warn her to let it go, but she decides to attend the wake. Upon her arrival, Sonia demands that Marina leave, and Gabo follows her out and apologizes. Later, Bruno and his friends accost and kidnap Marina, threatening her and wrapping her face in scotch tape before leaving her in an alleyway. Marina then walks to a gay club where she meets a man and later hallucinates seeing Orlando. Later she spends the night with Wanda and Gastón.
She decides to visit a sauna where Orlando had left a numbered key. She nervously enters the sauna and books in before locating the lockers and opening Orlando's, only to find it empty.

title: Vox Lux
tagline: A twenty-first century portrait.
overview: In 1999, teenage sisters Celeste and Eleanor survive a seismic, violent tragedy. The sisters compose and perform a song about their experience, making something lovely and cathartic out of a catastrophe - while also catapulting Celeste to stardom. By 2017, Celeste is a mother to a teenage daughter of her own and is struggling to navigate a career fraught with scandals when another act of terrifying violence demands her attention.
plot:
In early January 2000, a boy named Cullen Active walks into his school in the Staten Island neighborhood of New Brighton, goes to an 8th grade class and shoots the teacher, Mrs. Dwyer. One student, 13-year-old Celeste Montgomery, calmly and compassionately talks to Cullen and offers to pray with him. However, he shoots all the students and kills himself; Celeste is later seen to be in one of only three ambulances carrying survivors from the scene.

As she slowly recovers from her injuries, Celeste and her older sister, Eleanor, write music together. Soon afterward, at an event led by Father Cliff in memory of the shooting victims, Celeste sings a song that she and Eleanor wrote titled "Wrapped Up". The song becomes an instant hit and Celeste is soon picked up by a manager.
By April 2000, Celeste is recording an EP in New York City. Over the next 20 months, Celeste manages and navigates the increasing pressures of her newfound fame. She and Eleanor indulge in bouts of partying that soon get in the way of Celeste's work. Celeste is subjected to sexual misconduct by an older musician and Eleanor has sex with Celeste's manager the night before the September 11 attacks. Nevertheless, Celeste continues to successfully rise in the music industry; her songs are quickly picked up on radio stations and demand grows for her first music video, "Hologram (Smoke and Mirrors)".

In 2017, a terrorist shooting on a beach in Croatia is rumored to be linked to Celeste's music due to the masks worn by the criminals, which are similar to the masks from Celeste's 2001 "Hologram" video.
Celeste is now 31 years old and preparing for the first night of a concert tour for her sixth album, Vox Lux. Her manager tells her of the terrorist shooting, and then tells her to prepare for the ensuing press junkets. Before her first interview, Celeste takes her teenage daughter, Albertine (conceived in the encounter with the musician), to lunch. Once there, Celeste unveils her erratic and destructive behavior, aided by alcohol, resulting in Celeste and Albertine getting kicked out of the restaurant by the manager. It is revealed that, six years prior, Celeste permanently blinded herself in her left eye due to consuming excessive amounts of methanol while binge-drinking household cleaning products. Celeste then drove under the influence across three state lines, injuring a man in his left leg and pelvis in the process, which resulted in a public lawsuit.
After lunch, Celeste has a heated argument with Eleanor after discovering Albertine has recently lost her virginity. Eleanor has been Albertine's guardian since her birth. The press interviews begin soon after, with Celeste becoming increasingly unhinged after one interviewer mentions the driving incident. Her publicist decides to cancel the rest of the interviews scheduled that day and asks Celeste to rest before the concert. However, Celeste and her manager get high on drugs and have sex.

title: Adrift
overview: A true story of survival, as a young couple's chance encounter leads them first to love, and then on the adventure of a lifetime as they face one of the most catastrophic hurricanes in recorded history.
plot:
Adrift is a 2018 American romantic drama film directed by Baltasar Kormákur and written by Shana Feste. The movie is based on the true story of Tami Oldham and Richard Sharp, two sailors who survived a devastating storm at sea.

The film begins with Tami (played by Shailene Woodley), a young woman from California who has always been drawn to the ocean. She meets Richard (played by Sam Claflin), a British sailor, on a boat in Hawaii, and they quickly fall in love. The two decide to set sail together on their own boat, the Satori, with the goal of exploring the Pacific Islands.

As they navigate through the islands, Tami and Richard's relationship deepens, but they also face numerous challenges, including rough seas and equipment failures. However, their romance seems strong enough to overcome any obstacle, and they continue to sail together, enjoying the freedom and adventure that comes with life at sea.

Tragedy strikes when a severe storm hits the Satori, causing it to take on water and become severely damaged. Tami and Richard are forced to abandon ship and cling to a liferaft as the storm rages on around them. The two are separated in the chaos, and Tami is left alone, clinging to the raft for her life.

The film's second half follows Tami's harrowing journey as she tries to survive the storm and find her way back to land. She faces numerous challenges, including dehydration, exposure to the elements, and encounters with wild animals. Meanwhile, Richard is also struggling to stay alive, but he eventually succumbs to his injuries.

As the days pass, Tami becomes increasingly desperate, and she begins to question whether she will ever see Richard again or make it back to land. In a dramatic turn of events, Tami spots a ship on the horizon and manages to signal for help, finally finding safety after 13 long days at sea.

The film ends with Tami reflecting on her ordeal and the lessons she has learned about love, survival, and resilience. She realizes that her relationship with Richard was real, but it was also fragile and fleeting. Despite their love for each other, they were both young and inexperienced sailors who underestimated the power of the ocean.

Throughout the film, Shailene Woodley delivers a powerful performance as Tami Oldham, capturing the character's vulnerability, determination, and spirit. Sam Claflin is equally impressive as Richard Sharp, conveying the complexity and depth of their relationship. The film's cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty and fury of the ocean in breathtaking detail.

Overall, Adrift is a gripping and emotional drama that explores the human side of survival at sea. With its strong performances, stunning visuals, and true story basis, it's a must-see for fans of romantic dramas and adventure films.

title: 12 Strong
tagline: The declassified true story of the horse soldiers
overview: A team of special forces head into Afghanistan in the aftermath of the September 11th attacks in an attempt to dismantle the Taliban.
plot:
12 Strong is a 2018 American war film directed by Nicolai Fuglsig and written by Ted Tally and Peter Craig, based on Doug Stanton's nonfiction book Horse Soldiers about U.S. Army Special Forces sent to Afghanistan after the September 11 attacks. Chris Hemsworth plays Captain Mitch Nelson, with Michael Shannon as Chief Warrant Officer Hal Spencer, Michael Peña as Sergeant First Class Sam Diller, Navid Negahban as Northern Alliance general Abdul Rashid Dostum and William Fichtner as Colonel John Mulholland.

On September 11, 2001, Green Beret captain Nelson is moving into a new home with his family after accepting a staff job when news of the attacks breaks, and he volunteers to lead his former team, Operational Detachment Alpha 595, into Afghanistan. His commander refuses until veteran warrant officer Spencer, who had planned to retire, persuades him and volunteers to go too. After evaluation in Uzbekistan, the team is chosen by Mulholland to fight alongside Dostum and is flown covertly into Afghanistan, landing 40 miles south of Mazar-i-Sharif, a longtime Taliban stronghold. Nelson takes half the team into the mountains with Dostum, while Spencer holds a fortified camp nicknamed "the Alamo".

Dostum aims to take the city and defeat the brutal Taliban commander Mullah Razzan, who murdered his family. After early clashes, and joined by Spencer's half of the team, they win a series of victories using Dostum's horsemen and American air power. When Nelson reveals that another team has been sent to aid Dostum's rival, Atta Muhammad, Dostum's men walk away. Pressing on with only a few Afghan fighters, ODA 595 uses airstrikes against a large Taliban and al-Qaeda force but is discovered; Spencer is badly wounded by a suicide bomber, and the team is nearly overrun when Dostum returns. In the Army's first cavalry charge of the 21st century, the allied forces scatter the enemy and Dostum kills Razzan. Arriving at Mazar-i-Sharif to find Atta already there, Dostum gives Nelson his prized riding crop and calls him a brother. Spencer survives, and all twelve men return home after 23 days of near-constant combat.

Warner Bros. Pictures released the film on January 19, 2018. It grossed $71.1 million worldwide on a $35 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with 50% on Rotten Tomatoes and 54 on Metacritic; critics praised the cast and action but faulted its lack of depth.

Extinction is a 2018 American science fiction action film directed by Ben Wheatley and written by Jeff Wadlow. The movie stars Nicolas Cage, Olivia Wilde, and Brendan Fletcher.

The story follows Will Sawyer (Nicolas Cage), a former Army Ranger who has lost his family to an alien invasion that has devastated the world. The aliens, known as "The Others," have taken over the planet and are hunting down humans for sport. Will's wife, Evelyn (Olivia Wilde), was killed by one of these creatures, leaving him with severe PTSD.

Will is recruited by a group of survivors who are working on a top-secret project to develop a cure for the alien virus that has infected most of humanity. The team, led by Dr. Kirsch (John Cusack), believes that Will's unique genetic makeup makes him the perfect candidate to be the test subject for their experiment.

The experiment involves injecting Will with a serum that will allow him to survive in an environment contaminated with the alien virus. However, as Will undergoes the treatment, he begins to experience strange and terrifying side effects. He starts to see visions of his deceased wife and becomes increasingly paranoid, suspecting that Dr. Kirsch is hiding something from him.

As Will delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the serum has an unexpected effect: it allows him to transform into a human-alien hybrid. This transformation grants him enhanced strength, agility, and durability, making him a formidable opponent against The Others.

However, as Will struggles to come to terms with his new identity, he realizes that Dr. Kirsch's true intentions are far more sinister than he initially thought. The scientist plans to use Will's hybrid form to create an army of super-soldiers to fight on behalf of humanity.

Will must now navigate a treacherous world where he is both human and alien, all while trying to uncover the truth about Dr. Kirsch's plan and save humanity from extinction. Along the way, he forms alliances with other survivors, including a young girl named Ruby (Brendan Fletcher), who becomes his unlikely ally.

The movie builds towards an intense climax as Will confronts Dr. Kirsch and his minions in a desperate bid to stop the scientist's sinister plans. In the end, Will emerges victorious but not without scars, both physical and emotional.

Throughout the film, Nicolas Cage delivers a performance that is both captivating and unsettling, bringing depth and nuance to a character who is both human and alien. The movie's visuals are also noteworthy, with a blend of practical and CGI effects that create a believable and terrifying alien threat.

Overall, Extinction is a thought-provoking and action-packed sci-fi thriller that explores themes of identity, humanity, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond our control.

title: Pandora
tagline: We knew this day would come.
overview: When an earthquake hits a Korean village housing a run-down nuclear power plant, a man risks his life to save the country from imminent disaster.
plot:
Pandora (Korean: 판도라) is a 2016 South Korean disaster film written and directed by Park Jung-woo. Kim Nam-gil leads the cast, with Kim Joo-hyun, Kim Myung-min, Jung Jin-young, Moon Jeong-hee, Lee Kyung-young and Kim Young-ae in supporting roles. Made in the wake of the 2011 Fukushima nuclear disaster, the film imagines a comparable catastrophe in South Korea and was released in cinemas there in December 2016, later reaching a global audience through Netflix.

Kang Jae-hyeok works at the aging Hanbyul nuclear power plant, the main source of jobs and energy for the town of the same name. His father and brother both died working at the plant, and he lives with his mother, his widowed sister-in-law and his nephew. He would rather earn money on a fishing boat, but family and his longtime girlfriend Yeon-joo talk him out of leaving. Inside the plant, senior operator Pyeong-seok and a group of worried workers and activists have repeatedly warned that the facility is unsafe and should be shut down, but their warnings are brushed aside by plant managers and senior government officials, including the prime minister.

When a powerful earthquake hits the region, the reactor begins to overheat and the plant's outdated safety systems fail to cool it. In Seoul, the president and his advisers argue over whether to vent radioactive material or to begin mass evacuations, while the prime minister's faction works to control information. A limited evacuation is ordered, but with no real contingency plan the only road out of town quickly jams. Before the crew can open the pressure valves by hand, the reactor building explodes, killing or injuring many workers. Jae-hyeok helps drag survivors from the wreckage before collapsing from radiation sickness, and the town's residents, led in part by Yeon-joo, struggle to escape as the authorities abandon them. As firefighters and plant workers fight to stop a second, potentially worse disaster, Jae-hyeok and his colleagues face a desperate decision.

Pandora was a commercial success in South Korea, drawing more than four million admissions. Its release coincided with intense public debate over nuclear safety in the country, and it was widely discussed for its pointed criticism of government secrecy and mismanagement during a crisis.

When Rachel and Edward's eighteenth birthday comes, Rachel wishes to leave with Edward, and in doing so hopefully leave the family curse behind. Edward, out of trauma due to witnessing his parents' suicide and the legacy they left him and his sister, has become a recluse and refuses to leave. Tensions rise when troubled war veteran Sean (Eugene Simon) returns to the nearby village. He is immediately drawn to the mysterious Rachel, who in turn sees in Sean a chance for freedom and so begins to break the rules set out by the lodgers. overview: A young girl is kidnapped during a powerful storm. Her mother joins forces with her mysterious neighbour to set off in pursuit of the kidnapper. Their journey will test their limits and expose the dark secrets of their past.
plot:
In 1986, on Orcas Island in Washington, Lou is a loner living with her dog Jax, who goes to the village to buy some supplies. The sheriff talks to her about a copper bracelet that could help her arthritis, as it helped him. A mother, Hannah, plays hide-and-seek with her young daughter Vee outside their home. Her landlord Lou stops by on her way back home to remind her rent is due the next day.
A large storm is predicted so Hannah's male friend Chris offers to buy supplies. It begins to rain as Chris heads home in his van. He picks up a hitchhiker who kills him. The hitchhiker then cuts power to Hannah's home. While she is outside trying to restore it, he kidnaps Vee and flees with her on foot.
Hannah runs to Lou's house, interrupting her suicide attempt, and tells her that Vee is missing. Before they can leave, Lou's truck blows up from a bomb set by the hitchhiker. Eventually, Hannah and Lou set off tracking him and Vee into the night during the storm.
Hannah informs Lou that the hitchhiker is Vee's father Philip, a former Green Beret and war criminal she thought was dead. Lou finds and kills Philip's friends on the way, clearly showing she is more than she appears to be. She explains to Hannah that she spent 26 years as a CIA field agent.
Lou and Hannah track Philip and Vee to the beach at Eagle Bay. Lou sends Hannah to radio for help, while she goes to confront Philip and rescue Vee. After a standoff, it is revealed Philip is actually Lou's son, who tracked them down after she turned him in while hiding Hannah and Vee to protect them. It is also revealed that Lou abandoned him as a child to avoid blowing her undercover mission in Iran. Philip injures Lou and leaves with Vee, intending to kill all of them together.
Hannah contacts the sheriff, but a call from the United States Marshals Service forces him to stand down, as it is now a federal case. The sheriff goes to Eagle Bay nonetheless, where he finds Lou and gives her a copper bracelet. Meanwhile, Hannah arrives at the lighthouse and manages to get Vee away from Philip. After a scuffle, Hannah injures Philip and flees with Vee.
Lou finds the lighthouse filled with explosives and sets them off from a distance, destroying it to signal an approaching CIA helicopter. Lou and Philip fight on the beach, until she gains the upper hand and hugs him. She apologizes as a CIA agent fires on them, and both Lou and Philip go under the water's surface.
Later, Hannah and Vee are shown in Lou's house, packed up and ready to leave. After a few questions from CIA agents and a goodbye from the sheriff, they are seen on board a ferry with Jax, who looks at someone on the upper deck, not fully in frame. The camera shifts to show a woman's arm with a similar scar as Lou's and a copper bracelet, as she watches Hannah and Vee through binoculars.

title: Hell Fest
tagline: Fun going in. Hell getting out.
overview: On Halloween night at a horror theme park, a costumed killer begins slaying innocent patrons who believe that it's all part of the festivities.
plot:
Hell Fest is a 2018 American slasher film directed by Marcus Dunstan and written by Scott Derrickson, Derek Haas, and Chad Hayes. The movie takes place on Halloween night at Haddonfield Mall, where a group of friends gather to celebrate the holiday.

The story begins with a flashback of a young girl named Allison (played by Caitlin Stasey) who is terrorized by a killer in an abandoned house. The scene then cuts to the present day, where we meet our main characters: Amy (Aubrey Plaza), her boyfriend Ben (Ben Feldman), and their friends Emily (Haley Murphy), Matt (Elijah Attah), and Chris (Jeremy Sumpter). They all arrive at Haddonfield Mall on Halloween night, excited to celebrate the holiday.

As they explore the mall, they come across a creepy and abandoned funhouse called "Hell Fest," which is rumored to be haunted. Despite their initial reservations, they decide to check it out, hoping for a thrilling experience. However, things take a dark turn when they realize that the funhouse has been taken over by a killer who is using the attraction as a hunting ground.

The group soon discovers that the killer is targeting people who are wearing costumes, and they begin to suspect that one of their own friends might be behind the murders. As the night wears on, the group becomes increasingly paranoid and starts to turn on each other. The tension builds up as they try to figure out who the killer is and how to escape the mall alive.

Throughout the movie, the characters are subjected to a series of gruesome and creative kills, which are inspired by classic horror movies. The film's use of practical effects and clever camera work adds to the overall sense of tension and unease.

As the night reaches its climax, the group discovers that the killer is not just a random psychopath but someone who has been stalking them all along. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Allison, the young girl from the flashback scene, is actually the killer who has been terrorizing her friends all night.

The movie ends with Amy and Ben barely escaping the mall alive, while their friends are killed off one by one. The final shot of the movie shows Allison, still wearing her Halloween costume, walking away from the carnage she has caused, hinting that she may not be the only killer in town.

Overall, Hell Fest is a fun and gory horror movie that pays homage to classic slasher films while also offering something new and unique. The film's use of practical effects and clever camera work makes it a standout in the horror genre, and its twisty plot keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: Spider-Man: Far from Home
tagline: It’s time to step up.
overview: Peter Parker and his friends go on a summer trip to Europe. However, they will hardly be able to rest - Peter will have to agree to help Nick Fury uncover the mystery of creatures that cause natural disasters and destruction throughout the continent.
plot:
Spider-Man: Far From Home is a 2019 superhero film directed by Jon Watts and produced by Marvel Studios and Sony Pictures Releasing. The movie takes place after the events of Avengers: Endgame and follows Peter Parker, aka Spider-Man (played by Tom Holland), as he tries to balance his personal life with his responsibilities as a superhero.

The story begins with Peter Parker attending a school trip to Europe, accompanied by his friends Ned Leeds (Jacob Batalon) and MJ (Zendaya). However, the trip is disrupted when Mysterio (Jake Gyllenhaal), a mysterious and charismatic figure, appears on social media, claiming to be a superhero who has been fighting alongside Spider-Man in the Avengers. Mysterio's presence sparks Peter's interest, and he begins to investigate his claims.

As Peter delves deeper into Mysterio's identity, he discovers that the man is actually Quentin Beck (Jake Gyllenhaal), a former special effects artist who created an elaborate illusion to gain fame and recognition as a superhero. Beck uses advanced technology to create fake battles and heroic feats, which he broadcasts on social media to gain sympathy and admiration from the public.

Meanwhile, Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson) reappears, revealing that Mysterio is actually a threat to global security. He has been using his technology to manipulate people's perceptions of reality, creating chaos and destruction in various parts of the world. Peter, along with Ned and MJ, joins forces with Beck's allies, including Maria (Rita Moreno), to stop Mysterio.

As the story unfolds, Peter begins to question his own identity as Spider-Man and whether he is truly making a difference as a superhero. He also starts to develop feelings for MJ, who becomes increasingly concerned about Peter's well-being.

The climax of the movie features an epic battle between Spider-Man and Mysterio, with Peter using his wits and agility to outsmart Beck's illusions. In the end, Peter manages to defeat Mysterio, but not before realizing that he has been living in a world of fantasy created by Beck.

In the aftermath, Peter comes to terms with the fact that being a superhero is not just about having powers or gadgets, but also about taking responsibility and making sacrifices for the greater good. He also begins to rebuild his relationships with his friends and loved ones, including MJ, who becomes more than just a friend to him.

The movie concludes with Peter reflecting on the lessons he has learned from Mysterio's illusions, realizing that the line between reality and fantasy is often blurred, and that true heroism requires courage, empathy, and selflessness.

title: The Lighthouse of the Orcas
tagline: A place to dream
overview: A mother travels to Patagonia with her autistic son with the hope that a ranger and a pod of wild orcas can help him find an emotional connection.
plot:
Released in Spanish as El faro de las orcas, The Lighthouse of the Orcas is a Spanish-Argentine drama from 2016 directed by Gerardo Olivares, who wrote the screenplay with Lucía Puenzo and Shallua Sehk from the book Agustín corazón abierto by Roberto Bubas, the real Patagonian wildlife ranger on whom its hero is based. Maribel Verdú stars as Lola, with Joaquín Furriel as Beto Bubas, Joaquín Rapalini as Lola's autistic son Tristán, Ana Celentano as Marcela, Osvaldo Santoro, Ciro Miró and Zoe Hochbaum; Bubas himself makes a brief appearance. Together with Olivares's earlier Entrelobos and Brothers of the Wind, the film completes a trilogy about the bond between people and animals.

Beto is a ranger who lives in a small cottage beside a lighthouse on the windswept coast of the Valdés Peninsula in Argentina, where orcas come to hunt the sea lions crowding the beaches. He swims and plays with the animals, calling them with a harmonica or by slapping the water, and videos of these encounters reach viewers in Spain. One of them is Tristán, who rarely responds to the world around him but reacts to the footage. Desperate to help him, Lola travels with the boy all the way to Patagonia in the hope that Beto and the orcas can reach him.

Beto turns them away at first but relents and lets them stay with him. Gradually he introduces Tristán to the landscape, the sea lions and the whales, takes him riding on his horse and rows him out in a small boat, where the orcas approach to be touched. The experience is not always gentle: watching the orcas seize sea lions on the shore disturbs the boy, and Lola protests that it is a cruel thing to show them. Tristán remains autistic, but he begins to show small new abilities, walking to the beach, riding the horse alone and calling the orcas himself. Meanwhile, Beto and Lola develop a deep respect and love for each other, until legal trouble with Tristán's father forces Lola to return to Spain, and the story ends on a bittersweet note.

Shot in 2016 in Patagonia and on Fuerteventura, with animatronics and digital effects used for the scenes with the orcas, the film opened in Spain on 16 December 2016 and in Argentina in April 2017, where it drew about 57,000 viewers; Netflix later acquired worldwide rights. El País admired its convincing documentary-like eye and well-orchestrated ending but found the romance clichéd, while other reviewers praised its photography and moving story.

title: Night Is Short, Walk On Girl
tagline: Meeting like this so often, it's due to fate.
overview: As a group of university students go out for a night on the town, a sophomore known only as "The Girl with Black Hair" experiences a series of surreal encounters with the local nightlife – all the while unaware of the romantic longings of "Senpai", a senior student who has been creating increasingly fantastic and contrived reasons to run into her in an effort to win her heart.
plot:
The film follows a night out for two university students: an unnamed woman – referred to as Kōhai (後輩; "Junior") throughout the film, and kurokami no otome (黒髪の乙女; "black-haired maiden") in the film's credits – and an unnamed man – referred to as Senpai (先輩; "Senior") in the film and its credits. The senpai plans to confess his romantic feelings for the kōhai to her that night, though circumstances keep them separated for a majority of the evening.
The kōhai meets a pervert, Tōdō, at a bar. She wins the admiration of two other patrons, Higuchi and Hanuki, after punching Tōdō when he makes an advance on her. Higuchi and Hanuki lead the kōhai in gate crashing strangers' parties, where she drinks an impressive amount of alcohol. She later participates in a drinking game with Rihaku, a supernatural being, and wins.
Meanwhile, the senpai and kōhai both go to a used book festival to search for a picture book from the kōhai's childhood. There, Rihaku is hosting a spicy food eating contest making used book enthusiasts compete to select a book from his rare collection. The senpai notices that kōhai's picture book is amongst the collection, and competes. He wins the book, but the contest is interrupted by the God of Used Book Festivals (aided by the kōhai) who redistributes all of Rihaku's books back to the festival at reasonable prices.
After obtaining the book, the senpai and the kōhai both go to the school festival. Senpai learns that the kōhai is to play the lead in the final scene of a guerilla theatre production. He attempts to replace the male lead in the scene, but is unsuccessful. Having caught a cold, the senpai returns home.
The kōhai visits the companions she has met throughout the night, all of whom have caught the same cold as the senpai, and nurses them back to health. Her final visit is to the senpai, who gives her the copy of Ratatatam and suggests visiting a used bookstore together, to which she enthusiastically assents. The film ends with the two meeting for coffee before going to the bookstore.

title: The Endless
tagline: Time is a prison.
overview: Two brothers return to the cult they fled from years ago to discover that the group's beliefs may be more sane than they once thought.
plot:
The Endless is a 2017 American science fiction horror film directed and produced by Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead, who also star in it. Benson wrote the screenplay and Moorhead shot it, with Callie Hernandez, Tate Ellington, Lew Temple and James Jordan co-starring. The film shares its universe and some characters with the duo's earlier films Resolution (2012) and Spring (2014).

Brothers Justin and Aaron Smith, who as children belonged to a commune called Camp Arcadia, receive a mysterious videotape from the group. Their memories of the place differ: Aaron remembers a friendly, harmless community, while Justin insists it was a UFO death cult whose talk of "ascension" hinted at mass suicide. Struggling with dead-end jobs and lonely lives, the brothers agree to return for a single day. At the camp in the hills outside San Diego, they are warmly welcomed, and none of the members seem to have aged in the decade since they left. Aaron is charmed by the place, while Justin keeps his distance. The group's leader, Hal, shows Justin an equation he cannot explain.

Strange events multiply. In one ritual, members compete in a tug-of-war against a rope that disappears into the night sky, and Justin senses an invisible presence watching him in the woods, which leaves him a photograph of a buoy. Hal admits that he understands no more than anyone else, explaining that two moons in the sky reveal the truth and that the third will bring ascension. Diving beneath the buoy, Justin recovers a tape on which he and Aaron are heard describing the camp to outsiders, and a furious argument reveals that Justin spread lurid stories about Camp Arcadia to the press, leaving Aaron feeling deceived.

Searching for help, Justin discovers that the area is a trap controlled by an unseen entity, in which people are caught in endlessly repeating time loops, many ending in violent deaths. He finds Aaron and tries to convince him to leave, but Aaron argues that an eternal life among people who care for him is better than the empty existence that awaits them outside. Only when Justin acknowledges that he has always forced his brother to follow his lead does Aaron agree to go, and the brothers escape just as the entity appears.

The Endless premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival in April 2017 and was released in April 2018. Critics praised its grounded approach to an increasingly bizarre story, and Metacritic gave it 80 out of 100.

title: Deep
tagline: Under pressure, everything gets complicated
overview: In 2100, when humanity has abandoned the earth, a colony of extravagant creatures still thrives in the deepest abyss of the ocean.
plot:
Deep is a 2017 English-language animated science fiction musical adventure comedy film directed by Julio Soto Gurpide, who wrote the screenplay with José Tatay and Salva Rubio from a story by Soto Gurpide and Tatay. A Spanish production, it was inspired by the director's own experiences of deep-sea diving. The voice cast includes Justin Felbinger as Deep, Jess Harnell, Phil LaMarr, Dwight Schultz and Stephen Hughes.

In a post-apocalyptic future, an ecological catastrophe has flooded the Earth, and the inhabitants of the sea have suffered disasters of their own. The giant colossal squid Kraken has rescued a group of sea creatures and formed a safe colony with them in the depths of the Atlantic Ocean. Kraken's grandson, a young octopus named Deep, finds life in the colony boring and is fascinated by objects left behind by humans, often drawing his best friends, the anglerfish Evo and the shrimp Alice, into his adventures. But one of Deep's pranks goes wrong, causing a rockslide that seals off the colony and traps its inhabitants.

Kraken tells Deep that only Nathan, a wise white whale, can help them, and gives him the landmarks needed to find him. Deep, Evo and Alice set out on a journey through the drowned world. At the wreck of the Titanic they meet Norma, a vampire squid with a passion for musical theater, who forces them to listen to her performance before telling them that they must travel to Broadway to find Nathan, and who is reluctant to let them leave. Along the way, Deep is attacked by a moray eel named Maura, who reveals that she is lonely and joins the group, despite the misgivings of Evo and Alice, whom she had accidentally swallowed. At the submerged Brooklyn Bridge, the friends are surrounded by crabs led by the yeti crab Rico, who challenges them to a dance battle. Through these encounters in the ruins of human civilization, Deep learns about friendship, responsibility and courage as he races to find Nathan and save his family.

Deep received mixed to negative reviews, with a 33 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on six reviews. Its setting, a drowned world littered with the ruins of human civilization such as the Titanic and the Brooklyn Bridge, and its musical numbers set it apart from other undersea animated adventures aimed at young audiences.

title: Gun Shy
tagline: Rock Out with Your Glock Out
overview: A mega-platinum, aging rock star's supermodel wife is abducted by pirates while vacationing in Chile.
plot:
Gun Shy is a 2017 British action comedy directed by Simon West and starring Antonio Banderas as Turk Henry, a washed-up rock star. Olga Kurylenko plays his wife Sheila, with Mark Valley, Aisling Loftus, Jesse Johnson, Martin Dingle Wall, Ben Cura and David Mitchell in supporting roles. The screenplay by Toby Davies and Mark Haskell Smith is adapted from one of Smith's comic novels. The film was released on 8 September 2017.

Turk Henry was once the bass player of Metal Assassin, a heavy metal band remembered for a crude hit song, but since leaving the group he has lived in lazy seclusion in his Malibu mansion, drinking beer and barely noticing his wife, a former supermodel. Sheila finally persuades him to leave the house for a vacation in Chile, the country of his birth, but once there Turk refuses to venture beyond the confines of their luxury resort. While he lounges by the pool, Sheila goes on a sightseeing tour to see llamas and is kidnapped by a group of hapless, financially desperate amateur pirates, who demand a ransom of one million dollars once they discover whose wife she is.

Turk can easily afford the ransom, and is relieved by how little they want, but paying it proves to be much more complicated than expected. Unable to reach his manager in England, he must rely on the manager's junior assistant, Marybeth, who travels to Chile with the money. An ambitious and obstructive official at the United States embassy, Ben Hardin, hopes to advance his career by treating the kidnapping as an act of terrorism and blocks the payment. Meanwhile, Sheila discovers that she is in little real danger, as her captors turn out to be fans of Metal Assassin who are new to crime and need her help with basic tasks. With the help of a crude Australian mercenary, the out-of-shape Turk is forced to take matters into his own hands and venture out to rescue his wife.

Gun Shy was panned by critics. It holds a 0 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 11 reviews and a Metacritic score of 21. Variety called it a witless, graceless farce, and other reviewers criticized its script and direction, although several credited Banderas with providing a few moments of amusement through his committed, over-the-top performance.
