title: The Killer
overview: In lawless badlands, reclusive Cabeleira sets out to discover the fate of his gunman father and grows to be a feared assassin himself.
plot:
The Killer (Portuguese: O Matador) is a 2017 Brazilian neo-western written and directed by Marcelo Galvão. Set in the arid backlands of northeastern Brazil, it belongs to the regional genre sometimes called the "nordestern," which blends the conventions of the American western with the history and folklore of the cangaço bandits. Diogo Morgado stars as Cabeleira, known in English as Shaggy, with Étienne Chicot, Deto Montenegro, Nill Marcondes, Igor Cotrim, Maria de Medeiros and Paulo Gorgulho. Filming began in August 2016, and Netflix released the film worldwide on 10 November 2017.

The story takes place between the 1910s and the 1940s in the state of Pernambuco. As a baby, Cabeleira is found abandoned by Sete Orelhas, or Seven Ears, a local cangaceiro bandit and gunman, who raises him in the wilderness of the sertão, completely cut off from civilization. Under the outlaw's guidance the boy grows into a skilled marksman, knowing nothing of the world beyond their isolated life.

When Seven Ears mysteriously disappears, the grown Cabeleira finally ventures into town to look for him. There he finds a lawless place ruled by Monsieur Blanchard, a tyrannical Frenchman who controls the lucrative trade in precious stones and had previously employed Seven Ears as his hired killer. Drawn into Blanchard's service, Cabeleira himself becomes a feared assassin, carrying out killings for the Frenchman while searching for answers about his foster father's fate. Over the years, his violent career brings him into contact with a gallery of characters, including the local authorities represented by Lieutenant Raul Sobral, and as he discovers the truth about what happened to Seven Ears and about Blanchard's power, he is forced to confront the brutal world that shaped him.

The Killer was the first Brazilian fiction feature produced as a Netflix original and released exclusively on the platform. Brazilian critics praised its cinematography and its evocative re-creation of the sertão, but many found the screenplay overloaded with characters and subplots and criticized its heavy use of narration and its visual effects.

plot:
To All the Boys I've Loved Before is a romantic comedy film released in 2018, produced by Susan Johnson and Matt Tyler. The movie follows the story of Lara Jean Covey, played by Lana Condor, a high school student who writes letters to all the boys she's ever had a crush on, but never intends to send them.

The story begins with Lara Jean, who lives with her single mother, Margot (Janel Parrish), and her older sister, Kitty (Anna Cathcart). After their father's death, the sisters are left to navigate high school life together. Lara Jean's life is turned upside down when she accidentally sends out the letters to all the boys on her list, including Josh Sanderson (Jordan Fisher), Peter Kavinsky (Noah Centineo), and Chris Evans (Israel Broussard).

To avoid awkwardness and potential relationships with these boys, Lara Jean tries to convince them that the letters were never meant to be sent. However, things become complicated when Josh, who is now interested in her, asks her out on a date. Meanwhile, Peter, who is also charming and popular, offers to pretend to be Josh's boyfriend in exchange for Lara Jean's help with his college applications.

As Lara Jean navigates her relationships with these two boys, she must confront her own feelings and learn to prioritize her own happiness. Along the way, she discovers that she has more in common with Peter than she initially thought, despite their initial differences. The movie takes a romantic turn as Lara Jean finds herself falling for both Josh and Peter.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges, including family drama, peer pressure, and self-discovery. Lara Jean's relationships with her sisters and mother are also explored, highlighting the importance of female friendships and support.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note as Lara Jean finds love and acceptance in unexpected ways. With its lighthearted tone, witty dialogue, and charming performances, To All the Boys I've Loved Before has become a beloved favorite among audiences worldwide.

Overall, To All the Boys I've Loved Before is a delightful romantic comedy that explores themes of identity, relationships, and self-discovery. The film's relatable characters, engaging storyline, and sweet romance make it a must-watch for fans of the genre.

Stephanie's journey is one of self-discovery, as she grapples with her past and tries to forge a new sense of purpose. Her transformation from a grieving widow to a skilled spy raises questions about the nature of identity and whether we can ever truly escape our past.

The movie also delves into the theme of revenge and its consequences. Stephanie's desire for revenge becomes an all-consuming force that drives her actions, but it also leads her down a path of destruction and chaos. The film suggests that seeking revenge may not bring us the closure or satisfaction we hope for, but rather perpetuates a cycle of violence and harm.

title: Gnome Alone
tagline: Little dudes. Big trouble.
overview: When Chloe discovers that her new home's garden gnomes are not what they seem, she must decide between the pursuit of a desired high school life and taking up the fight against the Troggs.
plot:
Gnome Alone is a 2017 computer-animated fantasy comedy directed by Peter Lepeniotis and written by Michael Schwartz and Zina Zaflow from a story by Robert Moreland. Produced by Vanguard Animation and 3QU Media, it features the voices of Becky G, Josh Peck, Olivia Holt, George Lopez, Patrick Stump, David Koechner and Tara Strong. The film follows a teenage girl who discovers that the garden gnomes around her new home are secretly guardians protecting the world from a race of ravenous monsters.

Chloe and her mother Catherine move to the small town of Tenderville, into a huge old house whose grounds are dotted with odd-looking gnomes. Exploring the house, Chloe finds a hidden room containing a glowing green gem, which she turns into a necklace. Without realizing it, she has opened a portal in the basement through which small, destructive creatures called Troggs begin to pour. At her new school, Chloe is desperate to fit in with the popular clique led by Brittany, and she gives away the necklace to win Brittany's favor.

When Catherine leaves for an extra shift at work, the gnomes reveal that they are alive. Led by Zook, and including the knowledgeable Quicksilver, they explain that the gem is the Keystone, the object that keeps the Troggs sealed away. The Troggs had long ago devoured the plant life on which the gnomes' world depended, and the gnomes' former leader Zamfeer disappeared after venturing into the Troggs' realm to stop them. The gnomes enlist Chloe to help hold back the invading creatures until the Keystone can be recovered, and Chloe recruits her awkward neighbor and classmate Liam to join the fight. As the house turns into a battlefield, Chloe must also face the consequences of trying too hard to be accepted by people who do not value her.

The film blends slapstick action with a story about friendship, self-acceptance and the difference between popularity and genuine loyalty.

Gnome Alone premiered in Greece and Cyprus in late 2017, with wider international releases following in 2018, and it was released on Netflix in the United States on October 19, 2018. It received mixed reviews, holding a score of about 45 percent on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Bring It On: Worldwide #Cheersmack
overview: When Destiny, captain of three-time national champions "The Rebels," is challenged to a global cheer showdown by an edgy new team called "The Truth," the Cheer Goddess organizes a virtual battle for squads from all around the world. plot:
Bring It On: Worldwide #Cheersmack, released in the United Kingdom as Bring It On: Worldwide Showdown, is a 2017 cheerleading film directed by Robert Adetuyi and the sixth installment in the Bring It On series. It was released direct-to-video on August 29, 2017.

Destiny, the bossy, victory-obsessed captain of the Rebels, an American squad with many world titles, rarely listens to anyone, including her best friend, Willow, although she idolizes Cheer Goddess, a retired five-time champion who now hosts a popular podcast. During a local competition, a mysterious masked squad called the Truth hacks the arena's audio and video feeds and vows to dethrone the Rebels. Humiliated, Destiny runs off and is mocked by a crew of street dancers. As public opinion turns against the Rebels, members quit and rival squads around the world grow bold. After failing to recruit new male members at a diner, Destiny bets the street dancers that they will join if the Rebels beat them in a dance-off, and the Rebels win.

The two groups clash in practice, though Destiny falls for Blake, the dancers' leader and a graffiti artist, while Willow devises new routines with one of the dancers and starts a romance of her own. Destiny dismisses Willow's ideas, records video diaries insulting her new teammates, and only later resolves to become a more open-minded captain. The Truth then appears on Cheer Goddess's show and proposes a worldwide competition decided by public vote. When Destiny's rants leak online, much of the squad, including the dancers, walks out. Destiny works out that Willow formed the Truth with Hannah, a seemingly dim teammate, to teach her a lesson, but that Hannah used it to try to destroy the squad. Forgiving Willow, Destiny rebuilds the Rebels with returning members, including Roxanne, and some of the dancers, and they beat the unmasked Truth in the final.

Cristine Prosperi plays Destiny, with Gia Ré as Willow, Sophie Vavasseur as Hannah, Jordan Rodrigues as Blake, Natalie Walsh as Roxanne and Vivica A. Fox as Cheer Goddess. Reviews were poor: Common Sense Media gave it one star and said it was made on the cheap and lacked flair, depth and wit, and DVD Talk found it forgettable, though it was nice to look at. Cliché Magazine disliked the plot but praised Fox and the friendships between some of the characters.

Unsane is a 2018 American psychological thriller directed by Steven Soderbergh and written by Jonathan Bernstein and James Greer. It premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival in February 2018 and was released in the United States in March 2018 by Fingerprint Releasing and Bleecker Street.

Sawyer has moved away from Boston to escape a man who has been stalking her, but she remains anxious and traumatised. She consults a counsellor at the Highland Creek Behavioral Center, and, believing she is filling out routine paperwork, signs a consent form that commits her to a locked psychiatric ward for twenty-four hours. When she calls the police, they tell her that nothing can be done because she signed voluntarily. Her panicked reaction to her confinement, including lashing out at a patient and a staff member, leads the facility to extend her stay by a week.

Another patient, Nate, explains that Highland Creek runs a scheme to profit from health insurance: it tricks people into committing themselves, keeps them for as long as their insurance pays, and then declares them cured. Sawyer's situation becomes even more nightmarish when she recognises one of the orderlies as David Strine, her stalker, working under a false name. No one believes her, and David drugs her so that she appears unstable. Her mother comes to rescue her, but is intercepted, and Nate, who has been secretly documenting the facility's abuses with a hidden phone, is also targeted. Sawyer is left to fight for her survival against a man who has obsessively pursued her, while the audience is left to wonder at first whether he is real or a product of her paranoia.

Soderbergh uses the smartphone format to create a claustrophobic, unsettling look, and the film critiques both the treatment of women who report stalking and the exploitation of patients by the private healthcare system.

Unsane received generally positive reviews, with about 80 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and particular praise for Foy's performance. It was a commercial success, grossing more than 14 million dollars worldwide.

title: In the Heights
tagline: The time has come.
overview: The story of Usnavi, a bodega owner who has mixed feelings about closing his store and retiring to the Dominican Republic or staying in Washington Heights.
plot:
In the Heights is a 2021 American musical drama directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Quiara Alegría Hudes, adapted from the 2005 stage musical she created with Lin-Manuel Miranda. Anthony Ramos stars as Usnavi, with Melissa Barrera, Corey Hawkins, Leslie Grace in her film debut, Olga Merediz, Daphne Rubin-Vega, Gregory Diaz IV and Jimmy Smits. Like the stage show, it is set in the largely Dominican neighbourhood of Washington Heights in Upper Manhattan, following residents as they chase their sueñitos, or little dreams.

Usnavi tells a group of children a story about the neighbourhood. Years earlier, he runs a bodega and dreams of returning to the Dominican Republic to revive his late father's beach bar, which has just come up for sale. Around him are Abuela Claudia, the matriarch who raised him; Kevin Rosario, owner of a taxi company, and his dispatcher Benny, Usnavi's best friend; the salon owner Daniela and her staff; Usnavi's teenage cousin Sonny; and Vanessa, an aspiring fashion designer on whom Usnavi has a crush. Kevin's daughter Nina returns from Stanford, secretly having dropped out. When the bodega sells a winning lottery ticket worth $96,000, the whole neighbourhood imagines what it would do with the money.

During a sweltering summer, rising rents force Daniela's salon to move to the Bronx. Kevin sells his business to pay Nina's tuition, but she reveals she left because of the racism she experienced, while she and Benny rekindle their romance. Usnavi learns that Sonny, an undocumented immigrant, cannot go with him to the Dominican Republic. A nervous Usnavi ruins his date with Vanessa at a salsa club, and a citywide blackout follows. In the heat, Abuela Claudia recalls her life in Cuba and her hard-won journey to New York, and dies peacefully; the neighbourhood mourns her together.

Nina decides to return to Stanford to help undocumented students, and Usnavi quietly secures a co-signer for Vanessa's apartment. Discovering that Abuela held the winning ticket and left it to him, he gives it to fund Sonny's immigration case. When Vanessa shows him a fashion line inspired by Graffiti Pete's murals, Usnavi decides to stay, and the story returns to the present, where he is telling it in the renovated bodega to his and Vanessa's daughter.

The film was acclaimed by critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 94% approval, but it underperformed at the box office, grossing about $45 million worldwide against a $55 million budget.

title: The Children Act
tagline: We all make choices. Hers make history.
overview: In the midst of a marital crisis, a High Court judge must decide if she should order a life-saving blood transfusion for a teen with cancer despite his family's refusal to accept medical treatment for religious reasons.
plot:
The Children Act is a 2017 drama directed by Richard Eyre and produced by Duncan Kenworthy, with a screenplay by Ian McEwan based on his 2014 novel. Emma Thompson stars as Fiona Maye, a High Court judge, with Stanley Tucci as her husband Jack and Fionn Whitehead as Adam Henry.

Fiona sits in the Family Division of the High Court of England and Wales. She is assigned the urgent case of Adam, a 17-year-old with leukemia whose doctors want to give him a blood transfusion so they can continue treatment. Adam and his parents are Jehovah's Witnesses and refuse on religious grounds. Fiona visits him in the hospital to find out whether the decision is truly his. Adam says he understands that refusal could leave him disabled rather than dead, and he would accept that. When he plays "Down by the Salley Gardens", Fiona sings along, and Adam, deeply drawn to her, begs her to stay. She rules under the Children Act 1989 that Adam's welfare is paramount and allows the transfusion without his or his parents' consent.

Meanwhile, Fiona's marriage is collapsing. Jack, tired of her devotion to work, openly announces an affair with a younger colleague, insisting he still loves her, and leaves. Fiona changes the locks; when Jack returns two days later, they argue bitterly. The transfusion works, and Adam, now recovering, bombards Fiona with messages, poems and letters, saying she has changed his view of the world. He follows her to Newcastle, where she attends a ceremony, and says he wants to live with her, unable to understand why his parents were willing to let him die. She sends him home, though they share a kiss. Later, just before Fiona performs at a lawyers' concert, she learns that Adam has relapsed. She plays "Down by the Salley Gardens" and rushes to see him, but he has refused another transfusion. At home, Fiona breaks down in front of Jack and falls asleep holding his hand. After Adam dies, she attends his funeral and leaves with Jack.

Filming took place in London in late 2016, with Sir Alan Ward, a judge in a conjoined twins case that had inspired the novel, serving as an adviser. The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on 9 September 2017. Entertainment One released it in the United Kingdom on 24 August 2018, and A24 gave it a limited U.S. release that September. Reviews were positive. Rotten Tomatoes reported 74% approval, saying Thompson's powerful performance elevates a flawed film into an affecting adult drama.

title: Revenge
tagline: Why do women always have to put up a fight?
overview: Jen's romantic getaway with her wealthy married boyfriend is disrupted when his friends arrive for an impromptu hunting trip. Tension mounts at the house until the situation culminates in an unexpected way.
plot:
Revenge is a 2017 English-language French action thriller written and directed by Coralie Fargeat in her feature debut. Matilda Lutz stars as Jen, a young woman who is assaulted and left for dead in the desert, with Kevin Janssens as her wealthy married lover Richard, and Vincent Colombe and Guillaume Bouchède as his hunting companions Stan and Dimitri. The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2017 and was released in France by Rezo Films in February 2018.

Jen, a young American who dreams of moving to Los Angeles, flies by helicopter with her married boyfriend, Richard, to his isolated luxury villa in the desert for a romantic getaway. The next morning, Richard's friends Stan and Dimitri arrive a day early for their annual hunting trip, and Richard is forced to introduce Jen to them. That night the four of them party, and Jen dances flirtatiously with Stan. The following morning, while Richard is away, Stan makes advances toward her and, when she rejects him, rapes her, while Dimitri ignores what is happening.

When Richard returns, he offers Jen money and a new life in Canada in exchange for her silence. She threatens to tell his wife, and he slaps her. Jen flees into the desert, pursued by the three men, and at the edge of a cliff Richard pushes her off. She is impaled on a tree and left for dead. Regaining consciousness, she frees herself and, under the influence of peyote she took from Richard's supplies, cauterizes her wound with a heated beer can, leaving the imprint of an eagle on her skin. Transformed from victim into hunter, Jen arms herself and tracks the men across the desert as they search for her body, killing them one by one in brutal, bloody confrontations, culminating in a final showdown with Richard inside the villa.

Revenge received widespread acclaim, with critics praising Fargeat's stylish direction, Lutz's performance and the film's feminist reworking of the rape-revenge genre, which subverts the male gaze traditionally associated with such films. Its vivid colors, graphic violence and excessive bloodshed were widely noted, and the film established Fargeat, who later directed The Substance.

title: The Professor
overview: A world-weary college professor is given a life-changing diagnosis and decides to throw all pretense and conventions to the wind and live his life as boldly and freely as possible with a biting sense of humor, a reckless streak and a touch of madness.
plot:
The Professor is a 2018 American satirical science fiction film written and directed by Michael Paul Stephenson. 

The movie revolves around a young man, who after being diagnosed with a rare brain disorder that prevents him from learning new information, sets out to become the world's smartest person. He achieves this through an unconventional method of memorizing everything he reads, but his newfound intelligence comes at a great cost.

At its core, The Professor explores themes of obsession, identity, and the consequences of playing god with one's own mind. The main character's relentless pursuit of knowledge and power raises questions about the nature of intelligence, creativity, and what it means to be human. As he delves deeper into his research, he becomes increasingly isolated from the world around him, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition.

The film also touches on the idea of the "tortured genius" trope, where a brilliant mind is often accompanied by mental health issues, social awkwardness, and a general sense of disconnection. The Professor's character embodies these traits, making for a complex and thought-provoking portrayal of a mind both extraordinary and troubled.

Ultimately, The Professor presents a cautionary tale about the risks of exploiting one's intelligence for personal gain, and the importance of maintaining balance in life to avoid losing oneself in the process.

The movie also touches on the theme of obsession, as Carrey becomes increasingly consumed by Kaufman's persona and the world he created. This fixation serves as a catalyst for Carrey's own creative growth, but it also raises questions about the nature of authenticity and the impact of celebrity culture on personal relationships.

Ultimately, Jim & Andy: The Great Beyond is a thought-provoking exploration of the tensions between reality and performance, identity and character. Through its nuanced portrayal of Kaufman's legacy and Carrey's enduring fascination with his alter ego, the film invites viewers to consider the ways in which art can both reflect and shape our understanding of ourselves and the world around us.

title: Nicky Larson and the Cupid's Perfume

overview: Nicky Larson is tasked to recover the perfume of Cupid, a perfume that would make anyone who uses it irresistible.
plot:
Nicky Larson and the Cupid's Perfume (French: Nicky Larson et le parfum de Cupidon), also released internationally as City Hunter, is a French action comedy directed by Philippe Lacheau, who co-wrote the screenplay with Julien Arruti and Pierre Lacheau. It is a live-action adaptation of Tsukasa Hojo's Japanese manga and anime series City Hunter, which was broadcast in France under the name Nicky Larson; Hojo approved the project after reading the script. Lacheau plays the title role, with Élodie Fontan, Tarek Boudali and Julien Arruti, and Didier Bourdon, Kamel Guenfoud, Sophie Mousel and Pamela Anderson in supporting roles. The film premiered in December 2018 and was released in French cinemas on 6 February 2019.

Nicky Larson is an unconventional private detective, a skilled street fighter and an expert marksman who is hired to solve problems that nobody else can handle. Working with his partner Laura, he offers a range of services to his clients, some far more dangerous than others. For all his professionalism and fame, however, Nicky has one great weakness: an uncontrollable attraction to beautiful women, which constantly gets him into trouble and exasperates Laura, who is often left to clean up after him.

A client hires the pair to protect "Cupid's perfume," an experimental fragrance that makes anyone who wears it completely irresistible to others. During a moment of distraction on Nicky's part, a group of criminals steals the precious bottle, and he must race to recover it before it falls into the wrong hands. The chase takes him and Laura from Paris to Monaco and draws in a string of eccentric characters, as the perfume changes hands and creates comic chaos. In keeping with the original series, the film combines slapstick, crude humor and fast-paced action scenes, along with numerous nods to the anime familiar to French audiences who grew up with it on television.

The film was well received by fans and by many critics, who praised its affection for the source material and the energy of the action sequences, though some found the dialogue weak. Simon Riaux of Écran Large noted that it maintained a surprising balance between pastiche and sincerity. The film was a commercial success in France, drawing a large audience in cinemas.

title: Trauma
tagline: Evil requires loyalty
overview: Four friends visit a rural locality of Chile, are brutally attacked by a man and his son. After not finding help in the town, they decide to confront these men with the help of a pair of policemen. But in this way, they will discover that their attackers have in their blood the direct legacy of the darkest period of Chilean history and will have to face the most brutal enemy.
plot:
Trauma is a 2017 Chilean horror film written, directed and co-edited by Lucio A. Rojas. An extreme work of gore and exploitation cinema that doubles as a political allegory, it was produced by Trauma SpA, Border Motion Cinema and Chris Reiben Productions, with cinematography by Sebastián Ballek and music by Ignacio Redard, and was shot over six weeks on the outskirts of Santiago. The film had its world premiere at the Mórbido Film Fest in Mexico in October 2017 and went on to play festivals in Europe and the Americas, including the Brussels International Fantastic Film Festival and Fantaspoa; because of its controversial content it received no commercial theatrical release in Chile.

A prologue set during the early years of Augusto Pinochet's military dictatorship shows a boy being indoctrinated and forced by his father to take part in the torture and abuse of the regime's victims. Decades later, four young women, Andrea (Catalina Martin), her sister Camila (Macarena Carrere), Julia (Ximena del Solar) and Magdalena (Dominga Bofill), travel to a remote rural village for a few days away. What first seems like paradise becomes a nightmare when they are brutally attacked and sexually assaulted by Juan (Daniel Antivilo) and his son Mario (Felipe Ríos). Juan is the boy from the prologue, who still believes the principles of the regime must live on, has been terrorising the locals for years, and is raising his son to follow in his footsteps. Finding no help in the town, the survivors join forces with a pair of police officers to confront their attackers, and their resolve hardens when Juan seizes a local girl, leading to a violent final showdown during which Juan sings an old military song.

The film provoked controversy for its scenes of torture, rape, incest, necrophilia and infanticide, and for its condemnation of the Pinochet regime and the way its brutality is handed down from fathers to sons. Rojas and the cast explained that the four leads insisted he show the violence without restraint so that the message would come through; the assault scene took three days to film.

Screen Anarchy's review of the premiere called it one of the most brutal, graphic and disturbing horror films in recent memory, comparable to A Serbian Film but more overt in its political message, praising the four actresses and singling out Antivilo's portrayal of Juan as one of the most terrible villains of the year, while finding the final act's arming of the protagonists somewhat silly.
